confirmed.title: Wallet-paid ride: a cheaper route change is refunded to the wallet twice (credited now and again at completion)
confirmed.description: When a route change makes the trip cheaper and the rider keeps the default 'Movera Wallet' refund, `_creditWallet` credits `-quote.differenceKr` to the local wallet ledger straight away. `apply` has already saved the snapshot with the new, lower `price`. When the trip completes, `WalletController.chargeCompletedRide` debits a wallet-paid ride for `snapshot.price`, which is already the reduced fare. So the reduction is counted twice: once as the wallet credit and once because the debit is smaller. The 'use wallet first' split has the same problem when the new fare is below `walletAmountMinor`, because the debit is `min(walletAmountMinor, fare)`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Wallet ride booked at 300 kr. In the trip the rider removes a stop and the new price is 250 kr. Refund goes to Wallet, so +50 kr is credited now. At completion the wallet is debited 250 kr. In total the wallet pays 200 kr for a 250 kr trip.
confirmed.suggested_fix: For wallet-paid rides, do not credit the wallet locally, or charge the booked price minus the refunds already credited at completion. One ledger rule must own the difference.

verdicts.reason: A wallet ride is never debited at booking. The only debit is chargeCompletedRide at completion (wallet_controller.dart:257-318), and its only caller is ride_completed.dart:163. A cheaper route change saves the snapshot with the new lower price (route_change_controller.dart:287,296). _creditWallet then credits -differenceKr to the local wallet right away (route_change_flow.dart:158-166), because the refund destination defaults to wallet whenever a wallet exists (route_change_sheet.dart:77-82). At completion the debit is snapshot.price, which is already the reduced fare (wallet_controller.dart:282-283). Example: booked at 300, changed to 250. The wallet gets +50, then -250, so it pays 200 for a 250 trip. The money was refunded without ever being charged.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. I grepped every wallet mutation in lib/ (chargeRide, refund): only route_change_flow.dart:166 and the completion charge exist, and there is no charge or hold at booking. I followed apply -> RideSnapshotStore.save -> chargeCompletedRideById -> snapshot.price.

verdicts.reason: A wallet ride is not debited until completion. The only debit is WalletController.chargeCompletedRide (wallet_controller.dart:282-283, amount = snapshot.price), and there is no debit at booking time. RouteChangeController.apply saves the snapshot with price: newPrice (route_change_controller.dart:287 and :296), and completion reads that snapshot from the store (active_ride_controller.dart:368-383). RouteChangeSheet defaults the refund to the wallet whenever a wallet exists (route_change_sheet.dart:77-82), and _creditWallet (route_change_flow.dart:159-166) credits -differenceKr straight away. So the price reduction is counted twice.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u42_test.dart: balance 500, wallet.refund(amount: 50) as _creditWallet does for 300->250, then chargeCompletedRide on a wallet snapshot with price 250. Output: 'wallet.ride_charged {amount: 250.0}' and 'start 500, after = 300.0, net paid = 200.0' for a 250 kr trip. The file was deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: Driver drop while a child route is open pops that route instead of Waiting; Waiting is left dead and Finding never restarts the search
confirmed.description: `_onLiveTick` handles `cancelledByDriver` immediately and deliberately bypasses the route-current gate (lines 405-415). `_researchAfterDriverCancel` disposes tracking, reconciles the session back to `findingDriver`, sets `_leaving = true`, then does `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(true); return; }` (651-659). The app has a single navigator (app.dart:34, MoveraSheet.show uses rootNavigator: true), so `pop(true)` pops whatever route is on top: the driver profile (`_openProfile`, 976), Chat (waiting_sheet_bits 215), the arrived sheet, the cancel/reason sheets, the Safety Kit or the RoutePickerPage opened by `_changeRoute`. Waiting itself stays mounted with `_leaving = true`, `_mapParked = true` and a disposed `DriverTrackingController`; `FindingDrivers._openWaiting` (finding_drivers.dart 535-557) never receives `true`, so `_resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel` never runs and `FindingDriverController.active` stays null. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (Waiting pushed over a parent, DriverProfilePage pushed above it, `MockRideRealtime.cancelByDriver()`): output was `profile still mounted: false`, `waiting still mounted: true`, `waiting route result: null`, `session status: RideStatus.findingDriver`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider is on Waiting and opens the driver's profile (or chat, or the cancel sheet, or 'Change route'); the driver drops the ride. The profile page closes by itself, the rider lands back on a grey, parked Waiting screen showing the old driver with no live updates and no way to cancel (`_confirmCancel` returns on `_leaving`), while the server trip is back in `searching` and the next driver's acceptance is never shown.
confirmed.evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:410-415 `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByDriver) { if (!_leaving && !_completedOpened) { unawaited(_researchAfterDriverCancel()); } return; }` ; 651-659 `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (navigator.canPop()) { _researching = false; navigator.pop(true); return; }` ; movera_sheet.dart:48-51 `Navigator.of(context, rootNavigator: true).push<T>(route)` ; finding_drivers.dart:556 `if (!mounted || researchDriver != true) return;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pop Waiting's own route by reference (store `ModalRoute.of(context)` in initState and use `Navigator.of(context).popUntil`/`removeRoute` on that route, or `closeRouteByReference`-style logic), or defer the research until `_routeIsCurrent` like the other stage navigations do.

verdicts.reason: waiting_for_driver.dart:410-415 handles cancelledByDriver right away and skips the _routeIsCurrent gate. _researchAfterDriverCancel then calls Navigator.of(context).pop(true) at 651-659. That pops whatever route is on top, not Waiting's own route, and nothing first closes child routes such as _openProfile (Navigator.push at 976) or Chat (waiting_sheet_bits.dart:215). So the child route is popped and Waiting stays mounted with _leaving=true and a disposed tracker. FindingDrivers._openWaiting never gets true back (finding_drivers.dart:556 `if (!mounted || researchDriver != true) return;`), so _resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel never runs. Meanwhile the session has already been reset to findingDriver by resumeSearchingAfterDriverCancel (active_ride_controller.dart:318-335).
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_r27_test.dart, based on test/finding_driver/audit_fix_research_route_test.dart: Finding, then assignNow to reach Waiting, then push a plain child page, then holdAssignment + cancelByDriver, pumped 60x50ms. Output: 'AUDIT child mounted: false', 'AUDIT waiting mounted: true', 'AUDIT finding active controller: null', 'AUDIT session: RideStatus.findingDriver'. The test passed (it only prints). File deleted.

verdicts.reason: _researchAfterDriverCancel calls Navigator.of(context).pop(true) whenever canPop() is true (waiting_for_driver.dart:651-659). That pops whatever route is on top, not Waiting's own route, and nothing checks _routeIsCurrent: the cancelledByDriver branch (410-415) skips that check on purpose. When a child route such as DriverProfilePage (976), chat or a sheet is on top, that child is the one popped. Waiting stays mounted with _leaving=true, its map parked and its tracking disposed. FindingDrivers._openWaiting never gets `true` back (finding_drivers.dart:556), so _resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel never runs and the search controller is never restarted. The rider is left on a dead Waiting screen while the server is searching again.
verdicts.repro: Wrote and ran test/_audit_r27_test.dart (now deleted), based on test/finding_driver/audit_fix_research_route_test.dart. Steps: Finding pushed, assignNow, Waiting shown, a child MaterialPageRoute pushed from Waiting's context, then holdAssignment and cancelByDriver. Output: `child mounted before: true`, `child still mounted: false`, `waiting still mounted: true`, `FindingDriverController.active: null`, `session status: RideStatus.findingDriver`, `waiting route isCurrent: true`. After another assignNow: `waiting count 1, status RideStatus.findingDriver`, so the next driver is never shown.

confirmed.title: History archives book-now rides with a UTC DateTime that is then rendered field-by-field, so times/dates show in UTC
confirmed.description: recordFor stores `scheduledPickupAt: ended.toUtc()` (line 201) and `createdAt: snapshot.createdAt.toUtc()`. The History UI then formats that DateTime with helpers that read the DateTime's own fields rather than converting to local: ReservationFormat.time (lib/features/reservations/presentation/reservation_format.dart:70-74 uses `when.hour`/`when.minute`), ReservationFormat.moment/historyWhen (221-227 compare `when.year/month/day` to a local `DateTime.now()`), weekdayDate/_dayMonth via L10n.formatDate (intl formats the instance's fields; a UTC DateTime prints UTC), called from lib/features/history/presentation/ride_history.dart:546 `ReservationFormat.historyWhen(ride)`. HomeJourneySection.fromRides (lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_journey_section.dart:74-83) likewise buckets by `at.year/at.month` and `weeks[(at.day - 1) ~/ 7]` on the UTC value against a local `now`. The only consumer that converts, SupportController (`when: ride.scheduledPickupAt.toLocal()`), shows the correct intent. Verified by throwaway test: a ride ended at 14:30 CEST archived via recordFor and formatted with ReservationFormat.time gave '12:30'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Stockholm rider finishes a ride at 14:30 local (CEST). History lists it as '12:30'. A ride ended 00:40 on 1 May shows as 30 Apr 22:40 and is counted in April on the home 'Your month' card; near midnight the Today/Yesterday split is wrong. In Tunisia (UTC+1) every History time is one hour early.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either store `ended.toLocal()` in the archived Reservation (consistent with how book-later Reservations hold wall-clock local times) or make every formatter/aggregator call `.toLocal()` before reading fields (ReservationFormat.time/moment/cardDate/weekdayDate, HomeJourneySection.fromRides). Add a test with a UTC-constructed DateTime.

verdicts.reason: recordFor stores scheduledPickupAt as ended.toUtc() (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:201). The value stays UTC both after the local store round-trips it through toIso8601String/DateTime.tryParse (reservation.dart:408-410) and on the server path via WireTime. ride_history.dart:546 then calls ReservationFormat.historyWhen, which uses cardDate and time (reservation_format.dart:70-74, 138-147, 204-206). Both read the hour, minute and day fields straight off the DateTime without toLocal(), and DateFormat formats a UTC instance's own fields. Every History time and date is therefore shown in UTC, and the day split is computed against a local now.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test (test/_audit_r3637_test.dart, since deleted), run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm. recordFor(..., endedAt: DateTime(2026,6,10,14,30)) and then ReservationFormat.time printed 'AUDIT36 tzOffset=2:00:00.000000 isUtc=true time=12:30'.

verdicts.reason: on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:200-201 stores `scheduledPickupAt: ended.toUtc()`. The stored ISO string ends in 'Z', so Reservation.tryParse (reservation.dart:408-420, DateTime.tryParse) reads it back as a UTC DateTime. ReservationFormat.time (reservation_format.dart:70-74) reads .hour/.minute directly, and historyWhen/cardDate use the same value without toLocal(). HomeJourneySection.fromRides (home_journey_section.dart:74-83) buckets by at.year/month/day. Apart from SupportController:42, nothing in the History or Home paths calls toLocal(). Both the device store (demo) and ApiRideHistoryRepository (release, WireTime UTC) feed this path, so every Book-now History row shows UTC wall-clock time.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c4b2_hist_test.dart (deleted afterwards), run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm. It calls recordFor(endedAt: DateTime(2026,10,14,14,30)), round-trips the result through toJson/tryParse, and formats it. Output: `R36 tzOffset=2:00:00.000000 time=12:30 afterRoundTrip=12:30 isUtc=true historyWhen=Wed, 14 Oct · 12:30 late=Sat, 31 Oct · 23:40 lateMonth=10`. So a 14:30 ride shows as 12:30, and a ride at 00:40 on 1 Nov shows as 31 Oct 23:40 and is counted in October. `+2: All tests passed!`

confirmed.title: Server-backed History silently drops every fully settled trip (RideStatus.closed) and every paymentFailed trip
confirmed.description: ApiRideHistoryRepository._record (lib/features/history/data/ride_history_repositories.dart:56-66) feeds each server TripProjection through RideProjection.toSnapshot and then OnDemandRideHistoryStore.recordFor(snapshot, terminalStatus: snapshot.status, ...). recordFor maps the status with _reservationStatus (lines 243-259), which returns ReservationStatus.completed only for status.isCompletedSurface (tripCompleted | paymentProcessing | paymentFinalized | ratingPending per lib/core/contracts/ride_status.dart:85-89) and ReservationStatus.cancelled only for an explicit cancelled list. RideStatus.closed (trip completed + payment settled + rating submitted/skipped) and RideStatus.paymentFailed are in neither branch, so _reservationStatus returns null and recordFor returns null (line 194), i.e. the trip is omitted from History. In release builds (ApiRideHistoryRepository) almost every finished trip the server returns is eventually `closed`, so the History tab loses the rider's past rides and their receipts; a payment-failed ride (which the rider must settle) also vanishes. Verified with a throwaway test (test/_audit_datamath_test.dart, since deleted): recordFor(...terminalStatus: RideStatus.closed) and paymentFailed both returned null while ratingPending returned a record (`3 passed` for these cases).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider completes a trip, pays, rates the driver. Server projection now has status completed/paymentStatus settled/ratingStatus submitted -> RideStatusWire.fromTrip -> RideStatus.closed. The History screen loads /trips, _record returns null for it, and the ride (and every older settled ride) is not listed. A rider with 50 past trips sees an empty or near-empty History; a trip whose card payment failed also disappears, so the rider cannot see what is owed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _reservationStatus treat RideStatus.closed and RideStatus.paymentFailed as ReservationStatus.completed (optionally carry a payment-failed flag on the Reservation for the receipt), or add a separate mapping for server trips in ApiRideHistoryRepository. Add a test that a `completed`+settled+rated projection appears in History.

verdicts.reason: _reservationStatus (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:243-259) maps a status to 'completed' only when isCompletedSurface is true (ride_status.dart:85-89), and that excludes closed and paymentFailed. Neither status is in the cancelled list either, so recordFor returns null at :194. In release, di.dart:154 uses ApiRideHistoryRepository, and its _record (ride_history_repositories.dart:56-66) passes snapshot.status. fromTrip (trip_status.dart:178-191) maps completed + settled + rating submitted/skipped to closed, and payment failed to paymentFailed. loadOnDemand then skips those null records at :43-44, so every fully settled and rated trip, and every trip whose payment failed, is missing from History.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test (test/_audit_r3637_test.dart, since deleted). recordFor printed 'closed -> null', 'paymentFailed -> null' and 'ratingPending -> ReservationStatus.completed'. A MockClient /api/v1/rider/trips response with one trip (completed, captured, ratingStatus 'submitted') gave 'api list length=0'. The same trip with ratingStatus 'pending' gave 'api list length=1'.

verdicts.reason: ApiRideHistoryRepository._record (ride_history_repositories.dart:56-66) passes snapshot.status to recordFor. RideStatusWire._afterCompletion (trip_status.dart:179-192) maps completed+settled+rating submitted/skipped to RideStatus.closed, and payment failed to RideStatus.paymentFailed. _reservationStatus (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:243-259) handles neither one: isCompletedSurface (ride_status.dart:85-89) excludes them and so does the cancelled list. It returns null, recordFor returns null at :194, and the trip is dropped. ApiRideHistoryRepository is the History source in release builds (di.dart:150-154). A trip the rider has paid for and rated, or skipped rating, ends up `closed`, so it disappears from History. The same happens to a payment-failed trip.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c4b2_hist_test.dart (deleted afterwards). It feeds InProcessMockClient rides with wire projections {completed, captured, submitted}, {completed, captured, skipped}, {completed, failed}, {completed, captured} and {cancelled_by_rider} through ApiRideHistoryRepository.loadOnDemand. Output: `R37 ids=[ondemand-canc, ondemand-final]`, so the closed, skipped and payment-failed trips were all dropped, while paymentFinalized and cancelled were kept.

confirmed.title: The profile is never read from the server, so an empty device copy overwrites the rider's name and consents on the server with blanks
confirmed.description: SyncedProfileRepository calls itself 'the profile the server knows', with the device copy only a cache (FLOW-7). But hydrate() only reads the local cache (`await _cache.hydrate()`). No GET is made. After any sign-out the cache is empty, because UserDataWipe removes movera_profile_v1 and clearLocal resets it to defaults; the same is true on a new device. Sign-in for a returning rider (isNewRider false) goes straight to Home, so the cache is never filled. Every later save sends the whole cached profile through body(): `'name': profile.name.trim()` (''), `language` 'en' and the default consents. The mock accepts an empty name, since it only rejects non-strings or names over 80 characters, and stores it. This was seen in a throwaway run, where the server profile became `{name: , language: en, consents: {rideUpdates: true, emailUpdates: false, promotions: false}}`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rider named 'Ada Lovelace' with promotions on signs out, then signs back in with the same phone (a returning rider, so no name step). She changes the app language in Account. The app sends PATCH /rider/profile {name: '', consents: {promotions: false, ...}}. Her name on the server (which the driver app shows) is erased and her marketing consent is switched off without her doing it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read the server profile on hydrate or after sign-in (a GET or the verify response). Until it is known, send only the fields the rider changed, never the whole cached default profile.

verdicts.reason: SyncedProfileRepository.hydrate (synced_profile_repository.dart:42-45) only reads the device cache. Nothing in lib ever calls GET /rider/profile, even though contracts/openapi.yaml:680-715 defines getRiderProfile. Sign-out runs UserDataWipe, which removes movera_profile_v1 and calls scope.profile.clearLocal() (user_data_wipe.dart:33, 127), so the cache goes back to defaults (profile.dart:46-48: name '', rideUpdates true, emailUpdates true, promotions false). A returning rider (isNewRider false, phone_verify.dart:140) never reaches RiderNameScreen, so nothing refills the cache. The next save from language_picker.dart:29 or privacy.dart:98/116/135 goes through save -> _sync, and body() (lines 60-68) sends the whole cached profile: name '' plus every consent. The mock (in_process_mock_client.dart:1132-1150) accepts an empty name, stores it, and overwrites all three consents. No guard stops it.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: hydrate/save/_sync/body in synced_profile_repository.dart, UserDataWipe.resetInMemory, the phone_verify returning-rider branch, the three profile-save call sites and the mock PATCH handler. Grep of lib for 'rider/profile' finds only the PATCH path and the mock, with no GET. The contract's GET operation exists but is unused.

verdicts.reason: synced_profile_repository.dart:42-45: hydrate() only reads the device cache and never asks the server for the profile. docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:55 defines only a PATCH, with no GET. On sign-out, user_data_wipe.dart:127 clearLocal() resets the cache to RiderProfileData.defaults() (profile.dart:190, name ''). After that, any save sends the whole default body (synced_profile_repository.dart:60-68). The mock (in_process_mock_client.dart:1136-1149) accepts an empty name and stores it, and the consents sent overwrite the stored ones. Nothing on the returning-rider sign-in path fills the cache. One detail in the scenario is wrong: promotions defaults to false, but emailUpdates defaults to true, so a rider who opted out of e-mail updates is opted back in.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u148_test.dart (deleted afterwards): save 'Ada Lovelace' with promotions=true and emailUpdates=false, then reset SharedPreferences and call clearLocal()+hydrate() as a sign-out and sign-in would, then update(language:'sv'). Output: before `{name: Ada Lovelace, language: en, consents: {rideUpdates: true, emailUpdates: false, promotions: true}}`; cache name after re-sign-in ""; after `{name: , language: sv, consents: {rideUpdates: true, emailUpdates: true, promotions: false}}`. Test passed.

confirmed.title: Duplicate of rider-u148: the server profile is never read, so a returning rider's first save sends name '' and the default consents
confirmed.description: SyncedProfileRepository is described as 'the profile the server knows', but it has no GET. hydrate() only reads the device cache (`await _cache.hydrate(); if (_syncPending) await _sync(...)`). Every save sends the full body built from that cache: name, language and all three consents. Two cases leave the cache empty or at defaults for a rider who already has a server profile: (a) sign-out, where UserDataWipe removes `movera_profile_v1` and clearLocal() resets the cache to RiderProfileData.defaults(); (b) a fresh device or browser. Nothing on the sign-in path fills the cache from the server: enterMoveraApp only shows Home, and RiderNameScreen is shown only for isNewRider. The returning rider's first profile write is any Privacy switch, a language pick or a gender pick. It PATCHes `{name: '', language: ..., consents: {rideUpdates: true, emailUpdates: true, promotions: false}}` (the defaults, apart from the one switch they changed). The mock and the proposed contract accept an empty name and merge the consents, so the server-side name (which the driver app shows) is erased. A rider who opted out of e-mail updates on another device is silently opted back in. Account also shows 'Add your name' to a rider who has one.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rider whose server profile is {name: 'Anna Berg', emailUpdates: false} signs out and back in (or signs in on a new phone). Account shows 'Add your name'. They pick Svenska under Language, and pickAppLanguage -> ProfileController.update -> PATCH /api/v1/rider/profile {name:'', language:'sv', consents:{rideUpdates:true, emailUpdates:true, promotions:false}}. The server's name is now empty, so the driver sees no rider name, and the e-mail consent is flipped back to true without the rider asking.
confirmed.evidence:
synced_profile_repository.dart:42-45 `Future<void> hydrate() async { await _cache.hydrate(); if (_syncPending) await _sync(_cache.current); }` (no server read)
synced_profile_repository.dart:60-68 `static Map<String, dynamic> body(RiderProfileData profile) => { 'name': profile.name.trim(), 'language': profile.language, 'consents': { 'rideUpdates': ..., 'emailUpdates': ..., 'promotions': ... } };`
profile.dart:190-199 defaults(): name '', and rideUpdates/emailUpdates default to true
user_data_wipe.dart:127 `scope.profile.clearLocal();` plus removal of the movera_profile_v1 key
language_picker.dart:29 `await owner.update(owner.profile.copyWith(language: next));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Fetch the server profile (GET /api/v1/rider/profile) after sign-in or on hydrate, and seed the cache from it before any save. Until it has loaded, either block saves or send only the fields the rider changed.

verdicts.corrected_title: Duplicate of rider-u148: the server profile is never read, so a returning rider's first save sends name '' and the default consents
verdicts.reason: Same root cause as rider-u148. synced_profile_repository.dart:42-45 has no server read, and body() at lines 60-68 sends the full cached profile. After sign-out the cache is reset to defaults (user_data_wipe.dart:127, profile.dart:46-48 with emailUpdates true), and nothing fills it on a returning sign-in. The mock merges the consents and stores name '' (in_process_mock_client.dart:1135-1146). A rider who had turned emailUpdates off is turned back on, and their server-side name is erased. Personal info also shows 'Not added' for the name (personal_info.dart _valueOrNotAdded).
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the same path as rider-u148: language_picker.dart:29 -> ProfileController.update -> SyncedProfileRepository.save -> _sync -> PATCH with body(defaults-based profile). The default values were checked in profile.dart:46-48.

verdicts.reason: Same defect as rider-u148, a duplicate report. There is no server read (synced_profile_repository.dart:42-45, with only a PATCH in docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:55). The whole default body is sent from the cleared cache (synced_profile_repository.dart:60-68, profile.dart:46-48 defaults rideUpdates=true and emailUpdates=true, user_data_wipe.dart:127). The mock stores name '' and the default consents. Its description of the consent effect (emailUpdates flipped back to true) matches the run exactly.
verdicts.repro: The same throwaway run as rider-u148, after re-sign-in and a language pick: server profile `{name: , language: sv, consents: {rideUpdates: true, emailUpdates: true, promotions: false}}`. The server name was erased and emailUpdates went from false to true.

confirmed.title: Scheduled-ride completion screen shows the previous Book Now ride's driver and receipt (or 'unavailable')
confirmed.description: When a reservation completes, `onCompleted` pushes `RideCompleted(persistOnDemandState: false, ...)`. That screen always renders `RideCompletedDriverInfo` and `RideCompletedTripDetail`. Both read `LastCompletedRide.value` (DriverRepository.current / TripReceiptRepository.last). Only Book Now paths (`ActiveRideController.markCompleted`, `_commitCancelled`, restore) ever call `LastCompletedRide.remember`. A normal Book Now close (`closeCompletedRide`) does not clear it. So the reservation's own driver, addresses, price and payment are never shown. The screen shows the last Book Now ride of the session instead, or the 'details unavailable' empty states. The tip options (`_tripCurrency`) also come from that stale ride.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider takes a Book Now ride Slussen → Kista (kr 189, driver Ali) in the morning. Later the scheduled 23:50 ride Home → Arlanda (kr 450, driver Erik) completes. The completion screen says driver Ali, Slussen → Kista, total kr 189. With no earlier Book Now ride, it shows 'Driver details unavailable' / 'Trip details unavailable' for a ride that just finished.
confirmed.evidence:
reservation_live_ride.dart:102-109 `Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement(RideStageTransition(RideCompleted(status: status, rideId: ride.reservationId, realtime: completionRealtime, persistOnDemandState: false, feedbackAvailableOnCompletion: true, ...`
ride_completed.dart:387-391 `child: const RideCompletedDriverInfo(), ... child: RideCompletedTripDetail(controller: _controller, ...`
driver_repository.dart:106 `final ride = LastCompletedRide.value;` (also :40 for the driver)
active_ride_controller.dart:105-108 LastCompletedRide.clear() only in leaveEndedEarlySummary
confirmed.suggested_fix: Before opening RideCompleted for a reservation, build a RideSnapshot from the Reservation and call LastCompletedRide.remember. Or pass the receipt/driver explicitly to RideCompleted.

verdicts.reason: Reservation completion goes through the custom onCompleted (waiting_for_driver.dart:705-711), so ActiveRideController.markCompleted (and its LastCompletedRide.remember) never runs. reservation_live_ride.dart:102-118 pushes RideCompleted(persistOnDemandState:false) without seeding any receipt. RideCompletedDriverInfo calls rideComplete.driver() -> DriverRepository.current() -> LastCompletedRide.value (driver_repository.dart:40). RideCompletedTripDetail calls receipt() -> TripReceiptRepository.last() -> LastCompletedRide.value (106). Neither checks rideId. LastCompletedRide is cleared only by leaveEndedEarlySummary (active_ride_controller.dart:105-108) and by the user data wipe; closeCompletedRide (448-462) does not clear it. So after a Book Now ride in the same session, the scheduled ride's completion screen shows that earlier ride's driver, addresses, total and payment, and its _tripCurrency for tips (ride_complete_controller.dart:57-58). With no earlier ride it shows the 'unavailable' empty states.

confirmed.title: After a reload, a Ride check whose alert failed comes back as 'Movera safety team alerted', and closing it sends alert:false, so the team is never alerted
confirmed.description: resume() rebuilds the card from the saved event. It sets alertState to `sent` only when the payload has an alertId, and to `none` otherwise. It never restores `failed`. If the rider called 112 (or tapped a red row), the alert POST failed (offline), and the app was then reloaded or killed and reopened, the event is still `acknowledged`, so unanswered() returns it. The answers contain call112, so `called112` is true, but alertState is `none`. _MainStep shows _AlertBanner whenever called112 is true, and _AlertBanner maps `RideCheckAlertState.none` to the success copy (ride_check_card.dart:909). When the rider then taps Done or I'm OK, _close submits with `alert: closing.alertState != RideCheckAlertState.none` (line 697), which is false. The server only alerts on alert==true or an existing alert, so no alert is ever created. The red-row case behaves the same: after a reload the failed red-row alert is silently dropped on close.

confirmed.title: Ride check buttons (Call 112, I'm OK, Done, answer rows, options, Record) have no semantic tap action because excludeSemantics also drops the InkWell's action
confirmed.description: _BigButton, _Call112Now, _RecordAudio, _RowTile and _OptionButton all wrap their InkWell in `Semantics(button: true, label: ..., excludeSemantics: true, child: Material(child: InkWell(onTap: onTap ...)))` and never pass `onTap` to the Semantics. In Flutter, `excludeSemantics` makes RenderSemanticsAnnotations skip visitChildrenForSemantics (rendering/object.dart:4931), so the descendant InkWell's RenderSemanticsGestureHandler never contributes its tap action. The resulting node is a labelled 'button' with no SemanticsAction.tap. The codebase's own pattern elsewhere (safety_ui.dart:161-170, side_menu.dart:709-713) forwards `onTap:` to the Semantics for exactly this reason, and safety_test.dart:111 asserts hasAction(tap) for Safety hub rows; nothing tests the Ride check card this way. RideCheckLayer makes the card modal (non-dismissible ModalBarrier, PopScope canPop: !answering), so a screen-reader user who cannot activate these nodes cannot answer, call 112 or close it.

Double-tap sends ACTION_CLICK, but the node has no tap action, so nothing happens. The card blocks the screen (barrier not dismissible, back blocked), so the rider is stuck on a safety prompt. confirmed.title: Cold start awaits push re-registration (Firebase init, getToken, POST /push/devices) before runApp, blocking the first frame on the network
confirmed.description: `await _registerExistingPushSession()` runs before `runApp`. In staging/production with stored tokens and an accepted push consent it calls `PushPermissionGate.registerIfConsented` -> `FirebasePushService.register()` (lib/core/notifications/firebase_push_service.dart:198-227), which awaits `_gateway.initialize`, `requestPermission`, `getToken` (FCM network round-trip, no timeout in this code) and `_replaceToken` -> `_api.post('/api/v1/push/devices')` (ApiClient `_timeout` 15 s). Nothing in the app is painted until it resolves. The comment at lines 143-147 states the rider must not be kept waiting on push registration and defers `_pushCoordinator.start()` for that reason, but this earlier await defeats it. On the web the HTML boot screen's fallback timer (web/index.html:144 `setTimeout(clear, 20000)`) can remove the loading screen before Flutter paints, leaving a blank page.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Production rider on a poor connection opens the app: the splash/boot screen stays up to ~15 s (API timeout) plus however long FCM getToken takes before Home appears; on web the boot screen can vanish at 20 s into a blank page.
confirmed.evidence: lib/app/bootstrap.dart:130 `await _registerExistingPushSession();` ... :134-136 `runZonedGuarded(() { runApp(const MoveraApp());` ; :40-42 `await AppScope.instance.pushPermission.registerIfConsented(logEvent: 'push.session_restore_deferred')`; firebase_push_service.dart:210-226 `await _gateway.initialize(...); final permission = await _gateway.requestPermission(); ... final token = await _gateway.getToken(...); ... await _replaceToken(token.trim());`; api_client.dart:42 `static const _timeout = Duration(seconds: 15);`; bootstrap.dart:143-147 comment `...before anything slower runs, so the rider is not kept waiting on push registration.`

confirmed.description: DECISIONS R-web requires a live ride to survive a reload on public Pages. The UI does survive it: RideSnapshotStore restores Finding, Waiting or RideCompleted. confirmed.title: Route-change pricing starts from the booked fare, so any route change (even re-quoting the same route) cancels and refunds the rider's offer raise
confirmed.description: `_routeChangePricing` builds `newMinor` from `_bookedMinor(ride)`, which is `bookedFare`, the fare at booking *before* offer raises. It then works out `differenceMinor` against `_fareMinor(ride)`, the current fare, which *includes* the raise. So the raise the rider paid to get a driver comes out of every route quote and every applied route change. On PATCH routeChange, `_setFare(ride, newMinor)` lowers the fare and `maxOfferMinor` is recomputed from it. For non-cash methods a `refunded` paymentAdjustment is recorded. On the client, `route_change_flow.dart:166` credits the wallet with `-quote.differenceKr`. Path: Finding `confirmPriceIncreaseBy` sends PATCH {offerIncrease}, which `_setFare(fare+increase)` applies at line 993. Later, Waiting runs RouteChangeController.quote/apply, which calls POST route-quote and then PATCH routeChange, and those call `_routeChangePricing`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider books for kr 287 and raises the offer by kr 50 while searching (fare kr 337), then a driver accepts. On Waiting the rider adds a destination tweak or re-confirms the same destination. The route quote shows the new price as kr 287 with a kr 50 refund. Applying it lowers the fare to kr 287, records a kr 50 refund (or a wallet credit) and resets the offer ceiling, so the driver loses the raise they accepted.
confirmed.evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:2055 `final bookedMinor = _bookedMinor(ride) ?? 0;`
2082-2091 `final newMinor = rates.roundToStep((bookedMinor + stops.length * rates.convertKronor(25) + (routeKm - bookedKm) * rates.perKmMinor)...); final currentMinor = _fareMinor(ride) ?? bookedMinor; return {'newMinor': newMinor, 'differenceMinor': newMinor - currentMinor, ...`
1928 `/// The fare at booking, before offers and route changes.`
Reproduced with a throwaway test: booked fare 28700, after +5000 raise 33700, route-quote of the *unchanged* route -> `newTotalMinor=28700 differenceMinor=-5000`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Price route changes from the current fare (or bookedFare plus the accumulated offerIncrease), not from bookedFare alone; keep the raise when computing newMinor.

verdicts.reason: _routeChangePricing starts newMinor from _bookedMinor(ride) (in_process_mock_client.dart:2055), which is bookedFare from before offer raises (line 1928). It computes differenceMinor against _fareMinor(ride), which includes the raise (lines 2088-2091). The offer PATCH raises only 'fare' and leaves bookedFare unchanged (lines 993-995). A PATCH routeChange then calls _setFare(ride, newMinor) (lines 891-893), so any route change after a raise throws the raise away and records it as a refund. When the refund goes to the wallet, the client credits -differenceKr there (route_change_flow.dart:158-167). No guard keeps the raise.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u14_test.dart (since deleted). Booked a ride, PATCH offerIncrease 5000, printed 'after raise fare={amountMinor: 27800} booked={amountMinor: 22800}'. Set driver_to_pickup and requested a route-quote for the unchanged route: 'same-route quote newTotal=22800 diff=-5000'. Result: '00:00 +1: All tests passed!'

verdicts.reason: _routeChangePricing (in_process_mock_client.dart:2055, 2082-2091) starts newMinor from _bookedMinor(ride). That is bookedFare, which is set only at creation (line 2315) and is not raised by the offer bump at line 993 (which calls _setFare(fare + increase) only). differenceMinor is then taken against _fareMinor(ride), the raised fare. Any route quote after an offer raise therefore drops the raise. PATCH routeChange then calls _setFare(ride, newMinor) (line 893), resets maxOfferMinor, and on a card ride records a refunded paymentAdjustment for the raise. The driver loses the raise they accepted and the rider is refunded money the server never meant to return. The path is realistic: a rider raises the offer while searching (a main Finding feature), then edits the destination or stops on Waiting.

confirmed.title: Route-change pricing charges booked stops again: bookedKm is the straight pickup-to-destination distance while routeKm goes through the stops, plus a 25 kr fee for every stop
confirmed.description: `_ride()` stores `bookedKm` as the straight pickup->destination distance (lines 2319-2330) even when the booking body carries `stops` (which `_quote` priced through, via `_routedMeters`, lines 2103-2124 / 2134-2137). `_routeChangePricing` (lines 2046-2096) then prices a change as `bookedMinor + stops.length * 25 kr + (routeKm - bookedKm) * perKm`, where `routeKm` is pickup -> stops -> destination (lines 2071-2080). For a ride booked with a stop, a route change that keeps the same stop charges the stop's detour kilometres a second time plus a 25 kr stop fee that the quote never contained. The result is returned as `newTotal`/`difference` from `POST .../route-quote` and `PATCH .../rides/{id}` (routeChange) and, for non-cash methods, written as a `paymentAdjustments` capture (lines 919-932). Reproduced: booking pickup (59.3293,18.0686) -> stop (59.35,18.10) -> dest (59.3326,18.0649), fare 29 100 öre; route-quote of the identical route: `AUDIT B1: bookedKm=0.42 routeKm=5.69 newTotal=37900 difference=8800` (+88 kr for changing nothing).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo/dev/test flavors (the stand-in backend the live GitHub Pages build uses). Rider books a multi-stop trip, then edits the destination by a few metres (or just re-confirms the same route) during the ride: the sheet shows a large surcharge (here +88 kr), and for card/wallet methods the mock records a captured adjustment for it. Money shown and 'charged' is wrong on every route change of a multi-stop trip.
confirmed.evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:2319-2330 `'bookedKm': body['pickupLat'] is num && ... ? _km(body['pickupLat'] as num, body['pickupLng'] as num, body['destinationLat'] as num, body['destinationLng'] as num) : null,` (no stops)
in_process_mock_client.dart:2071-2087 `for (final stop in stops) { routeKm += _km(lat, lng, stop['lat'] as num, stop['lng'] as num); ... } routeKm += _km(lat, lng, dLat, dLng); ... final newMinor = rates.roundToStep((bookedMinor + stops.length * rates.convertKronor(25) + (routeKm - bookedKm) * rates.perKmMinor).clamp(bookedMinor * 0.5, double.infinity));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store `bookedKm` from the routed distance through the booked stops (reuse `_routedMeters(body)`), and only add the 25 kr fee for stops that are new relative to the booked `ride['stops']` (or drop the per-stop fee, since `_quote` never charges one).

verdicts.reason: _ride() stores bookedKm as the straight pickup-to-destination distance and ignores stops (in_process_mock_client.dart:2319-2330). _quote prices the booking through the stops (_routedMeters, :2103-2137). _routeChangePricing (:2046-2096) computes routeKm through every stop in the body and adds 25 kr for each stop. The client always sends the full stop list, existing stops included (route_change_controller.dart:174-187 builds `located` from all stops, reusing known points), so a route change on a multi-stop trip bills the booked stops' detour distance and a stop fee a second time. Nothing guards against this: the clamp is only a lower bound. For non-cash methods the PATCH writes a 'captured' paymentAdjustment (:919-932). Medium rather than high or critical: it is wrong money on an edge path (multi-stop trip plus route change), in the demo/stand-in backend only.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r89_test.dart (since deleted). Quoted and booked pickup (59.3293,18.0686), stop (59.35,18.10), destination (59.3326,18.0649), then POSTed route-quote for the identical route. Test passed.

confirmed.title: A brand-new install on iOS signs in as the previous owner: Keychain tokens survive uninstall and nothing clears them on first launch
confirmed.description: Tokens (and the ride PIN, SecureRidePinStore) live in the iOS Keychain through flutter_secure_storage with default options. iOS keeps Keychain items after the app is uninstalled, but it wipes SharedPreferences, including `movera_rider_fingerprint`. Nothing records a first run and clears the secure store on first launch. On a 'fresh' install, RideRestoreCoordinator._root -> _shouldRequireSignIn -> _hasSession() reads the surviving access and refresh tokens and skips Sign in. It then calls adoptServerActiveTrip() and opens Home, or the previous rider's live trip, under that rider's account. The fingerprint is gone too, so enterSessionAs can never notice that the rider changed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider A uses the app on a family iPad and uninstalls it without signing out. Rider B installs Movera and opens it for the first time. There is no Sign in screen: B lands on Home signed in as A, with A's server-side history, payment methods and any live trip, and can book on A's account.
confirmed.evidence:
secure_token_store.dart:38-43 return _NativeSecureStore(const FlutterSecureStorage(aOptions: AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true))); (no first-run reset)
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:171-175 _defaultHasSession reads tokens; 444-453 no sign-in when a session exists -> pageFor(snapshot ?? await adoptServerActiveTrip())
user_data_wipe.dart:167-169 previous fingerprint read from prefs (gone after reinstall) -> no wipe
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep a first-run marker in SharedPreferences. When it is missing at bootstrap, clear the secure token store and the ride PIN before the restore gate reads the session.

verdicts.reason: secure_token_store.dart:38-42 uses FlutterSecureStorage with default iOS options. Keychain items survive an uninstall. Nothing in lib uses a first-run marker or calls deleteAll (grep found none). On a cold start, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:171-174 (_defaultHasSession) only checks that the access and refresh tokens are non-empty, and :177-179 then skips Sign in. :444-453 then opens pageFor(snapshot ?? adoptServerActiveTrip()), and bootstrap.dart:33-42 even re-registers push for that session. A reinstall on the same device (shared iPad, a device passed to someone else without signing out) restores the previous rider's session for as long as the server still accepts the refresh token. The fingerprint-based wipe cannot catch this because SharedPreferences is cleared on uninstall. It needs a device reused without sign-out, so this is an edge path, not the main one.
verdicts.repro: Traced SecureTokenStore._active -> _NativeSecureStore, RideRestoreCoordinator._root cold path -> _shouldRequireSignIn -> _defaultHasSession, and bootstrap _registerExistingPushSession. Grepped lib for first_run/firstRun/deleteAll: no matches.

verdicts.reason: SecureTokenStore._active (lib/core/auth/secure_token_store.dart:38-42) uses FlutterSecureStorage with default iOS options. iOS Keychain items survive an app uninstall. No code anywhere in lib keeps a first-run marker or clears the store (grep for firstRun/first_launch/deleteAll finds nothing). On cold start, RideRestoreCoordinator._defaultHasSession (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:171-175) returns true when the access and refresh tokens are non-empty. _shouldRequireSignIn (:177-178) then returns false, and :444-453 goes to pageFor(snapshot ?? await adoptServerActiveTrip()) without showing Sign in. bootstrap.dart:33-48 also registers push for that session. UserDataWipe.enterSessionAs (user_data_wipe.dart:164-173) needs the previous fingerprint from SharedPreferences, which the uninstall erased, so it cannot catch the change of rider either. The only limit: the previous owner's refresh token must still be valid.
verdicts.repro: Traced the cold-start path bootstrap -> RideRestoreCoordinator root -> _shouldRequireSignIn -> _defaultHasSession -> SecureTokenStore -> Keychain. Found no reset on first launch. Keychain persistence after uninstall is how iOS behaves; it cannot be run in a flutter test.

confirmed.title: Cancel-first sends /cancel without the reasonCode openapi CancelCommand requires; a contract server's 400 is treated as transient, so the cancel stays queued and the search stays live (the in-process mock hides this)
confirmed.description: openapi.yaml `CancelCommand` has `required: [expectedVersion, reasonCode]`, and CONTRACT.md §1 says validation errors are `400 invalid_request`. With cancel-first, Finding calls `_match.cancelSearch()` with no reason (finding_drivers.dart:580). `_requestServerCancel` then posts `entry.body(reasonId)`, which is `{...CancelReasonCodes.riderCancelBody(null), 'expectedVersion': v}`. `riderCancelBody(null)` returns `{}`, so the body has no `reasonCode`. BookingCoordinator's stand-down and duplicate cancels (booking_coordinator.dart:778 and 808) send only `{expectedVersion}` too. The in-process mock hides this because it only checks `reasonCode` when one is sent (in_process_mock_client.dart:684 `reasonCode != null && ...`). A server that follows openapi answers 400. `isPermanentCancelFailure` (pending_cancel_store.dart:161) treats only 404/409/410/422 as final, so a 400 falls through to `SearchCancelResult.queued`. The ride stays live and the outbox replays the same rejected body on every reconnect. The why-sheet reason is sent later as a second `/cancel` on an already `cancelled_by_rider` trip. The contract table has no row for that (terminal → `409 invalid_transition`), so on a contract server the reason is also lost. The mock's R-O3 branch (in_process_mock_client.dart:690) answers 200 there instead.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Against a backend built from openapi.yaml, the rider taps Cancel request on Finding. The server returns 400 invalid_request (reasonCode missing). The app shows the ride as cancelling but it is never cancelled: the search goes on, a driver can still be matched and charged, and every reconnect resends the same 400 body.
confirmed.evidence:
cancel_reasons.dart:39-42 `static Map<String, Object> riderCancelBody(String? reason) => { if (isRiderCode(reason)) 'reasonCode': reason!, if (reason != null) 'reason': reason, };`
finding_drivers.dart:580 `final result = await (request ??= _match.cancelSearch());`
pending_cancel_store.dart:77-80 `Map<String, dynamic> body([String? fallbackReason]) => { ...CancelReasonCodes.riderCancelBody(reasonId ?? fallbackReason), 'expectedVersion': ?expectedVersion, };`
openapi.yaml CancelCommand: `required: - expectedVersion - reasonCode`
pending_cancel_store.dart:161 `return status == 404 || status == 409 || status == 410 || status == 422;`
in_process_mock_client.dart:684 `} else if (reasonCode != null && !_reasonAllowed(...`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Always send a contract rider code: use the chosen reason, or a default such as `something_else` for cancel-first. Send the later why-sheet reason as feedback, not as a second cancel. Make the mock require `reasonCode` the way openapi does, and treat 400 as a permanent refusal in `isPermanentCancelFailure`.

verdicts.reason: contracts/openapi.yaml:7526-7531 CancelCommand has required: [expectedVersion, reasonCode]. Cancel-first calls cancelSearch() with no reason, and finding_driver_controller.dart:1183-1187 posts entry.body(reasonId). That is pending_cancel_store.dart body() => {...riderCancelBody(null), expectedVersion}, and cancel_reasons.dart:39-42 adds nothing for null, so reasonCode is missing. isPermanentCancelFailure (pending_cancel_store.dart, 404/409/410/422 only) does not cover 400. A 400 therefore loops twice and returns SearchCancelResult.queued (controller :1216). The ride stays live (_cancelQueued, :1123-1136) and the outbox replays the same body (:1482-1488). Not reachable against the shipped in-process mock: it checks reasonCode only when one is sent (in_process_mock_client.dart:683-689). It is a latent contract violation that hits any contract-conformant server. One part is misdescribed: the later second /cancel carrying the why-sheet reason is the documented R-O3 owner decision (mock comment at :690-697, controller :1379-1380), not a defect, although ARCHITECTURE.md:17 says the reason goes as feedback.

No test was run, since the mock accepts the body.

confirmed.title: `MatchedDriver.fromJson` reads `id`/`vehicleMake`/... but the contract `DriverSummary` carries `driverId` and a nested `vehicle`, so a contract-conformant projection parses to no driver
confirmed.description: The production transport `ApiRideRealtime` builds the driver from the projection with `MatchedDriver.fromJson` (api_ride_realtime.dart lines 201-204), as do `ride_projection.dart:68` and the restore path. `fromJson` requires `json['id']` (line 80, returns null when empty, line 83) and reads flat `vehicleMake/vehicleModel/vehicleColor/plate/photoAsset`. `contracts/openapi.yaml` `DriverSummary` (lines 5281-5305, required `driverId, firstName, vehicle`) and CONTRACT.md §2 (`DriverSummary { driverId, firstName, ..., photoUrl?, vehicle: { make?, model?, color?, plate? } }`) never send `id` or flat vehicle fields. The in-process mock sends `MatchedDriver.toJson()` (`id`, `vehicleMake`, ...), so the mock and the parser agree with each other but not with the shipped contract, and no test can catch it. Against a server that follows `openapi.yaml`, every projection yields `driver == null`.

confirmed.title: isLateEcho drops every camera report for 600 ms after a web flight lands, including the rider's own pan or pinch, so MapView.pose goes stale and the next glide jumps back
confirmed.original_title: isLateEcho drops every camera report for 600 ms after a web flight lands, including the rider's own pan or pinch, so MapView.pose goes stale and the next glide jumps back
confirmed.description: After a JS (web) flight lands, _jsGlide sets view.pose to the goal and _landedAt to now (lines 366-368). For the next cameraEchoGrace (600 ms), CustomGoogleMap._onMove discards any reported pose that is not near the landing pose (custom_google_map.dart:202). The check assumes such reports are late echoes of flight frames. Nothing clears _landedAt when the rider touches or moves the map: interrupt() (lines 80-94) and the touching setter leave it set, and _movedByHand only sets movedByHandAt. So the camera moves from a pan, pinch or wheel zoom in that window are thrown away too, as are those of an app animateCamera bounds fit (runCameraUpdate). view.pose stays at the landing pose. The next stepped glide starts from view.pose (easeCameraTo line 325, _glide line 391) and its first frame is sent from that stale origin. This affects a requested trip-map refit (fitBounds with the 450 ms default, a Dart glide) or a follow update once the 12 s hold ends.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the web Home map, the rider taps recenter (a 1 s JS flight). Right after it lands, they quickly drag the map a few hundred metres and let go, all within 0.6 s. Every report is dropped as a late echo, so pose still holds the recenter point. Later an app glide (for example the follow update after the 12 s hold, or a 450 ms refit on a trip map) steps from that stale pose. Its first frame moves the camera back next to the old recenter point, then it glides, which looks like a jump. Worked by reading the code: easing is false after landing, so _onMove's only remaining filter is isLateEcho.
confirmed.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:115-121 `bool isLateEcho(CameraPosition reported) { final landed = _landedAt; ... if (now().difference(landed) > cameraEchoGrace) return false; return !_settled(reported, current); }`; :366-368 `view.pose = view._goal; view._landedAt = MapView.now();`; interrupt() :80-94 never resets _landedAt. custom_google_map.dart:202-204 `if (view != null && !view.easing && !view.isLateEcho(position)) { view.pose = position; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Clear _landedAt in interrupt() and in the touching setter, and when movedByHandAt is set, so only echoes that arrive before any newer gesture or command are filtered.

verdicts.reason: isLateEcho (map_camera_motion.dart:115-121) rejects any report that is not near the landing pose for 600 ms after _landedAt is set (:366-368). The only thing that writes _landedAt is _jsGlide. interrupt(), the touching setter (:70-75) and _movedByHand (custom_google_map.dart:186-193) never clear it. A web drag sets touching (pointerdown) and calls release() -> _movedByHand, which only stamps movedByHandAt and does not interrupt because easing is already false. Its bounds_changed reports reach _onMove (custom_google_map.dart:202) with easing false, and isLateEcho drops them. If the gesture's last report falls inside the 600 ms window, pose stays at the landing pose. _settleTilt on idle then sees the landing pose's tilt already matching its zoom and does nothing. The next stepped glide (a follow update once the 12 s hold ends, or a 450 ms fitBounds) starts its first _approach frame from that stale pose and jumps back. This needs a fast gesture right after a recenter, so it is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only (read-only run). Read isLateEcho, _jsGlide, interrupt and the touching setter, and in CustomGoogleMap: _onMove, _movedByHand, _settleTilt and the RiderMapBridge.listen wiring; also release() in web/rider_map_camera.js. I confirmed by grep that nothing else resets _landedAt.

verdicts.reason: _landedAt is set only at map_camera_motion.dart:368 and nothing clears it. interrupt() (:80-94), the touching setter (:71-77) and _movedByHand (custom_google_map.dart:186-193) all leave it set. For 600 ms after landing (cameraEchoGrace, :147), _onMove (custom_google_map.dart:202) drops every report that is not _settled with the landing pose. The tolerance is 0.00002 deg, about 2 m (:158-163). So the rider's own pan reports in that window are thrown away. A drag that ends inside the window produces no later CameraMoveEvent, and onIdle carries no pose, so view.pose stays at the landing pose. On the web the touch pan is done by the JS layer itself, with no inertia to emit later events. Once the 12 s followHold ends, a follow easeCameraTo starts from that stale pose (:325, _glide :391), and its first frame moves the camera back near the recenter point. A requested fitBounds does the same at once, because _mayMove clears movedByHandAt. The window is narrow (the gesture must finish within 0.6 s of landing), so this is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Read-only, no run. Worked it by hand. A recenter flight lands at T, so _landedAt = T. The rider drags 300 m between T+100 ms and T+500 ms. Each report r has |r.lat - landing.lat| > 0.00002, so isLateEcho returns true and the report is dropped. After T+500 ms there are no more reports. At T+12.5 s, a GPS fix calls animateCamera(follow:true): heldByRider is false because 12.5 - 0.5 = 12 s has passed, so easeCameraTo runs. It sets from = the landing pose, and the _approach frame sends a pose about 5% of the way from the landing point toward the goal, far from where the camera actually is.
verdicts.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:115-121 isLateEcho; :366-368 sets _landedAt; interrupt() :80-94 never resets _landedAt; custom_google_map.dart:202-204.

confirmed.title: Firebase-configured web builds (none deployed today) would replace the root-scope Firebase SW with Flutter's self-unregistering flutter_service_worker.js on every cold start, forcing a reload and killing the push subscription
confirmed.description: `getToken` passes `serviceWorkerScriptPath: 'firebase-messaging-sw.js'` and firebase_messaging_web registers it with `navigator.serviceWorker.register(path)` and no `scope`, so the registration's scope is the app root (`/movera-rider-app/`). The build never passes `--pwa-strategy=none` (publish-web-live.yml line 45), so Flutter 3.47's `flutter build web` still emits `flutter_service_worker.js` and a `flutter_bootstrap.js` with `serviceWorkerSettings` (flutter_tools web.dart: `includeServiceWorkerSettings = strategy == offlineFirst`, compile.dart defaults to offlineFirst). Flutter's loader (`service_worker_loader.js` lines 105-113) calls `navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration()` and, whenever ANY registration covers the page, registers `flutter_service_worker.js?v=...` at the same default scope, which replaces the Firebase registration's script. The 3.47 `flutter_service_worker.js` template is a cleanup worker: on activate it `unregister()`s and `client.navigate(client.url)` for every window client. index.html's cleanup (lines 169-176) deliberately keeps the Firebase registration, so on each boot where push consent was accepted: boot waits up to 4 s for SW activation, the page is force-reloaded mid-boot, the push subscription dies with the registration, and `_registerExistingPushSession` then re-registers the Firebase SW and POSTs a brand-new FCM token (`_replaceToken` only unregisters the previous token held in memory, so stale tokens accumulate server-side). The same `getRegistration()` path also fires once for demo visitors who still carry an old `flutter_service_worker.js` registration, because index.html's async `unregister()` races the deferred bootstrap.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Staging/production web build with Firebase defines; rider accepted ride-update notifications. Every cold start: boot screen, 1-4 s pause, page reloads itself once, then boots; `/api/v1/push/devices` receives a new token on every launch and old tokens are never unregistered. If the reload lands during an active search, the search restores from the snapshot but the rider sees the app restart.
confirmed.evidence: lib/core/notifications/firebase_push_service.dart:112-121 `_messaging.getToken(vapidKey: vapidKey, serviceWorkerScriptPath: kIsWeb ? moveraFirebaseMessagingServiceWorker : null)`; firebase_messaging_web-4.2.5 interop/messaging.dart:50-53 `navigator.serviceWorker.register(serviceWorkerScriptPath.toJS)` (no scope); web/index.html:172-176 keeps registrations whose scriptURL contains 'firebase-messaging-sw.js'; web/index.html:570 `<script src="flutter_bootstrap.js" defer>`; /opt/flutter/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/web/file_generators/js/flutter_service_worker.js:7-30 `await self.registration.unregister(); ... client.navigate(client.url)`; engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/flutter_js/src/service_worker_loader.js:106-113 `getRegistration().then(registration => { if (registration) return registerAndActivate(); })`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Build with `--pwa-strategy=none` (or ship a custom web/flutter_bootstrap.js that calls `_flutter.loader.load()` without `serviceWorkerSettings`), and/or register firebase-messaging-sw.js under its own scope (e.g. `firebase-cloud-messaging-push-scope`) so the loader's root-scope `getRegistration()` finds nothing.

confirmed.title: Inbound push routing (foreground, opened and the launch notification) is attached only after the backend acknowledges the device token
confirmed.description: register() calls `_attachInboundStreams()` only after `await _replaceToken(token)` succeeds. That call POSTs /push/devices and throws when the request fails or is not acknowledged. `_attachInboundStreams` is the only place that listens to onMessage and onMessageOpenedApp and that reads getInitialMessage into `_initialMessage`. If the registration POST fails at cold start (5xx, timeout, offline; bootstrap catches and only logs it), PushCoordinator.start() gets null from takeInitialMessage(), and no foreground or opened push reaches it for the rest of the session. The OS still shows the notifications, because the FCM token exists. Sign-out's unregister() cancels the subscriptions, so a failed re-registration after the next sign-in has the same effect.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The API is briefly unavailable when a rider taps a 'Your driver has arrived' notification that launches the app. POST /push/devices fails, so the tap lands on the default root instead of the ride. Later notification taps in that session also do nothing in the app.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Attach the inbound listeners and read getInitialMessage as soon as Firebase is initialised and permission is granted, separately from whether the server acknowledged the token.

verdicts.reason: firebase_push_service.dart:225-226: register() awaits _replaceToken (the POST to /api/v1/push/devices, which throws if the request fails or is not acknowledged, :277-288) before it calls _attachInboundStreams. Only _attachInboundStreams (:229-251) forwards FirebaseMessaging.onMessage and onMessageOpenedApp into the _foreground and _opened controllers and reads getInitialMessage (:251). The failure is swallowed in push_permission_gate.dart:83-89 (_register catch -> PushOptInResult.failed) and in bootstrap.dart:43-48. PushCoordinator.start (push_coordinator.dart:31-59) subscribes to the broadcast controllers, which never receive anything, and takeInitialMessage returns null. No retry runs except a later sign-in (auth_controller _registerPushBestEffort). So for the rest of the session, a notification tap (including the one that launched the app) and foreground pushes are not routed in-app.
verdicts.repro: Traced bootstrap() -> _registerExistingPushSession -> registerIfConsented -> FirebasePushService.register, then PushCoordinator.start -> takeInitialMessage. Checked every caller of register (push_permission_gate.dart:81 only) for a retry: none.

verdicts.reason: In FirebasePushService.register (lib/core/notifications/firebase_push_service.dart:226-227), `await _replaceToken(token)` runs first. It throws PushRegistrationException when the POST /api/v1/push/devices fails or is not acknowledged (:283-295). In that case `_attachInboundStreams()` never runs, and that is the only place that subscribes to onForegroundMessage/onOpenedMessage and fills _initialMessage from getInitialMessage (:244-267). PushPermissionGate._register (push_permission_gate.dart:79-91) catches the error and only logs it. bootstrap.dart:33-48 awaits this before PushCoordinator.start() (bootstrap ~:138-148). start() then gets null from takeInitialMessage (push_coordinator.dart:56), and its stream listeners subscribe to controllers that are never fed. Nothing retries: registerIfConsented is called only at bootstrap and after sign-in (auth_controller.dart:77).
verdicts.repro: Traced every caller of push.register()/registerIfConsented with grep: bootstrap.dart:40, auth_controller.dart:77, push_permission_gate.dart:81. None retries after a failure, and nothing attaches the streams on the failure path.

confirmed.title: Polling transport misses a driver drop when the first poll of a new subscription (after the Finding to Waiting handover or a retry) already sees searching, or when a later poll jumps straight to a different driver's accepted status
confirmed.description: ApiRideRealtime reports a driver drop only when `status.isSearching && (poll.lastStatus?.isMatched ?? false)` (lines 193-199). `poll.lastStatus` lives on the per-subscription `_RidePoll`, and `onCancel` (lines 78-84) removes that poll as soon as its only listener cancels. Every handover cancels the only listener: Finding `_openWaiting` calls `_match.dispose()`, which cancels `_sub` (finding_driver_controller.dart:1682), before Waiting subscribes again. `_retryLiveFeed` does the same. So Waiting's tracking always starts with a new poll whose `lastStatus` is null. (a) When the driver drops in the 'just assigned' stage, before Waiting's first poll returns, that first projection is `searching`, `reassigned` is false, and the event goes out as plain `findingDriver`. The first poll can be late because it fails and backs off for 1, 2, 4... s. DriverTrackingController accepts it. Waiting `_onLiveTick` (waiting_for_driver.dart:410-433) only re-dispatches on `cancelledByDriver`, so Waiting stays up with the dropped driver's card. (b) Even inside one poll, a drop is missed when driver B accepts before the next successful poll: every 2 s, or a backgrounded app whose timers paused. The stream then goes straight from driverArriving/driverWaiting(A) to driverAssigned(B). Nothing compares driver ids, so no notice is shown.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Release build on the polling transport. The rider is at the 'driver waiting' stage, the arrived sheet showing driver A (Elin, plate MVR 204) is up, and the phone is pocketed so the app is backgrounded. A drops and dispatch matches B within a minute. On resume, the first poll returns `accepted` with driver B. Waiting swaps the card to B with no 'your driver cancelled' notice. The arrived sheet with A's name and plate stays on top, because it closes only on trip start (line 396). B's arrival is never announced, because `_arrivalAnnounced` is already true (line 452). Variant (a): A accepts and drops within about 1 s. Waiting shows 'Driver found / leave now, Elin' while the server is searching. If no one accepts, `expired` reaches Waiting as noDriverFound and `markExternalTerminal` clears it without archiving (noDriverFound is not in the archive list at active_ride_controller.dart:353-358). The rider is also never offered RIDE-19 'Try again'.
confirmed.evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:193-199: `final reassigned = status.isSearching && (poll.lastStatus?.isMatched ?? false); ... if (reassigned) status = RideStatus.cancelledByDriver;`

confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep reassignment state (last lifecycle status and driver id) per ride id, outside the per-subscription poll, for example in a map like `_sequences`. Also treat a change of `driver.id` between two matched projections as a driver-cancelled reassignment, so Waiting re-dispatches or at least shows the notice, closes the old arrived sheet and resets `_arrivalAnnounced`.

Finding's _openWaiting calls _match.dispose() (finding_drivers.dart:528), which cancels _sub (finding_driver_controller.dart:1682), then awaits endOfFrame before pushing Waiting.
