confirmed.title: After the not-found pause, a successful resync never restarts periodic polling: the ride freezes while the connection reports connected
confirmed.description: `_endNotFound` (lines 347-353) cancels `poll.timer` and sets `poll.timer = null` after `notFoundLimit` consecutive 404s. `reconnectAndResync` (lines 379-390) only flips `poll.ended = false`, lowers `poll.notFound` and runs one forced `_poll`. Nothing re-creates the `Timer.periodic` that `subscribe()`'s `onListen` made (lines 69-77), and `onListen` does not run again because the broadcast controller already has its listener. When the forced poll succeeds, the success path calls `connection.markConnected()` (line 256) so the UI banner clears, but no further GET is ever issued for that ride: the Waiting/in-trip screen keeps showing the projection from that single read until the user triggers another manual resync. Reproduced with a throwaway test (3x404, resync -> 200, pollInterval 20 ms): `AUDIT A: events after resync = 1, state = RealtimeState.connected` then `AUDIT A: calls after 200ms of connected state = 4` (no new polls). Callers: `FindingDriverController` lines 897/1156/1288/1642, `WaitingForDriver` line 929, `RideRestoreCoordinator` line 167, `notification_navigation.dart` line 89 all use `reconnectAndResync` as the recovery path.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Production transport (staging/production flavors). The trip endpoint answers 404 three polls in a row (replica lag, a brief routing fault). Polling pauses and the banner shows failed. The rider taps retry / the app resumes -> `reconnectAndResync` -> 200, banner says connected. From then on the driver's position, arrival, boarding and completion never arrive on this screen; the ride appears stuck at that status indefinitely although the connection state claims it is live.
confirmed.evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:347-353 `void _endNotFound(_RidePoll poll) { poll.ended = true; poll.timer?.cancel(); poll.timer = null; ... connection.markFailed(); }`
api_ride_realtime.dart:379-390 `Future<void> reconnectAndResync(String rideId) async { ... if (poll.ended) { poll.ended = false; poll.notFound = poll.notFound > 0 ? notFoundLimit - 1 : 0; } await _poll(poll, force: true); }`
api_ride_realtime.dart:69-77 the only place a timer is created: `onListen: () { if (poll.timer != null) return; ... poll.timer = Timer.periodic(pollInterval, (_) => unawaited(_poll(poll))); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: In `reconnectAndResync` (or in `_poll`'s success path when `poll.timer == null` and the controller has listeners) re-create `poll.timer = Timer.periodic(pollInterval, (_) => unawaited(_poll(poll)))` once the forced read succeeds; keep it cancelled while `poll.ended` is true.

verdicts.reason: After notFoundLimit consecutive 404s, _endNotFound (api_ride_realtime.dart:347-353) cancels poll.timer and sets it to null. reconnectAndResync (:379-390) only resets poll.ended and poll.notFound and runs a single forced _poll. The only place a Timer.periodic is created is the broadcast controller's onListen (:69-77), and onListen does not fire again while the existing listener (DriverTrackingController._sub, FindingDriverController._sub) stays subscribed. When the forced read succeeds, connection.markConnected() runs, so the UI reports a live connection, but no further GET is ever issued for that ride. Driver position and status changes stop arriving until another manual resync or a resubscribe. All the listed recovery callers (waiting_for_driver.dart:929, finding_driver_controller.dart:897/1156/1288/1642, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:167, notification_navigation.dart:89) use only reconnectAndResync.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r23_poll_test.dart (deleted afterwards): MockClient answering 404 three times and then 200 projections with a rising version, pollInterval 20ms, and a clock that skips the backoff. Output: `AUDIT before resync calls=3 events=0 state=RealtimeState.failed`, `AUDIT after resync calls=4 events=0 state=RealtimeState.connected`, `AUDIT 300ms later calls=4 (was 4) events=1 state=RealtimeState.connected` -- no polls after the resync while the state reports connected.

verdicts.reason: `_endNotFound` cancels the poll timer and sets it to null (api_ride_realtime.dart:347-353). `reconnectAndResync` (:379-390) only resets `ended`/`notFound` and runs one forced `_poll`. The only place a `Timer.periodic` is created is the broadcast controller's `onListen` (:69-77), and that does not fire again while the existing listener stays subscribed. Callers do not re-subscribe after a resync (waiting_for_driver.dart:929, finding_driver_controller.dart:897/1156/1288/1642, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:167). A successful forced poll calls `connection.markConnected()` (:256), so the banner clears while no further GET is ever sent. ApiRideRealtime is the transport in non-mock flavors (di.dart:196-206). This is an edge path: it needs 3 consecutive 404s on an active ride.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_vq7c1b3_test.dart: ApiRideRealtime over a MockClient, pollInterval 20 ms, server returning 404 three times, then reconnectAndResync with the server switched to 200. Output: `AUDIT23 calls before resync=3 state=RealtimeState.failed`, then `AUDIT23 after resync calls=4 events=0 state=RealtimeState.connected`, then `AUDIT23 after 300ms calls=4 events=1 state=RealtimeState.connected`. That is no new GET in 300 ms (about 15 intervals) while the state reports connected. Test file deleted.

confirmed.title: Mock driver position and arrival are computed against a hard-coded central-Stockholm pickup (never hydrated on resume, hydrated only after the first assignment fix), so after a reload the driver approaches and 'arrives' at Stockholm instead of the trip's pickup
confirmed.description: `_pickupLat/_pickupLng` default to (59.3293, 18.0686) in both the resume path (lines 183-184) and `_assignNow` (lines 263-264), and the driver start position is derived from that default (`lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072`, lines 209-210 and 265-266). The real pickup is only fetched by `_hydratePickup()` after the `driverAssigned` event (line 305) and never on the `primeResume` path; after a web reload the stand-in server is empty anyway so `_pickup()` 404s and keeps the default (line 660). `_startGps` therefore lerps toward and declares `driverWaiting` within 50 m of central Stockholm for a Paris/Tunis/Södertälje pickup, `_etaSeconds` is computed against that point, and the resumed `emit()` sets `_acceptedAt ??= now` / `_waitingSince ??= now` (lines 328-333) which `DriverTrackingController` adopts (`acceptedAt = event.acceptedAt ?? acceptedAt`) so the free-cancel/waiting clocks restart at reload time. Reproduced: a Paris trip resumed via `primeResume(driverArriving)`: `AUDIT D: resumed event lat=59.3365 lng=18.0638 eta=102s acceptedAt=<now>`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo build (R-web: 'a live ride must survive browser reload'). Rider books Gare du Nord -> Louvre (Q7 Paris zone) or a Södertälje pickup, gets a driver, reloads the tab: the driver marker appears in central Stockholm, the ETA reads ~2 min then jumps, the car 'arrives' and the trip starts from a point tens or hundreds of km from the pickup, and the free-cancel countdown restarts from the reload.
confirmed.evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:179-184 `if (resumeStatus != null && resumeStatus.isMatched) { ... _pickupLat ??= 59.3293; _pickupLng ??= 18.0686;`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:209-211 `lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; lastLng ??= _pickupLng! - 0.0048; _startGps();`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:263-266 and 303-305 `_pickupLat ??= 59.3293; ... lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; ... _emit(RideStatus.driverAssigned); _startGps(); unawaited(_hydratePickup());`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:328-333 `} else if (status.isMatched) { _acceptedAt ??= DateTime.now().toUtc(); } if (status == RideStatus.driverWaiting) { _waitingSince ??= DateTime.now().toUtc(); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Let `primeResume` (and the first assignment) take the pickup coordinates and the snapshot's `acceptedAt`/`waitingArrivedAt`; hydrate the pickup before emitting `driverAssigned`, and do not stamp `_acceptedAt`/`_waitingSince` with the resume time.

verdicts.corrected_title: Mock driver position and arrival are computed against a hard-coded central-Stockholm pickup (never hydrated on resume, hydrated only after the first assignment fix), so after a reload the driver approaches and 'arrives' at Stockholm instead of the trip's pickup
verdicts.reason: On resume, subscribe() runs with a fresh instance after reload, so _pickupLat is null. Lines 179-211 default it to (59.3293, 18.0686), seed lastLat/lastLng from that default and start _startGps, which lerps toward that point and declares driverWaiting within 50 m (lines 386-411). _hydratePickup() is only called from _assignNow (line 305), never on the primeResume path, and RideRestoreCoordinator.primeResume (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:340-344) does not pass the snapshot's pickup even though it has it (line 330). DriverTrackingController uses event.latitude/longitude for the driver marker and ETA (driver_tracking_controller.dart:152-163) with no sanity guard. On a fresh assignment, the first driverAssigned fix is also derived from the default before hydration (lines 263-266). The acceptedAt part is misattributed: the snapshot stores no acceptedAt and WaitingForDriver falls back to `_shownAt` (waiting_for_driver.dart:759), so the free-cancel clock would restart at reload time even without the mock's stamp at lines 328-333.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_r24_resume_test.dart (fakeAsync, MockRideRealtime().primeResume(status: driverArriving), subscribe('ride_paris'), elapse 7 s). Output: `AUDIT24 status=RideStatus.driverArriving lat=59.3365 lng=18.0638 eta=102 ...`, then lat=59.3352/59.3341 moving toward 59.3293,18.0686; `All tests passed!`. The coordinates do not depend on the ride's pickup. Test file deleted and git status is clean.

verdicts.reason: In lib/core/realtime/mock_ride_realtime.dart the resume path (lines 179-211) sets `_pickupLat ??= 59.3293; _pickupLng ??= 18.0686`. It places the driver at that point plus (0.0072, -0.0048) and starts _startGps, which moves the driver toward _pickupLat and declares driverWaiting within 50 m of it (lines 386-420). This path never calls _hydratePickup. RideRestoreCoordinator.pageFor (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:340-344) calls primeResume with only status, driver and version, even though the snapshot holds pickupLat/pickupLng (line 330). The first-assignment path (lines 263-266) also spawns the driver near the same hard-coded Stockholm point and only fetches the real pickup after emitting driverAssigned (line 305), so non-Stockholm zones (Paris and Tunis are in rider_zones.dart) start far away. emit() stamps `_acceptedAt ??= now` and `_waitingSince ??= now` (lines 325-333). DriverTrackingController adopts them (driver_tracking_controller.dart:140-144), and WaitingForDriver's free-cancel uses `_tracking.acceptedAt ?? _shownAt` (waiting_for_driver.dart:759), so after a reload the clocks restart from reload time. This only affects the mock or demo transport (di.dart:196, allowsMockTransport), but there the app tells the rider the driver arrived at a point that is not their pickup.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway fakeAsync test test/_audit_c2b3v_test.dart, since deleted. It called primeResume(driverArriving, version 5), subscribed and flushed microtasks. Output: `AUDIT24 first status=RideStatus.driverArriving lat=59.3365 lng=18.0638 eta=102 accepted=2026-10-21 01:38:45.333698Z`, so acceptedAt is the resume moment. After advancing 120 s: `AUDIT24 later status=RideStatus.driverWaiting lat=59.32966689372341 lng=18.068355404184388`. The driver was declared waiting at central Stockholm, with no knowledge of the ride's real pickup.

confirmed.title: Reload while the driver is waiting at pickup regresses the ride to 'driver arriving' with the car about 800 m away
confirmed.description: pageFor primes the mock with the snapshot status (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:339-344). For any matched status that is not on board, subscribe() takes the pre-trip branch: it places the driver at `pickup + 0.0072 / -0.0048` and starts _startGps(). It does this for driverWaiting too. The first GPS tick 3 s later moves only 18% toward pickup, so the distance is still far over 50 m. It then sets `status = RideStatus.driverArriving` and emits it with a higher sequence. DriverTrackingController accepts it, because the version is newer than the seeded one. _persistLiveStatus then saves driverArriving: _wouldRegress allows a lower stage when the incoming version is greater. Waiting goes back to 'driver on the way'. About 15 ticks (roughly 45 s) later the driver 'arrives' a second time and the arrived sheet and the boarding timer run again.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo build: the driver reaches pickup (Waiting shows 'Your driver has arrived'). The rider reloads, or Safari kills the tab. Waiting comes back as driverWaiting, and 3 s later it switches to 'driver arriving' with the car drawn about 800 m away. The stored snapshot is overwritten with driverArriving. The car then drives back and announces its arrival again.
confirmed.evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:206-211 `// The remaining isMatched statuses are the pre-trip approach: driverAssigned, driverArriving, driverWaiting.` `lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; lastLng ??= _pickupLng! - 0.0048; _startGps();`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:401-412 `var status = RideStatus.driverArriving; ... if (distance < 50) status = RideStatus.driverWaiting; lastStatus = status; _emit(status);`
driver_tracking_controller.dart:233-241 `_wouldRegress` returns false when incoming version > stored version
confirmed.suggested_fix: On resume with driverWaiting, put the driver at pickup and call _startTrip() instead of _startGps(). Never emit an approach status lower than the primed one.

verdicts.reason: For a restored driverWaiting ride, RideRestoreCoordinator.pageFor primes the mock (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:338-344). MockRideRealtime.subscribe then takes the pre-trip branch for driverWaiting (mock_ride_realtime.dart:206-211). It puts the driver at pickup+0.0072/-0.0048 and calls _startGps. The first GPS tick (mock_ride_realtime.dart:398-412) sets status to driverArriving because the distance is still over 50 m, and emits it with a higher sequence. backendReconcile (ride_session.dart:98-151) only checks ordering, so it accepts the event. DriverTrackingController._wouldRegress (driver_tracking_controller.dart:232-239) lets a lower stage through when the incoming version is newer, so the stored snapshot is overwritten with driverArriving. On resume the pickup is also never hydrated, so on a fresh page it stays at the Stockholm default.
verdicts.repro: Ran a throwaway test, test/_audit_u27v_test.dart (since deleted). In fakeAsync it called MockRideRealtime().primeResume(status: driverWaiting, version: 5), subscribed to 'r1', flushed microtasks and advanced 4 s. Output: `AUDIT seen=[driverWaiting@6, driverArriving@7] lat=59.335204000000004`, then 'All tests passed!'. The resumed waiting ride drops to driverArriving@7 on the first tick, about 700 m from pickup.

verdicts.reason: When the mock is primed with driverWaiting, it takes the pre-trip branch at mock_ride_realtime.dart:206-211. That branch sets `lastLat = pickup+0.0072` and calls `_startGps()`, not `_startTrip()`. The first GPS tick (lines 397-412) moves the car only 18% of the way, which leaves it about 700 m from pickup, so it emits driverArriving with version+2. RideSession.backendReconcile accepts any fresher version and deliberately does not apply the transition graph (ride_session.dart:140-151). DriverTrackingController therefore takes the status, and `_wouldRegress` (driver_tracking_controller.dart:232-239) allows the lower stage because the incoming version is greater than the stored one, so the snapshot is overwritten with driverArriving. Arrival and the boarding timer then run a second time.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u27u28u29_test.dart (now deleted) ran `MockRideRealtime(); primeResume(status: driverWaiting, version: 10); subscribe('r1')` and waited 3.3 s. Output: `u27 events: [driverWaiting@11 lat=59.3365, driverArriving@12 lat=59.335204000000004]`. All tests passed.

confirmed.title: Pickup coordinates are not reset between rides, so the next ride's driver spawns near the previous ride's pickup
confirmed.description: For a new ride, `subscribe` resets lastLat/lastLng, progress, trip start and clocks, but not `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng`. `_assignNow` then uses `_pickupLat ??= ...` and `lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072` *before* `_hydratePickup()` fetches the new ride's pickup. On the second and later rides of a session, the driver is spawned next to the *previous* ride's pickup. That position is committed to the server through `_persistAssignment` (driverLat/driverLng) and is emitted to the UI, and the GPS walk then has to cross the whole distance. This is a different root cause from the known hard-coded Stockholm spawn (that one concerns the first ride or a resume, when the field is null).
confirmed.failure_scenario: In one session the rider takes a ride from Södertälje and then books a ride from Arlanda. The 'driver found' marker and ETA show a driver about 50 km away at the old pickup, who then speeds across the map for about 100 s; the server projection stores that position too.
confirmed.evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:151-178 (reset block: `_rideId = rideId; _acceptedAt = null; ... lastLat = null; lastLng = null; ... _tripStartLng = null;`, no reset of `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng`)
263-266 `_pickupLat ??= 59.3293; _pickupLng ??= 18.0686; lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; lastLng ??= _pickupLng! - 0.0048;`
305 `unawaited(_hydratePickup());` (only after the emit)
Throwaway test: ride r1 pickup Södertälje (59.1955), cancelRide, ride r2 pickup Arlanda (59.6498) -> `r2 assigned driver at 59.2027,17.6205; server driverLat=59.2027`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reset `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng` in subscribe for a new ride, and hydrate the pickup before spawning or emitting the assigned driver.

verdicts.reason: There is a single MockRideRealtime for the whole app (lib/app/di.dart:196, AppScope.instance.rideRealtime). When subscribe gets a new ride id, its reset block (mock_ride_realtime.dart:151-178) clears lastLat/lastLng, progress and trip start, but not _pickupLat/_pickupLng. _assignNow then runs `_pickupLat ??= ...; lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072` (mock_ride_realtime.dart:263-266) with the previous ride's pickup still set. It persists that position through _persistAssignment (line 275) and emits driverAssigned (line 303) before unawaited(_hydratePickup()) (line 305) loads the new pickup. Nothing re-seeds the pickup between rides. On the second and later rides of a session, the driver therefore appears near the old pickup and drives the whole distance across the map.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of subscribe's reset block and _assignNow ordering in lib/core/realtime/mock_ride_realtime.dart, plus the singleton in di.dart:196. This agrees with the finder's throwaway test (ride r1 from Södertälje, cancel, ride r2 from Arlanda -> driver assigned at 59.2027,17.6205 and the same driverLat stored on the server). I did not rerun it.

verdicts.reason: The new-ride reset block in subscribe (mock_ride_realtime.dart:142-174) clears lastLat/lastLng but not `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng`. `_assignNow` (lines 263-266) then uses `_pickupLat ??=`, which keeps the previous ride's pickup that `_hydratePickup` stored, and spawns the driver next to it. It commits that position to the server through `_persistAssignment` before `_hydratePickup()` fetches the new pickup (line 305). AppScope keeps one MockRideRealtime for the whole session (di.dart:196-201), so every ride after the first is affected. The GPS walk closes 18% of the gap per 3 s tick. From about 50 km it needs ln(1000)/ln(1/0.82) ≈ 35 ticks, about 105 s, to get within 50 m.
verdicts.repro: Same throwaway test. The stand-in server was seeded with r1 (pickup 59.1955,17.6253) and r2 (pickup 59.6498,17.9238). The test subscribed r1, let the assignment fire, called cancelRide, then subscribed r2. Output: `r2 driverAssigned 59.2027,17.6205` and `u28 server r2 driverLat=59.2027 driver=true status=accepted`. That position is r1's pickup plus the 0.0072/-0.0048 offset, about 50 km from r2's pickup.

confirmed.title: A queued (offline) end-early that the server later applies is committed as a plain cancel: no receipt, History shows 'Cancelled · booked price', and the reason is lost
confirmed.description: When an on-board end-early cannot reach the server, it stays in the outbox (`command: endEarly`). Later the flush, or `_dropIfCancelQueued` on restore, sends it. `_dropIfCancelQueued` deliberately keeps the snapshot for end-early so that 'the restored trip resyncs and shows how the server closed it' (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:144-150). Realtime then reports cancelledByRider, and Waiting's `_handleExternalTerminal` calls `completeServerConfirmedCancel()` (waiting_for_driver.dart:570-576). That method calls `_commitCancelled(rideId)` with no `endedEarly` and no `reasonId`. So there is no `LastCompletedRide`, no ended-early summary, History gets `endedEarly: false` and no `chargedFare`, the stored reason is dropped, and the rider is sent straight Home.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider taps 'End trip here' on board with no connection and gets 'We couldn't reach Movera…'. On reconnect the outbox posts /end-early, and the server sets fare to the distance price, e.g. 80 kr. Polling reports cancelledByRider, and the app goes Home with no receipt. History shows 'Cancelled ride · Movera · Booked price 245 kr' with no 'Ended early' and no reason, although 80 kr was charged.
confirmed.evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:159-161 `Future<void> completeServerConfirmedCancel() async { await _commitCancelled(AppScope.instance.ride.rideId); }`
waiting_for_driver.dart:570-575 `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByRider && widget.onTerminal == null) { await _ride.completeServerConfirmedCancel(); ... RideNavigator.home(context);`
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:144-150 `// An end-early that went through ends the trip ... the restored trip resyncs and shows how the server closed it.`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the queued command and reason (or read `cancellation`/`fare`/`endedEarly` from the projection). For an end-early, commit it with an EndedEarlyTrip (charged = projection fare) and open the ended-early summary instead of going Home.

verdicts.reason: A queued end_early that the reconnect flush sends (finding_driver_controller.dart:1427-1438) moves the server to cancelled_by_rider. That is the contract's end-early outcome (CONTRACT.md:79,106), and the mock adds the distance fare and ratingStatus pending (in_process_mock_client.dart:733-743). On the restore path, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:144-150 keeps the snapshot on purpose so that the trip 'shows how the server closed it'. But Waiting only has one handler for cancelledByRider: waiting_for_driver.dart:570-576 calls completeServerConfirmedCancel(), and that runs _commitCancelled(rideId) with no reasonId and no endedEarly (active_ride_controller.dart:159-161). So no LastCompletedRide or receipt is created (lines 309-317), History records endedEarly=false with no chargedFare, the reason is dropped, and the rider goes Home. The app never reads `endedBy` or the projection fare here (no endedBy use in lib outside the mock and ride_completed.dart:285), so it cannot tell this end-early from a plain cancel. The ended-early rating the contract allows is skipped too.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: the outbox flush on reconnect (watchReconnectForPendingCancels) and _dropIfCancelQueued (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:120-162) lead to realtime cancelledByRider, then Waiting._handleExternalTerminal, completeServerConfirmedCancel and _commitCancelled with null endedEarly and null reasonId. A grep for endedBy/ended_by in lib/ found no reader on this path. No test run.

verdicts.reason: A failed on-board end-early stays in the outbox with command endEarly (active_ride_controller.dart:191-207, pendingRetry at 254-258). The reconnect watcher (finding_driver_controller.dart:1428-1444) or the restore flush sends it. The flush calls observeProjection (finding_driver_controller.dart:1488), and the mock's end_early leaves the trip at cancelled_by_rider with fare set to the distance price (in_process_mock_client.dart:715-741, 1437). Waiting's listener sends a terminal non-completed status to _queueStageNavigation (waiting_for_driver.dart:417). Then the cancelledByRider branch calls completeServerConfirmedCancel (waiting_for_driver.dart:570-576). That is `_commitCancelled(rideId)` with no reasonId and no endedEarly (active_ride_controller.dart:159-161), so LastCompletedRide.remember is skipped (295-303), _archive gets endedEarly null (304-310), and recordFor sets endedEarly false and chargedFare null (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:235-236). It then goes Home with no summary. The restore coordinator keeps the snapshot for endEarly on purpose (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:144-150), but nothing downstream reads the ended-early result. The queued reasonId is also dropped. No guard found.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand, no test run. Followed the outbox entry (PendingCancelStore.enqueue with command endEarly) through flushPendingCancels, observeProjection, the Waiting listener, _handleExternalTerminal and completeServerConfirmedCancel into _commitCancelled and recordFor. Checked that nothing that consumes PendingCancelStore.outcomes handles a 'sent' endEarly: ActiveRideController only filters refused/stale (active_ride_controller.dart:66-87).

confirmed.title: The cancel fee charged for a Book-now ride is never stored on the History record, so History shows 'Cancelled · Booked price X' with no fee line
confirmed.description: When the rider cancels on Waiting after the free window, the mock server works out `_riderCancelFee` and stores it as `ride.cancellation.fee` in the cancel response (in_process_mock_client.dart:712, 724-733). `ActiveRideController._requestServerCancel` only reads `fare` from that response (`_chargedFare`, lines 282-285). `_commitCancelled` then archives with `_archive(snapshot, RideStatus.cancelledByRider, ...)`, which has no fee argument. `OnDemandRideHistoryStore.recordFor` (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:184-235) builds the `Reservation` without `cancellationFee`, and so does the server-backed `ApiRideHistoryRepository._record`. History does have a fee display: `ReservationFormat.historyStatus` shows 'Cancelled · fee X', and the detail sheet shows the `cancelFee` line (ride_history.dart:537). Neither ever appears for an on-demand ride. `Reservation.cancellationFee` is only ever set by the reservation repository.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Economy ride at 245 kr. The driver accepted 3 minutes ago. The rider opens Cancel and the sheet says 'Cancelling now costs 35 kr.' They confirm, and the server stores cancellation.fee = 3500 öre. In History > Cancelled the card says just 'Cancelled', and the detail says 'Movera · Booked price 245 kr' with no fee line. The rider cannot see that they were charged 35 kr, and the screen suggests 245 kr.
confirmed.evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:232-236 `return (outcome: RideCancelOutcome.confirmed, command: entry.command, charged: _chargedFare(response));` (only `fare`)
active_ride_controller.dart:308-314 `await _archive(snapshot, RideStatus.cancelledByRider, expectedRideId: id, cancellationReason: reasonId, endedEarly: endedEarly);`
on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:198-234 `return Reservation(... cancellationReason: ..., endedEarly: ..., chargedFare: charged,);` (no cancellationFee)

confirmed.title: A trip that ends in paymentFailed is cleared without a History record or receipt; the rider is told only 'the trip is not active'
confirmed.description: paymentFailed is a post-completion state: the trip was driven and completed, and the payment failed (trip_status.dart:183). Waiting treats it as an external terminal (waiting_for_driver.dart:417, 589-595). markExternalTerminal archives only the cancel/no-show/failed statuses, then always runs _store.clear(). So a completed trip whose payment failed is not archived to the device History and gets no completion or receipt screen. The rider sees the generic 'Payment could not be completed ... The trip is not active' sheet and lands on Home. The trip they took is no longer visible anywhere on the device.
confirmed.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a throwaway widget test: an in-trip Waiting with a stored snapshot, then MockRideRealtime.emit(RideStatus.paymentFailed). Afterwards OnDemandRideHistoryStore.read() had length 0 and RideSnapshotStore.read() was null. The rider is driven to the destination and the payment fails, then the ride vanishes: no History entry, no receipt, no way to retry payment.
confirmed.evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:353-361 `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByDriver || ... || status == RideStatus.tripFailed) { await _archive(snapshot, status, expectedRideId: id); } await _store.clear();` (paymentFailed is not in the list)
waiting_for_driver.dart:589-595 `await _ride.markExternalTerminal(status); ... RideNavigator.home(context, status: status);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Archive paymentFailed (it is a completed trip) before clearing, and/or route it to the completion surface that can show the payment problem.

verdicts.reason: markExternalTerminal (active_ride_controller.dart:353-361) archives only the cancel/noShow/failed statuses and then always clears the snapshot. paymentFailed is terminal and not a completed surface (ride_status.dart:59-90), so Waiting sends it there (waiting_for_driver.dart:417, 589-595). The history store treats paymentFailed as a completed trip to keep (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:237, 261-266, the rider-37 comment), so dropping it contradicts that intent. It is reached when Waiting sees paymentFailed before any completed-surface status, for example a resync or restore after the app was offline or killed at drop-off; the projection maps completed plus payment failed straight to paymentFailed (trip_status.dart:183). RideCompleted ignores paymentFailed (ride_completed.dart:122-127), so the normal path does not handle it either. The impact is limited: in server-backed mode History comes from /rider/trips (di.dart:154), so only device-local History loses the record. The missing receipt affects both modes.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the Waiting realtime listener through _queueStageNavigation, _handleExternalTerminal and markExternalTerminal, where the archive list omits paymentFailed and _store.clear() follows; also checked _reservationStatus in on_demand_ride_history_store.dart. The finding's widget test emits synthetically; I did not rerun it.

verdicts.reason: paymentFailed is terminal and not isCompletedSurface (ride_status.dart:59-89), so Waiting routes it to markExternalTerminal (waiting_for_driver.dart:417, 589-595). markExternalTerminal archives only cancelledByDriver, cancelledBySystem, cancelledByAdmin, endedByDriver, noShow and tripFailed, then clears the snapshot (active_ride_controller.dart:353-362). The intent written in on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:258-265 (rider-37: 'one whose payment failed is still a completed trip; History keeps both') and recordFor's paymentFailed flag (line 237) are therefore never used on this path. Waiting gets paymentFailed directly when a projection arrives as completed with payment failed (trip_status.dart:169, 183). Release-like builds read History from the server (di.dart:150-154), so there the loss is the receipt only. In local/demo builds the device History entry is lost as well.
verdicts.repro: Ran throwaway test test/_audit_u34b5_test.dart (deleted afterwards). It saves an in-trip snapshot, restores the session at tripInProgress, then calls ActiveRideController().markExternalTerminal(RideStatus.paymentFailed). Output: 'AUDIT history=0 snapshot=null'. The control case with cancelledBySystem printed 'AUDIT control history=1'. Result: '+2: All tests passed!'

confirmed.title: A destination or pickup moved on the map is discarded when its label matches the current address; the rider is told the route was updated
confirmed.description: `preview` picks the coordinates by comparing the address string: if the new destination text equals `ride.destinationAddress`, it uses the old point and ignores the `destinationPoint` the picker passed. The pickup is handled the same way at :153. ConfirmPickupSpot often returns the same label after a pin move: it keeps `initialAddress` until the reverse geocode settles, a nearby pin resolves to the same street address, and an unresolvable point gives the 'Pickup location' fallback. In those cases the moved point is thrown away, the server prices and applies the old route ('Same price'), and Waiting shows 'Route updated · driver told'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Destination 'Mall of Scandinavia'. The rider opens 'Pick on map', drags the pin 400 m to the other entrance and confirms before the label changes (or it resolves to the same name). The sheet shows 'Same price', the rider confirms and gets 'Route updated, driver told', but the destination coordinates did not change.
confirmed.evidence:
route_change_controller.dart:172-174
    final destinationAt = destination == ride.destinationAddress
        ? GeoPoint(ride.destinationLat, ride.destinationLng)
        : destinationPoint ?? await _locate(destination);
:153-155 same for pickupAt
confirm_pickup_spot.dart:134 _address = widget.initialAddress; :300 confirmedPickupAddress(_address, position)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use the explicit point whenever one was given (`destinationPoint ?? (same label ? old point : locate)`), and the same for pickup.

verdicts.reason: route_change_controller.dart:153-155 and :172-174 choose the coordinates by comparing labels: if the label matches, they use the old ride point, and the explicit pickupPoint/destinationPoint is never read. The map pick does give a point (route_change_flow.dart:70-86 returns RoutePickerMapPick with the pin position, and route_picker_page.dart:384/401 forwards it as destinationPoint). But ConfirmPickupSpot starts _address at initialAddress, which is ride.destinationAddress when the field holds the current destination (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:134, route_change_flow.dart:76-78). _address only changes in _idle after the reverse geocode finishes (:222-234). The confirm button is enabled as soon as the initial coordinates are valid (:135-140, :527). So confirming quickly after a drag, or a nearby pin that resolves to the same label, returns the old label with a new point. preview then drops the point, the quote and apply are built on the old coordinates (:206-212, :272-278), and Waiting's _applyRouteChange adopts the unchanged point as if the route was updated.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: RoutePickerPage._choose/_finish -> onFinish -> RouteChangeController.preview label comparison -> apply -> waiting_for_driver.dart:1089/_applyRouteChange. No guard prefers the explicit point.

verdicts.reason: route_change_controller.dart:172-174 picks the old destination point whenever the label equals ride.destinationAddress, even when the picker passed an explicit destinationPoint. Pickup does the same at :153-155. In the real flow, route_change_flow.dart:70-87 opens ConfirmPickupSpot at the old destination with initialAddress = ride.destinationAddress. confirm_pickup_spot.dart:134 sets _address to that label. Moving the pin only updates _center (:338-341). The label changes only when _idle()'s async reverse geocode finishes (:222-233). The confirm button is gated only on _hasUsablePickupCoordinates (:527-529), not on the reverse lookup settling. So a confirm tapped right after a drag returns the moved position with the old label (:296-303). route_picker_page.dart:383-384 stores the label through _show, and _expand (:164-167) maps it back to the full original string. The equality test in preview therefore holds, and the moved point is thrown away. The same happens when the reverse lookup resolves to the same string as the original address. Nothing in DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md or QA_HOOKS.md covers this.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand from the real caller (route_change_flow onPickOnMap -> RoutePickerPage._pickOnMap/_choose -> _finish -> changes.preview), with the exact strings: initialAddress == ride.destinationAddress, confirm before onCameraIdle/_idle completes, _expand(_show(label)) == ride.destinationAddress, then preview line 172 takes the old GeoPoint. No test run: the map camera callbacks need a GoogleMap platform view.

verdicts.corrected_title: A stop chosen on the map or from a suggestion loses its coordinates and is re-geocoded from its label (in demo: a hash point about 0.5-0.7 km from Stockholm Central, or 'Current location')
verdicts.reason: The stop branch of _choose (route_picker_page.dart:376-380) keeps only the text and drops `point`. RoutePickerSelection has no per-stop points (lines 397-406). openRouteChange passes `stops:` without `stopPoints` (route_change_flow.dart:97). preview therefore falls through to `_locate(address)` for any stop that is not already on the ride (route_change_controller.dart:179-183). The 'Try the map' button (route_picker_page.dart:992) and suggestion taps that carry a point (line 947) both reach this branch while a stop is active. The finding overstates the demo error: in_process_mock_client.dart:362-367 offsets by at most 0.006 deg latitude and 0.008 deg longitude, which is about 0.67 km and 0.45 km, not 6-8 km. Also, in-process reverse geocoding labels every map pick 'Current location' (line 332), so the stop is forward-geocoded from that string. The point that is priced, saved (apply, line 296) and sent to the driver is still wrong.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _pickOnMap -> _choose(stop branch) -> _finish -> onFinish -> RouteChangeController.preview stop loop -> _locate, plus the mock geocode handler at in_process_mock_client.dart:337-380.

verdicts.corrected_title: A stop picked on the map loses its pinned point and is re-geocoded from its label (in demo: a hashed point within about 0.7 km of Stockholm Central, wherever the pin was)
verdicts.reason: route_picker_page.dart:376-380: in the 'stop' branch, _choose sets only the text and drops `point`. RoutePickerSelection (route_picker_page.dart:22-35) has no field for stop points, and route_change_flow.dart:91-97 calls preview without stopPoints. route_change_controller.dart:176-183 therefore falls back to _locate(address) for any new stop. The mock geocoder (in_process_mock_client.dart:363-370) returns 59.3293 + ((hash%1201)-600)/1e5 and 18.0686 + (((hash~/1201)%1601)-800)/1e5. That is at most ±0.006° latitude (about 0.67 km) and ±0.008° longitude (about 0.45 km), not ±6/±8 km as the finding says. Because the result is anchored to Stockholm Central, a pin dropped anywhere else (another city, or a precise door) is replaced. The wrong point is priced, saved in apply and sent to the driver. With a real geocoder the precise pin is still lost and replaced by a forward lookup of the label.
verdicts.repro: Traced _pickOnMap -> _choose(address, point) -> the stop branch drops point -> _finish builds the stops list from text only -> preview stopPoints is empty -> _locate. Worked the mock hash bounds by hand: lat range ±600/100000 = ±0.006°, lng range ±800/100000 = ±0.008°.

confirmed.title: Scheduled ride's live screen takes the waiting-fee terms and cancel-fee preview from the on-demand RideSession's last booked category
confirmed.description: WaitingForDriver is reused for scheduled rides. Its widget comment says it runs 'without touching the on-demand ride session'. Two places still take the category from `AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId`, falling back to the on-demand `RideSnapshotStore` snapshot without checking its ride id: `_loadWaitingTerms` (waiting-fee counter) and `_cancelFeeNote` (the 'Cancelling now costs …' line). For a reservation, `widget.rideId` is the reservation id. The session's booked category belongs to whatever Book-now ride ran last in this process. It is never cleared: `RideSession.reset()` leaves `bookedCategoryId`/`bookedPaymentMethodId`/`bookedMaxOfferMinor` untouched, so it can even be the previous rider's after a sign-out. The reservation's own `categoryId` is never consulted. With no Book-now ride in this process, the note and counter silently disappear.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Earlier in the session the rider booked an Economy ride (bookedCategoryId = 'economy'). Later their XL reservation goes live and the driver has accepted. Tapping Cancel shows 'Cancelling now costs 35 kr', the economy live fee (fixed 3500 öre after 2 free min). The XL live rule is 15% with a 50 kr minimum, and the reservation cancel that actually runs (`reservations.cancel`) applies reservation rules. When the driver waits at pickup, the fee counter uses economy's 5 free minutes instead of XL's 3. Not run; worked from the seed config in rider_app_config.dart:612-690.
confirmed.evidence:
lib/features/active_ride/presentation/waiting_for_driver.dart:294-296 `final stored = await RouteChangeController.storedRide(); final category = AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId ?? stored?.categoryId;`
lib/features/active_ride/presentation/waiting_for_driver.dart:772-788 same lookup feeding `LiveCancelFeePreview.of(config, categoryId: category, ...)`
lib/features/reservations/presentation/reservation_live_ride.dart:64-77 `WaitingForDriver(... rideId: ride.reservationId, realtime: realtime, persistRideSnapshot: false, ...)` (category not passed)
lib/features/ride_booking/application/ride_session.dart:205-217 `reset()` does not clear bookedCategoryId/bookedPaymentMethodId/bookedMaxOfferMinor
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass the trip's categoryId into WaitingForDriver (the reservation's categoryId; for Book-now, the snapshot's) and use it instead of the session. Accept the stored snapshot only when its rideId equals `_rideId`. Clear the booked* fields in RideSession.reset().

verdicts.reason: waiting_for_driver.dart:295-296 and 779-780 take the category from AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId, or else the on-demand snapshot. ReservationLiveRide.pageFor (reservation_live_ride.dart:64-77) passes rideId: reservationId and persistRideSnapshot: false, but never passes the reservation's categoryId (Reservation has a categoryId field, reservation.dart:152). bookedCategoryId is cleared only when the session reconciles a different ride id (ride_session.dart:117-122). It is set at booking_coordinator.dart:498/701, and reset() at ride_session.dart:205-217, which runs on sign-out via user_data_wipe.dart:120, does not clear it. So a reservation that goes live after a Book-now ride uses the last booked category. The seed config shows a real difference: economy waiting is 5 free min and the live cancel fee is a fixed 3500; xl waiting is 3 free min and the fee is 15% with a 50 kr minimum (rider_app_config.dart:612-690). With no earlier Book-now ride, category is null and both the counter and the note silently disappear. This is a preview only: the server charges its own fee.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Followed the WaitingForDriver construction in reservation_live_ride.dart, every write to bookedCategoryId (grep), RideSession.reset and backendReconcile's isNewRide branch, and the seed category config. No test run.

verdicts.reason: waiting_for_driver.dart:294-296 and :778-780 take the category from AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId, falling back to the stored on-demand snapshot. ReservationLiveRide.pageFor (reservation_live_ride.dart:64-77) never passes the reservation's categoryId (Reservation.categoryId exists, reservation.dart:152). bookedCategoryId is set only by booking (booking_coordinator.dart:498/701) and restore (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:396). It is cleared only when a different ride id is reconciled (ride_session.dart:120), never in reset() (ride_session.dart:205-217). So after a finished Economy Book-now ride it stays 'economy' while an XL reservation is live. The seed config then gives economy waiting terms (5 free min, rider_app_config.dart:619) instead of xl (3 free min, :637). The cancel note also uses LiveCancelFeePreview with live economy rules (fixed 3500), while the cancel that actually runs goes through reservations.cancel. With no Book-now ride in this process and no stored snapshot, category is null and both the counter and the note silently disappear. Nothing guards on rideId == widget.rideId.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand from ReservationLiveRide.pageFor through _loadWaitingTerms and _cancelFeeNote, and grepped every writer and clearer of bookedCategoryId. Not run.

confirmed.title: After a reload, the server's waiting.arrivedAt and acceptedAt are thrown away, so the waiting fee clock restarts on every rebuild and the cancel-fee preview counts from reload time
confirmed.description: DriverTrackingController applies event.acceptedAt and event.waitingArrivedAt only inside `if (accepted)` (driver_tracking_controller.dart:127-145). A restore seeds the session with the snapshot's version (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:312-326), and tracking saves the latest version into the snapshot. The first projection after a reload therefore usually has the same version and status, and backendReconcile rejects it as a duplicate (ride_session.dart:168-173). So waitingSince and acceptedAt stay null although the projection carries them. Waiting then passes `since: _tracking.waitingSince ?? DateTime.now()` to WaitingFeeCounter. That value is recomputed on every Waiting rebuild (sheet settle, measurement, signature change), so the free-wait countdown restarts each time and never reaches the fee. The cancel-fee preview falls back to _shownAt (759), which is the reload time, although the server sent acceptedAt. The comment at 752-754 accepts that fallback only when 'the projection has no acceptedAt'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a throwaway widget test: snapshot version 5 at driverWaiting with category economy, session reconciled at version 5, then mock emit(driverWaiting, sequence: 5), which carries waitingArrivedAt. WaitingFeeCounter.since was 01:39:30.719. After one Waiting rebuild it was 01:39:32.013, so it moved by 1.29 s and equals 'now' on each build. A rider who reloads while the driver waits sees 'free waiting 5:00 left' reset each time the sheet moves while the server is already charging. The cancel sheet may also say 'free for N more minutes' when a fee applies.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:321-322 `return WaitingFeeCounter( since: _tracking.waitingSince ?? DateTime.now(),`
waiting_for_driver.dart:759 `DateTime get _acceptedAt => _tracking.acceptedAt ?? _shownAt;`
driver_tracking_controller.dart:127-145 `if (accepted) { ... acceptedAt = event.acceptedAt ?? acceptedAt; if (event.waitingArrivedAt != null) { waitingSince = event.waitingArrivedAt; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Apply acceptedAt and waitingArrivedAt (timestamps from the server) even when the status part of a same-version event is not accepted. At minimum, compute the WaitingFeeCounter fallback once and keep it, rather than DateTime.now() on each build.

verdicts.reason: driver_tracking_controller.dart:120-146 applies acceptedAt/waitingArrivedAt only when backendReconcile accepts the event. The restore seeds the session at the snapshot's version (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:322-327). _isFreshBackendProjection rejects a same-version, same-status event (ride_session.dart:168-173). ApiRideRealtime polls the projection and uses the aggregate ride.version as the event version (api_ride_realtime.dart:130-233). That version does not change while the driver waits, so after a reload every poll during the wait is rejected and waitingSince/acceptedAt stay null. waiting_for_driver.dart:322 then passes DateTime.now() on every parent rebuild, and the cancel preview uses _shownAt (765). The mock hides this because its resume emits resumeVersion+1 (mock_ride_realtime.dart:180,321), but the API transport does not.
verdicts.repro: Traced the restore seed, backendReconcile/_isFreshBackendProjection, the tracking listener, and ApiRideRealtime's version handling. The reporter's throwaway widget test (forced emit at the same sequence 5) showed WaitingFeeCounter.since moving 1.29 s between rebuilds. That matches the code path. I did not rerun it.

verdicts.reason: A restore seeds the session with snapshot.version (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:321-326). When the next projection has the same version and status, backendReconcile rejects it (ride_session.dart:168-173: same version and same status returns false). DriverTrackingController applies acceptedAt and waitingArrivedAt only inside `if (accepted)` (driver_tracking_controller.dart:127-145), so waitingSince and acceptedAt stay null. The status is still driverWaiting from initialStatus. _waitingFeeCounter then passes `since: _tracking.waitingSince ?? DateTime.now()` (waiting_for_driver.dart:321-322), which is re-evaluated on every parent build. WaitingFeeState.at computes from widget.since on each build (waiting_fee_counter.dart:112-117), so each Waiting rebuild resets the free-wait countdown. _acceptedAt falls back to _shownAt, the reload time (:759). The comment at :752-754 accepts that fallback only when the projection lacks acceptedAt, but here the projection carried it and it was dropped. The wrong values last until a higher-version event arrives.
verdicts.repro: Traced the version-equality path through backendReconcile, the tracking listener and the WaitingFeeCounter build. Not run myself. The reporter's widget test moved since by 1.29 s across one rebuild, which matches the trace.

confirmed.title: Reload during re-dispatch after a driver drop restores Waiting with the dropped driver; Waiting never reacts to a searching status
confirmed.description: `DriverTrackingController._persistLiveStatus` skips terminal statuses (211-212), and `ActiveRideController.resumeSearchingAfterDriverCancel` explicitly does not persist (327-334), so after a driver drop the stored snapshot still says `driverArriving`/`driverAssigned` with the old driver until the next accept. A reload in that window (`RideRestoreCoordinator.surfaceFor`, 285-291) restores `WaitingForDriver` with `driver: snapshot.driver`. With `ApiRideRealtime` the first poll carries `searching`; `reassigned` is only derived when `poll.lastStatus?.isMatched` (api_ride_realtime.dart 193-199), which is null on a fresh poll, so the event is a plain `findingDriver`. `_onLiveTick` has branches only for `cancelledByDriver`, terminal and completed statuses (410-423); a searching status falls through to the normal sheet rendering, so the screen keeps the 'Driver found' headline (`_headlineFor` → `eta?.headline(status: findingDriver)`), the dropped driver's card, plate and message/call buttons, and no reassignment notice. The rider only learns a new driver was assigned when the next accept arrives; a second reload would restore Finding because `_persistLiveStatus` then saves `findingDriver`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Release build: driver accepts, then drops the ride; the rider reloads the web app (or the process is restarted) before the next driver accepts. Waiting shows the old driver as 'on the way' while the server is searching; messages go to a driver who is no longer on the trip.
confirmed.evidence: driver_tracking_controller.dart:211-212 `if (!persistRideSnapshot || status.isTerminal) return;` ; active_ride_controller.dart:329-333 comment 'Snapshot persistence is deliberately not on this critical path ... remains the correct recovery record' ; api_ride_realtime.dart:193-194 `final reassigned = status.isSearching && (poll.lastStatus?.isMatched ?? false);` ; waiting_for_driver.dart:417-433 only `isTerminal`/completed branches before rendering
confirmed.suggested_fix: Persist the `findingDriver` status (without driver) when the research starts, and have Waiting treat an incoming `isSearching` status the same way as `cancelledByDriver` (back to Finding).

verdicts.reason: After a driver drop nothing saves a non-matched snapshot. _persistLiveStatus skips terminal statuses (driver_tracking_controller.dart:211-212). resumeSearchingAfterDriverCancel deliberately does not persist (active_ride_controller.dart:327-334). FindingDriverController only saves again at searchDelayed (finding_driver_controller.dart:586-593) or on assignment (983-993). So a reload in that window restores Waiting (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:285-291). The resync in resumeIfNeeded (577-580) is a no-op on a cold start: ApiRideRealtime.reconnectAndResync returns when there is no poll (api_ride_realtime.dart:379-381). On a fresh poll lastStatus is null, so `reassigned` stays false (193-199) and the event arrives as a plain findingDriver. The tracker accepts it (driver_tracking_controller.dart:118-131), but _onLiveTick has no searching branch (waiting_for_driver.dart:410-433) and the file never checks isSearching. Waiting therefore keeps the dropped driver's card ('Driver found' when eta is null) with no notice until the next accept. The window lasts until the next accept or the delayed-search threshold, not forever.

FindingDriverController.start/startFrom saves nothing when the search starts (finding_driver_controller.dart:237-400); it saves only on the delayed phase, about 590. So the stored snapshot keeps driverArriving and the old driver. confirmed.title: A terminal or completion status that arrives while a cancel/end-early is in flight is dropped. After a rejected or pendingRetry outcome, Waiting stays on an ended trip until the next live tick, and for a truly terminal status (noShow, cancelledByAdmin) that tick may never come
confirmed.description: _confirmCancel sets _leaving=true (820) while it awaits _ride.markCancelled, which can take two network attempts. During that time _onLiveTick sends terminal statuses to _queueStageNavigation, and that returns before it stores _pendingStageStatus (515). _maybeOpenCompleted also returns early (542). If the server then answers rejected (409: 'the ride already ended — realtime reports the real outcome', active_ride_controller.dart:256-259) or the call ends as pendingRetry, _confirmCancel resets _leaving=false (848-851). Nothing replays the swallowed status. A terminal status gets no further events, so nothing ever navigates. Only the 'stale' outcome triggers a resync (923-936); 'rejected' does not.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On board, the rider taps End trip just as the driver completes the trip. tripCompleted arrives on realtime while the POST is in flight and is ignored. The server answers 409 invalid_transition, so the outcome is rejected. The rider sees 'This ride can no longer be cancelled' and stays on the Waiting screen with the trip ended and no completion screen. The same happens with noShow or cancelledByAdmin during an in-flight cancel.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:515 `if (!mounted || _leaving || _completedOpened) return;
    _pendingStageStatus = status;`
waiting_for_driver.dart:542 `if (!mounted || _leaving || _completedOpened) return;`
waiting_for_driver.dart:847-852 `if (result != RideCancelOutcome.confirmed) { setState(() { _cancelling = false; _leaving = false; }); _showCancelProblem(result); return; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the status in _pendingStageStatus even while _leaving, and drain it (or re-check _tracking.status) after a non-confirmed cancel outcome. Alternatively, resync on rejected as is done for stale.

confirmed.title: A queued on-board End trip that the outbox later delivers is committed as a plain cancel, with no ended-early receipt or rating
confirmed.description: If the rider taps End trip on board while the server cannot be reached, markCancelled returns pendingRetry and queues an end_early command in the outbox (active_ride_controller.dart:207-211). The outbox flush later sends it. The server applies end_early, which moves the trip to cancelled_by_rider (trip_transitions.dart:103-104) and charges the distance fare. Realtime then reports cancelledByRider to Waiting. _handleExternalTerminal takes the cancelledByRider branch and calls completeServerConfirmedCancel(), which calls _commitCancelled with no endedEarly. As a result: LastCompletedRide.remember is skipped, the History record has endedEarly:false and no charged amount, and RideNavigator.home is called. UI-01 says an on-board end 'is a finished trip with a receipt, not a silent return to Home' (waiting_for_driver.dart:860-862), and R-O6 says the rider rates an ended-early trip on the trip-end screen. Neither happens here. Nothing in Waiting listens for the outbox's `sent` outcome; it only listens for refused/stale.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider is in the car with a flaky connection and taps End trip. They see 'couldn't reach Movera ... we'll retry'. The connection returns, the queued end-early is accepted and the rider is charged for the distance. The app then jumps straight to Home: no ended-early summary, no fare, no rating, and History shows a plain 'Cancelled' ride with no charge.

waiting_for_driver.dart:570-576 `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByRider && widget.onTerminal == null) { await _ride.completeServerConfirmedCancel(); ... RideNavigator.home(context); return; }`
active_ride_controller.dart:159-161 `Future<void> completeServerConfirmedCancel() async { await _commitCancelled(AppScope.instance.ride.rideId); }`

The only consumers of outcomes are the refused/stale streams (active_ride_controller.dart:67-87) and FindingDriverController._onOutboxOutcome, which is not the owner here. confirmed.title: A 'closed' projection reaching Waiting throws ArgumentError in markExternalTerminal and leaves Waiting dead

confirmed.title: On the reservation live screen, the cancel-fee note and waiting terms use the Book Now session's leftover category and live fee rule, not the reservation's
confirmed.description: For a reservation, `ReservationLiveRide.pageFor` mounts WaitingForDriver. `_cancelFeeNote` and `_loadWaitingTerms` take the category from `AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId ?? RouteChangeController.storedRide()?.categoryId`. Those belong to the global Book Now session and snapshot, not to the reservation (whose `categoryId` is not passed in). The note then applies the LIVE fee rule (`LiveCancelFeePreview`, minutes since accept), not the reservation's late-cancel terms. With no Book Now ride the category is null, so the sheet shows no fee at all. With a stale Book Now session it shows another category's live fee. This differs from the known finding that the live-screen cancel records no fee: here the fee line the rider confirms against is wrong.

If an older Economy Book Now session is still in memory, it shows 'Free to cancel for 2 more minutes' from the live economy rule.

waiting_for_driver.dart:772-776 `final stored = await RouteChangeController.storedRide(); final category = AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId ?? stored?.categoryId; if (category == null) return null;`
:782-787 `final preview = LiveCancelFeePreview.of(config, categoryId: category, ..., acceptedAt: _acceptedAt, ...`

confirmed.title: Back gesture while the Waiting cancel/end-early request is in flight pops Waiting; Finding underneath stays parked and the cancel result is lost
confirmed.description: `_confirmCancel` sets `_leaving = true; setState(() {});` (820-821) before `await _ride.markCancelled(...)` (838). `PopScope(canPop: _leaving, ...)` (1441) therefore lets a system back pop Waiting while the server request is still out (up to two attempts with 15 s timeouts each). The `_cancelling` overlay only blocks pointer input, not back. After the pop, `if (!mounted) return;` (846) discards the outcome: if the server confirmed, `_commitCancelled` already cleared the snapshot and set the session to `cancelledByRider` but `RideNavigator.home` is never called; if it was `pendingRetry`/`rejected`, the ride stays live with no screen. Waiting was pushed by `FindingDrivers._openWaiting` with `await Navigator.push<bool>` (finding_drivers.dart 535-556); the pop returns null, so `researchDriver != true` and Finding remains with `_leaving = true`, `_mapParked = true` and a disposed `_match` (528-531): a blank parked screen whose close button is inert (`_confirmCancel` returns on `_leaving`, 568).
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Waiting the rider confirms 'Cancel ride', the network is slow, and they press the Android back button during the 'Cancelling…' card. Waiting disappears and the rider sees a dead grey Finding screen; depending on the server answer the ride is either cancelled with no Home navigation or still live with no way to see or cancel it from this screen.
confirmed.evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:819-821 `if (!outcome.cancelled) return; _leaving = true; setState(() {});` ; 837-846 `setState(() => _cancelling = true); final result = await _ride.markCancelled(...); if (!mounted) return;` ; 1441-1443 `PopScope(canPop: _leaving, onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, _) async { if (didPop) return;` ; finding_drivers.dart:556 `if (!mounted || researchDriver != true) return;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep `canPop` false while `_cancelling` is true (set `_leaving` only after the outcome is known), or handle `didPop` by finishing the flow from the result.

verdicts.reason: _confirmCancel sets `_leaving = true; setState` (waiting_for_driver.dart:820-821) before `await _ride.markCancelled(...)` (838). confirmed.title: Cancel confirmed on a sheet opened before boarding sends a charged end_early if the trip starts while the sheet is open
confirmed.description: `_confirmCancel` fixes the phase (`CancelPhase.matched`) and the fee note ('free…') when the sheet opens (lines 804-812). Then it awaits two sheets, the confirm sheet and the reason sheet. Nothing closes or re-checks them when the stage changes: `_onLiveTick` only closes the arrived sheet on trip start (lines 396-403). After the rider confirms, `markCancelled` chooses the command from the session status at send time (`onboard = tripRiderOnboardStatuses.contains(...)`, active_ride_controller.dart:207-211). It therefore posts `/end-early`, and the server charges base fare plus distance (`_endEarlyFare`). The app then opens the 'ended early' receipt. Finding has a guard for this exact race (RIDE-15, `driverMatched` closes the sheet); Waiting has none for boarding.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo: the driver reaches pickup, and the mock boards the rider 8 s later (`boardAfter`). The rider taps Cancel while the driver waits and sees 'Cancel ride? … Cancelling is free for less than a minute more.' They pick a reason. Meanwhile tripStarted arrives. On confirm, POST /rides/{id}/end-early runs and the rider lands on an 'Ended early' summary charged the base fare (e.g. 45 kr) for a cancel the app called free.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:804-812 `final feeNote = await _cancelFeeNote(); ... phase: _isInTrip ? CancelPhase.inTrip : CancelPhase.matched, feeNote: feeNote,`
waiting_for_driver.dart:838 `final result = await _ride.markCancelled(`

confirmed.title: Ride check 'long stop' fires when the rider's own connection drops mid-trip, because connectionDegraded is never set on the polling transport (default threshold 2 min, not 4)
confirmed.description: The 15-second stillness timer is meant to run only 'while the trip is under way and the live feed is up', and it uses `_tracking.connectionDegraded` as that check. `DriverTrackingController` sets that flag only from the stream's `onError`/`onDone`. `ApiRideRealtime._poll` never adds an error to the stream: a failed poll only calls `connection.markFailed()` and backs off. So when the rider's phone loses network during the trip, no new fixes arrive, `connectionDegraded` stays false, and `RideCheckMonitor.checkStill(now)` measures the time since the last fix as a stop. After admin's `longStop` minutes (4 by default) it opens the 'long stop' Ride check card, though the car may be driving normally.

About 4 minutes after the last fix the Ride check card opens asking whether everything is OK because the car 'stopped for 4 minutes'. The rider is alarmed by a false alert, and an answer may be posted to admin's Ride check log. Traced by reading the code.

verdicts.reason: The still timer's only feed-health check is `_tracking.connectionDegraded` (waiting_for_driver.dart:1119). That flag is written only in the stream's onError/onDone (driver_tracking_controller.dart:186-193) and reset at line 107. ApiRideRealtime._poll never adds an error to the stream and never closes it on failure: the catch only calls connection.markFailed() and sets a backoff (api_ride_realtime.dart:256-272). confirmed.title: On web, the moving driver car makes a new blob URL that is never revoked, plus an image load, about 20 times a second for the whole live ride
confirmed.description: The car's ease now runs for almost the whole gap between fixes, because driverEaseDuration copies that gap (0.4 to 4 s). Its listener rebuilds the marker set every 50 ms (lines 1999-2013). Each set has a driver Marker at a new position (lines 2298-2308). Its icon is a BytesMapBitmap with no width or height: `BitmapDescriptor.bytes(data.buffer.asUint8List())` at lib/shared/widgets/movera_map_markers.dart:173. GoogleMap sees the driver marker as changed on every update. google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2 then runs, per update: `_changeMarker` -> `_markerOptionsFromMarker` -> `_gmIconFromBitmapDescriptor` -> `urlFromMapBitmap`, which calls `URL.createObjectURL(Blob(bytes))` (convert.dart:754-760). The URL cache is cleared after every batch (`_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches()`, google_maps_controller.dart:577), so every update gets a fresh Blob copy of the PNG. The plugin never calls revokeObjectURL for marker icons, so each Blob lives until the page unloads. With no width or height given, `_getBitmapSize` -> `_fetchBitmapSize` also creates an HTMLImageElement and waits for it to load on every update (convert.dart:404). Then `marker.options = ...` gives Google Maps a new icon URL to fetch and decode. The U7 change only kept the map leaf from rebuilding. It did not stop the per-update icon churn on the web, which is the main shipped platform. The comment in home_controller.dart:172-178 shows the team knew each repaint costs "a new blob URL and image decode on the web". It does not account for those URLs never being freed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rider on iPhone Safari (public web demo or a real web build) follows a 30-minute trip: driver to pickup, then in trip. The mock or live feed sends a fix every 2-3 s, so the ease never stops. Worked by hand: about 20 marker updates/s x 1800 s = about 36,000 Blob URLs of the 31x31 car PNG (about 1-2 KB each), so about 36-72 MB kept in the blob store. Also about 36,000 image elements loaded, and an icon swap on every frame. Memory grows without bound and the map stutters. On a longer trip, iOS Safari kills the tab mid-ride and the page reloads. Not run (read-only audit); traced through the plugin source in ~/.pub-cache.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:1999-2012 `)..addListener(() { ... if (_driverAnim.isAnimating && last != null && now.difference(last) < const Duration(milliseconds: 50)) { return; } _lastAnimRebuild = now; _markers = _buildMarkers(); });`
waiting_for_driver.dart:2298-2307 `Marker(markerId: const MarkerId('driver'), position: driverPosition, rotation: _currentDriverHeading(), ... icon: _driverCar ?? ...)`
movera_map_markers.dart:173 `return BitmapDescriptor.bytes(data.buffer.asUint8List());`
google_maps_flutter_web convert.dart:754-760 `_bitmapBlobUrlCache.putIfAbsent(bytesMapBitmap.byteData.hashCode, () { final Blob blob = Blob(...); return URL.createObjectURL(blob as JSObject); })`
google_maps_controller.dart:577 `_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches();`

One option is an AssetMapBitmap (BitmapDescriptor.asset with explicit width/height), which resolves to a stable asset URL with no Blob and no size probe. Another is to cap web driver-marker updates to once per fix (no 20 fps interpolation). At minimum, pass width/height to BitmapDescriptor.bytes to skip the per-update image probe.

verdicts.reason: The ease listener rebuilds the marker set up to every 50 ms while the ease runs (waiting_for_driver.dart:2005-2019). The ease lasts 0.4-4 s, following the fix interval (lines 73-81). The ValueListenableBuilder feeds the new set to GoogleMap (line 2439), and the driver Marker's position changes on each rebuild, so it lands in markersToChange. Its icon is BitmapDescriptor.bytes with no width or height (movera_map_markers.dart:173). In google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2, each _changeMarker rebuilds the options (markers.dart:114-121). urlFromMapBitmap then creates a new Blob URL (convert.dart:754-760), because updateMarkers clears _bitmapBlobUrlCache after every batch (google_maps_controller.dart:577, convert.dart:422-425). confirmed.title: In-trip road route and Ride check's planned route go driver to destination only and ignore stops (booked or added), so driving to a stop more than 2 km off the direct line fires a false 'off route' alert
confirmed.description: During the trip `_routeEndpoints` returns only driver → destination, and `_refreshRoadRoute` asks `roadRoutePolyline(from,to)` for those two points, so the drawn route never passes the rider's stops (the stop markers sit off the line). The same polyline goes to `RideCheckController.setPlannedRoute` through `onTripRoute`. `RideCheckMonitor._offRoute` measures distance only against `_route`; stops are not excluded. After the rider adds a stop more than `offRouteKm` (2 km) from the direct road, a driver correctly heading to the stop triggers an offRoute Ride check card. `replan` on route change resets `_route`, but the next route it gets is again stopless.

confirmed.title: Sign-out wipe deletes the recording index but leaves the previous rider's Safety audio files on disk
confirmed.description: UserDataWipe.run says it removes everything a rider left on this device. It removes `movera_safety_cache_v1`, which is the list of recordings, and resets the Safety mock. confirmed.title: OTP expiry is checked against the device clock, so a phone whose clock runs a few minutes fast can never sign in
confirmed.description: OtpChallenge.isExpired compares the server's absolute `expiresAt` (mock: now + 5 min) with `DateTime.now().toUtc()` on the device. PhoneVerification._verify returns 'code expired' locally when it is true, before any request, and AuthRepository.verifyOtp throws StateError in the same case. If the device clock is ahead by more than the OTP lifetime, every challenge, including each one from Resend, is already expired on arrival and the code is never sent. The server is the authority and would answer 410 itself. The client check can only block valid codes.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A laptop or phone with its clock set 6 minutes ahead opens Sign in. The rider types the correct code and gets 'This code has expired'. Resend gives the same result every time, so the rider cannot sign in.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Work out the expiry from the local receipt time plus the server's remaining lifetime (expiresAt minus the server's issue time, or a TTL field), or let the server's 410 decide.

verdicts.reason: otp_challenge.dart:21 compares the server's absolute expiresAt (parsed at auth_repository.dart:34-49) with the device's DateTime.now(). phone_verify.dart:126-129 stops locally with codeExpired before sending any request, and auth_repository.dart:61-63 also throws StateError. If the device clock runs ahead of the server by more than the OTP lifetime (5 min in in_process_mock_client.dart:402), every challenge, including each one from Resend, counts as expired on arrival, so a valid code can never be submitted. The contract does not define OTP issuance (openapi.yaml:26), and no document makes this check intentional. With the in-process mock, both times come from the device clock, so the bug only shows with a real server and a skewed clock (auto time turned off). That makes it an edge path, but it blocks sign-in completely.
verdicts.repro: Read otp_challenge.dart, auth_repository.dart:30-63, phone_verify.dart:118-137 and the mock OTP handler at in_process_mock_client.dart:388-430. No guard uses a server-relative TTL.

verdicts.reason: AuthRepository.requestOtp (auth_repository.dart:34,49) stores the server's absolute expiresAt. OtpChallenge.isExpired (otp_challenge.dart:21) compares it with the device's DateTime.now().toUtc(). PhoneVerification._verify (phone_verify.dart:126-129) and AuthRepository.verifyOtp (auth_repository.dart:61-63) both stop before any request when it is true. Nothing compensates for clock skew, and the response has no TTL or server-time field. If the device clock runs ahead of the server by more than the OTP lifetime, every challenge, including each resend, is expired the moment it arrives. This is an edge path: the device clock must be wrong by more than the TTL.
verdicts.repro: Wrote throwaway test test/_audit_u73_otp_test.dart (since deleted): expiresAt = (deviceNow - 6min) + 5min, which models a device 6 minutes ahead. Output: 'isExpired=true remaining=0:00:00.000000' and 'All tests passed!'.

confirmed.title: A pasted international number (+46 …) at sign-in or Add phone is either rejected or, in the spaced form, cut short and accepted as a wrong number (+4646…) that the OTP is sent to
confirmed.description: `AuthPhoneField` filters input to digits and spaces (auth_controls.dart:289-292), so a pasted `+46 70 123 45 67` becomes `46 70 123 45 67`. `swedishNumberFromField` then prefixes `+46` to anything not starting with `0` (993) giving `+4646701234567`; `toE164` sees 11 digits after +46 and returns null, so the screen shows "invalid Swedish mobile" for a valid number the rider pasted from Contacts.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider pastes their number from the clipboard/contacts in international format on Sign in or Add phone; Continue is refused with an "invalid" error.
confirmed.evidence:
auth_controls.dart:289-292 `inputFormatters: [FilteringTextInputFormatter.allow(RegExp(r'[0-9 ]')), LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter(14)],`
auth_navigation.dart:990-994 `final digits = typed.replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), '').trim(); ... return SwedishPhone.toE164(digits.startsWith('0') ? digits : '+46$digits');`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Strip a leading `46`/`0046` before prefixing, or pass the raw digits to `toE164` which already handles `46…`/`0046…` prefixes.

verdicts.reason: The field strips '+' (auth_controls.dart:290 allows only [0-9 ]) and truncates to 14 characters (:291). swedishNumberFromField (auth_navigation.dart:68-72) then puts '+46' in front of anything that does not start with '0'. SwedishPhone.toE164 (safety/domain/phone_e164.dart:4-18) only checks for 7-10 digits after +46. A pasted '+46701234567' is rejected as invalid. Worse, the common spaced form '+46 70 123 45 67' becomes the field text '46 70 123 45 6', which is accepted as the wrong number +464670123456. sign_in.dart:96-106 then calls requestOtp with it, so the OTP goes to a non-existent or someone else's number. add_phone.dart:52 uses the same parser. '0046…' and '07…' inputs are handled correctly.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r30_test.dart (since deleted) applied the field's two formatters, then swedishNumberFromField. Output: '"+46 70 123 45 67" -> field "46 70 123 45 6" -> +464670123456', '"+46701234567" -> field "46701234567" -> null', '"0046701234567" -> ... -> +46701234567', '"070 123 45 67" -> ... -> +46701234567'. 1 test passed.

confirmed.title: Sign-in Continue/Verify and the Apple/Google buttons expose no tap action to screen readers
confirmed.description: AuthPrimaryButton and AuthProviderButton wrap their InkWell in `Semantics(button: true, enabled: ..., label: ..., excludeSemantics: true)` and pass no `onTap`. excludeSemantics drops the InkWell's semantics node, which is where the tap action lives. The resulting node is announced as a button but has no SemanticsAction.tap. On Android, TalkBack marks it as not clickable and double-tap does not activate it. Web semantics also gives it no click handler. These buttons are the only way through sign-in (Continue, Verify, Let's ride, Apple, Google).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A TalkBack user focuses 'Continue' on Sign in after entering a number and double-taps. The node has no tap action, nothing happens and no code is requested, so the rider cannot sign in with a screen reader.
confirmed.evidence:
auth_controls.dart:26-30 `return Semantics( button: true, enabled: enabled, label: label, excludeSemantics: true, child: ...InkWell(onTap: enabled ? onPressed : null` (no Semantics.onTap)
auth_controls.dart:116-120 the same for AuthProviderButton
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass `onTap: enabled ? onPressed : null` to the outer Semantics, or drop excludeSemantics and use MergeSemantics.

verdicts.reason: AuthPrimaryButton (auth_controls.dart:26-30) and AuthProviderButton (116-120) wrap their InkWell in Semantics(button: true, excludeSemantics: true) with no onTap. excludeSemantics drops the InkWell's tap action, so the merged node is a button with no SemanticsAction.tap. On Android, TalkBack therefore treats it as not clickable. iOS VoiceOver may fall back to a simulated touch, but Android and web have no such fallback. These buttons are the only controls for Continue, Verify, Let's ride, Apple and Google, so a screen-reader user can be stuck at sign-in.

On Android, TalkBack's ACTION_CLICK has nothing to dispatch to. iOS VoiceOver may still fall back to a synthesized touch, which is why I rate it medium and not high.
