confirmed.title: Names over 80 characters (40+1+40 at sign-up, or any length in Personal info) are rejected by the mock/proposed profile PATCH, and SyncedProfileRepository hides this permanent 422 as 'pending', so later consent and language syncs fail silently
confirmed.description: AuthTextField caps each name field at 40 characters, and RiderNameScreen saves '$first $last'. That can be 81 characters. The Personal info editor (showAccountTextEditor) has no length limit at all. The profile contract and the in-process mock reject `name.trim().length > 80` with 422 invalid_profile. SyncedProfileRepository._sync catches every error the same way: it sets `_syncPending = true` and logs a warning. The UI therefore never says anything. Every later save resends the same over-long name, so every PATCH is rejected, including consent and language changes, and the 'resend' can never succeed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A new rider types a 40-character first name and a 40-character last name and taps Let's ride. PATCH {name: <81 chars>} returns 422 and the app enters normally. Later the rider turns off Offers in Privacy. That PATCH also returns 422 because it carries the same name. The server never learns the name or any consent change, and the rider is shown no error.
confirmed.evidence:
auth_controls.dart:377 `inputFormatters: [LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter(40)],`
rider_name.dart:68 `profile.profile.copyWith(name: last.isEmpty ? first : '$first $last')`
account_widgets.dart:339-345 the editor's TextField has no length formatter
in_process_mock_client.dart:1136-1140 `if (name is! String || name.trim().length > 80 || ...) { status = 422; ...invalid_profile }`
synced_profile_repository.dart:78-80 `} catch (error) { _syncPending = true; AppLog.warning('profile.sync_failed', ...); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Validate the combined name against the server limit (80) in the sign-up and Personal info editors. Treat a 4xx validation answer as a user-facing error instead of as pending.

confirmed.title: A booking that may have been created is not checked against the server before a retry gets a fresh key, so a retry books a second live ride
confirmed.description: RC-09 accepts that a timeout, dropped connection or 5xx may still have created the ride. `_sendOrRecover` recovers only inside the same call (one replay plus `GET /rider/trips/active`), and when the network is down that recovery fails too. The rider is then told `bookingUncertain` ('Check your connection and try again'). The kept `BookingAttempt` is reused only when the next intent matches exactly and less than 5 minutes have passed since the first tap (`matches` uses `startedAt`). The intent includes pickup and destination rounded to 1e-4 degrees, so a pin a metre away across a cell edge, a GPS-preselected pickup that moved, or a retry after 5 minutes all produce a new `BookingAttempt` with a new idempotency key. Nothing calls `_adoptActiveTrip` or `fetchActive` before that new key is sent. The server has no one-live-trip rule (the mock `POST /rides` just creates another ride, and the contract defines none). So the ghost ride from the first attempt stays live on the server with no screen watching it, and a second ride is created.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider taps Book now. The POST reaches the server and creates ride R1, then the connection drops before the answer arrives. The replay and the active-trip lookup also fail offline, and the rider sees 'We couldn't confirm your booking. Check your connection and try again.' The network comes back after 5 minutes, and the rider taps Book now again (or after 10 seconds, with the pickup pin re-confirmed a few metres away). `_attemptFor` creates a new attempt with a new key, `POST /rides` creates R2, and Finding opens for R2. R1 is still searching on the server and can be matched with a second driver. Two rides are booked. Traced by hand through booking_coordinator.dart, booking_attempt.dart and the in-process mock.
confirmed.evidence:
booking_attempt.dart:31-33 `bool matches(String otherIntentKey, {DateTime? now}) => intentKey == otherIntentKey && (now ?? DateTime.now()).difference(startedAt) < reuseWindow;`
booking_coordinator.dart:52-58 `if (current != null && current.matches(intentKey)) return current; final next = BookingAttempt(intentKey: intentKey); _attempt = next;`
booking_coordinator.dart:208-211 `return [(lat * 1e4).round(), (lng * 1e4).round()];`
booking_coordinator.dart:451-453 `final adopted = await _adoptActiveTrip(destinationLat, destinationLng); if (adopted != null) return adopted; rethrow;`
in_process_mock_client.dart:597-610 `} else if (path == '/api/v1/rides' && method == 'POST') { ... final ride = _ride(body, requestId); rides[ride['id'] as String] = ride;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: When the previous attempt ended 'maybe created' (an attempt with a replay that never succeeded or was refused), call `_adoptActiveTrip`/`fetchActive` before minting a new key for any intent, and adopt or block if the server already has a live trip. Alternatively keep the uncertain key until the server has been asked.

verdicts.reason: After a maybe-created failure where the replay and fetchActive also fail, select_ride.dart:1558-1570 shows bookingUncertain and only reloads quotes. A later tap creates a fresh BookingAttempt with a new key when the intent changes even slightly or the 5-minute window from startedAt has passed (booking_attempt.dart:31-33, booking_coordinator.dart:52-58, 343-355). Nothing on that path calls _adoptActiveTrip or fetchActive before sending. Those run only after a send fails (:451). RideRestoreCoordinator.adoptServerActiveTrip runs only on root restore, app resume or a notification tap, not while Select Ride stays in the foreground. The _findingAlreadyActive guard (:262) checks only for a mounted Finding UI. The mock POST /api/v1/rides (in_process_mock_client.dart:597-610) has no one-live-trip rule and the contract states none, so a second ride is created while R1 is still searching. Rated medium: it needs the uncertain-outcome edge, and the server's own expire transition eventually limits R1.
verdicts.repro: Static trace through select_ride.dart:1530-1590, BookingCoordinator.requestFinding/_prepareFinding/_sendOrRecover/_adoptActiveTrip, BookingAttempt, and the RideRestoreCoordinator.adoptServerActiveTrip callers (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:453, notification_navigation.dart:94), plus the mock POST /rides handler. No test run.

verdicts.reason: booking_attempt.dart:31-33 reuses the key only when the intent matches and less than 5 minutes have passed since startedAt. booking_coordinator.dart:52-58 otherwise creates a new BookingAttempt with a new key. On a maybe-created failure, _sendOrRecover (booking_coordinator.dart:~438-455) replays once, calls _adoptActiveTrip once, then rethrows, and _releaseWhenDone keeps the attempt but nothing queries the server before the next new key. The only other fetchActive callers are in ride_restore_coordinator.dart (cold restore and app-resume adoption), which does not run while the rider stays in the app. The mock POST /api/v1/rides (in_process_mock_client.dart:597-610) only checks the quote binding and has no rule against a second live ride. After 5 minutes, or with a pickup pin re-confirmed across an 11 m rounding cell, a second ride is created while R1 is still live. This needs a network drop at the exact moment of booking and a delayed or modified retry, so it is an edge path rather than the main path.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand. The first POST creates R1, the response is lost, the replay throws ClientException and fetchActive throws offline, so bookingUncertain is shown. When the rider taps again more than 5 minutes later, matches() is false because the elapsed time is not under 5 minutes, so a new idempotency key is minted. The POST goes straight to _submitFinding and the mock creates R2 with nothing checking for R1.

confirmed.title: Swapping the last stop and the destination in Change route makes preview re-geocode both from text instead of using the booked coordinates
confirmed.description: RoutePickerPage never receives the destination's point (`_destinationPoint` starts null), and stops never carry points. `RouteChangeController.preview` makes up for this by matching text: it uses `ride.destination*` when the destination text equals `ride.destinationAddress`, and a stop's coordinates when the text matches an entry in `ride.stops`. After `_swap` that matching fails. With stops, the old destination moves into the last stop (it is not in `ride.stops`), and the old stop becomes the destination (it is not equal to `ride.destinationAddress`). confirmed.title: Choose-on-map passes the shortened or translated pickup field text, so Home treats the GPS or placeholder label as typed and geocodes it instead of opening at GPS
confirmed.description: The pickup field shows _show(widget.pickupAddress), which is compactAddress(...). Home._openPickupMapPicker decides 'typedByRider' by comparing that text with the stored English, full _pickupAddress. In fr/sv the translated location-off label is not recognised as a placeholder, so chosen becomes the geocoder's hit and positionIsFallback becomes false.

confirmed.title: Re-dispatch after a driver drop restores the offer ceiling from the booking-time RideSession copy, discarding the ceiling a route change set
confirmed.description: The offer ceiling (ARCH-20) exists in two places: `RideSnapshot.maxOfferMinor` (in the store and in Finding's `_snapshot`) and `RideSession.bookedMaxOfferMinor`. Only booking and restore write `bookedMaxOfferMinor`. A route change sets a new ceiling: the mock server recomputes it, and `RouteChangeController.apply` saves `maxOfferMinor: serverMax` into the stored snapshot. The session copy is left at the booking value. When the driver drops the ride on Waiting, Waiting pops to Finding. `_resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel` adopts the stored route and price, then calls `_startMatching` -> `startFrom`. `startFrom` builds a new snapshot whose ceiling is `session.bookedMaxOfferMinor`, the stale booking-time value. `maxOfferPrice` and `confirmPriceIncreaseBy` then use the wrong ceiling. `_evaluatePhase` and `_persistAssigned` later write it back over the store's correct value, so even a reload keeps it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Booked at 200 kr, so the server and client ceiling is 1.8 x 200 = 360 kr (36000 öre). On Waiting the rider changes the destination and the price becomes 300 kr. The server ceiling becomes 540 kr and the stored snapshot gets 54000. The driver then cancels. Finding resumes at 300 kr with maxOfferMinor 36000, so maxOfferPrice is 360. Raising by 100 kr (to 400 kr) returns false client-side, although the server allows up to 540. In the opposite case (route lowered to 100 kr, server ceiling 180 kr), the client still allows +150 kr (250 kr). The server refuses with 409 offer_above_maximum and the rider sees 'couldn't update offer'. About 90 s later the delayed-search save overwrites the stored 54000 with 36000. Worked by hand from the code; not run.

The event is reachable while Finding is still the subscriber: `ApiRideRealtime` maps a matched→searching projection to `cancelledByDriver` (api_ride_realtime.dart 193-199), and Finding stays subscribed after an accept whenever `_completeAssigned` is deferred (`_assignmentPending` because an offer raise/pickup edit or a cancel is in flight, 939-945) or during the `_persistAssigned` await before `_openWaiting` disposes the controller.

It does not check `_assigned`, and the only filter for assigned rides is `_assigned && status == driverAssigned` (381). A `cancelledByDriver` event (api_ride_realtime.dart:193-199 maps matched->searching to it) passes `backendReconcile`, because driverAssigned->cancelledByDriver is legal (ride_transition.dart:55-58). It is `isTerminal` (ride_status.dart:62), so it goes to `_completeTerminal` (394-397). That method guards only on terminated/cancelled/disposed/!isTerminal (1006), archives cancelledByDriver to History (1027-1035), clears the snapshot (1037) and fires onTerminal. `_handleTerminal` then shows the terminal sheet and calls `RideNavigator.home` (finding_drivers.dart:331-334). Finding is disposed only inside `_openWaiting` (finding_drivers.dart:528). The match is deferred whenever `_drainDeferredNavigation` returns early because the route is not current or `_pickupEditOpen` is true (finding_drivers.dart:269-276), for example while the route-change page from `_changeRoute` is open (665). It is also deferred while `_editInFlight`/`_cancelInFlight` sets `_assignmentPending` (939-945). In all of these windows the subscription is still live. The intended handling is a reversible re-dispatch: Waiting re-searches (active_ride_controller.dart:327, ride_status.dart:31-35).

verdicts.reason: In finding_driver_controller.dart:394-397 the Finding listener sends any `isTerminal` status to `_completeTerminal`. `cancelledByDriver` is in `isTerminal` (core/contracts/ride_status.dart:31-36, where the comment says it is never terminal on the wire). `_completeTerminal` (1009-1046) archives it as a cancelled ride at 1028, clears the snapshot and calls `_onTerminal`. `_onTerminal` (finding_drivers.dart:316-334) shows the 'Driver cancelled / Continue' sheet and then `RideNavigator.home`. Finding stays subscribed after a match while an edit or cancel is in flight, because `_completeAssigned` (937-945) only sets `_assignmentPending` and returns. In production `ApiRideRealtime` (api_ride_realtime.dart:193-199) turns a matched-to-searching projection into `cancelledByDriver`, and it does the same for an admin reassign; only the event kind differs. No guard drops the event: the gate passes it and `backendReconcile` accepts it. The server trip is still searching, but the rider is sent Home with no snapshot, so a driver who accepts next has no rider screen. confirmed.title: Price raise the server accepted is thrown away and reported as failed when the rider taps Cancel during the PATCH; the fare shown stays the old one
confirmed.description: `cancelSearch` does not check `_editInFlight`. It just bumps `_editEpoch` (line 1102), and the Cancel X stays tappable while the price-bump card is busy. When the raise PATCH response then arrives, `ride.observeProjection(response)` records the new version, but `_editInvalid(editToken)` is true, so the method returns false before `_snapshot` or the store is updated and before `_bumpDismissed`/`offerConfirmation` are set. `_raiseOffer` then shows `editFeedback ?? editOfferFailed`, and `editFeedback` was reset to null, so the rider sees "couldn't update your offer". If the cancel does not commit (409 driver accepted, or `stale` because the raise bumped the version), the search goes on with the pre-raise price: the card shows again, `_persistAssigned` saves the old price, and Waiting gets `price: _match.currentPrice` (old). A second raise is computed from the old fare while the server adds it on top of the already-raised fare.
confirmed.failure_scenario: After 45 s the rider taps +20 kr. While the PATCH is in flight they hit X → Cancel request. The server applies the raise (279 kr). The cancel comes back 409 (version changed / driver accepted). Finding says the offer failed and keeps showing 259 kr, Waiting and History show 259 kr, and the rider is charged 279 kr. If they raise again (+20), the server makes it 299 kr while the button previewed 279 kr.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When the PATCH succeeded, apply the server fare to `_snapshot` (and the store) even if a cancel started meanwhile, unless the cancel committed. Or make `cancelSearch` wait for / refuse while `_editInFlight`, and disable the X while an edit is busy.

verdicts.reason: cancelSearch (finding_driver_controller.dart:1097-1102) does not wait for or refuse an _editInFlight raise; it just bumps _editEpoch. The Cancel X has no busy guard (finding_drivers.dart:866-869, _confirmCancel 567-583 checks only _leaving/_cancelSheetOpen/matchCount). When the PATCH answers, observeProjection runs, and then `if (_editInvalid(editToken)) return false;` (831-833) returns before _snapshot/_store get the server fare. _raiseOffer then shows editOfferFailed (finding_drivers.dart:713-719). The cancel's expectedVersion was taken before the raise bumped the version (_requestServerCancel enqueue, ~1180), so 409 version_mismatch -> stale (1207) is the likely result. The stale branch only shows rideJustChangedMessage (finding_drivers.dart:609-611) and restarts the tick. Nothing re-reads the fare, so Finding and then Waiting (price: _match.currentPrice, finding_drivers.dart:544) keep the pre-raise fare.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of confirmPriceIncreaseBy, cancelSearch, _requestServerCancel and the UI result handling. The audit's repro output (raised=false, cancel=stale, clientPrice=259, serverFare=279) matches the trace. I did not re-run it.

verdicts.reason: cancelSearch (finding_driver_controller.dart:1098-1102) bumps _editEpoch with no check of _editInFlight, and the Cancel X (finding_drivers.dart:866-869) has no busy guard. When the raise PATCH succeeds, the code calls observeProjection, then `if (_editInvalid(editToken)) return false;` (831-833) returns before _snapshot or the store take the server fare. If the cancel is then refused as stale (the raise bumped the server version), the search resumes at the old fare, _raiseOffer shows editOfferFailed (finding_drivers.dart:713-720), and Waiting is later given _match.currentPrice. Today's in-process mock does not bump the version on an offer raise (in_process_mock_client.dart:990-1010 has no _touch), so on the mock the cancel commits and nothing lasting is wrong. On a server that versions every change, the failure happens.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u96_test.dart (deleted): InProcessMockClient at 50 ms latency, version 3, then confirmPriceIncrease(20), cancelSearch 5 ms later, and a server version bump after the PATCH applied. Output: `raised=false cancel=SearchCancelResult.stale clientPrice=259.0 server=279.0 status=searching feedback=null`. Without the version bump (the mock as it is): `cancel=SearchCancelResult.confirmed ... status=cancelled_by_rider`, which is harmless.

confirmed.title: Cold-start/reconnect outbox flush moves a cancel queued during search onto the accepted trip's version and replays it, cancelling the matched ride and charging the live cancel fee (contradicts RC-03 'match overtakes queued cancel')
confirmed.description: `_completeAssigned` says a match that overtakes a queued cancel removes it 'so it cannot cancel the matched ride later' (lines 947-959), and tells the rider 'driver already accepted'. But the flush (`_flushPendingCancels` / `_rereadForReplay`) re-reads the trip and replays the cancel whenever `TripStateMachine.apply(status, 'cancel', rider)` allows it. Rider cancel is allowed from accepted, driver_to_pickup and arrived. The flush also moves the entry onto the current version (`forVersion`), which removes the version check that would have refused it. On cold start `_dropIfCancelQueued` flushes before any screen exists. On reconnect the flush runs in parallel with the realtime match. Either way the cancel reaches the server for an accepted trip. The mock then charges `_riderCancelFee` counted from acceptedAt.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider taps Cancel while searching with no signal and gets 'Cancelling…' (queued, free). They close the app. A driver accepts at 12:00 and drives toward the pickup. At 12:06 the rider reopens the app. The restore flush re-reads `accepted`/`driver_to_pickup`, the state machine allows `cancel`, and the cancel is posted. The server cancels the trip and stores a 35 kr live cancel fee, for a cancel the rider made while it was free.
confirmed.evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:1559-1577 `final applies = TripStateMachine.apply(status, command, TripActor.rider, ...) != null; if (!applies) { ... stale } return (result: null, version: version);`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1473-1477 `cancel = cancel.forVersion(version);`
finding_driver_controller.dart:948-953 `// ... the stale request leaves the outbox so it cannot cancel the matched ride later. ... PendingCancelStore.remove(id)`
in_process_mock_client.dart:712 `final fee = command == 'cancel' ? _riderCancelFee(ride) : null;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: When replaying a `cancel` queued during search, drop it as stale once the trip is past searching/offered (accepted or later), or send the version from when it was queued. Report it as refused/stale so the rider decides again with the fee shown.

verdicts.reason: A cancel that cannot reach the server leaves the ride live and sets `_cancelQueued` (finding_driver_controller.dart:1124-1140). The only place a match drops the queued entry is `_completeAssigned` (948-953), and that needs a live Finding controller. On cold start, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:118-170 flushes the outbox before any screen is built. Its comment says a refusal ('a driver accepted first') restores the ride. In practice no refusal comes back. `_rereadForReplay` (1530-1577) re-reads the trip and finds `accepted`/`driver_to_pickup`, and `TripStateMachine.apply(status,'cancel',rider)` allows the cancel there. `_flushPendingCancels` then rewrites the entry onto the current version (`cancel.forVersion(version)`, 1473-1477; pending_cancel_store.dart:67 also mints a new key). That removes the `version_mismatch` 409 the original version would have caused. The mock passes the version check (in_process_mock_client.dart:705) and charges `_riderCancelFee`, counted from `_acceptedAt` (712, 1640-1672). The restore then reconciles the ride to cancelledByRider and sends the rider Home. No document (DECISIONS/ARCHITECTURE/API_V1_MOCK) says that replaying onto an accepted trip, or the fee, is intended. Cancelling still matches what the rider asked for. What is wrong is the inconsistency with RC-03 and the fee for a cancel made while it was free.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: cancelSearch -> _requestServerCancel returns queued (1170-1205) -> app reopened -> RideRestoreCoordinator._dropIfCancelQueued -> flushPendingCancels -> _rereadForReplay (status accepted, applies) -> forVersion(current) -> POST cancel -> mock 200 with fee (in_process_mock_client.dart:705-735). No test run.
verdicts.corrected_title: Cold-start/reconnect outbox flush moves a cancel queued during search onto the accepted trip's version and replays it, cancelling the matched ride and charging the live cancel fee (contradicts RC-03 'match overtakes queued cancel')

verdicts.reason: A cancel queued while searching stays in the outbox and the ride stays live (finding_driver_controller.dart:1123-1136). Only a mounted search that sees the match removes it (947-959). The cold-start flush (bootstrap.dart:131, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:118-133) and the reconnect flush (finding_driver_controller.dart:1428-1446) run _rereadForReplay. That function only drops the entry when TripStateMachine.apply refuses the rider 'cancel' (1559-1577). Rider cancel is allowed from accepted and driver_to_pickup, so the entry is re-keyed with forVersion(currentVersion) (1473-1477), which removes the server's version-mismatch guard, and is then posted. The mock prices the cancel with _riderCancelFee, which counts from acceptedAt (in_process_mock_client.dart:712, 1663-1667). _dropIfCancelQueued then archives the ride as cancelled. This contradicts the documented RC-03 rule that a driver who accepted first wins and the stale cancel leaves the outbox (comment at 947-953, and the test 'a driver who accepted first wins; the stale cancel leaves the outbox' in test/ride/rc_cancel_outbox_test.dart). The impact is limited because the rider did ask to cancel. That is why this is medium, not high.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u103_test.dart (since deleted). It enqueued PendingCancel(rideId r1, expectedVersion 2) and ran flushPendingCancels against a MockClient whose GET returns status driver_to_pickup at version 4. Output: requests [GET /api/v1/rides/r1 , POST /api/v1/rides/r1/cancel {"expectedVersion":4}], result {r1: PendingCancelResult.sent}. The cancel was replayed against the accepted trip at the new version.

confirmed.title: "Try again" after no driver found leaves the screen poppable while the new booking is created, orphaning a live search
confirmed.description: `_handleTerminal` sets `_leaving = true` (line 323) before showing the no-driver sheet. On Try again, `_requestAgain` awaits `submitFinding` (a quote plus POST /rides, two round trips) and only resets `_leaving = false` after success (line 380). The screen's `PopScope(canPop: _leaving)` therefore lets a system back / swipe pop Finding during the request, and the X is inert (`_confirmCancel` returns on `_leaving`). The booking still creates the server ride and saves its snapshot (BookingCoordinator._submitFinding), but `_requestAgain` sees `!mounted` and returns false. No Finding owns the new live ride, `FindingDriverController.active` is null (cleared by `_completeTerminal`), and nothing navigates to it until a later lifecycle resume/reload restore.
confirmed.failure_scenario: No driver found → the rider taps Try again, sees nothing change for a second and swipes back. Finding pops to Select Ride/Home. The server has a new searching ride with the stored snapshot, but no screen shows it. A driver can accept it unseen. If the rider books again from Select Ride, `_findingAlreadyActive` is false, so a second live ride is created.
confirmed.evidence:
finding_drivers.dart:323 `_leaving = true;`
finding_drivers.dart:338-341 `final choice = await showNoDriverFoundSheet(context); ... if (choice == NoDriverChoice.tryAgain && await _requestAgain(ended)) {`
finding_drivers.dart:352 `rideId = await (widget.booking ?? BookingController()).submitFinding(`
finding_drivers.dart:376 `if (!mounted || rideId.trim().isEmpty) return false;`
finding_drivers.dart:808-811 `return PopScope(canPop: _leaving, onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, _) { if (!didPop) _confirmCancel(); },`
booking_coordinator.dart:44 `bool get _findingAlreadyActive => FindingDriverController.active != null;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Set `_leaving = false` (or keep a separate rebooking flag that keeps canPop false and shows progress) while `_requestAgain` is in flight. If the widget unmounted after the ride was created, hand the ride to `RideRestoreCoordinator.recoverCreatedFinding`.

verdicts.reason: _handleTerminal sets _leaving = true (finding_drivers.dart:323) and keeps it through _requestAgain. _requestAgain awaits submitFinding (quote plus POST) and then storedRide, and resets _leaving only at line 380. PopScope(canPop: _leaving) (808-812) therefore lets a system back or swipe pop Finding during that wait. Afterwards `if (!mounted ...) return false` (376) drops the new ride id, and the booking coordinator has already saved the snapshot and created the server ride. Nothing hands it to recoverCreatedFinding: it is only called from select_ride.dart:1575/1589, and no route calls didPopNext. FindingDriverController.active is null, so _findingAlreadyActive (booking_coordinator.dart:44) does not block a second booking once _inflight has cleared, and I found no server-side one-live-ride guard in the mock.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _handleTerminal, _requestAgain, the PopScope in build, BookingCoordinator.submitFinding/_inflight, and every recoverCreatedFinding caller found by grep. Not run as a widget test.

verdicts.reason: _handleTerminal sets `_leaving = true` (finding_drivers.dart:323) and keeps it true through `await submitFinding(...)` in _requestAgain. It is reset only after success (~380). So `PopScope(canPop: _leaving)` (808) lets system back or a swipe pop Finding while the quote and POST /rides are in flight, and no progress UI is shown. The coordinator still commits the ride and reconciles the session (booking_coordinator.dart _submitFinding). Then `if (!mounted ...) return false` (376) drops it without handing it to a new owner. FindingDriverController.active was cleared by _completeTerminal (finding_driver_controller.dart:1015), so `_findingAlreadyActive` (booking_coordinator.dart:44) is false and a second booking from Select Ride is not refused. SelectRide handles the same unmounted-after-create case with RideRestoreCoordinator.recoverCreatedFinding (select_ride.dart:1574-1578). Finding has no equivalent, which shows the gap is unintended.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand from the callers: _handleTerminal → showNoDriverFoundSheet → _requestAgain → BookingController.submitFinding → _submitFinding (POST /api/v1/rides, backendReconcile). Finding.dispose (747-760) only disposes _match and does not cancel the server ride. No widget test was run, because driving a pop during the in-flight POST needs a full app harness.

confirmed.title: 'Try again' after no driver found reports a may-have-booked failure as a plain failure and sends the rider Home while the new ride may exist
confirmed.description: `_requestAgain` catches every error with `rebookFailed` ('We couldn't request a new ride. Choose your route and try again.') and returns false, and `_handleTerminal` then goes Home. It never checks `BookingController.mayHaveBooked(error)`, which Select Ride uses (RC-09) for exactly this case. A timeout or dropped connection after the POST may have created the ride. The rider is told it failed and is told to rebook from Home, so the ghost ride stays live with no screen. If the rider rebooks with any different intent, that books a second ride (see the BookingAttempt finding).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The search ends with no driver found and the rider taps Try again. The POST /rides creates the ride but the connection drops before the answer. The replay and adopt fail, and the rider sees 'We couldn't request a new ride. Choose your route and try again.' and lands on Home. The server ride keeps searching, may be matched with a driver who comes to an empty pickup, or the rider books again and has two rides. Traced by reading the code.
confirmed.evidence:
finding_drivers.dart:370-375 `} catch (_) { _showCancelNotice( L10n.current.rebookFailed, ); return false; }`
finding_drivers.dart:340-344 `if (choice == NoDriverChoice.tryAgain && await _requestAgain(ended)) { return; } if (!mounted) return; RideNavigator.home(context, status: status);`
select_ride.dart:1558 `final uncertain = BookingController.mayHaveBooked(error);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: When `BookingController.mayHaveBooked(error)` is true, show `bookingUncertain`, stay on the screen, and try `fetchActive` to adopt the ride (or offer Retry, which reuses the same attempt) instead of sending the rider Home.

verdicts.reason: finding_drivers.dart:370-375 catches every error and shows `rebookFailed` ('We couldn't request a new ride. Choose your route and try again.', app_en.arb:550). It returns false, and :340-344 then calls `RideNavigator.home`. It never checks `BookingController.mayHaveBooked` (booking_controller.dart:14). Select Ride does check it (select_ride.dart:1560) and shows bookingUncertain. The coordinator's `_sendOrRecover` (booking_coordinator.dart:440-460) replays once and then tries `_adoptActiveTrip`. When both fail with a retryable error (connectivity down), it rethrows the retryable error, so the may-have-booked case reaches this catch. Two things soften it. (1) The BookingAttempt is kept for non-refusal errors (:72-77, :424), so a rebook of the same intent reuses the idempotency key. (2) RideRestoreCoordinator.resumeIfNeeded runs on app resume (app_lifecycle.dart:22), and a push notification can adopt the ride. In-session, though, the rider is told it failed and lands on Home while the server ride may be searching. A rebook with a different intent creates a second ride.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: finding_drivers.dart:316-376; booking_coordinator.dart:52-87, 355-460 (maybeCreated, _adoptActiveTrip); select_ride.dart:1557-1571 for comparison; FindingDriverController.active is cleared on terminal (finding_driver_controller.dart:1015), so the call is not short-circuited. No test run.

verdicts.reason: finding_drivers.dart:370-375 catches every error and shows `rebookFailed` ('We couldn't request a new ride...'), then returns false. :340-344 then calls `RideNavigator.home`, which clears the snapshot (ride_navigator.dart:51). `BookingController.mayHaveBooked` is never checked, unlike select_ride.dart:1560, which shows `bookingUncertain` for the same RC-09 case. BookingCoordinator._sendOrRecover (booking_coordinator.dart:428-446) rethrows the retryable error when the replay fails and `_adoptActiveTrip` returns null (for example, fetchActive also fails offline). So the rider is told plainly that the request failed while the ride may exist. One mitigation: on the next app resume, RideRestoreCoordinator.adoptServerActiveTrip (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:76-99) can pick the ride up again. Until then the rider sees Home with a wrong 'failed' message.
verdicts.repro: Traced `_requestAgain` -> submitFinding -> _prepareFinding -> _sendOrRecover. Checked that `maybeCreated` treats timeouts, ClientException and 5xx as possibly created, and that the Finding catch block never branches on it. No test was run.

confirmed.title: After location is revoked and then allowed again, Home never restarts live tracking; the puck freezes while the state says 'live'
confirmed.description: When the position stream errors with PermissionDeniedException, startTracking cancels the subscription, sets permissionRequired and returns without arranging a resubscribe. When the rider allows location again and returns to the app, Home.didChangeAppLifecycleState calls resumeLiveUpdates(). That only asks for one fix (_refreshAfterResume -> latestFix) and sets the state to live. The resume handler restarts tracking only for `temporarilyUnavailable` (recoverLiveLocation) or when `_currentLatLng == null` (a fresh detect). A rider who had a fix before the revoke matches neither branch. The stream is never subscribed again, so the puck and the pickup label stop following the rider, although the location notice has cleared.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On iOS, Home is showing the rider's position. The rider switches location to 'Never' in Settings: the stream errors and Home shows 'location denied'. The rider then sets 'While using' and comes back. Home shows one fresh fix and the notice clears, but as the rider walks the blue puck and 'Current location' pickup no longer move. Bookings start from the stale point until Home is rebuilt.
confirmed.suggested_fix: On resume, when the controller has no active _positionSub and permission is granted, call startTracking again (for example through recoverLiveLocation), not only for temporarilyUnavailable.

verdicts.reason: In startTracking's onError (home_controller.dart:472-480), a PermissionDeniedException cancels the subscription, sets _positionSub to null, sets permissionRequired and returns without _scheduleResubscribe. When the app resumes, Home.didChangeAppLifecycleState (home.dart:244-268) calls resumeLiveUpdates. That only runs _refreshAfterResume (home_controller.dart:749-764), which takes one latestFix, sets the state to live and calls onFix. The branch check runs synchronously while the state is still permissionRequired, so it is not temporarilyUnavailable and recoverLiveLocation is skipped. _currentLatLng is non-null, so _detectCurrentAddress is skipped too. The only other callers that start tracking are bindLiveLocation (home.dart:380, reached only from _runDetectCurrentAddress) and recoverLiveLocation (home.dart:257). The unpark path (home.dart:239) also only calls resumeLiveUpdates. So the stream is never subscribed again, while the state reads live. This is realistic on iOS, where revoking location in Settings does not kill the app (Android kills the process on revoke).
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grepped every caller of startTracking, bindLiveLocation and recoverLiveLocation, and read the lifecycle handler and _refreshAfterResume.

verdicts.reason: When the stream reports PermissionDeniedException, the handler at home_controller.dart:474-481 sets _positionSub to null and the state to permissionRequired, with no resubscribe. On resume, home.dart:244-268 calls resumeLiveUpdates, whose _refreshAfterResume (home_controller.dart:741-764) takes one latestFix and sets the state to live. _trackingMounted/_trackingOnFix are not cleared on error, so that one fix is delivered. Tracking restarts only for temporarilyUnavailable (recoverLiveLocation) or when _currentLatLng is null (_detectCurrentAddress -> bindLiveLocation). A rider who already had a fix is in permissionRequired with a non-null _currentLatLng, so neither branch runs. The notice then clears because the state is live, which hides its Retry (home.dart:1976), the only other path that restarts tracking. The bug applies on iOS and on web. On Android, revoking a runtime permission kills the process, so a cold start restarts tracking there.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: stream onError -> permissionRequired; the rider re-grants and resumes; wasPaused is true, so _refreshAfterResume runs and the state becomes live; the state is not temporarilyUnavailable and _currentLatLng is non-null, so startTracking is never called again. No device run was done.

confirmed.title: Home puck pulse on web creates a never-revoked blob URL every 850 ms while Home is open
confirmed.description: startPulse flips pulseExpanded every 850 ms and calls onTick, which is Home's _updateLocationVisuals. On web that runs _paintWebPuck (home.dart:1588-1601). It swaps the puck icon between the cached 'expanded' and 'compact' rotated BitmapDescriptors, both BitmapDescriptor.bytes (home.dart:1562). paintUserPuck sees a non-identical icon and publishes a new marker Set (home_controller.dart:702-713). google_maps_flutter_web then runs _changeMarker for the puck, and urlFromMapBitmap makes a fresh `URL.createObjectURL(Blob(png))` each time, because its cache is cleared after every batch and the URL is never revoked. Every GPS fix (a position change) does the same. RotatedPuckCache (U7) only avoids re-rasterising in Dart. Each icon swap still allocates a new Blob in the browser that lives until the page unloads. The pulse runs for as long as Home is the current route and the camera is still, which is the app's idle state.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rider leaves the web app open on Home (for example, an installed PWA on iPhone left in the foreground) with location granted. Worked by hand: 3600/0.85 = about 4,235 pulse swaps/hour plus one per GPS fix, each a new Blob of the 65x75 puck PNG (a few KB). That is about 10-20 MB/hour that is never freed, plus one Google Maps icon decode each time. Over a long session this adds to the WebGL map's memory and raises the risk of iOS Safari killing the tab. Not run; traced by reading the code and the plugin source.
confirmed.evidence:
home_controller.dart:642-646 `_pulseTimer = Timer.periodic(const Duration(milliseconds: 850), (_) { if (!isMounted() || _livePaused || cameraMoving) return; pulseExpanded = !pulseExpanded; onTick(); });`
home.dart:1596-1601 `_locationCtl.paintUserPuck(target: target, icon: rotated ?? (...)!, heading: rotated == null ? heading : 0);`
home_controller.dart:702-713 `markers = { Marker(markerId: const MarkerId('live_user_location'), ... icon: icon, ...) }; notifyListeners();`
home_controller.dart:174-175 comment: `swaps the marker bitmap (a new blob URL and image decode on the web)`
confirmed.suggested_fix: On web, draw the pulse without swapping marker bitmaps, for example with a Circle overlay whose radius alternates, or with asset-backed icons. Another option is to keep one icon and stop pulsing on web. Do not send BytesMapBitmap icon changes at timer cadence.

verdicts.reason: Web is a supported target (DECISIONS.md:69 R-web, ARCHITECTURE.md:9,48). startPulse (home_controller.dart:642-646) flips pulseExpanded every 850 ms and calls onPulse = _updateLocationVisuals (home.dart:393). On web that goes to _paintWebPuck (home.dart:1575-1601), which swaps between two different BitmapDescriptor.bytes icons. The identical() guard in paintUserPuck (home_controller.dart:683-690) does not apply when the icon changes, so a new marker Set is published (702-713). In google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2 (the version in pubspec.lock), _changeMarker goes through _markerOptionsFromMarker, then _gmIconFromBitmapDescriptor (convert.dart:514, 428), then urlFromMapBitmap (convert.dart:752-760). That calls URL.createObjectURL(Blob) through a cache keyed on byteData.hashCode, and the cache is cleared after every marker batch (_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches, convert.dart:422-425, called from google_maps_controller.dart:577). Nothing in the plugin's marker path calls revokeObjectURL; its only revoke is in overlay.dart:64 for tile overlays. So every pulse swap and every GPS-driven repaint leaves one blob URL that is never freed, for as long as Home sits idle. The in-code comment at home_controller.dart:174-175 acknowledges the new blob URL per repaint, but no document accepts the leak.
verdicts.repro: Static trace through home.dart, home_controller.dart and the resolved plugin source at /root/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/google_maps_flutter_web-0.5.14+2/lib/src (convert.dart, markers.dart, google_maps_controller.dart). I grepped for revokeObjectURL: the only hit is overlay.dart:64. Not run in a browser.

verdicts.reason: home_controller.dart:642-646 flips pulseExpanded every 850 ms. The only things that stop it are _livePaused and cameraMoving, and cameraMoving (home_controller.dart:196-200, mapBusy = touching||easing) is false while the map is idle. On web, home.dart:1575-1580 goes to _paintWebPuck. That returns cached BytesMapBitmap icons (home.dart:1529-1531), but the expanded and compact icons are different objects, so the identical() check in paintUserPuck (home_controller.dart:683-690) fails and a new markers Set is published on every tick. HomeMapLayer passes it on (home_map_layer.dart:96). In google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2 (the locked version), updateMarkers calls _changeMarker, which goes through _gmIconFromBitmapDescriptor and then urlFromMapBitmap (convert.dart:752-761). That calls URL.createObjectURL(Blob) through _bitmapBlobUrlCache, and the cache is cleared after every batch by _cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches (google_maps_controller.dart:577, convert.dart:422-425). revokeObjectURL is never called for marker icons; it only appears in overlay.dart:64 for tile overlays. So every pulse tick creates a Blob URL that is never freed. The app's own comment at home_controller.dart:174-175 admits the 'new blob URL' cost.
verdicts.repro: Not run on web (flutter test has no browser target). Traced the app path and the locked plugin source in /root/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/google_maps_flutter_web-0.5.14+2/lib/src (convert.dart:422-425, 428-450, 752-761; markers.dart:101-123; google_maps_controller.dart:569-578). Worked by hand: 3600 s / 0.85 s = 4,235 ticks per hour, each one an unrevoked Blob URL for a 65x75 PNG of a few KB, so about 10-20 MB per hour, plus one Blob per GPS fix or heading-bucket change.

confirmed.title: Home's load() keeps only the first 8 custom places and every Home persist() writes that cut list back, so places 9 and later are deleted from storage
confirmed.description: HomePlacesController.load() maps `saved.places ... .take(maxCustom)` (8) into savedPlaces, and persist() writes `places: savedPlaces.map((place) => place.toJson()).toList()` to the shared HomeAddressRepository keys. SavedPlacesController.save() has no cap and appends freely (saved_places_controller.dart:98-99). Home persists on every booking/route change (_showRouteAddressPicker -> _persistAddressData, home.dart:1003) and after any saved-place edit, so the first Home persist after a 9th place exists removes places 9+ from storage for good. Reproduced: 9 stored places -> load gives 8 -> persist stores 8 (test output `loaded 8 of 9`, `stored after persist: 8`).

confirmed.title: After signing back in mid-ride on web, Home says 'Your ride search was interrupted. Book again' while the kept ride is being resumed
confirmed.description: Whether a ride is live is recorded twice on web: in `RideSnapshotStore` and in a sessionStorage flag (`movera_search_live`). Every `RideSnapshotStore.save` sets the flag (`markSearchLive`). Only `RideRestoreCoordinator.goHome` and the sign-out wipe clear it; `RideSnapshotStore.clear()` does not. Home's initState treats a set flag as proof the search was dropped. Its comment still assumes the old document-load wipe ('the web build's snapshot is gone before Flutter starts'), which R-web removed. When a session expires mid-ride (staging/production, authRequired), `onSessionExpired` deliberately keeps the snapshot and roots Sign in. After the rider signs back in, `enterMoveraApp` mounts Home first, and Home takes the flag and posts the 8-second toast. Only then does `resumeIfNeeded` (which awaits the session check, the snapshot read and a network resync) swap the root to the live Finding/Waiting screen. The SnackBar lives in the root ScaffoldMessenger, so it is still showing on the ride screen. The same mismatch occurs when `_dropIfCancelQueued` ends a ride on reload: it clears the store without clearing the flag, so Home claims the search was interrupted although the rider's own cancel went through.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Web staging: the rider's refresh token expires while a driver is on the way, and Sign in is shown with the ride kept. The rider signs in and lands on Home with the toast 'Your ride search was interrupted. Book again when you are ready.' A moment later the Waiting screen for the same ride appears under the same toast. The rider may book a second ride or think the trip was lost. Traced by reading the code; not run.
confirmed.evidence:
lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:189-191 `final interrupted = SearchInterruptedNotice.shared.take() | takeWebSearchInterrupted();`
lib/features/ride_booking/data/ride_snapshot_store.dart:381 `markSearchLive();` (every live save) vs :512-519 `clear()` never calls clearSearchLive
lib/features/auth/presentation/auth_navigation.dart:19-27 `showMoveraRoot(const Home(), ...); if (shown) { unawaited(RideRestoreCoordinator.instance.resumeIfNeeded()); }`
lib/app/di.dart:104-115 session expiry keeps the snapshot
lib/features/ride_booking/application/ride_restore_coordinator.dart:155-163 `_dropIfCancelQueued` clears the snapshot, flag left set
confirmed.suggested_fix: Derive the notice from the snapshot store, not a second flag. Call clearSearchLive() inside RideSnapshotStore.clear(). Have Home skip the notice while `RideSnapshotStore.read()` still returns a fresh live ride, or announce only after the restore decision (the first root/resumeIfNeeded result) says the ride was dropped.

verdicts.reason: The web flag `movera_search_live` is set on every live snapshot save (lib/features/ride_booking/data/ride_snapshot_store.dart:381, :462). It is cleared only by RideRestoreCoordinator.goHome (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:229) and UserDataWipe.run (user_data_wipe.dart:95). RideSnapshotStore.clear() (ride_snapshot_store.dart:512-519) does not clear it. When the session expires mid-ride, onSessionExpired (lib/app/di.dart:104-115) keeps the snapshot and shows Sign in without clearing the flag. If the same rider signs back in, UserDataWipe.run does not run (it runs only on a rider switch or sign-out, auth_controller.dart:59/107/118). enterMoveraApp (auth_navigation.dart:19-27) then mounts Home first. Home.initState -> _announceInterruptedSearch (home.dart:189-191) takes the flag and posts the 8 s 'search interrupted' toast. Only afterwards does resumeIfNeeded (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:560+, which awaits the session check, the snapshot read and a resync) swap the root to the live ride. The Home comment at home.dart:187-188 ('the web build's snapshot is gone before Flutter starts') is out of date: a cold start now restores from the snapshot. The _dropIfCancelQueued path (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:155-163) also clears the store and leaves the flag set, so Home shows the toast after the rider's own cancel went through.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: from the onSessionExpired callback (di.dart), through Sign in -> enterMoveraApp -> showMoveraRoot(Home) and Home.initState -> takeWebSearchInterrupted, to resumeIfNeeded and replaceRootSurface. Checked every writer and clearer of movera_search_live with a grep across lib. No guard skips the notice while a live snapshot exists.

verdicts.reason: Every live save sets the sessionStorage flag (ride_snapshot_store.dart:381, :462). Only RideRestoreCoordinator.goHome (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:229) and UserDataWipe.run (user_data_wipe.dart:95) clear it. RideSnapshotStore.clear (ride_snapshot_store.dart:512-519) and archiveCancelledThenClear do not. Path 1: the session expires mid-ride on web with authRequired. di.dart:104-115 keeps the snapshot and shows Sign in as the new root, so the old Home is disposed. The same rider signs back in, and enterSessionAs does not wipe because the fingerprint is unchanged. enterMoveraApp (auth_navigation.dart:19-27) mounts a new Home first. Its initState runs takeWebSearchInterrupted() (home.dart:190-191), which finds the flag and posts the 8 s 'search interrupted' toast. Only after that does resumeIfNeeded (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:560-603), after the session check, the reads and the resync, swap the root to the live Waiting/Finding page. Path 2: on a cold reload, _dropIfCancelQueued (:155-163) confirms the cancel and clears the store but leaves the flag set. _root then returns Home via pageFor(null) (:453), and the toast falsely says the search was interrupted. No guard checks the snapshot before announcing.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: the flag is set and cleared only in the places listed above. A VM test is not possible because takeWebSearchInterrupted has a non-web stub that returns false, and the sessionStorage version runs only in a web build. The comment at home.dart:187-189 ('the web build's snapshot is gone before Flutter starts') contradicts DECISIONS.md R-web, which removed the document-load wipe.

confirmed.title: Resume-recovery after a failed first fix tracks GPS but never draws the puck, never moves the camera and keeps 'Location off, set pickup'
confirmed.description: If the first detectCurrent() throws (the 16 s detectFixTimeout or a platform error), the controller state is temporarilyUnavailable and _runDetectCurrentAddress returns after setting _pickupAddress = locationOffPickupLabel. It never reaches _prepareLocationPuckIcons, bindLiveLocation or the camera move. On the next app resume Home calls _locationCtl.recoverLiveLocation(...), which only starts the position stream. Its onFix sets _currentLatLng and calls _updateLocationVisuals(), which returns early because _locationPuckCompact/_locationPuckExpanded are still null. _refreshPickupLabelIfMoved sees _pickupLabelAt == null, stores the fix and returns, so the label stays 'Location off, set pickup'. The pulse and compass are never started and the camera stays on the default Stockholm view.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the web, the first GPS fix takes longer than 16 s (indoors), then the rider switches tabs and comes back. The location stream now delivers fixes and the recenter button appears, but no rider puck is ever painted. The map stays on central Stockholm, and the pickup still reads 'Location off, set pickup' although location works.
confirmed.suggested_fix: On a recovered first fix, run the same first-fix work as _runDetectCurrentAddress: prepare the puck icons, bind pulse and heading, set the pickup label/_pickupLabelAt and do a follow camera move. Or simply call _detectCurrentAddress() when no fix has ever been bound.

verdicts.reason: If detectCurrent fails (16 s timeout or a platform error), the controller is left in temporarilyUnavailable (home_controller.dart:438-446). _runDetectCurrentAddress then returns at home.dart:365-370, before _prepareLocationPuckIcons (home.dart:379, its only caller), bindLiveLocation and animateCamera. On resume, didChangeAppLifecycleState (home.dart:256-265) calls recoverLiveLocation (home_controller.dart:766-773), which only runs startTracking. Its onFix sets _currentLatLng, but _updateLocationVisuals returns at home.dart:1572-1573 because both puck icons are null. _refreshPickupLabelIfMoved (home.dart:706-709) sees _pickupLabelAt == null, stores the fix and returns, so the 'Location off' label stays. The pulse timer is never started and no camera move happens. Because _currentLatLng is now non-null and the state turns live, the `else if (_currentLatLng == null) _detectCurrentAddress()` branch (home.dart:266-267) never runs on later resumes either. So the state never heals.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: detectCurrent catch -> _runDetectCurrentAddress early return -> lifecycle resume -> recoverLiveLocation -> startTracking -> _deliverFix -> onFix -> _updateLocationVisuals (icon == null) and _refreshPickupLabelIfMoved (at == null). A grep confirms _prepareLocationPuckIcons has one caller, at home.dart:379.

verdicts.reason: _prepareLocationPuckIcons is called only from the success path (home.dart:379). After the first detectCurrent fails, the controller is in temporarilyUnavailable. On app resume, home.dart:256-265 calls recoverLiveLocation, which only runs startTracking (home_controller.dart:766-773). Its onFix sets _currentLatLng and calls _updateLocationVisuals, which returns early because the icons are null (home.dart:1572-1573). _refreshPickupLabelIfMoved stores _pickupLabelAt the first time and returns (home.dart:707-709), so the pickup label is never set again. No camera move is made. The recenter button appears because _currentLatLng is now set (home.dart:1943), but pressing it also goes through _updateLocationVisuals, so the puck is still not painted.
verdicts.repro: I wrote test/_audit_u118_test.dart, which pumps the real Home with a fake GeolocatorPlatform (services on, whileInUse permission, getCurrentPosition never completes). I advanced 20 s, sent app lifecycle paused then resumed, and emitted two stream fixes. Output: 'after resume: state=recovering streams=1' and then 'after fixes: state=HomeLocationState.live markers=0'. As a control, the same test with getCurrentPosition succeeding printed 'after fixes: state=HomeLocationState.live markers=1'. Both files were deleted.

confirmed.title: When the first GPS fix on Home times out, no position stream starts, no notice or retry is shown, and the puck stays missing until the app is resumed or a booking starts
confirmed.description: HomeLocationController.detectCurrent times out after 16 s (detectFixTimeout). It then catches the error, sets state temporarilyUnavailable and returns target null (home_controller.dart:438-446). _runDetectCurrentAddress then writes the 'Location off, set pickup' label and returns, so bindLiveLocation/startTracking never runs and no position stream exists. accessIssue maps only servicesDisabled and permissionRequired to a notice, so temporarilyUnavailable shows no notice and no Try again button. Nothing schedules a retry. The only recovery is an app pause/resume (didChangeAppLifecycleState → recoverLiveLocation) or a booking action that calls _awaitCurrentFix.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An Android rider opens the app indoors with location permitted and services on. The high-accuracy cold fix takes longer than 16 s. Home keeps the default map with no puck and the pickup label 'Location off, set pickup', and offers no retry. The puck never appears while the rider stays on Home, even after the GPS gets a fix seconds later, until the app is backgrounded or the rider starts a booking.
confirmed.evidence:
home_controller.dart:438-445 `} catch (_) { _setState(HomeLocationState.temporarilyUnavailable); return const DetectedLocation(target: null, address: locationOffPickupLabel, ... failure: HomeLocationFailure.unavailable);`
home.dart:365-370 `if (detected.denied || target == null) { ... setState(() => _pickupAddress = locationOffPickupLabel); } return; }`
home_controller.dart:303-310 `accessIssue => switch (state) { servicesDisabled => ..., permissionRequired => ..., _ => null }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: On an 'unavailable' result, start the position stream anyway (startTracking has its own resubscribe backoff), or schedule detectCurrent again. Do not label a timeout as 'Location off'.

verdicts.reason: On timeout, detectCurrent returns target null with failure 'unavailable' and state temporarilyUnavailable (home_controller.dart:438-446). _runDetectCurrentAddress writes locationOffPickupLabel and returns (home.dart:365-370), so no position stream or retry timer is started. accessIssue (home_controller.dart:303-310), the only input to HomeLocationNotice (widgets/home_location_notice.dart:35), maps temporarilyUnavailable to null, so no notice and no retry button appear. The recenter button needs _currentLatLng != null (home.dart:1943). _detectCurrentAddress has only three callers (home.dart:267 lifecycle, 294 initState, 346 _awaitCurrentFix in booking). verdicts.repro: Static trace of every _detectCurrentAddress caller and every HomeLocationState.temporarilyUnavailable reference in lib. Confirmed that nothing reschedules detection and no UI offers a retry in that state.

confirmed.title: Late first GPS fix glides whichever map is on top (pickup / Set pickup / Select ride), not Home's
confirmed.description: _runDetectCurrentAddress ends with `AppScope.instance.maps.animateCamera(target, zoom: homeOpeningZoom, follow: true)` with no check that Home's map is the active owner. While Home is parked (NAV-3 or _withParkedHomeMap) its controller is detached (home.dart:233) and GoogleMapProvider.controller returns `_owners.last.controller` (google_map_provider.dart:24-25), i.e. the map of ConfirmPickupSpot (owner 'pickup', confirm_pickup_spot.dart:333), SetPickupPage (set_pickup_page.dart:870) or SelectRide. _mayMove(map, follow:true) only checks heldByRider (google_map_provider.dart:79-85), so the booking screen's camera eases to the rider's GPS point at zoom 11.7. The sibling path _centerCameraOnQuickFix explicitly guards `if (maps.activeOwner != MapOwners.home) return;` (home.dart:312), showing this guard was intended. detectCurrent can take up to 16 s (detectFixTimeout) while _awaitCurrentFix gives up after 8 s and the flow continues with the fallback pickup, so the fix routinely lands after the rider is on a map screen.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Cold start on web/Safari, slow first fix. Rider taps Where to, picks a destination; _awaitCurrentFix times out at 8 s, SelectRide opens, rider taps Book, Set pickup opens with the fallback pin. At ~12 s the fix lands: Set pickup's camera glides to the GPS point at city zoom 11.7; onCameraMove recomputes _center, _onCameraIdle sets _routeStart/_usable=true, re-resolves the address and re-quotes. The pickup silently moved under the rider; in ConfirmPickupSpot the pin likewise jumps and the shown address changes.

home.dart:395-399 `await AppScope.instance.maps.animateCamera(GeoPoint(target.latitude, target.longitude), zoom: homeOpeningZoom, follow: true);`
home.dart:311-312 `// Map not created yet: onMapCreated picks the hint up.` / `if (maps.activeOwner != MapOwners.home) return;` (quick fix is guarded, accurate fix is not)
google_map_provider.dart:24-25 `GoogleMapController? get controller => _owners.isEmpty ? null : _owners.last.controller;`
google_map_provider.dart:81 `if (follow) return !view.heldByRider;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _runDetectCurrentAddress skip the animateCamera when `_mapParked.value || AppScope.instance.maps.activeOwner != MapOwners.home` (onMapCreated already re-centres from _currentLatLng when Home's map comes back).

confirmed.title: A failed forward geocode after the route picker closes, or when a saved place is tapped, aborts the flow silently with an unhandled async error
confirmed.description: After RoutePickerPage pops with a draft, _showRouteAddressPicker runs `Future.wait([_normaliseAddress(rawPickup...), _normaliseAddress(rawDestination...), ...])`. HomeLocationController.normaliseAddress calls `geocoding.forward(clean)` with no try/catch (home_controller.dart:258); AppGeocoding._forwardFromApi does `api.post(...).timeout(requestTimeout)` and ApiClient._send throws ApiError on HTTP >= 400, NETWORK and TIMEOUT (api_client.dart:98, 123, 131). The exception propagates through _handleDestinationTap -> _runRouteFlow (finally only resets the flag) -> WhereToCard.onTap, which is a VoidCallback, so it becomes an unhandled zone error. Nothing is shown to the rider, nothing is persisted and SelectRide never opens. The picker itself catches onFinish failures (route_picker_page.dart:408-411) but this post-pop step does not. Same unguarded pattern: _useSavedPlaceAsDestination (home.dart:545), _saveAddressFor (home.dart:469, 477), PickupMapController.search used by ConfirmPickupSpot._lookup (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:286) and SetPickupPage._searchAddress (set_pickup_page.dart:702).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider is offline or the geocode endpoint times out. They pick pickup and destination in the route picker (onFinish succeeds because resolvePlace is cached or the point came with the suggestion), the picker closes, the forward geocode of the raw strings throws, the flow aborts: Home shows the old sheet, no error, no SelectRide, Recents not updated. Tapping a saved place (Home/Work card) while offline likewise does nothing.

home.dart:952-959 `final normaliseBatch = _locationCtl.beginNormalisationBatch(); final normalizedRoute = await Future.wait<String>([ _normaliseAddress(rawPickup, generation: normaliseBatch), ...`
home_controller.dart:258 `final result = await geocoding.forward(clean);` (no try/catch)
api_client.dart:122-123 `if (response.statusCode >= 400) { throw _errorFromResponse(response, requestId); }` and :131 `throw ApiError(code: 'TIMEOUT', ...)`
where_to_card.dart:25 `final VoidCallback onDestinationTap;` (future dropped)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the post-pop normalisation (and the saved-place / favourite / pickup-search paths) in try/catch; on failure fall back to the raw strings (the draft already carries pickupLat/Lng and destinationLat/Lng) or show homeChooseValidRoute / routeCouldNotReach, instead of letting the exception escape.

verdicts.reason: _showRouteAddressPicker awaits Future.wait of _normaliseAddress calls (home.dart:953-960). _normaliseAddress has no try/catch (home.dart:433-435), and neither does HomeLocationController.normaliseAddress (home_controller.dart:253-262). A pickup or destination that arrived with a point never went through forward() inside onFinish (home.dart:784-788, 841), so it is not in the cache and the post-pop call goes to the network. The saved-place path (home.dart:545) fails the same way. The demo's in-process mock always answers a non-empty query (in_process_mock_client.dart:337-360), so this only happens against a real server. confirmed.title: Confirm tapped while the map is still gliding books the new pin point with the previous street and the previous fare
confirmed.description: onCameraMove updates _center continuously, but _addressIsStale, the resolve and the requote are only started in _onCameraIdle. If Confirm is tapped after the finger lifts but before the camera settles (a fling's deceleration), _resolving and _requoting are both false, so nothing is awaited. _addressIsStale is still false, so the address booked is the old street, and fareTotalKr is the old pin's fare, while position is the new _center. The method's own contract (RIDE-12) says the street and the fare confirmed are the pin's own.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider flings the map 400 m up the street and taps 'Confirm and search' while it is still sliding. The ride is booked at the new point but labelled with the original street ('Drottninggatan 5'), and SetPickupResult.fareTotalKr is the old pin's price. The driver is sent to the wrong-named address and the price-change check compares against the wrong total.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _confirm, treat _moving (or _isAwayFrom(_center, _routeStart)) as pending: mark the address stale and wait for the next idle, resolve and requote. Or disable Confirm while the camera moves.

verdicts.reason: onCameraMove (set_pickup_page.dart:873-881) updates _center on every frame of a fling, but only _onCameraIdle (:489-506) sets _addressIsStale, _resolving and _requoting. _confirm (:730-768) waits only when _resolving or _requoting is already true (:735-738). Nothing in _confirm or _confirmButton (:1446-1452, enabled whenever _usable) checks _moving. A tap on Confirm in the sheet does not stop the fling. So during the deceleration window, position=_center (the new point) is booked with confirmedPickupAddress(_address, ...) for the old street and _fare.totalKr for the old pin. That contradicts the method's own RIDE-12 comment.

confirmed.title: A 422 from the profile PATCH is treated as 'pending, retry later', so an over-long name blocks every later profile sync while the UI shows success
confirmed.description: _sync catches every error, sets `_syncPending = true` and returns normally. A permanent 422 invalid_profile (the contract and mock reject names over 80 characters) therefore looks the same as a network failure. Every later save resends the same cached invalid name and fails again, so no consent or language change reaches the server. Callers are never told: PersonalInfoPage._save only shows saveFailed when update() throws, and it never throws for this. The name editor (showAccountTextEditor) has no length limit, and RiderNameScreen allows 40 + 1 + 40 = 81 characters. A throwaway run with an 81-character name showed `thrown=null pending=true server=null`. A later consent change gave `pending=true server=null`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rider enters a long full name (over 80 characters) in Personal info. The tile shows the new name and no error appears. The server never gets it, and from then on every privacy or language change fails silently, so the server keeps stale consents.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mark only network/5xx/timeout errors as pending. Rethrow 4xx (422) errors so the screen can show them, and limit the name field to the contract's 80 characters.

verdicts.reason: _sync (synced_profile_repository.dart:70-82) catches every error, including the permanent 422 invalid_profile the mock returns for names over 80 characters (in_process_mock_client.dart:1135-1139, docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:55). It sets _syncPending = true and never rethrows. save() then returns normally, so PersonalInfoPage._save (personal_info.dart:54-61) never shows saveFailed. showAccountTextEditor (account_widgets.dart:300-366) has no maxLength or formatter, so an 81+ character name is accepted. Every later save resends the same cached invalid name and gets 422 again, so no consent or language change reaches the server. Nothing in lib reads syncPending, so the rider is never told.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: the name editor has no length limit, the personal_info.dart:118-128 path leads to _save, then update, then save, then _sync, and the catch-all at lines 78-81 swallows the 422. Grep for 'syncPending' outside the repository finds no readers.

confirmed.title: Leaving Delete account during the in-flight request signs the rider out and wipes the device, but never routes to Sign in
confirmed.description: While `_sending`, the main Delete account view has no PopScope, and its AccountScaffold back button calls Navigator.pop. If the rider leaves during the request, AccountDeletionController.requestDeletion still completes: it calls signOutLocally, which clears the tokens and runs UserDataWipe. Then `if (!mounted) return;` skips everything, including the _sentView whose Done and back buttons are the only way to reach showSignInRoot. The rider is left on Account/Home with no session and wiped data. In release builds every API call then fails without a token (no 401 refresh path, because there is no access token), and no Sign in screen appears until a cold start.

The server accepts with 202: tokens are cleared and local data wiped, but the rider stays on Account and Home looking signed in. Booking or loading anything fails with errors, and Sign in only appears after the app is restarted.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Block pop while _sending, or call showSignInRoot from the controller path when the page is no longer mounted (the root navigator is available through moveraNavigatorKey).

confirmed.title: Privacy switches build the next profile from a stale copy and do not move until the PATCH returns, so a second toggle reverts the first one locally and on the server
confirmed.description: Each Switch's onChanged calls `_profile.update(ride.copyWith(...))`, where `ride` was captured at build time. ProfileController.update calls notifyListeners only after `_store.save(next)` returns. SyncedProfileRepository.save awaits the network PATCH (`await _sync(saved)`, up to the 15 s ApiClient timeout) before returning. So during the round trip the page does not rebuild: the tapped switch still shows its old value, and `ride` is still the old profile. If the rider taps another switch in that window, the new profile is built from the stale `ride` and overwrites the first change, both in the cache and in a second PATCH. This was reproduced with InProcessMockClient(latency: 2s): after tapping Offers, the switch still showed false while the model was true. Tapping Email then left promotions=false, both locally and on the server.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a slow connection the rider turns Offers on. The switch stays off, so they turn Email updates off as well. Offers ends up off on the device and on the server, although the rider turned it on.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Notify listeners right after the cache write, before the network sync. Build each change from `_profile.profile` read at tap time, not from the build-time copy.

verdicts.reason: privacy.dart:41 captures `ride = _profile.profile` at build time, and every onChanged (lines 97-98, 115-116, 134-135) builds the next profile from that copy. ProfileController.update (profile_controller.dart:30-33) calls notifyListeners only after `_store.save` returns. The real store from di.dart:181 is SyncedProfileRepository, and its save (synced_profile_repository.dart:54-57) awaits the network PATCH in `_sync` before returning. So the page does not rebuild until the PATCH comes back: the switch keeps showing its old value and `ride` stays stale. A second toggle in that window is built from the stale copy, which overwrites the first change in the cache and sends a second PATCH that reverts it on the server. Nothing guards against this: there is no optimistic notify, no read of the current profile at tap time, and no serialisation of saves.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of privacy.dart -> ProfileController.update -> SyncedProfileRepository.save/_sync -> ApiClient.patch. The reporter's run with InProcessMockClient(latency: 2s) matches this code path (switch shown=false, model=true, final promotions=false). I did not rerun it.

So the page does not rebuild until the network replies. A second tap in that window builds from the stale `ride` and overwrites the first change, both in the cache and in a second PATCH. File deleted.

confirmed.title: Zone wall-clock pickup time is stored as a device-local DateTime and compared with DateTime.now()
confirmed.description: Q9 makes every Book-later time the pickup zone's wall-clock time: `ZoneClock.wallTime` returns a plain local `DateTime(local.year, …)` (zone_clock.dart:57-69) and `PickupSchedule` works in those (stockholm_schedule.dart:105-121). The picker returns that wall-clock value (select_date_time.dart:131, 153-158) and it flows unchanged into `ReservationDraft.scheduledPickupAt` (scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:21-32). The backend path converts it to a UTC instant (`PickupSchedule(timezone).toUtc(at)`, scheduled_rides_controller.dart:63-64), but the local reservation path never does: `startLiveIfDue` computes `ride.scheduledPickupAt.difference(currentTime)` with `currentTime = DateTime.now()` (334, 329), the chrono counts down with `DateTime.now()` (home_reservation_chrono.dart:206, 242-249; reservation_format.dart:99,117), `isNoDriverFound` (313-316) and the cancel-fee window (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:93-103) do the same. Whenever the device time zone differs from the pickup zone's (any browser outside CET on the public web build; a Stockholm phone booking a Tunis pickup in summer; a traveller abroad), every one of these is off by the offset. Throwaway test in this UTC container: minimumPickup() for 10:00Z gives wall-clock 12:30 (local, isUtc=false); `pickup.difference(now)` = 2:30:00 and the chrono label reads `2h 30m` for a ride 30 minutes away.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Web rider with browser in UTC (or a Stockholm phone in Tunis zone in summer) books a Stockholm pickup for 12:30 local (30 min ahead). Home chrono shows 2 h 30 m; `startLiveIfDue` reaches T-2 two hours after the real pickup; "No driver found" fires two hours late; free-cancel window shown/charged against the wrong instant.
confirmed.evidence:
zone_clock.dart:57-69 `static DateTime wallTime(...) { ... return DateTime(local.year, local.month, local.day, local.hour, ...); }`
select_date_time.dart:131 `Navigator.pop(context, _selectedDateTime);`
scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:31 `scheduledPickupAt: when,`
reservation_controller.dart:329-334 `final currentTime = now ?? _clock(); ... final untilPickup = ride.scheduledPickupAt.difference(currentTime);`
home_reservation_chrono.dart:206 `DateTime get _now => widget.now?.call() ?? DateTime.now();`
scheduled_rides_controller.dart:63-64 `scheduledAt: switch (scheduledAt) { final at? => WireTime.format(PickupSchedule(timezone).toUtc(at)), ... }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Convert the picked wall-clock time to an instant (`PickupSchedule(timeZone).toUtc(when)`) before building the ReservationDraft, and render it back with `ZoneClock.wallTime` in the reservation screens; or store the IANA zone with the reservation and use it in every comparison.

verdicts.reason: PickupSchedule works in zone wall-clock values. zoneNow returns ZoneClock.wallTime, a plain local DateTime (zone_clock.dart:57-69; stockholm_schedule.dart:29-35). The picker returns that value (select_date_time.dart:131), and it goes unchanged into ReservationDraft.scheduledPickupAt (scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:21-31) and into ReservationPatch on edit (scheduled_ride_booking.dart:62-65). Nothing in the reservation path calls toUtc or PickupSchedule.toUtc. The only conversion is on the backend path, as the finding says. The stored value is then compared with the device clock in three places: startLiveIfDue (reservation_controller.dart:329,334), isNoDriverFound (:313-316) and the home chrono (DateTime.now()). LocalReservationRepository is the live store whenever scheduledRides/bookingLater is on or the build is not release (di.dart:143-146). So any device whose time zone differs from the pickup zone gets the T-2 start, the no-driver timeout, the countdown and the cancel window all off by the offset difference. Q9 makes pickup-zone wall time the intended display and input format, but it does not make the comparison against device-local now correct.

confirmed.title: Queued dispatch/lifecycle writes resurrect a ride the rider just cancelled (no status check inside the serialized change)
confirmed.description: `_oneAtATime` serializes changes, but each change re-applies a status decided from an older snapshot. `startLiveIfDue` picks `ride` from `upcoming()` before its awaits, then calls `_store.assignDriver(id)` (→ driverAssignmentPending/driverAssigned) or `_store.updateReservation(... driverEnRoute)`. The mock trip's writeStep checks `current.status != from` synchronously and then queues `update(id, ReservationPatch(status: to))`. If a rider cancel is already queued in `_oneAtATime` (its prefs write in flight), these later changes run after it. Neither `assignDriver` nor `updateReservation` checks that the ride is still upcoming, so a cancelled ride gets its status overwritten. `cancellationActor`, `cancelledAt` and `cancellationFee` stay set.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the live scheduled ride the rider taps Cancel at the moment the 20 s 'arrived' timer fires. writeStep sees driverEnRoute (the cancel is not committed yet) and queues driverEnRoute→driverArrived behind the cancel. The cancel commits, then the update sets driverArrived. The ride is 'upcoming' again, the trip continues to completed, and the rider was already sent Home.
confirmed.evidence:
local_reservation_repository.dart:266-287 `final current = _require(reservationId); ... : current.copyWith(status: ReservationStatus.driverAssigned, driver: driver, ...); await _commit(...)` (no isUpcoming check); :193-214 updateReservation likewise.
reservation_controller.dart:405-408 `if (current == null || current.status != from || current.driver == null) { return false; } await update(id, ReservationPatch(status: to));`
reservation_controller.dart:375-378 `if (ride.status == ReservationStatus.scheduled) { await _store.assignDriver(ride.reservationId);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Inside the serialized change, re-check the current status (e.g. assignDriver/updateReservation status patches refuse when `!current.status.isUpcoming`, or take an expected `from` status) and return the current record unchanged.

verdicts.reason: local_reservation_repository.dart:134-141 `_commit` awaits `_storage.write` before it updates `_items`. So while a cancel's prefs write is in flight, `byId` still returns the old status. The writeStep guard at reservation_controller.dart:405-408 passes, and `update(id, ReservationPatch(status: to))` is queued behind the cancel in `_oneAtATime`. `updateReservation` (:193-214) and `assignDriver` (:262-288) re-read `current` but never check `current.status.isUpcoming`, so the queued write replaces `cancelled` with `driverArrived`. `cancellationActor` and the other cancel fields stay set. `startLiveIfDue` (:332-394) has the same problem: it works from the `upcoming()` list it took before its awaits. The window lasts only as long as one prefs write, so this is a timing race.
