Set the ride to driverEnRoute, started `cancel()` without awaiting it, read `byId()` (the writeStep check), then called `update(status: driverArrived)` and released the write. Output: `seed=ReservationStatus.driverEnRoute final=ReservationStatus.driverArrived actor=TripCancellationActor.rider` (+1 All tests passed). File deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: The status check is done outside the serialized change. writeStep reads `byId(id)` (reservation_controller.dart:402-405), and that comes from `_store.cached`, which `_commit` only updates after `_storage.write` finishes (local_reservation_repository.dart:137-144). So while a cancel's write is in flight, the ride still reads driverEnRoute. The update then queues behind the cancel in `_oneAtATime` (:123-131). `updateReservation` (:193-216) re-applies `status` without checking `current.status.isUpcoming`, so the cancelled ride becomes driverArrived. `cancellationActor` and `cancelledAt` stay set. Only demo/dev/test builds have the mock dispatch (reservation_dispatch.dart:11-15), and the window is the length of one prefs write, so this is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_v159x_test.dart (now deleted). It used a demo AppEnv, a capturing ReservationDispatch, and a MemoryReservationStorage subclass whose write waits on a Completer. Steps: ride set to driverEnRoute with a driver, then startLiveIfDue, then the write gate is closed, then c.cancel(id), then the captured writeStep(driverEnRoute, driverArrived), then the gate is opened. confirmed.title: Pickup and creation times are persisted as offset-less local ISO strings, so a device time-zone change moves the booked pickup instant
confirmed.original_title: Pickup and creation times are persisted as offset-less local ISO strings, so a device time-zone change moves the booked pickup instant
confirmed.description: toJson writes scheduledPickupAt, createdAt and estimatedDropoffAt with DateTime.toIso8601String(). For a local DateTime (what the booking flow passes) that gives '2026-10-22T10:00:00.000' with no offset. tryParse (DateTime.tryParse) reads it back as local time in whatever zone the device is in at hydrate. cancelledAt is stored as UTC (local_reservation_repository.dart:232), so only some timestamps keep their instant. This is the persistence side, separate from the known zone wall-clock construction issue at line 334: even a booking made correctly in the device zone changes instant after a zone change and an app restart. ARCHITECTURE.md names WireTime (RFC 3339 UTC) as the time contract.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In Stockholm (UTC+2) the rider books 10:00 tomorrow, stored as '...T10:00:00.000' (08:00Z). They fly to London (UTC+1) and relaunch. Hydrate parses 10:00 London time = 09:00Z. The chrono counts down to a pickup an hour late, startLiveIfDue starts assignment and en-route an hour late, and the free-cancel window and fee are worked out against the wrong instant.
confirmed.evidence:
reservation.dart:368-371:
  'createdAt': createdAt.toIso8601String(),
  'scheduledPickupAt': scheduledPickupAt.toIso8601String(),
  if (estimatedDropoffAt != null) 'estimatedDropoffAt': estimatedDropoffAt!.toIso8601String(),
reservation.dart:407-410: DateTime.tryParse(map['createdAt'] ...), DateTime.tryParse(map['scheduledPickupAt'] ...)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Serialize with toUtc().toIso8601String() (WireTime) and convert to local only for display.

verdicts.reason: The pickup time is a local DateTime. select_date_time.dart:284 and :443 build it with `DateTime(...)` and scheduleFor passes it on (select_ride.dart:952, ride_selection_controller.dart:620). It reaches the repository unchanged (local_reservation_repository.dart:167). toJson (reservation.dart:368-371) writes toIso8601String() with no offset, and tryParse (reservation.dart:407-410) reads it back as local time in the device zone at hydrate. No toUtc() is applied on the write path, while cancelledAt is stored as UTC (local_reservation_repository.dart:232). ARCHITECTURE.md:83 names WireTime (RFC 3339 UTC) as the contract. Nothing in DECISIONS.md makes local storage intentional. A device zone change followed by a restart moves the stored instant, and isNoDriverFound and startLiveIfDue (reservation_controller.dart:306-372) then use the shifted time. It needs a device time-zone change, so it is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Read-only static trace of the booking path from the date picker to the repository, then toJson and tryParse. Worked by hand: '2026-10-22T10:00:00.000' stored at UTC+2 (08:00Z) and parsed at UTC+1 gives 09:00Z.

verdicts.reason: reservation.dart:368-371 serialises createdAt, scheduledPickupAt and estimatedDropoffAt with toIso8601String(). For a local (non-UTC) DateTime, Dart writes no offset or Z. tryParse at reservation.dart:407-410 uses DateTime.tryParse, which reads an offset-less string as local time in the device's zone at hydrate time. cancelledAt, by contrast, is written as UTC (local_reservation_repository.dart:232). Every check that uses the instant (isNoDriverFound at reservation_controller.dart:306-316, startLiveIfDue's untilPickup at :334, the chrono countdown) compares against DateTime.now(), so after a zone change and an app restart the pickup instant moves by the offset difference. ARCHITECTURE.md:83 names WireTime (RFC 3339 UTC) as the contract, and DECISIONS.md does not exempt this. It only happens when a rider with a pending booking changes zone and restarts, so I rate it an edge path (medium).
verdicts.repro: Read only, no run. Dart semantics: DateTime(2026,10,22,10).toIso8601String() gives '2026-10-22T10:00:00.000' with no Z. DateTime.parse of that string in Europe/London (UTC+1 on 22 Oct) gives 09:00Z, versus 08:00Z when written in Stockholm (UTC+2): a shift of one hour.

confirmed.description: The Upcoming page computes the terms and passes the agreed fee: `cancelTermsFor(ride)` then `_reservations.cancel(id, reason:, fee: terms.fee)` (upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142). The two other cancel entry points for the same reservation never pass a fee: `ReservationLiveRide.onCancel` calls `reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: reasonId ?? 'rider_cancelled_live')` (78-85) and `ReservationRideRealtime.cancelRide` does the same (reservation_ride_realtime.dart:255-265). The live screen is exactly where the rider is once the driver is en route (T-2 min, `startLiveIfDue` 383-394 + chrono `_openLiveIfNeeded`), i.e. inside the late-cancel window the rules define (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:86-118, default 60 min / 50 kr). The cancelled ride is then saved with `cancellationFee == null`, History shows plain "Cancelled" (reservation_format.dart:27-33) and no fee is recorded, while the same cancel five minutes earlier from the Upcoming page records 50 kr.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rules: free until 60 min before pickup, 50 kr after. Rider lets the driver start (T-2), the live screen opens, taps Cancel: the ride is cancelled with no fee recorded; History and the receipt show no fee, contradicting the terms the rider was shown.

reservation_live_ride.dart:78-82 `onCancel: (context, reasonId) async { await reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: reasonId ?? 'rider_cancelled_live'); ...`
reservation_ride_realtime.dart:259-263 `unawaited(controller.cancel(reservationId, reason: 'rider_cancelled_live'));`
upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142 `final terms = _reservations.cancelTermsFor(ride); ... await _reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: outcome.reasonId, fee: terms.fee);`

verdicts.corrected_title: Cancelling a reservation from its live screen skips the reservation late-cancel terms, so no fee is recorded
verdicts.reason: The Upcoming page computes the terms and passes them on: cancelTermsFor, then cancel(..., fee: terms.fee) (upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142). The live-screen handler only calls reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: reasonId ?? 'rider_cancelled_live') (reservation_live_ride.dart:78-82), with no fee. ReservationController.cancel (reservation_controller.dart:208-235) does not compute a fee itself, and LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation (local_reservation_repository.dart:220-237) stores cancellationFee: null when no fee is passed. The live sheet's fee note comes from the Book Now live rules (waiting_for_driver.dart:765-799, LiveCancelFeePreview), not from the reservation terms. Per API_V1_MOCK.md:76 the late-cancel fee is only recorded on the device copy and charged nowhere yet. So the effect is a wrong or missing fee record and receipt, not money actually taken, which is why this is medium.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: ReservationLiveRide -> WaitingForDriver(onCancel) -> _confirmCancel (waiting_for_driver.dart:802-830) -> customCancel -> ReservationController.cancel(fee: null) -> LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation. Compared this with upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142 and the scheduled terms in contracts/CONTRACT.md:133. I did not run a test.

verdicts.corrected_title: Cancelling a reservation from the live (driver en route) screen records no late-cancel fee, while the same cancel from Upcoming records the rule's fee
verdicts.reason: ReservationLiveRide.onCancel (reservation_live_ride.dart:78-82) and ReservationRideRealtime.cancelRide (reservation_ride_realtime.dart:141-150) call reservations.cancel without `fee`. LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation then stores cancellationFee=null (local_reservation_repository.dart:220-235). UpcomingReservation._cancel computes cancelTermsFor and passes terms.fee (upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142). The live screen opens when the driver is en route, around T-2 min, which is inside the default 60-minute window. There, cancelTermsFor works out a positive fee (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:86-118): minutesBeforePickup=2 < freeMin=60 gives 5000 minor (50 kr), and missedByMovera is false because a driver is assigned. confirmed.title: Cancel confirmed on a stale ride overwrites a ride that already went live or completed, and records a late fee
confirmed.description: `_cancel(ride)` uses the `ride` captured at build time and works out `terms` before the two cancel sheets open. After the sheets it calls `_reservations.cancel(...)` without re-reading the ride or checking `status.canCancel`. `LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation` has no status guard either: it always sets `status: cancelled`, `cancellationActor: rider`, `cancelledAt` and the fee. While the sheets are open, the Home chrono tick keeps running `startLiveIfDue`, which moves the ride driverAssigned → driverEnRoute, and the mock trip then runs to completed in about 46 s. `_handoffIfLive` does not fire because the page route is not current while a sheet is up.
confirmed.failure_scenario: At 23:47 the rider opens Cancel on the 23:50 ride and lingers on the reason sheet. At 23:48 the ride goes en route, and about 46 s later it is completed. The rider then taps a reason. The completed ride is rewritten as cancelled by the rider with a 'Cancelled · fee kr 50' chip. It moves from History › Completed to Cancelled, and a fee is recorded for a trip that was delivered.
confirmed.evidence:
upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142 `final terms = _reservations.cancelTermsFor(ride); final outcome = await showCancelReservationFlow(context, ride, terms: terms); if (!outcome.cancelled) return; await _reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: outcome.reasonId, fee: terms.fee);`
local_reservation_repository.dart:227-234 `final current = _require(reservationId); final next = current.copyWith(status: ReservationStatus.cancelled, ... cancellationFee: fee != null && fee.isPositive ? fee : null);`

verdicts.reason: upcoming_reservation.dart:125-143 awaits showCancelReservationFlow and then calls _reservations.cancel without re-reading the ride or checking status.canCancel. ReservationController.cancel/_cancelNow (reservation_controller.dart:208-235) and LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation (local_reservation_repository.dart:220-236) also have no status guard: they always write status cancelled with actor rider and the fee. While the sheet is up, Home's 30 s timer keeps running (home_reservation_chrono.dart:65-73 -> startLiveIfDue) and moves driverAssigned to driverEnRoute (reservation_controller.dart ~392-402). _driveMockTrip then runs the trip forward (mock_reservation_dispatch.dart: arrive 20 s + board 8 s + trip 18 s) to completed. The page's _handoffIfLive is blocked by !_routeIsCurrent while the sheet route is on top. The guard in _driveMockTrip only protects the simulation from overwriting a cancellation, not the other way round. A completed ride is therefore rewritten as cancelled by the rider with a late fee. This needs the demo mock dispatch and a rider who keeps the sheet open for about a minute, so it is an edge path.

No status re-check exists anywhere between the sheet closing and _commit.

ReservationController.cancel/_cancelNow (reservation_controller.dart:208-233) and LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation (local_reservation_repository.dart:225-238) have no canCancel or status check: they always write cancelled, actor rider and the fee. While the sheets are open, HomeReservationChrono's 30 s Timer.periodic (home_reservation_chrono.dart:63-73) keeps calling startLiveIfDue. That moves driverAssigned to driverEnRoute inside 2 minutes of pickup (reservation_controller.dart:383-392), and the mock trip then steps en route -> arrived -> inProgress -> completed after 20+8+18 = 46 s (mock_reservation_dispatch.dart:26-28, 112-139). _driveMockTrip stops only when the status changed under it, not the other way round. The page's _handoffIfLive is skipped while a sheet is up, because !_routeIsCurrent (upcoming_reservation.dart:67, 83). A completed ride is therefore rewritten as cancelled by the rider, with the late fee.

confirmed.title: Cold start of a signed-in rider with no local ride waits up to about 30 s on GET /rider/trips/active, showing a blank white screen
confirmed.description: _root() returns `pageFor(snapshot ?? await adoptServerActiveTrip())`, so with no local snapshot (the normal case) the root page waits for ApiActiveTripRepository.fetchActive(). That call goes through ApiClient.get → _getWithRetry: a 15 s timeout, retried once on timeout, plus a refresh round trip on a 401. Until it resolves, RideRestoreGate renders `_child ?? ColoredBox(white)`, and bootstrap has already dismissed the web splash on the first frame. adoptServerActiveTrip catches the eventual error, so the app does open on Home in the end, but only after the full timeout. Server-backed builds (staging/production) compose ApiActiveTripRepository.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A signed-in rider opens the production app on a poor or captive network where the connection hangs instead of failing at once. They stare at a blank white screen for about 30 s before Home appears. With a 401 refresh in between it takes even longer. Nothing says the app is working, and an Active trip is not needed to show Home.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:453 `return pageFor(snapshot ?? await adoptServerActiveTrip());`
api_client.dart:273-279 `for (var attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) { try { return await _client.get(uri, headers: headers).timeout(_timeout); } on TimeoutException ...`
ride_restore_gate.dart:80-82 `final child = _child ?? const ColoredBox(color: Color(0xFFFFFFFF), child: SizedBox.expand());`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Render Home immediately and adopt the server trip in the background (replace the root if one comes back), or give the cold-start lookup a short deadline.

verdicts.reason: In release builds di.dart:155 composes ApiActiveTripRepository. With defaultSkipRestore() returning false (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:225) and no local snapshot, _root() blocks on `pageFor(snapshot ?? await adoptServerActiveTrip())` (:453). That reaches ApiClient.get -> _request -> _getWithRetry (api_client.dart:146, 268-280), which runs two attempts with a 15 s timeout each (:42, :275). adoptServerActiveTrip (:78-99) has no deadline of its own and only catches the error after the timeouts run out. Until root() resolves, RideRestoreGate shows the bare white ColoredBox (ride_restore_gate build). Bootstrap removes the web splash on the first frame (bootstrap.dart:141-147), so nothing hides the blank page. docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:103 says release builds ask this route on cold start, but no document says cold start should wait on it with nothing shown. The only short deadline in the class is queuedCancelWait (4 s), and it covers queued cancels only.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: gate initState -> RideRestoreCoordinator.root() -> _root() line 453 -> adoptServerActiveTrip -> _serverActiveTrip -> AppScope.activeTrips.fetchActive -> ApiClient.get -> _getWithRetry (2 x 15 s). Checked _skipRestore, _shouldRequireSignIn and authPreview: none of them bypasses this path for a signed-in release rider.

verdicts.reason: ride_restore_coordinator.dart:453 awaits adoptServerActiveTrip() before root() returns whenever there is no local snapshot. In release builds di.dart:155 uses ApiActiveTripRepository, whose fetchActive goes through ApiClient GET, which ends in _getWithRetry (api_client.dart:268-280): a 15 s timeout (api_client.dart:42), retried once, so up to 30 s on a hanging connection. Until then RideRestoreGate.build (ride_restore_gate.dart:80-82) draws a plain white ColoredBox, and bootstrap.dart:146 has already dismissed the web splash. adoptServerActiveTrip:93-99 catches the TimeoutException and returns null, so Home does appear, but only after the full wait. Nothing in DECISIONS.md or ARCHITECTURE.md calls this hold intentional. The trigger is an edge case: the network has to hang rather than fail fast.
verdicts.repro: Traced the code by hand. With no local snapshot, root() -> _root() -> pageFor(await adoptServerActiveTrip()) -> fetchActive -> _api.get -> _request -> _getWithRetry: 2 attempts x Duration(seconds: 15) = 30 s before TimeoutException, which the catch at :93 turns into null and Home. While that runs, the gate's _child stays null, so the white ColoredBox shows. I did not run a test for this one.

confirmed.title: A leftover suppressRestore from a ride closed earlier makes resumeIfNeeded delete a just-adopted server trip on a push tap, so the ride does not open
confirmed.description: `RideSession.suppressRestore` is set true by every terminal `localTransition`/`backendReconcile` (ride_session.dart 82, 148) and is only reset by a non-terminal transition or `reset()` (sign-out wipe). After the rider closes or cancels a ride on this device the flag stays true indefinitely. `openRideFromNotification` → `_openRide` (notification_navigation.dart 88-125) reads no snapshot, calls `adoptServerActiveTrip(expectedRideId)` which saves the server trip as the snapshot (ride_restore_coordinator.dart 78-100), then calls `resumeIfNeeded()`. `resumeIfNeeded` reads the new snapshot, resyncs, and then hits `if (AppScope.instance.ride.suppressRestore) { unawaited(RideSnapshotStore.clear()); return null; }` (595-598): the just-adopted trip is deleted and nothing opens, although the flag belongs to a different, finished ride. The cold-start path (`_root` → `pageFor`) has no such check, so the same trip is restored after a restart.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Release build (ApiActiveTripRepository): rider finishes ride A on their phone (Done → closed). Later they book ride B on the web; the push for B taps on the phone. `_openRide` adopts B from the server, then `resumeIfNeeded` clears it and returns; the rider sees Home with no ride, and 'This ride has ended.' may be shown by `openNotificationRide`.
confirmed.evidence: ride_session.dart:82 `suppressRestore = status.isTerminal;` and 148 `suppressRestore = backendStatus.isTerminal;` ; ride_restore_coordinator.dart:595-598 `if (AppScope.instance.ride.suppressRestore) { unawaited(RideSnapshotStore.clear()); return null; }` ; notification_navigation.dart:93-96 `await RideSnapshotStore.read() ?? await RideRestoreCoordinator.instance.adoptServerActiveTrip(expectedRideId: expected)` then 123 `await RideRestoreCoordinator.instance.resumeIfNeeded();`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Scope `suppressRestore` to the ride id it was set for (ignore it when the snapshot's rideId differs from `session.rideId`), or clear it in `adoptServerActiveTrip`.

verdicts.reason: Once a ride ends, nothing clears the restore-suppress flag. markClosed/closeCompletedRide (active_ride_controller.dart:442/459) call localTransition(closed), which sets suppressRestore=true (ride_session.dart:82). The only resets are a non-terminal transition or reset() on sign-out wipe (ride_session.dart:210, user_data_wipe.dart:120), and Home calls neither. On a push tap, _openRide (notification_navigation.dart:88-124) adopts the server trip B as the snapshot. resumeIfNeeded then calls _resync(B), which does nothing for a ride the polling transport has no poll for (api_ride_realtime.dart:380-381). It reaches `if (AppScope.instance.ride.suppressRestore) { RideSnapshotStore.clear(); return null; }` (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:595-598), deletes the snapshot it just adopted and opens nothing. The cold path _root -> pageFor has no such check. One detail in the finding is off: openRideFromNotification returns true here, so 'This ride has ended' is not shown. The rider just stays on Home with nothing opened.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r67_test.dart (since deleted). A RideRestoreCoordinator with an ApiActiveTripRepository over InProcessMockClient holds ride_b=driverAssigned, debugAtRoot=true and onReplaceRoot captured. Without a prior ride: 'page=WaitingForDriver replaced=WaitingForDriver snapshotAfter=ride_b'. After backendReconcile(tripCompleted, id:'ride_a') + localTransition(closed): 'suppress=true ... adopted=ride_b surface=RestoredSurface.waiting / page=null replaced=null snapshotAfter=null'. Both tests passed (the prints are the evidence).
verdicts.corrected_title: A leftover suppressRestore from a ride closed earlier makes resumeIfNeeded delete a just-adopted server trip on a push tap, so the ride does not open

verdicts.reason: suppressRestore is in-memory and only goes back to false on a non-terminal transition or on reset() (ride_session.dart:82,148,210). The only caller of reset() is the sign-out wipe (user_data_wipe.dart:120). So after the rider cancels or closes ride A (finding_driver_controller.dart:969, active_ride_controller.dart:442/459), the flag stays true for the rest of the process. When a push for ride B (booked on another device) is tapped, _openRide (notification_navigation.dart:88-124) finds no local snapshot and adoptServerActiveTrip saves B (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:77-90). resumeIfNeeded then runs into `if (AppScope.instance.ride.suppressRestore) { clear(); return null; }` (595-598) and deletes B before surfaceFor/pageFor runs. Nothing resets the flag on the way. In the release ApiRideRealtime, reconnectAndResync returns early when nothing is subscribed to that ride (api_ride_realtime.dart:380-381), so backendReconcile never runs for B and never sets the flag back to false. One part of the description is wrong: _openRide still returns true (line 124), so the 'This ride has ended.' toast does not appear. The rider just stays on Home with no ride, and B's snapshot is gone until a cold start adopts it again from the server.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r67_test.dart (now deleted) using the real ApiActiveTripRepository over InProcessMockClient, with the server returning ride_B in findingDriver. Control run with suppressRestore false: 'resume page=FindingDrivers replaced=FindingDrivers snapshotAfter=ride_B showing=RestoredSurface.finding'. Stale run, after backendReconcile(findingDriver, id: ride_A) then localTransition(cancelledByRider): 'suppressRestore before=true rideId=ride_A ... adopted=ride_B surface=RestoredSurface.finding / resume page=Null replaced=Null snapshotAfter=null showing=RestoredSurface.home'. Both tests passed, so the adopted trip was wiped.

confirmed.title: An ended-early trip paid fully or partly by wallet is never debited from the local wallet ledger (demo/dev builds only)
confirmed.description: An ended-early trip opens RideCompleted with endedEarly set and persistOnDemandState: false (waiting_for_driver.dart:895-899). initState returns at line 102 before the subscription and before _maybeChargeWallet. _maybeChargeWallet would also bail out on !persistOnDemandState. The server's charged fare (EndedEarlyTrip.charged, shown on the receipt as 'You pay X') is never taken off the local wallet ledger for a wallet-paid ride, and no other code calls chargeCompletedRide/chargeRide. The result is a receipt that says the rider pays X while the wallet balance stays the same.

confirmed.title: The completion screen ignores paymentFailed, so a declined card shows 'Payment processing' until the rider taps Done, and the trip is filed as Completed
confirmed.description: Release realtime is ApiRideRealtime. A card declined at the end of a trip arrives as status completed plus paymentStatus failed. RideStatusWire._afterCompletion (core/contracts/trip_status.dart:183) maps that to RideStatus.paymentFailed. paymentFailed is isTerminal but not isCompletedSurface (core/contracts/ride_status.dart:65,85). Once Waiting has pushed RideCompleted, its tracker is disposed, and RideCompleted's own subscription is the only listener. That listener throws away every event whose status is not a completion surface. The decline is never reconciled into RideSession, never persisted and never shown. _CompletionSpec has no paymentFailed case, and the paymentFailed terminal sheet in ride_terminal_state_sheet.dart:287 is only reachable from Waiting. The rider stays on 'Trip complete / Payment processing' with rating locked ('rating after payment'). Done then runs closeCompletedRide: OnDemandRideHistoryStore.archive gets the snapshot status (paymentProcessing, a completion surface), so History lists the trip as Completed, and the session moves to closed. The payment is still outstanding and nothing tells the rider. Handoff race: if the decline lands while Waiting parks the map (active_ride_controller markCompleted, then waiting_for_driver.dart:717), the tracker has already set the session to paymentFailed. RideCompleted's initState accepts only completion-surface session statuses (line 114), so it starts at tripCompleted. Done then calls localTransition(closed) from the terminal paymentFailed, transitionRide throws InvalidRideTransition, and the rider is trapped on 'feedback could not be saved'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Release build. A rider pays with a card. The trip completes, RideCompleted opens, the server reports payment authorized (Payment processing), then the card is declined (paymentStatus failed). The screen stays on 'Payment processing' indefinitely, and the decline also survives a reload because the snapshot keeps paymentProcessing. The rider taps Done, History shows the ride as Completed, and the rider gets no 'payment could not be completed / review your payment method' message. If the decline arrives during the Waiting-to-Completed handoff, Done instead fails with 'feedback could not be saved' every time.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Handle paymentFailed (and other terminal non-completion statuses) in the RideCompleted listener and in initState's session check. Reconcile it into RideSession, persist it, and show the payment-failed state or terminal sheet with a path to change the payment method. In closeCompletedRide, do not call localTransition(closed) when the session is already terminal.

verdicts.reason: In release, ApiRideRealtime lets payment updates through after a terminal status (api_ride_realtime.dart:149-154 gate, plus `_projectionKind` returning paymentUpdated at :311-312). completed + paymentStatus failed maps to RideStatus.paymentFailed (trip_status.dart:183), which is terminal but not isCompletedSurface (ride_status.dart:65, 85-89). RideCompleted's listener drops every event that is not a completion surface (ride_completed.dart:121-128). So the decline is never reconciled into RideSession, never persisted and never shown, and the screen stays on 'Payment processing'. Done then archives with snapshot.status = paymentProcessing, which is a completion surface, so History lists the trip as Completed (active_ride_controller.dart:453-457). localTransition(closed) succeeds from paymentProcessing (ride_transition.dart:113-117), so the rider is never told the payment failed. Nothing in DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md or QA_HOOKS.md defers this. The handoff-race part (InvalidRideTransition trapping Done/Back) is real but was already reported and confirmed separately (docs/audit-2026-10-21/raw/rider_audit_results.json:906-935). I rated it medium because it needs a card decline after the trip ends, which is an edge path, although it does hit release builds.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: ApiRideRealtime._poll -> gate admits paymentUpdated after terminal -> RideStatusWire.fromProjection -> paymentFailed -> RideCompleted listener `!status.isCompletedSurface` return -> Done -> closeCompletedRide archives paymentProcessing. I checked canTransition for paymentProcessing->closed. No test was run.

verdicts.reason: Release ApiRideRealtime maps `completed` + `paymentStatus: failed` to RideStatus.paymentFailed (trip_status.dart:183, via RideStatusWire.fromProjection at api_ride_realtime.dart:112). paymentFailed is terminal but not isCompletedSurface (ride_status.dart:65, 85-89). RideCompleted's listener (ride_completed.dart:121-128) returns early for any status that is not a completion surface, so the event is never reconciled or persisted. The only other subscribers, the driver tracking and finding controllers, are disposed by then. _CompletionSpec.fromStatus has no paymentFailed case and falls to the tripCompleted default (ride_completed.dart:706-707). On Done, closeCompletedRide (active_ride_controller.dart:447-461) archives the snapshot with its stored completion status, so History shows the trip as Completed. Handoff race: if the session is already paymentFailed, initState keeps widget.status (line 114 accepts only completion surfaces), and localTransition(closed) throws InvalidRideTransition. canTransition returns false for any terminal `from` (ride_transition.dart:141-145). _leave's catch then shows feedbackSaveFailed every time (ride_completed.dart:262-267).
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand through trip_status.dart:179-192, ride_status.dart:58-89, ride_completed.dart:98-143 and :677-716, active_ride_controller.dart:447-461, ride_session.dart:79-80 and ride_transition.dart:108-145. Grepping lib/ for paymentFailed finds no handler on the completion screen; it is only handled in ride_terminal_state_sheet.dart:287, which only Waiting reaches. No test was run, because a release transport with a declined card would need a stubbed backend.

confirmed.title: The wallet debit depends on RideCompleted still being mounted when paymentFinalized arrives; leaving at tripCompleted/paymentProcessing (or ending early) never charges the local wallet (demo/dev builds)
confirmed.description: D-022 says a wallet-paid ride is deducted once it reaches paymentFinalized. The only caller of WalletController.chargeCompletedRideById is RideCompleted._maybeChargeWallet, which runs from initState and from the realtime listener on this screen. The Done button is enabled at every completion status (`onPressed: _leaving ? null : _closeAndHome`), and Back with nothing selected leaves at once. If the rider leaves while the status is still tripCompleted or paymentProcessing, three things happen: _leave calls closeCompletedRide, which archives the ride and runs `_store.clear()` on the snapshot; dispose cancels _completionSub; and the later paymentFinalized event reaches nobody. Nothing tries the charge again: the snapshot is gone and nothing else calls chargeCompletedRide. Ended-early trips are never charged at all, because initState returns before both _maybeChargeWallet calls (`if (widget.endedEarly != null) return;`).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo/dev build. The wallet holds 500 kr and the rider books a 259 kr ride paid by Movera Wallet. When the trip completes, the mock realtime only sends paymentFinalized after about 1 s (paymentProcessingAfter plus paymentFinalizedAfter, 500 ms each). The rider taps Done straight away and the balance stays at 500 kr for good. I reproduced this with a throwaway widget test built on phase105_wallet_ride_charge_test: pump RideCompleted at tripCompleted, replace it with SizedBox, then emit paymentFinalized. Output: 'balance after leaving early then paymentFinalized: 500.0' (expected 241). The same happens for any ended-early trip paid from the wallet.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_completed.dart:102 `if (widget.endedEarly != null) return;` (before _maybeChargeWallet at 143)
ride_completed.dart:151-154 `if (_completionRank(_status) < _completionRank(RideStatus.paymentFinalized)) { return; }`
ride_completed.dart:414 `onPressed: _leaving ? null : _closeAndHome,`
ride_completed.dart:252-253 `await _controller.closeCompletedRide(widget.rideId!);`
active_ride_controller.dart:461 `await _store.clear();`
wallet_controller.dart:238-244 chargeCompletedRideById reads LastCompletedRide or RideSnapshotStore.readForArchive(); its only caller is ride_completed.dart:163
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not tie the debit to this screen's lifetime. Either record a pending wallet charge for the ride id when it completes and settle it from an app-level listener once the payment is final, or charge when the ride closes, using the booked wallet part or the ended-early `charged` amount, keeping the existing charged-rides guard against double charging.

confirmed.title: A terminal status (e.g. paymentFailed) reconciled during the Waiting->RideCompleted handoff makes closeCompletedRide throw InvalidRideTransition, so Done and Back both fail with a misleading 'feedback could not be saved' and the rider cannot leave
confirmed.description: `_leave` wraps feedback submission and `closeCompletedRide` in one try/catch; any throw from the latter sets `_submitError = context.l10n.feedbackSaveFailed` and `_leaving = false` (259-265), and both Done and Back route through `_leave`, so the rider can never leave. `closeCompletedRide` can throw after the feedback was accepted: `localTransition(RideStatus.closed)` (active_ride_controller.dart 459) throws `InvalidRideTransition` when the session is already terminal, which happens when a `paymentFailed` (or other terminal) projection is reconciled by the still-live `DriverTrackingController` during the Waiting→RideCompleted `pushReplacement` handoff (RideCompleted's own listener ignores non-completed statuses, 123-127, so the screen keeps showing 'Trip complete'); `archive` can also throw its `StateError` after six lost writes (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart 172-176). The message then blames the rating/tip, which was in fact sent (`_acceptedFeedbackIntent` is set).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Payment fails on the server right as Waiting hands over to the summary. The rider rates the driver and taps Done: the rating is sent, then 'Your feedback could not be saved' appears every time, and neither Done nor Back leaves the screen.
confirmed.evidence: ride_completed.dart:252-265 `await _controller.closeCompletedRide(widget.rideId!); ... } catch (_) { ... _leaving = false; _submitError = context.l10n.feedbackSaveFailed;` ; active_ride_controller.dart:459 `AppScope.instance.ride.localTransition(RideStatus.closed);` ; ride_transition.dart:141-145 `if (from.isTerminal) return false;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Separate the two failure classes: keep the error only for a refused feedback submission, and make leaving tolerant (catch `InvalidRideTransition`/archive errors, clear the snapshot and still navigate Home).

verdicts.corrected_title: A terminal status (e.g. paymentFailed) reconciled during the Waiting->RideCompleted handoff makes closeCompletedRide throw InvalidRideTransition, so Done and Back both fail with a misleading 'feedback could not be saved' and the rider cannot leave
verdicts.reason: waiting_for_driver.dart:713-718 deliberately keeps the DriverTrackingController subscription alive through map parking and the pushReplacement; driver_tracking_controller.dart:118-124 reconciles every event into AppScope.instance.ride, and the resulting terminal tick is dropped by _drainStageNavigation because _completedOpened is already true (waiting_for_driver.dart:520-526). If paymentFailed arrives while the map parks, RideCompleted even opens at tripCompleted (720-723 fall back to `status`). RideCompleted's own listener ignores non-completed statuses (ride_completed.dart:123-127), so the screen still says the trip is complete. On Done or Back, _leave calls closeCompletedRide (ride_completed.dart:252-253), which calls localTransition(RideStatus.closed) (active_ride_controller.dart:459). canTransition refuses any terminal source (ride_transition.dart:141-142, paymentFailed is terminal per ride_status.dart:65), so InvalidRideTransition is thrown. The catch at ride_completed.dart:259-264 resets _leaving and shows feedbackSaveFailed. _store.clear never runs, so every retry throws the same way. PopScope(canPop:false) sends Back through _handleBack and then _leave(submitFeedback:false), which fails too. Unlike RideNavigator.home (ride_navigator.dart:29-39), closeCompletedRide has no canTransition guard.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: Waiting._openCompleted -> markCompleted/_parkMapForStageChange/pushReplacement while tracking stays subscribed -> DriverTrackingController backendReconcile(paymentFailed) -> RideCompleted._leave -> ActiveRideController.closeCompletedRide -> RideSession.localTransition -> transitionRide throws. I read every guard on the path (mounted, _leaving, _completedOpened, _completionRank, isCompletedSurface) and none prevents it. No test was run.

verdicts.corrected_title: A terminal status (e.g. paymentFailed) reconciled into RideSession during the Waiting to RideCompleted handoff makes closeCompletedRide throw InvalidRideTransition, so Done and Back both fail with the feedback/History error and the rider cannot leave
verdicts.reason: ride_completed.dart:252-265 runs closeCompletedRide inside the same try/catch as feedback, and any throw sets _leaving=false and shows feedbackSaveFailed. Back with nothing selected (_handleBack at :185) and Done both go through _leave. closeCompletedRide (active_ride_controller.dart:448-461) calls ride.localTransition(RideStatus.closed). That goes to transitionRide/canTransition (ride_transition.dart:133-145), which refuses any terminal `from`. paymentFailed is terminal (core/contracts/ride_status.dart:65). The bad state can be reached: Waiting._openCompleted (waiting_for_driver.dart:694-745) keeps its DriverTrackingController subscribed through markCompleted, map parking and pushReplacement. That tracker writes every event into the session with backendReconcile (driver_tracking_controller.dart:119-125), and Waiting ignores the terminal because _completedOpened is set (:515). RideCompleted is built with tripCompleted because tracked paymentFailed is not a completed surface (:716-719). Its initState and listener only accept completed-surface statuses (ride_completed.dart:113-127), so the screen shows 'Trip complete' while the session holds paymentFailed. The error text is 'Couldn't save your trip feedback or History' (app_en.arb:931), so it is only partly misleading. Restarting the app restores from the tripCompleted snapshot and lets the rider out, so the trap does not persist. The race window is short (handoff only), which makes this an edge path rather than a main path.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_r72b_test.dart, using the harness from test/ride/ride_completed_leave_without_saving_test.dart. It pushes RideCompleted(status: tripCompleted, persistOnDemandState default), then calls AppScope.instance.ride.backendReconcile(RideStatus.paymentFailed), the same call the live tracker makes, then taps Back twice. Output: 'try 0 home=false err=1 status=RideStatus.paymentFailed' / 'try 1 home=false err=1 status=RideStatus.paymentFailed'. The rider never reaches Home and the error shows every time. File deleted.

confirmed.title: A wallet-paid ride is never debited if the rider taps Done before payment is finalized
confirmed.description: D-022 wallet deduction runs only from _maybeChargeWallet, inside RideCompleted. It fires only once _status reaches paymentFinalized or later (lines 149-158). chargeCompletedRideById is called from nowhere else (grep: ride_completed.dart:163 only). Done is enabled from the first frame, including tripCompleted and paymentProcessing. Tapping it runs closeCompletedRide, which clears the completion snapshot, and dispose cancels the subscription. The later paymentFinalized event therefore never reaches a charging listener, and no restore will bring the screen back because the snapshot is gone. In the demo transport, paymentProcessing comes 500 ms after completion and paymentFinalized 500 ms after that (mock_ride_realtime.dart:32-33), so a quick Done skips the debit. The same applies to the wallet part of a 'use wallet first' split.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo build, wallet balance 300 kr. The rider pays a 129 kr trip with Movera Wallet. The completion screen appears and they tap Done within about one second, while the status is tripCompleted or paymentProcessing. They land on Home and the wallet still shows 300 kr, permanently, so the ride was free.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Run the wallet debit from a place that outlives the screen, for example the realtime or session layer or closeCompletedRide when the ride is wallet-paid and payment later settles. Alternatively keep listening (or keep the snapshot) until the payment reaches a settled state.

verdicts.reason: The wallet debit only runs from RideCompleted._maybeChargeWallet (ride_completed.dart:149-158). It returns while _status ranks below paymentFinalized and runs again only from the _completionSub listener (lines 121-142). The only caller of chargeCompletedRideById in lib/ is ride_completed.dart:163. Done (line 414, `_leaving ? null : _closeAndHome`) is enabled at every completion status. Back with nothing selected also leaves at once (line 188). _leave calls closeCompletedRide (active_ride_controller.dart:448-461), which clears the snapshot store, and dispose cancels _completionSub (line 173). The later paymentFinalized event reaches no listener and nothing retries the debit. The 'charged rides' guard in wallet_controller.dart only prevents a double charge; it never catches up a missed one. In the demo transport paymentFinalized arrives about 1 s after completion (mock_ride_realtime.dart:32-33), so this is easy to hit. The wallet-first split path (wallet_controller.dart:284-289) is affected the same way.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. I grepped chargeCompletedRide(ById) across lib/ and found ride_completed.dart:163 as the only caller. I followed _leave -> closeCompletedRide -> _store.clear() and dispose -> _completionSub.cancel(), and checked that there is no charge in closeCompletedRide, the realtime layer or WalletController init.

verdicts.reason: The wallet debit only runs from _maybeChargeWallet in ride_completed.dart:149-158, gated on rank >= paymentFinalized. Its only caller is ride_completed.dart:163 (grep of lib shows chargeCompletedRideById/chargeRide has no other caller). The Done button at ride_completed.dart:414 is gated only by _leaving, not by status. _leave then calls closeCompletedRide (active_ride_controller.dart:453-467), which moves the ride to closed and clears the snapshot store. After that the listener ignores events because of the _leaving guard (ride_completed.dart:123-126), and dispose cancels the subscription. Nothing else ever debits the ride.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_u181_test.dart, built from the phase105_wallet_ride_charge_test harness: balance 500, wallet snapshot price 259, RideCompleted shown at tripCompleted. Done was enabled (onPressed != null). After tapping Done the log showed 'ride.transition {to: closed, rideId: wr-9}'. I then emitted paymentProcessing and paymentFinalized. Output: 'balance after paymentFinalized: 500.0', test passed, so no debit happened. The file was deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: Receipt dispute sheet double-pads for the keyboard, so Submit is out of reach while the rider types
confirmed.description: _openDispute's builder pads its non-scrolling Column with `20 + MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context).bottom`, on top of MoveraSheet.show's own keyboard Padding. The multiline field (minLines 2, maxLines 4) uses a newline return key, so on iOS the keyboard cannot be dismissed from the keyboard. Flutter does not unfocus on a touch tap outside the field on mobile. A tap on the transparent band falls through to the barrier and closes the sheet, losing the text.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Native iPhone 390x844, keyboard 336 px: the Column gets 844 - 336 - 336 - 40 = 132 px but needs about 213 px (title 25, body ~40, field ~72, spacers, button 40). The FilledButton 'Submit issue' starts at about 173 px, outside the Column, so it is not hit-testable. The rider types the issue and cannot submit it. Tapping above the sheet dismisses it and the typed text is lost.
confirmed.evidence:
trip_detail.dart:145-151 `return Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(
              20,
              20,
              20,
              20 + MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context).bottom,
            ),
            child: Column(` ; :163-166 `minLines: 2,
                  maxLines: 4,` ; movera_sheet.dart:36-41 already pads by the keyboard inset
confirmed.suggested_fix: Drop the viewInsets term (keep the 20), and wrap the Column in a SingleChildScrollView.

verdicts.reason: MoveraSheet.show already wraps the builder in Padding(bottom: viewInsetsOf(ctx).bottom) (lib/shared/design_system/movera_sheet.dart:36-41). Padding does not remove viewInsets from MediaQuery, so _openDispute's inner Padding adds `20 + MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context).bottom` a second time (trip_detail.dart:145-151). The non-scrolling Column(mainAxisSize.min) then overflows, and the Submit button is painted outside the Column's bounds, where it cannot be hit-tested. No other guard, such as a scroll view or resizeToAvoidBottomInset, prevents this.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u183_test.dart (now deleted). It used the same MoveraSheet.show plus the same Padding/Column/TextField(minLines 2, maxLines 4)/FilledButton structure at 390x844 dpr 1, then set tester.view.viewInsets bottom to 336. Output: 'kb button: Rect.fromLTRB(20.0, 268.0, 370.0, 316.0)', 'exception: A RenderFlex overflowed by 164 pixels on the bottom.', 'hit path has button render: false' (the hit path ends at sheet internals: _RenderDragGestureListener, _RenderSheetSkelton, ...). Without the keyboard the button sits at 776-824 and is reachable.

verdicts.reason: MoveraSheet.show already wraps the builder in Padding(bottom: viewInsets) (lib/shared/design_system/movera_sheet.dart:36-41). Padding does not change MediaQuery, so the dispute builder's own `20 + MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context).bottom` (lib/features/ride_complete/presentation/trip_detail.dart:145-151) adds the keyboard inset a second time, and the Column cannot scroll. With the keyboard up the Column overflows and the Submit button is pushed outside its parent's bounds, so taps on it are not hit-tested. The rider cannot submit while typing. On iOS the newline return key and touch taps outside the field do not dismiss the keyboard, so the rider has no easy way out.
verdicts.repro: Wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_u183_test.dart: the real RideCompletedTripDetail with rideId 'r1' at 390x844, dpr 1. It taps 'receipt-report-issue', then sets tester.view.viewInsets bottom to 336. Result with inset 0: no errors, submit rect (20,776)-(370,824), hittable at center: true. confirmed.title: Wallet is offered as the full payment method even when the fare is above the balance, and completing the ride drives the local wallet ledger negative (demo/dev builds, where the local wallet is enabled)
confirmed.description: The wallet row is listed whenever `walletBalance > 0` with no comparison against the fare (ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268), PayWithPage pops `'wallet'` on tap with no check (pay_with_page.dart:224-232), and `walletSplitFor` returns `WalletSplit.none` for the wallet method (200-202) so `walletAmountMinor` is 0 and the server-side range check in the mock (`walletMinor > serverTotal`) cannot catch it. At completion `RideCompleted._maybeChargeWallet` → `chargeCompletedRideById` → `chargeCompletedRide` charges `amount = snapshot.price` (wallet_controller.dart:282-283) and `LocalWalletRepository._apply` subtracts with no floor (wallet_repository.dart:215-218), so the stored balance becomes negative and WalletHome shows e.g. '-209 kr'. Reproduced: `brand=wallet walletMinor=0 remainderMinor=25900` and `balance after wallet-paid 259 kr ride from 50 kr: -209.0`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider has 50 kr in the wallet, picks a 259 kr ride, opens Pay with, taps the Movera Wallet row ('Balance: 50 kr'), books. Ride completes: wallet balance shows -209 kr, the wallet disappears from Pay with (balance not > 0), and the next 100 kr top-up shows -109 kr.
confirmed.evidence: ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268 `if (item.brand == 'wallet') { return _flags.enableWallet && walletBalance > 0 && walletMatchesTrip; }`; pay_with_page.dart:226-232 `_row(... title: context.l10n.walletBalance(...), onTap: () => Navigator.of(context).pop('wallet'),)`; wallet_controller.dart:282-283 `if (paidByWallet) { amount = snapshot.price;`; wallet_repository.dart:215-218 `final nextMinor = Money.fromLegacyMajor(current, currency).amountMinor + Money.fromLegacyMajor(deltaKr, currency).amountMinor; final next = Money(nextMinor, currency).major; await _source.saveBalance(next);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Offer the wallet as a full method only when `walletBalance >= fare` of the selected ride (or show it disabled with 'Balance too low'), and clamp `debitRide` to the available balance / refuse the charge with a logged error.

verdicts.corrected_title: Wallet is offered as the full payment method even when the fare is above the balance, and completing the ride drives the local wallet ledger negative (demo/dev builds, where the local wallet is enabled)
verdicts.reason: `payments()` lists the wallet whenever `walletBalance > 0` (ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268). PayWithPage pops 'wallet' on tap with no fare check (pay_with_page.dart:226-231). `walletSplitFor` returns `WalletSplit.none` for the wallet method (200-202), so the mock booking range check on `walletAmountMinor` (in_process_mock_client.dart:2247-2252) never sees it. No insufficient-balance guard exists anywhere in lib (grep for insufficient/balanceTooLow/walletBalance comparisons found none). At completion `chargeCompletedRide` charges `snapshot.price` in full (wallet_controller.dart:282-283), and `LocalWalletRepository._apply` subtracts with no floor (wallet_repository.dart:209-218). Release builds compose DisabledWalletRepository (ARCHITECTURE.md:68-71), so the bug is limited to demo/dev builds, which seed a demo balance (bootstrap.dart:108-110). In those builds the wallet is a main payment path.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_rider74_test.dart (deleted afterwards): RideSelectionController(store: RideSelectionRepository(), flags: FeatureFlags()) with walletBalance=50, then LocalWalletRepository.debitRide(amount: 259) from 50. Output: `brands=[wallet, google, cards, cash]`, `selected=wallet walletMinor=0 remainder=25900`, `balance after=-209.0`, `All tests passed!`.

verdicts.reason:
The steps chain with no guard:
- `RideSelectionController.payments()` lists the wallet whenever `walletBalance > 0` (ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268), with no comparison against the fare.
- The PayWith wallet row pops 'wallet' unconditionally (pay_with_page.dart:224-232).
- `walletSplitFor` returns `WalletSplit.none` for the wallet method (200-202), so nothing caps the amount at booking.
- `chargeCompletedRide` charges `amount = snapshot.price` when `paymentMethodId == 'wallet'` (wallet_controller.dart:282-283).
- `LocalWalletRepository._apply` (wallet_repository.dart:207-222) adds the delta with no floor.

A grep found no low-balance or insufficient-funds check anywhere in lib. The wallet is a documented device-local ledger that release builds switch off (API_V1_MOCK.md:113, backend-readiness-gate.md:12). It is still live in dev and staging, where it shows a negative balance that it never should, so medium.

confirmed.title: A quote in another currency drops the wallet row and shifts the index-based payment choice to a different method
confirmed.description: The chosen payment is held as an index into payments() (selectedPayment, line 114). payments() includes the wallet row only while walletMatchesTrip holds (line 267). Every other list change re-selects by brand: setWalletBalance, setZonePaymentMethods and loadSavedCards all do. adoptQuote changes `currency = quote.currency` without that. When the server prices the pickup in a currency other than the RiderZones guess (the controller explicitly supports this: 'the server decides'), walletMatchesTrip turns false and the wallet row, which is first in the list, disappears. Every index then points one row further down, so the selected method silently becomes a different one. This is separate from the known finding about prices mixing currencies.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rider with wallet credit picks Card. The quote comes back in EUR, so the wallet row disappears and the payment line switches to Cash without the rider touching it. Book then sends paymentMethod 'cash'.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_selection_controller.dart:114 `int selectedPayment = 1;`
ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268 `if (item.brand == 'wallet') { return _flags.enableWallet && walletBalance > 0 && walletMatchesTrip; }`
ride_selection_controller.dart:457 `currency = quote.currency;` (no selectPaymentByBrand afterwards)
Reproduced in a unit test: wallet balance 50 SEK, select 'cards', adopt a EUR quote. Output: `AUDIT payment before=cards after=cash list=[google, cards, cash]`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the currency setter (or adoptQuote), remember the selected brand before the change and call selectPaymentByBrand(brand) afterwards. Better still, store the selection as a brand instead of an index.

verdicts.reason: selectedPayment is an index (ride_selection_controller.dart:114). The wallet row is only in payments() while walletMatchesTrip holds (:267, walletMatchesTrip = walletCurrency == currency at :77). adoptQuote does `currency = quote.currency` (:457), and the setter (:65-69) only clears offeredPrices. Nothing re-selects by brand afterwards, unlike setWalletBalance (:599-602) and setZonePaymentMethods (:588-597). Both _loadQuote (:402) and quoteFromPin (:446) reach adoptQuote, and CatalogQuoteRepository prices in the zone of pickupPoint (catalog_quote_repository.dart:26), so a Set-location pin moved into another zone changes the currency even in the mock. selectedPaymentItem() then clamps the stale index to a different method, and booking/scheduled checkout read that method (select_ride.dart:1446, scheduled_ride_booking.dart:49).
verdicts.repro: Wrote the throwaway test test/_audit_u184v_test.dart: a controller with wallet balance 50 SEK and 'cards' selected, then adoptQuote with a EUR quote. Output: `list=[wallet, google, cards, cash]` then `AUDIT before=cards after=cash list=[google, cards, cash]`. 1 test passed. File deleted.

verdicts.reason: The selection is an index (ride_selection_controller.dart:114). The wallet row is first in payments() and shows only while walletMatchesTrip holds (:265-267, :77). adoptQuote sets `currency = quote.currency` (:457), and the setter (:65-68) only clears offeredPrices; nothing re-selects by brand afterwards. That differs from setWalletBalance (:599-601), setZonePaymentMethods (:586-595) and loadSavedCards (:230-233), which all re-select. A quote whose currency differs from the RiderZones guess (the code says 'the server decides', :59-62) can arrive two ways: through _loadQuote (:402) or through a pin re-quote (quoteFromPin :446). Either one silently moves the index onto the next method. It is an edge path, because the in-app CatalogQuoteRepository uses the same RiderZones lookup, so the currency changes only when a real server answers differently or the pin crosses into another zone.

confirmed.title: An expired quote makes the ride row show the catalog list price as if it were the fare, with no re-quote until Book is tapped
confirmed.description: priceFor discards an expired quote (_discardExpiredQuote removes offeredPrices and authoritativeQuotes) and returns `offeredPrices[id] ?? catalog`. A failed quote (_loadQuote catch) also removes offeredPrices. _hasPrice is true for any list price in the pickup's currency, so _rideTile shows the catalog price (e.g. 259 kr for every Movera trip, whatever the distance) as the fare. It is not marked as an estimate or as unavailable. Nothing schedules a re-quote at expiry. The next rebuild (sheet drag, tapping a row) simply swaps the quoted fare for the list price. The rider learns that there is no price only when Book answers 'price unavailable, refreshing'. DECISIONS P4: 'Clients display a quote; they do not invent totals.'
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider looks at Select Ride for more than the quote lifetime (2 min in the mock) on an Arlanda trip quoted at 412 kr. Dragging the sheet changes every row to its list price (Movera 259 kr, Comfort 339 kr ...), which looks like a price drop. Tapping Book then says the price is unavailable and re-prices.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_selection_controller.dart:498-501 `double priceFor(String id, double catalog, {DateTime? now}) { _discardExpiredQuote(id, now: now); return offeredPrices[id] ?? catalog; }`
ride_selection_controller.dart:524-525 `offeredPrices.containsKey(id) || catalogCurrency == currency;`
select_ride.dart:2304 `_hasPrice(ride) ? _kr(price) : '…',`
Reproduced with 2-second quotes of 412 kr: fresh `412kr=5 259kr=0`; after expiry plus one rebuild `412kr=0 259kr=1 calls=14 available=false` (no new quote requests).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Show '…' or 'updating' for ids in unavailableQuoteIds or with an expired quote instead of the catalog price, and schedule a re-quote shortly before quoteExpiresAt.

verdicts.reason: priceFor (ride_selection_controller.dart:498-501) runs _discardExpiredQuote (:487-496), which removes offeredPrices, quoteIds and authoritativeQuotes once the quote expires, and then returns the catalog price. hasPriceFor (:524-525) stays true when catalogCurrency == currency, so _rideTile (select_ride.dart:2182, 2306) and the confirm bar total (select_ride.dart:1310) show the list price as the fare. Per API_V1_MOCK.md:71, that price is 'display only' and the same for every distance. select_ride.dart has no timer that re-quotes at expiry: _loadQuotes runs only on init, on catalog or route changes, or from the Book guard. Book is guarded (select_ride.dart:1242-1247: quoteIsAvailable false -> 'price unavailable, refreshing' -> re-quote), so no wrong money is charged. The bug is a silently wrong displayed fare after about 2 minutes (quote lifetime, API_V1_MOCK.md:80), which goes against DECISIONS P4 ('Clients display a quote').
verdicts.repro: Static trace of priceFor, _discardExpiredQuote, hasPriceFor and the _rideTile and confirm-bar call sites. Grepped select_ride.dart for any expiry-driven re-quote (Timer, quoteExpiresAt) and found only the Book-time guard. Did not run my own test; the code path is direct.

confirmed.title: Saved 'wallet' default payment is silently replaced by Cash on every Select Ride open (load-order race)
confirmed.description: `SelectRide.initState` starts `_loadSavedCards(paymentName)` (line 353) and `_loadWalletBalance()` (line 361) concurrently. `_loadSavedCards` → `restoreDefaultPayment()` reads the saved brand and, because `payments()` only lists the wallet when `walletBalance > 0` (ride_selection_controller.dart:267) and the balance has not loaded yet, hits `if (saved == null || !list.any((item) => item.brand == saved)) { _selectDefaultPayment(); }` and selects Cash. `_loadWalletBalance` resolves later (`loadUseWalletFirst` → `WalletStore.loadPayments` performs four `prefs.remove` platform calls plus possible writes before returning) and calls `setWalletBalance`, which only re-selects the *current* brand (`if (current != null) selectPaymentByBrand(current);`, 598-602), i.e. Cash. The remembered wallet default (persisted by `selectPayment` → `_persistSelectedBrand` and by WalletScreen `_selectMethod('wallet')`) is therefore never restored, contradicting the R10 note in default_payment_store.dart ('the choice survives relaunch'). A return ride whose origin was paid with 'Movera Wallet' loses it the same way (`selectPaymentNamed` runs before the balance is known). Reproduced with a throwaway test driving the same sequence on the controller: `afterRestore=cash walletOffered=true afterBalance=cash savedDefault=wallet`.

confirmed.description: initState calls selectPaymentNamed(paymentName) and then _loadSavedCards(paymentName), which re-applies the name after the cards load (line 406). If the cards load first, 'Movera Wallet' is not in payments(). selectPaymentNamed finds nothing and leaves the constructor default (Cash), and setWalletBalance later re-selects that current brand (cash). The reservation's stored payment is lost. In the edit flow, ReviewChanges then saves Cash. This has the same root race as the known restoreDefaultPayment finding, but on the explicit initialPaymentMethod / editingReservationId path.

confirmed.description: When the rider backs out of Set pickup after a pin quote was adopted, Book now reloads the list quotes (line 1484: `if (_pinQuoteAdopted) unawaited(_loadQuotes());`) because 'the pin's price belongs to a point the rider did not confirm'. The scheduled path just returns (line 1137: `if (spot == null || !mounted) return;`). It never resets or checks _pinQuoteAdopted, so the selection keeps the moved pin's quote as the authoritative price at the unchanged original pickup. On the next Schedule tap, Set pickup opens at the original point and shows that price. Confirming without moving the pin creates the reservation at the moved pin's price for the original pickup.

select_ride.dart:1137 `if (spot == null || !mounted) return;` (scheduled)

confirmed.title: After a confirmed pickup-pin move, other categories (and the selected one when its pin re-quote failed) are booked with quotes priced at the original pickup
confirmed.description: Set pickup only re-quotes the selected category, and only when the pin moves (set_pickup_page.dart:493-507 `if (_isAwayFrom(_center, _routeStart)) { ... unawaited(_requote()); }`). When the rider confirms a moved pin, `_bookNow` stores the new position (`_pickupAddress = spot.address; _pickupPosition = spot.position; _pickupConfirmed = true;`, 1487-1489) but never reloads the list quotes. If the rider then declines the 'Price updated' dialog (1515-1520 returns after `setState`), or returns from Finding Drivers, every other category still holds `authoritativeQuotes` priced from the old pickup, and the tiles show those prices. Tapping Book on such a category passes `_book`'s `quoteIsAvailable` check (the quote is fresh for up to 2 min), opens Set pickup at the NEW position showing `fare: SetPickupFare(totalKr: _priceFor(ride) ...)` (1307-1309, the old-pickup quote), and because the pin does not move nothing re-quotes; `_quoteAfterPickup` returns `_bookableQuote(ride.id)` as long as it is not expired (559-560), so `submitFinding` sends `pickupLat/Lng` of the new point with `quoteId`/`quoteSignedPayload` of the old point. The same happens for the selected category itself when its pin re-quote timed out: `_requoteNow` keeps the old fare (set_pickup_page.dart:534-541), `shown == quote.totalMinor` so no dialog, and the old-point quote is booked. The in-process mock's `_validateQuoteBinding` (in_process_mock_client.dart:2188-2230) checks id, signature, expiry, total and category but not the pickup, so the booking is accepted at the wrong price. `_bookScheduled` has the same shape: it never awaits `_pinQuote`, so a pin re-quote still in flight when Set pickup pops (it waits at most 3 s) leaves `ScheduledRideCheckout.draftFrom` → `quotedPrice` on the old-point quote.

List now shows Comfort at the price quoted for the original pickup. Rider taps Comfort → Book → Set pickup opens at the new pin showing the old-pickup price → Confirm and search → ride is created at the new coordinates with the old-pickup quote and price; Finding/Waiting then show that price.

confirmed.title: A trigger detected while another card is open is used up and never shown or posted (for example dropped-far at trip end while the long-stop card is unanswered)
confirmed.description: `RideCheckMonitor._fire` adds the trigger to `_fired` before the controller tries to show it. The controller then calls `open()`, which returns `busy` when a card is already up. The detection is neither queued nor posted as a safety event, and because the monitor already marks it fired it can never trigger again for this trip. In this journey, the rider has not answered the long-stop card. The driver taps Finish 3.6 km from the drop-off. `tripEnded` makes the monitor fire droppedFar and `open()` returns busy. The dropped-far check never opens, is never recorded on the trip and never reaches the server. The same happens to a long stop that is detected while an off-route or crash card is still up.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Long stop card shows mid-trip and the rider does not answer. The trip is then finished 3.6 km from the drop-off. On the summary the rider answers the long-stop card ('I'm OK'). No 'Driver finished far from drop-off' check ever appears and no droppedFar safety event is posted, though the admin trigger is on.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_check_monitor.dart:251-253: `RideCheckDetection _fire(...) { _fired.add(trigger); return RideCheckDetection(trigger, reason); }`
ride_check_controller.dart:304-306: `final hit = monitor.tripEnded(end); if (hit == null) return RideCheckOpenResult.noTrigger; return open(hit.trigger, reason: hit.reason, rideId: rideId);`
ride_check_controller.dart:379: `if (_session != null) return RideCheckOpenResult.busy;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Queue detections that arrive while a card is open and show them after it closes, or at least post their safety event. Alternatively, only mark a trigger fired once it has actually been shown.

verdicts.reason: `RideCheckMonitor._fire` adds the trigger to `_fired` before anything is shown (ride_check_monitor.dart:251-253), and `_canFire` refuses it after that. `RideCheckController.open` returns `busy` whenever any session is open (ride_check_controller.dart:379), before `_shown` and before any event is posted, and nothing queues the detection. At trip end `_feedRideCheck` calls `tripEnded` exactly once (waiting_for_driver.dart:1219-1222, guarded by `_rideCheckEnded`). An unanswered long-stop card therefore makes droppedFar disappear for good: it is never shown, never saved locally and never posted. The same happens in addSample/checkStill (266-291) for any trigger that arrives while another card is up. No document describes dropping a detection while a card is open as intended.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of tripEnded -> monitor.tripEnded -> _fire (marks fired) -> open -> line 379 busy -> result discarded by unawaited caller at waiting_for_driver.dart:1222.

verdicts.reason: RideCheckMonitor._fire adds the trigger to _fired before the controller tries to show it (ride_check_monitor.dart:251-253). RideCheckController.tripEnded/addSample then call open(), which returns busy when any session is up (ride_check_controller.dart:379). Nothing queues the detection or posts it as an event. Once the open card is answered, the monitor's _canFire refuses the trigger for the rest of the trip. 'Never two at a time' is intentional (ride_check_triggers_test 'opens once per trigger per ride, and never two at a time'), but nothing documents throwing the second detection away for good.

Samples standing still for about 400 s opened longStop. tripEnded('r1', 3.6 km north of the drop-off) returned RideCheckOpenResult.busy. After imOk() and settle(), tripEnded with the same far point returned RideCheckOpenResult.noTrigger and the session was null. The droppedFar check never opened.

confirmed.title: A Ride check left open when the trip ends externally (admin cancel or failed) stays as the session forever, and no later trip can open a Ride check
confirmed.description: Only imOk()/done() clear `_session` (via `_close`). When a trip with an open card ends in a non-completed terminal status, `_handleExternalTerminal` calls markExternalTerminal and goes Home (waiting_for_driver.dart:548-596). Statuses that do this include cancelledByAdmin and failed. Home and later screens host no RideCheckLayer for that ride, so the card can never be answered. `_session` still holds ride X, so every later `open()` returns `busy` at line 379, and `resume()` returns early at line 426. On ride Y in the same process, `sessionFor(Y)` is null, so nothing shows and nothing blocks: long stop, off-route, crash and dropped-far are all silently dropped (the monitor marks them fired). This lasts until the app process restarts.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Ride 1: a long-stop card is open and unanswered when the admin cancels the trip. The rider lands on Home and the card is gone. Ride 2, same app session: the car stands still for 10 minutes at a non-planned spot. RideCheckController.open returns busy and no card ever appears. The Safety › RideCheck demo also reports 'busy'.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:379: `if (_session != null) return RideCheckOpenResult.busy;`
ride_check_controller.dart:426: `if (_session != null) return;`
waiting_for_driver.dart:589-595: `await _ride.markExternalTerminal(status); ... RideNavigator.home(context, status: status);` (no Ride check close)
confirmed.suggested_fix: When a ride ends without a completion surface, close or park the session for that ride (save it as unanswered on the event). Scope the `busy` check to the visible ride, so a stale session for another ride does not block new trips.

verdicts.reason: `_session` is cleared only in `_close` (ride_check_controller.dart:682), which runs only from imOk/done, and in `resetShared` on sign-out (safety_controller.dart:70-76). `_handleExternalTerminal` (waiting_for_driver.dart:548-596) handles cancelledByAdmin/failed by calling markExternalTerminal and going Home, and never closes the Ride check. `detachTrip` keeps the card on purpose (255-259). RideCheckLayer is hosted only on WaitingForDriver, RideCompleted and the demo page, so the card for the ended ride cannot be reached again. Every later `open()` then returns `busy` (379), `resume()` returns early (426), and `sessionFor(newRide)` is null (201-206), so nothing shows. This lasts until sign-out or a process restart. The demo page uses the shared controller too, so it also reports busy.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: external terminal path at waiting_for_driver.dart:589-595 has no RideCheckController call; open() line 379 has no ride scoping; grep shows no other writer of `_session = null`.

verdicts.reason: _session is cleared only in _close (ride_check_controller.dart:682), which is reached only through imOk()/done(). The resetShared on sign-out also drops it. When a ride with an open card ends externally (cancelledByAdmin, failed), _handleExternalTerminal marks it terminal and goes Home (waiting_for_driver.dart:589-595). It never closes the session, and no later screen hosts a RideCheckLayer for that ride. The only layers are at waiting_for_driver.dart:1662 and ride_completed.dart:443. For any later ride, open() returns busy (379) and resume() returns early (426), while sessionFor(newRide) is null, so nothing is shown. This lasts until the process restarts or the rider signs out. It is an edge path (admin cancel or failed while a card is unanswered), so medium.

confirmed.title: A Ride check the rider already answered reappears if any ride screen resumes while the close is still queued behind a slow alert
confirmed.description: _close sets `_session = null` immediately, but the final submit that marks the event `resolved` is only enqueued, behind any alert POST still in flight (_enqueue serialises writes). Until that job runs, the saved event stays `acknowledged`; the red-row alert submit set that status before awaiting the network. resume(rideId) runs from every RideCheckLayer initState or didUpdateWidget, for example when RideCompleted mounts. It sees `_session == null`, asks unanswered(), which returns any event that is not resolved or stale, and rebuilds the card. resume does not consult `_shown` or anything that records a just-closed check. When the queued close finally runs, nothing closes the resurrected session.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway test. Open a long-stop card and hold POST /ridecheck/answers. chooseRow(unsafe) starts the alert, then done() leaves session=null, then resume('r2') leaves the session open again. After the held request is released and the queue settles, the session is still open. On a slow or offline network the rider who answered 'I feel unsafe' and tapped Done sees the card come back on the next ride screen and must answer again. Back is blocked until they do.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mark the event resolved locally and synchronously in _close, before enqueuing the network work. Alternatively, keep a set of closed checkIds and make resume() skip them, or wait for settle() before it calls unanswered().

verdicts.reason: _close (ride_check_controller.dart:681-693) sets `_session = null` straight away, but the final submit that writes status=resolved (safety_store.dart submitRideCheckAnswers, isFinal -> resolved) is only enqueued behind the in-flight alert job (_enqueue serialises jobs, line 719). Until that job runs, the cached event stays `acknowledged`. resume() (lines 421-460) checks only `_session != null`. It then calls unanswered(), which returns any event that is not resolved or stale (ride_check_service.dart:97-107), and rebuilds the session. It does not check `_shown` or a closed-check set. Neither the close job nor the alert job clears the resurrected session; the alert job even updates it, because the checkId matches. RideCheckLayer calls resume from initState and didUpdateWidget (ride_check_card.dart:139-157), and the layer is mounted on RideCompleted (ride_completed.dart:443) and on the trip screen (waiting_for_driver.dart:1662). So if the rider moves to the next ride screen while the alert POST is slow, the card they already answered comes back.
verdicts.repro: Wrote and ran test/_audit_u198_test.dart (since deleted): a real SafetyStore over an InProcessMockClient that holds the first POST /ridecheck/answers. open(longStop, 'r2') -> chooseRow(unsafe) -> done() -> resume('r2') -> release the hold -> wait 2 s. Output: 'after done session=null', 'after resume session=true', then both answers POSTs and the respond POST returned 200, then 'after settle session=true'. Result: '+1: All tests passed!'

verdicts.reason: _close (ride_check_controller.dart:681-693) clears `_session` at once but only enqueues the final submit. _enqueue (719-733) chains it behind an alert job that is still waiting on the network. The alert's submitRideCheckAnswers (safety_store.dart keep(...) before `_remote.postRideCheckAnswers`) has already saved the event as `acknowledged`. resume (421-460) checks only `_session != null` and then `_service.unanswered` (ride_check_service.dart:97-107), which returns any event that is neither resolved nor stale. `_shown` is not consulted. So the session is rebuilt, and when the queued close finally runs, nothing clears it.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u198_test.dart, using the real SafetyStore/ApiSafetyRemoteDataSource with an InProcessMockClient subclass that holds POST /ridecheck/answers on a Completer. Steps: open(longStop, rideId 'r2'), chooseRow(unsafe), done(), resume('r2'), release, wait 500 ms.
