confirmed.title: The card and Kit keep showing 'Recording m:ss' after the OS has interrupted capture (112 call or app in background); the app has no background audio mode
confirmed.description: `isRecording` only reflects the service's own `_active` field. Nothing listens to the recorder's state or interruptions. The app declares no background audio (Info.plist UIBackgroundModes has only remote-notification, and the Android manifest has no microphone foreground service). So when the rider follows the journey and taps Call 112, the dialer takes the foreground and the call takes the microphone: iOS interrupts and suspends the recording, and Android 9+ records silence for a backgrounded app. Back in the app, the card's ticker still counts 'Recording 3:12 · Tap to stop' as if everything since the call had been captured.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider starts a Ride check recording, then taps Call 112 and talks to the operator for 3 minutes. Returning to the app, the card shows 'Recording 3:40'. The saved file has no audio after the dialer opened, which the rider learns only if they ever find the file.
confirmed.evidence:
safety_audio_service.dart:30: `bool get isRecording => _active?.isRecording == true;`
ride_check_card.dart:999-1006: `final recording = widget.controller.recording; ... final elapsed = ... DateTime.now().toUtc().difference(since.toUtc());`
ios/Runner/Info.plist:48-51: `<key>UIBackgroundModes</key><array><string>remote-notification</string></array>`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Subscribe to the recorder's state/interruption stream and update the card (stop, or show 'paused by call'). Declare background audio (iOS) or a microphone foreground service (Android) if recording must survive a call or a locked screen.

verdicts.reason: safety_audio_service.dart:30 `isRecording` reflects only `_active`. NativeSafetyRecorder (safety_recorder_native.dart:25-34) starts `record` with the default RecordConfig, whose audioInterruption defaults to AudioInterruptionMode.pause (record_platform_interface record_config.dart:89). The app never subscribes to onStateChanged or reacts to app lifecycle (grep finds no RecordState or onStateChanged under lib/features/safety). Info.plist:48-51 declares only remote-notification as a background mode, and the Android manifest has RECORD_AUDIO but no microphone foreground service. The Kit's Call 112 button (ride_safety_kit.dart:168) opens the dialer while a recording can be running. That sheet stays open, so the 'sheet_closed' stop at line 146 does not fire. The OS then pauses or silences the capture while ride_check_card.dart:999-1006 keeps counting elapsed time from recordingSince. On a safety-evidence feature, the card shows recording it is not doing.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the record package defaults in ~/.pub-cache record_platform_interface-2.1.0, safety_recorder_native.dart, safety_audio_service.dart, ride_check_card.dart ticker, Info.plist and AndroidManifest.xml. The OS interruption behaviour cannot be reproduced on the host, so no test was run.

verdicts.reason: safety_audio_service.dart:30 `isRecording => _active?.isRecording == true` only tracks the service's own state. NativeSafetyRecorder (safety_recorder_native.dart:30-33) starts `RecordConfig(encoder: AudioEncoder.aacLc)`, which uses the default `audioInterruption = AudioInterruptionMode.pause` (record_platform_interface record_config.dart:89). record_ios RecorderSessionExtension.swift:109-118 calls pause() when an interruption begins and resumes only in pauseResume mode, so after a phone call the recording stays paused for good. Nothing in lib/features/safety subscribes to onStateChanged or the app lifecycle. Info.plist:48-51 declares only remote-notification in UIBackgroundModes, and the Android manifest has no microphone foreground service. Call 112 and Record audio sit on the same Ride check card (ride_check_card.dart:587/604 and 627). After a 112 call the card keeps counting 'Recording m:ss', and stop() (safety_audio_service.dart:84-86) saves a wall-clock duration that is longer than the audio actually captured.

confirmed.title: Wipe disposes the Safety and Ride check controllers without stopping a running recording, so the microphone keeps recording with no owner
confirmed.description: UserDataWipe.resetInMemory calls SafetyController.resetShared(). That calls RideCheckController.resetShared() (dispose only sets _disposed and clears the QA owner), then `_shared?.dispose()`. SafetyController does not override dispose, so this is plain ChangeNotifier.dispose. Neither path calls `audio.stopIfRecording`. An RC5 recording started from the Ride check card is not stopped when WaitingForDriver is torn down either: its dispose only calls `RideCheckController.shared.detachTrip(rideId)`, which nulls the monitor. When the session expires mid-trip, showMoveraRoot(SignIn) pops the trip screen and the recording keeps running behind Sign in. When the next rider signs in, enterSessionAs -> run -> resetShared drops the only reference to that SafetyAudioService. Nothing can ever stop the recorder again before the process dies.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider A is in a trip, a Ride check opens and A taps 'Record audio'. The session expires (refresh rejected), so Sign in replaces the trip screen and the microphone is still recording. Rider B signs in: the wipe replaces the controllers, and the microphone stays on recording into A's file with no Stop button anywhere, until the app is killed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In resetShared (or in UserDataWipe.resetInMemory, before resetting), await or fire `_shared?.audio.stopIfRecording(reason: 'session_end')` and delete the result. Also stop the recording when the trip screen is disposed by a forced Sign in.

verdicts.reason: When the session expires, di.dart:104-115 only clears the last location fix and calls showMoveraRoot(SignIn). Waiting.dispose then calls only RideCheckController.shared.detachTrip (waiting_for_driver.dart:1264-1278), which nulls the monitor (ride_check_controller.dart:255-258). A Ride check (RC5) recording therefore keeps running behind Sign in. When a different rider signs in, enterSessionAs runs run(), which calls resetInMemory and then SafetyController.resetShared (user_data_wipe.dart:135, 165-173; safety_controller.dart:71-77). RideCheckController.dispose (ride_check_controller.dart:819-826) and plain ChangeNotifier.dispose never call audio.stopIfRecording, and the service has no time limit. The wipe drops the last reference to the SafetyAudioService that holds _active, so nothing can stop that recording again. Sign-out goes through the same wipe. The Safety Kit's own recording is not affected, because closing the kit stops it (ride_safety_kit.dart:146).
verdicts.repro: Static trace: session expiry, Sign in pops Waiting (detachTrip only), the next rider's sign-in runs UserDataWipe.enterSessionAs, then run, resetInMemory and SafetyController.resetShared, which disposes without stopping. A grep of stopIfRecording callers found only the ride end, the kit closing and the Ride check card closing, none on the auth or wipe path. No test run.

verdicts.reason: On session expiry, di.dart:104-116 keeps everything and calls showMoveraRoot(SignIn) (app.dart:14-17), which removes the trip screen. Waiting's dispose only detaches the monitor (ride_check_controller.dart:255-258), and RideCheckController.dispose does not stop audio (ride_check_controller.dart:819-826). So a Ride check recording keeps running behind Sign in, with no Stop control anywhere. When a different rider signs in, enterSessionAs runs UserDataWipe.run (user_data_wipe.dart:165-173). That calls resetInMemory, then SafetyController.resetShared (user_data_wipe.dart:135; safety_controller.dart:71-77), which disposes both controllers and drops the only reference to the SafetyAudioService while _active is still recording. Nothing calls stopIfRecording on this path. If the same rider signs back in, there is no wipe and the card's Stop control is reachable again, so the fully orphaned microphone needs a rider change. The recording behind Sign in happens either way.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: the onSessionExpired callback, showMoveraRoot, Waiting dispose/detachTrip, enterSessionAs, run, resetInMemory and SafetyController.resetShared. Grepped every stopIfRecording caller in lib: Safety Kit sheet close, ride end, Ride check _close. None is on the expiry or wipe path. No test run.

confirmed.title: Share trip uses the stored tripShareContactIds whenever that list is non-empty, so deleted contacts are sent the trip and contacts marked 'Share trips' are left out
confirmed.description: Two sources of truth decide who receives a shared trip: `preferences.tripShareContactIds` (set by the Trip share checkboxes) and `EmergencyContact.shareTrips` (set by the checkbox and by the contact editor's 'Share trips' switch). The Trip share page shows a contact as checked if either is set (trip_share_page.dart:150-154), and the Safety Kit guard accepts either (ride_safety_kit.dart:214-217). startShare, however, passes `preferences.tripShareContactIds` whenever it is non-empty. The store then uses those ids verbatim, without checking that they still exist or are enabled (safety_store.dart:257-258). Nothing removes an id from that list when a contact is deleted, disabled, or has 'Share trips' turned off in the editor. The share is therefore sent to stale ids, contacts enabled only through shareTrips are omitted, and the success toast counts share.contactIds.length, stale ids included.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway test. Add contact Anna, tick her on Trip share (prefs ids [Anna]), delete Anna, then add Bo with 'Share trips' on. Safety Kit > Share trip: share.contactIds=[<Anna's deleted id>] and Bo is not included. The toast says 'Trip sharing started for 1 trusted contact.' Bo, the only real contact, never receives the trip. The same happens when a contact ticked on Trip share is later disabled or has 'Share trips' switched off in the editor: that contact still receives the ride.
confirmed.evidence:
safety_controller.dart:297-303
  Future<TripShare> startShare(String rideId) async {
    final share = await _session.startShare(
      rideId,
      contactIds: preferences.tripShareContactIds.isEmpty
          ? null
          : preferences.tripShareContactIds,
safety_store.dart:257-258
    final ids = contactIds ??
        _cache.contacts.where((c) => c.shareTrips && c.isEnabled).map((c) => c.id).toList();
ride_safety_kit.dart:228-229  share.isActive && share.contactIds.isNotEmpty ? context.l10n.tripSharingStarted(share.contactIds.length)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Derive the recipient list from the current contacts only: enabled contacts that are in the selected ids or have shareTrips. Prune ids for deleted or disabled contacts in deleteContact and updateContact. Better, keep a single source of truth for the selection.

verdicts.corrected_title: Share trip uses the stored tripShareContactIds whenever that list is non-empty, so deleted contacts are sent the trip and contacts marked 'Share trips' are left out
verdicts.reason: safety_controller.dart:297-303 passes preferences.tripShareContactIds whenever it is non-empty. safety_store.dart:257-258 uses those ids verbatim, and the mock echoes them back (safety_mock_api.dart:268). deleteContact (safety_store.dart:223-238) and updateContact never remove ids from that list. The Safety Kit guard (ride_safety_kit.dart:214-217) passes as long as any enabled contact has shareTrips, so Anna (ticked, then deleted) plus Bo (shareTrips on) gives share.contactIds=[Anna's id], and the toast at :228-229 counts that stale id. Trip sharing does not reach the intended contact. Rated medium, not high: it needs a ticked contact to be deleted or changed later.

The finder's throwaway test was not re-run.

verdicts.corrected_title: Share trip uses the stale tripShareContactIds list whenever it is non-empty: contacts that were disabled or had Share trips turned off still get the ride, and contacts enabled only through shareTrips are left out
verdicts.reason: safety_controller.dart:297-303 passes preferences.tripShareContactIds whenever it is non-empty. safety_store.dart:257-258 uses those ids as given and only filters `shareTrips && isEnabled` when the list is null. Only setTripShare (safety_controller.dart:288) writes tripShareContactIds, and deleteContact (safety_store.dart:223-238) and updateContact never prune it. The mock POST /rides/{id}/share stores body.contactIds as given (safety_mock_api.dart:262-275). The real harms are that a disabled contact, or one whose Share trips was switched off in the editor, still receives the live trip, and that a contact who only has shareTrips set is omitted.

The Safety Kit guard passes because Bo.shareTrips is true. startShare sends contactIds [Anna] and Bo is excluded. If Anna is then disabled, her id stays in the list and she still gets the share.

confirmed.title: Safety audio recording stops capturing when the app backgrounds or the 112 dialer opens; no iOS audio background mode or Android foreground service, and the default interruption mode pauses without resume
confirmed.description: NativeSafetyRecorder starts `record` with a bare RecordConfig. The audioInterruption default is AudioInterruptionMode.pause, which pauses on an interruption such as a phone call and needs a manual resume. Nothing in the app ever resumes. Info.plist UIBackgroundModes holds only remote-notification, not audio, so iOS suspends the recorder when the screen locks or the app leaves the foreground. On Android there is no foreground service (no FOREGROUND_SERVICE/FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE permission, no AndroidRecordConfig service), and since Android 9 a backgrounded app gets silence from the mic. The UI copy says recording continues until Stop or until the kit closes. SafetyAudioService.stop computes durationMs from wall-clock start/end, so the saved record claims the full duration. The Safety Kit and Ride check put 'Record audio' next to 'Call 112', and the 112 button opens the external dialer (backgrounds the app and starts a call), which is exactly the moment audio matters.
confirmed.failure_scenario: During a ride the rider taps Record audio, then Call 112 (or locks the phone). The dialer or call takes the foreground. iOS suspends or pauses the AVAudioRecorder, and Android delivers silence. When the rider returns, the card still shows 'Recording mm:ss'. Stop saves a file that holds only the seconds before the call, while the record lists the full wall-clock duration. Verified by reading the code and plugin defaults; nothing was run.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add the iOS 'audio' background mode and configure the audio session. On Android, record through the plugin's foreground service with FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE. Choose pauseResume, or listen to onStateChange and surface paused state. Compute the duration from the recorder, not the wall clock.

verdicts.reason: safety_recorder_native.dart:30-33 starts recording with a bare RecordConfig, so audioInterruption takes the plugin default AudioInterruptionMode.pause (record_platform_interface record_config.dart:89). No code in lib/features/safety listens to onStateChange or app lifecycle, and nothing ever resumes. ios/Runner/Info.plist UIBackgroundModes holds only remote-notification. AndroidManifest.xml has RECORD_AUDIO but no FOREGROUND_SERVICE or microphone foreground service. Call 112 opens tel:112 (safety README:66-67), which backgrounds the app or starts a call. safety_audio_service.dart:84-86 sets durationMs from wall-clock start/stop, so the saved record claims the full length even when audio stopped. No document marks this as intentional.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the recorder, the plugin defaults, Info.plist, AndroidManifest and SafetyAudioService.stop. This needs a device, so it was not reproduced; the iOS background suspension and the Android 9+ background mic silencing are documented platform behaviour.

verdicts.reason: safety_recorder_native.dart:30-33 starts the recorder with a bare RecordConfig, whose audioInterruption defaults to AudioInterruptionMode.pause (record_platform_interface-2.1.0 record_config.dart:89). Nothing in lib/features/safety resumes the recorder or watches its state. ios/Runner/Info.plist:48-51 lists only remote-notification in UIBackgroundModes, with no audio mode. AndroidManifest.xml:3-7 has RECORD_AUDIO but no foreground-service or microphone-service permission. On iOS and Android the system therefore stops mic capture once the app leaves the foreground, and Call 112 (ride_safety_kit.dart:166, which opens tel:112) does exactly that. safety_audio_service.dart:84-86 computes durationMs from wall-clock start and end, so the saved record claims the full duration even though the file holds less.
verdicts.repro: Checked by reading the code, the plugin source and the platform manifests. Not run on a device, since a widget test cannot show OS background or mic behaviour. The defaults and the missing background mode and foreground service are verified facts.

confirmed.title: Opening a Ride check card pops the Safety Kit sheet, which silently stops the rider's ongoing Safety Kit recording
confirmed.description: `_comeToFront` pops every route above the trip screen when a card opens. The Safety Kit tells the rider the recording keeps going until they tap Stop audio or close the kit ('safetyKitRecording'), so a rider who wants to keep recording leaves the kit open. When a trigger fires, popUntil closes the kit. The kit's dispose then calls `stopIfRecording(reason: 'sheet_closed')`. The recording ends at the moment the app has just detected something wrong, and neither the kit (now gone) nor the card says so. The card's Record row now shows 'Record audio'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider feels uneasy, opens the Safety Kit and taps Record audio, leaving the sheet open. Two minutes later the car stops off-route and the long-stop card opens. The kit is popped and the recording is stopped and saved. The rider sees the card with 'Record audio' and has to notice and tap again. Nothing was recorded in between.

confirmed.title: Safety Kit 'Contact 112' sends no SOS to Movera when the phone dialer cannot be opened
confirmed.description: _call112 calls emergency.callEmergencyNumber() first and _ctl.sos() only after it. SystemEmergencyDialer.open throws EmergencyCallException whenever launchUrl(tel:) returns false or throws. That exception jumps to the outer `on EmergencyCallException` handler, which only shows a toast, so the SOS event for the ride is never posted. RideCheckController.call112 handles the same failure by still alerting the safety team (_sendAlert runs regardless of the dialer result), so the Safety Kit is the only path where a failed dial also drops the alert.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a device that cannot place calls (Android tablet without a dialer, iPad, some in-app browsers), a rider in an emergency during a trip taps 'Contact 112' in the Safety Kit. launchUrl returns false, and the rider sees 'Could not open the system phone dialer.' Movera is not told either: there is no call and no SOS. That is the moment the in-app alert matters most.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_safety_kit.dart:166-182 `try { await _ctl.emergency.callEmergencyNumber(); try { final registered = await _ctl.sos(rideId: widget.rideId); ... } on EmergencyCallException catch (error) { ... MoveraToast.show(context, error.message); }`
emergency_call_service.dart:38-40 `final opened = await _launcher(uri); if (!opened) { throw EmergencyCallException(L10n.current.dialerOpenFailed); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Send the SOS whatever the dialer outcome (or before dialing), and report both results to the rider.

confirmed.title: Positional legacy ids collide after a delete, so deleting one custom place removes two and editing one overwrites another
confirmed.description: `_withIds` gives every custom place that has no stored id the id `place_legacy_$i`, where i is its current position in the list. Home's own add path (`HomePlacesController.applyResolved` case 'custom') appends `SavedPlaceData(title: type, type: type, address: address)` with no id, so places added from Home never have one. Once Saved Places writes the list, those positional ids are stored permanently (save and remove both persist the output of `_withIds`). After a delete shrinks the list, a place Home adds later lands at an index whose `place_legacy_<i>` id is already stored on another place. `remove` filters with `item['id'] != id`, so it drops every place with that id. `save` uses `indexWhere`, so it replaces the first place with that id instead of the one being edited.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Home, add a 'gym' place (A) and then a 'restaurant' place (B); neither gets an id. In Saved Places, delete A: B is stored as place_legacy_1. On Home, add a 'school' place (C): the list is now [B(place_legacy_1), C(no id, index 1)], so C also reads as place_legacy_1. Delete C in Saved Places and B disappears as well. Edit C instead and B's entry is overwritten with C's data while C's old entry stays.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Assign a fresh unique id (`place_${newRequestId()}`) to id-less entries and persist it, rather than a position-derived id. Also give places added from Home an id.

Home's add path (home_places_controller.dart:143-146) appends SavedPlaceData without an id, and Home reloads from the store on changes (home.dart:174; HomePlacesController.load keeps stored ids via fromJson). After a delete shrinks the list, a later Home-added place gets an index whose positional id is already stored on another place. remove filters out every item with that id (:124), and save's indexWhere (:91) overwrites the first match.

Output: `AUDIT ids=[restaurant:place_legacy_1, school:place_legacy_1]`. Then deleting school alone printed `AUDIT afterDeleteC=[]` (restaurant was deleted too). 1 test passed. File deleted.

confirmed.description: The date/time step shows `cancelBeforeAssigned`: 'You can cancel without a fee before a driver is assigned. Final terms are shown before booking.' The fee actually charged (`ScheduledRideRules.cancelTermsFor`) depends only on minutes before pickup (free while `minutesBeforePickup >= freeMin`, default 60 or the zone's per-category rule). Driver assignment does not matter; the only exception is a missed pickup. Nothing in the scheduled SelectRide/checkout path shows the cancel terms before booking: `cancelTermsFor`/`cancelRule` are only used on the Upcoming and Terms pages.

The sheet says 'Cancelling costs kr 50' and the fee is recorded. The booking screen had promised a free cancel before assignment, and no terms were shown before booking.

app_en.arb:1667 `"cancelBeforeAssigned": "You can cancel without a fee before a driver is assigned. Final terms are shown before booking."`
select_date_time.dart:532 `context.l10n.cancelBeforeAssigned,`
scheduled_ride_rules.dart:100-104 `final fee = CancelFeeCalculator.reservation(rule, fare, ride.scheduledPickupAt.difference(now).inMinutes);`

Final terms are shown before booking.', app_en.arb:1668). The real fee comes from scheduled_ride_rules.dart:86-110 cancelTermsFor, which uses only CancelFeeCalculator.reservation(rule, fare, minutesBeforePickup). Driver assignment only matters in the missedByMovera case (pickup time passed with no driver). The default slot is minimumPickup = roundToFive(now + 30 min) (stockholm_schedule.dart:33, leadMinutes=30 at :65), which is inside the default 60-minute free window, so the default booking is already in the paid window before any driver is assigned. verdicts.reason: select_date_time.dart:583 shows l10n.cancelBeforeAssigned ('cancel without a fee before a driver is assigned. Final terms are shown before booking.', app_en.arb:1668). confirmed.title: Schedule Continue exposes a hard-coded English semantics label with no tap action, hiding the localized and busy text
confirmed.description: The Continue CTA on the date/time step is wrapped as `Semantics(container: true, label: 'Schedule Continue', button: true, enabled: enabled, child: ExcludeSemantics(child: ElevatedButton(onPressed: ...)))`. The literal label replaces the localized visible text (continueLabel = 'Continuer'/'Fortsätt', or 'Continuing…' while busy). ExcludeSemantics removes the ElevatedButton's tap action, and the outer Semantics has no onTap, so the node cannot be activated by assistive tech. test/scheduled_rides/phase81_schedule_continue_test.dart is titled 'Schedule Continue is accessible' but only does `tester.tap(find.bySemanticsLabel('Schedule Continue'))`, a pointer tap, so it passes either way.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Swedish TalkBack user on Book for later hears 'Schedule Continue' in English, hears no 'Continuing…' busy state, and double-tapping does nothing because the node has no tap action. They cannot leave the date/time step.
confirmed.evidence:
select_date_time.dart:789-797 `child: Semantics(
                container: true,
                label: 'Schedule Continue',
                button: true,
                enabled: enabled,
                child: ExcludeSemantics(
                  child: ElevatedButton(
                    onPressed: enabled ? _goNext : null,` ; test phase81_schedule_continue_test.dart:35,53 `find.bySemanticsLabel('Schedule Continue')` + `tester.tap(...)`

verdicts.reason: select_date_time.dart:844-851 wraps the button in Semantics(container: true, label: 'Schedule Continue', button: true, enabled: enabled) around ExcludeSemantics(ElevatedButton). confirmed.title: 'Open settings' in the push primer calls Geolocator.openAppSettings, which throws UnsupportedError on web
confirmed.description: `_openSettings` defaults to `Geolocator.openAppSettings`. geolocator_web implements it as `throw _unsupported('openAppSettings')`. The primer is reachable on web in release-like builds (gate `enabled = !allowsMockTransport`): when the browser's `Notification.requestPermission()` answers 'denied' (or 'default'), `FlutterFirebasePushGateway.requestPermission` maps it to `PushAuthorizationStatus.denied`, `PushPermissionGate._register` stores `blockedBySystem`, and both the sheet (`_blocked`) and the Notifications screen banner then offer 'Open settings'. Tapping it throws inside the button callback; nothing opens, the rider gets no feedback, and the error is recorded as a crash by the zone handler. The location notice already handles this case correctly via `locationSettingsOpenerFor(isWeb: ...)` returning null, so the web branch was simply missed here.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Staging web build, rider taps 'Turn on' and declines the browser notification prompt. Next visit to Notifications shows 'Ride updates are off' -> 'Open settings'; tapping does nothing visible and logs `zone.error UnsupportedError: openAppSettings() has not been implemented on the web`.
confirmed.evidence: lib/shared/widgets/push_permission_primer.dart:85-86 `Future<void> _openSettings() async { await (widget.openAppSettings ?? Geolocator.openAppSettings)(); }`; line 149 `onPressed: _busy ? null : (_blocked ? _openSettings : _turnOn)`; geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/geolocator_web.dart `Future<bool> openAppSettings() => throw _unsupported('openAppSettings');`; lib/core/notifications/push_permission_gate.dart:83-86 stores blockedBySystem on PushPermissionDeniedException.
confirmed.suggested_fix: On web hide the settings action (or show copy explaining the browser's site-permission UI) the way `locationSettingsOpenerFor` does; wrap the call in try/catch and show a toast on failure.

verdicts.reason: In push_permission_primer.dart:85-86, _openSettings defaults to Geolocator.openAppSettings, and on web geolocator_web-4.1.4 implements that as `throw _unsupported('openAppSettings')` (geolocator_web.dart:128). The gate is enabled for non-mock flavors (di.dart:354-357), and on those flavors push is FirebasePushService (di.dart:121-123). On web, a browser 'denied' or 'default' answer maps to PushAuthorizationStatus.denied (firebase_push_service.dart:83-90). That throws PushPermissionDeniedException, and the gate stores blockedBySystem (push_permission_gate.dart:83-86). The primer then switches to `_blocked`, and the Notifications screen banner (notifications.dart:72, built with no openAppSettings override) reopens it with startBlocked. The primary 'Open settings' button calls _openSettings with no kIsWeb check and no try/catch. Tapping it throws UnsupportedError into the zone, and nothing visible happens. The location notice handles the same case on web by returning null (location_access_notice.dart:23); the push primer has no such check.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: notifications.dart:72 PushStatusBanner -> _open(blocked) -> PushPrimerSheet(startBlocked) -> FilledButton onPressed _openSettings -> Geolocator.openAppSettings -> GeolocatorPlugin (web) openAppSettings throws. Confirmed the throw in /root/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/geolocator_web.dart:128.

verdicts.reason: push_permission_primer.dart:85-86 calls Geolocator.openAppSettings by default, and neither caller injects an opener: maybeShowPushPrimer at auth_navigation.dart:33 and PushStatusBanner at notifications.dart:72. geolocator_web 4.1.4 (pubspec.lock:354-361) defines openAppSettings as `throw _unsupported('openAppSettings')` (geolocator_web.dart:128,151-155), which raises UnsupportedError. Web push is a supported path in release-like builds: di.dart:121-122 uses FirebasePushService when !allowsMockTransport, register() has web/VAPID handling (firebase_push_service.dart:204-213), and a browser denial maps to PushPermissionDeniedException → blockedBySystem (push_permission_gate.dart:83-86). The sheet then shows 'Open settings' wired to _openSettings (:149), and the banner reopens the sheet with startBlocked. Nothing catches the error, and location_access_notice.dart:23 shows the intended web guard (return null on web) that this code lacks. Not reachable in the mock demo build, where the gate is disabled (di.dart:356).
verdicts.repro: Traced the path by hand: di.dart push selection → PushPermissionGate.accept → FirebasePushService.register throws PushPermissionDeniedException → _turnOn sets _blocked → button calls _openSettings → Geolocator.openAppSettings → the geolocator_web plugin, whose source in the pub cache throws UnsupportedError('openAppSettings is not supported on the web platform.'). Not run, because flutter test runs on the VM, not the web plugin.

confirmed.title: Web FCM worker suppresses pushes when a tab is visible but never forwards them, so FirebaseMessaging.onMessage (foreground in-app push) never fires on web
confirmed.description: The worker loads no Firebase SDK (the test enforces no importScripts). In the Firebase JS SDK, the page's onMessage only fires when the messaging service worker posts the payload to window clients ({isFirebaseMessaging:true, messageType:'push-received'}). The browser delivers push events only to the service worker, never to the page. This worker sees a visible client and returns undefined. It shows no notification and calls no client.postMessage. The comment's claim that 'A visible Movera tab receives the message through onMessage instead' is false. FirebasePushService._attachInboundStreams subscribes to FirebaseMessaging.onMessage (firebase_push_service.dart:126), and that stream never emits on web, so PushCoordinator never shows the in-app ride update.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Production/staging web build with MOVERA_FIREBASE_* and VAPID set (as built in batch6-phase78-push.yml). The rider accepted ride updates and has the tab open. The backend sends 'driver arrived'. The SW sees a visible client and returns. No system notification appears, onMessage never fires, and no in-app toast is shown. The update is silently lost. Verified by reading the code; nothing was run.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When a client is visible, postMessage the payload to the clients in the Firebase internal format, or importScripts the Firebase messaging SW SDK and let it route foreground messages. Otherwise always show the notification.

verdicts.corrected_title: Web FCM worker suppresses pushes when a tab is visible but never forwards them, so FirebaseMessaging.onMessage (foreground in-app push) never fires on web
verdicts.reason: web/firebase-messaging-sw.js:73-78 returns without notifying when any window client is visible, and it never calls client.postMessage. The worker deliberately loads no Firebase SDK (header lines 8-11). The page-side Firebase JS onMessage, wrapped by firebase_messaging_web interop/messaging.dart:84-104, is fed only by isFirebaseMessaging postMessages from the messaging SW, because browser push events go only to the service worker. So the comment's claim that a visible tab gets the message through onMessage is false. FirebasePushService._attachInboundStreams subscribes to FirebaseMessaging.onMessage (firebase_push_service.dart:126, :247), and that stream gets nothing on web. The foreground push is dropped with neither a system notification nor an in-app message. This only applies to web builds configured with Firebase and VAPID (built in batch6-phase78-push.yml:97-99); the demo is inert. Ride state itself still comes from the backend and realtime, so the lost item is the push surface rather than ride truth. Hence medium.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the SW push handler, firebase_push_service.dart getToken(serviceWorkerScriptPath) and onForegroundMessage, and the firebase_messaging_web 4.2.5 interop. Nothing was run, because a browser and an FCM project are required.

verdicts.corrected_title: Custom FCM service worker swallows pushes while a Movera tab is visible, so web foreground pushes produce neither a notification nor an onMessage event
verdicts.reason: web/firebase-messaging-sw.js:73-78 returns without doing anything when any window client is visible. It loads no Firebase SDK (test/platform/audit_fix_release_readiness_test.dart:188 enforces no importScripts) and never calls client.postMessage. In the Firebase JS SDK used by firebase_messaging_web 4.2.5, the page's onMessage fires only when the service worker posts a message flagged isFirebaseMessaging/push-received. Push events go only to the service worker, never to the page. So FirebaseMessaging.onMessage (firebase_push_service.dart:126) never emits on web, and the comment at sw.js:74 is wrong. The file is inert in the demo build, which has no Firebase defines. In a build with Firebase configured, a rider with the tab visible loses the push entirely. Ride state still reconciles from the backend, which limits the impact to a missed alert or in-app toast.

Path: push event -> sw.js:72 matchAll -> visible client -> `return undefined` (no showNotification, no postMessage). confirmed.title: Web auth-preview: a wrong OTP while an earlier session's tokens are still in sessionStorage expires the session and re-roots Sign in instead of showing 'wrong code'
confirmed.description: `_send` enters the refresh/retry/expire path for any 401 whose request carried an access token (line 89); the comment relies on OTP verify never carrying one. `RideRestoreCoordinator` returns `SignIn()` when `AppEnv.current.authPreview && snapshot == null` (ride_restore_coordinator.dart lines 432-434, 449-452) without clearing tokens, and on web the tokens live in this tab's sessionStorage, so a reload with `?auth_preview=1` after an earlier sign-in reaches `PhoneVerify` with tokens present. A wrong code -> mock `401 invalid_otp` -> `_refreshAccess` (mock accepts any `mock-refresh-*`) -> retry -> 401 again -> `_expireSession` clears tokens, calls `onSessionExpired` (`LocationRepository.clearLastGoodFix()` + `showMoveraRoot(SignIn())`), then throws; `PhoneVerify` is unmounted so its `_error` is never shown.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Web demo with `?auth_preview=1`: rider who signed in earlier in the tab types one wrong OTP digit; instead of 'wrong code' the screen jumps back to the first Sign in step, the stored session is gone and the last good location fix is wiped.
confirmed.evidence:
api_client.dart:89-113 `if (response.statusCode == 401 && access?.isNotEmpty == true) { // An OTP rejection is not an expired session. Only requests that carried an access token enter the refresh/retry path. final refresh = await _refreshAccess(access!); ... if (replacement == null || response.statusCode == 401) { await _expireSession(replacement ?? access); } }`
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:449-452 `if (snapshot == null && AppEnv.current.authPreview) { reportRestoreSurface('signInPreview'); return const SignIn(); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Exclude `/api/v1/auth/*` paths from the refresh/expire path (or let callers opt out), or clear tokens before showing the preview Sign in.

verdicts.reason: api_client.dart:89 enters the refresh, retry and expire path for any 401 on a request that carried an access token, and that includes /api/v1/auth/otp/verify. The case is reachable on the web demo with ?auth_preview=1. env.dart:67-69 enables the preview, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:449-452 roots SignIn without checking or clearing tokens, the tokens persist in this tab's sessionStorage (secure_token_store.dart:9-17), and AuthRepository and PhoneVerify never clear them before verifying. A wrong code gets a mock 401 invalid_otp (in_process_mock_client.dart:433-435). The refresh succeeds because the mock accepts mock-refresh-*, the retry gets 401 again, and _expireSession (api_client.dart:220-226) clears the tokens and runs onSessionExpired, which calls clearLastGoodFix and showMoveraRoot(SignIn()) (di.dart:104-116, app.dart:15-17). PhoneVerify is replaced, so its 'wrong code' error is never shown. Production and staging are not affected, because SignIn shows there only when hasSession() is false.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r6_otp_test.dart (deleted afterwards): MemoryTokenStore pre-seeded with mock-access/mock-refresh, ApiClient(client: InProcessMockClient()), OTP request, then verify with code 9999. Output: `AUDIT R6: err=ApiError(unauthenticated, invalid_otp, ...) expired=1 access=null` -- onSessionExpired fired once and the tokens were cleared.

In the web demo with ?auth_preview=1 after an earlier sign-in in the tab, one wrong OTP is treated as session expiry: tokens are cleared and Sign in is re-rooted instead of showing 'wrong code'
verdicts.reason: api_client.dart:89 decides whether to refresh only by whether a stored access token exists, not by path. ride_restore_coordinator.dart:449-452 (and :433) returns SignIn whenever `authPreview && snapshot == null` and does not clear tokens. No code in the sign-in flow clears them either (the only callers of `_tokens.clear` are signOut and clearLocalSession, auth_repository.dart:135-141). On web, tokens live in tab sessionStorage (secure_token_store.dart:17), so they survive the reload. A wrong code gives mock 401 invalid_otp (in_process_mock_client.dart:433-435). The mock refresh accepts any `mock-refresh-*` token (:479-491), the retry gets 401 again, and `_expireSession` clears the tokens and calls onSessionExpired (di.dart:104-116: clearLastGoodFix plus showSignInOnSessionExpired). That unmounts PhoneVerify, so its 'wrong code' error is never shown. This path exists only in the web demo flavor's auth-preview mode (env.dart:67-69), so severity is low.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_vq7c1b3_test.dart: ApiClient(InProcessMockClient, MemoryTokenStore pre-filled with mock-access/mock-refresh tokens, onSessionExpired counter), then AuthRepository.requestOtp, then verifyOtp(code '9999'). Output: `AUDIT6 error=ApiError(unauthenticated, invalid_otp, ...) expired=1 access=null refresh=null`. The session was expired and both tokens were wiped by one wrong code. Test file deleted.

confirmed.title: `PATCH /rides/{id}` offer raise / searching edit changes the fare, pickup and destination without `_touch`, so version, updatedAt, sequence and eventId stay unchanged
confirmed.description: The non-routeChange PATCH branch (lines 947-1011) calls `_setFare(ride, fare + increase)` and rewrites `pickupAddress/pickupLat/pickupLng/destination*` but never calls `_touch(ride)`, unlike every other mutation (route change line 895, cancel via `_apply`, feedback line 646). The mock's own rule (lines 1351-1361) is 'one committed change: version + 1, new updatedAt, next sequence/eventId' and CONTRACT.md §1 requires a stale `expectedVersion` to be refused. After a raise the trip still reports the old `version`/`updatedAt`/`eventId`, so a second screen's `expectedVersion` from before the raise is accepted, `ApiRideRealtime` dedupes the projection by the unchanged eventId, and `updatedAt` misreports when the trip last changed. Reproduced: `AUDIT B2: fare 29100 -> 34100; version 1 -> 1; eventId ev_..._1 -> ev_..._1; updatedAt unchanged`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo flavor: rider raises the offer by 50 kr while searching; the projection's `version`, `updatedAt` and `eventId` do not move. A command sent from another tab/screen with the pre-raise `expectedVersion` is not refused as stale, and a polling consumer never sees a new event for the change.
confirmed.evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:989-1010 `final increase = _offerIncreaseMinor(body, rideCurrency); final fare = _fareMinor(ride); if (increase != null && fare != null) { _setFare(ride, fare + increase); ride['offerIncrease'] = _money(increase, rideCurrency); } if (body['pickupAddress'] != null) { ride['pickupAddress'] = body['pickupAddress']; } ... payload = {'code': 'OK', 'ride': ride, 'requestId': requestId};` (no `_touch`)
in_process_mock_client.dart:1351-1361 `/// One committed change: version + 1, new updatedAt, and the next server-assigned realtime sequence ... static void _touch(`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call `_touch(ride)` after applying the offer raise / pickup / destination edit in that branch.

verdicts.reason: In the searching-edit branch of PATCH /rides/{id} (lib/core/api/in_process_mock_client.dart:986-1010), _setFare and the pickup/destination rewrites are never followed by _touch(ride). _setFare (:1942-1945) changes only the fare. Every other committed change goes through _touch (:1354-1362), which bumps version, updatedAt and sequence/eventId. As a result, a later command carrying the pre-raise expectedVersion passes _versionMismatch (:1448-1456), against R-O2 and CONTRACT.md §1. Realtime events with the unchanged sequence/eventId are dropped by RealtimeGate as duplicates (finding_driver_controller.dart:359-367). Impact is limited: the rider who raised the offer updates its own snapshot from the PATCH response (finding_driver_controller.dart:828-860), so the fare it shows is right. Raises are also additive and keyed, so there is no money harm, only broken stale-write protection and an unchanged change marker in the demo backend.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r89_test.dart (since deleted) against InProcessMockClient: booked a ride, then PATCHed offerIncrease 10 kr with expectedVersion 1. Output: `R8 fare {amountMinor: 30100, currency: SEK} version 1 -> 1 eventId ev_ride_..._1 -> ev_ride_..._1 updatedAt same=true`. A second PATCH (pickupAddress) with the pre-raise expectedVersion 1 was accepted: `R8 stale-version edit accepted: OK`. Test passed: `+1: All tests passed!`.

verdicts.reason: The non-routeChange PATCH branch in lib/core/api/in_process_mock_client.dart:989-1010 calls _setFare and rewrites pickup/destination but never calls _touch (defined at :1351-1361 as 'one committed change: version + 1, new updatedAt, next sequence/eventId'). The route-change branch does call it at :895. The real caller is FindingDriverController's offer raise (lib/features/finding_driver/application/finding_driver_controller.dart:820-829), which PATCHes {offerIncrease, expectedVersion}. After the raise the version does not move, so _versionMismatch (:1448-1465) still accepts the pre-raise expectedVersion. The rider's own screen takes the fare from the response, so the visible effect is limited to stale-version protection and realtime dedupe by eventId. That is a contract deviation, not a main-path failure.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c3b1_rider_test.dart (since deleted) quoted and booked through the mock, then sent PATCH /api/v1/rides/{id} with offerIncrease 1000 öre and expectedVersion=1. confirmed.title: The Q40 pickup-move limit is checked per move against the current pickup, so chained moves after accept take the pickup past the limit without a cancel/rebook
confirmed.description: After accept, the pickup may move only `maxPickupMoveMeters`. Both the client (`preview`: `ride.pickupLat` vs the new point) and the server (`_pickupMoveMeters`: `ride['pickupLat']` vs the body) measure from the pickup as it stands now, and each applied change overwrites it. The pickup the driver accepted is never kept, so repeating the change moves the pickup by the limit each time with no total cap.
confirmed.failure_scenario: With a 300 m limit and the driver on the way, the rider moves the pickup 290 m four times in a row. Each move is accepted, and the driver is sent about 1.2 km from the accepted pickup without the 'that's a new ride' refusal.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the pickup at accept (`acceptedPickupLat/Lng`) and measure every later move from it, on both client and server.

verdicts.reason: The mock server checks the limit as the distance from the current ride['pickupLat'/'pickupLng'] (in_process_mock_client.dart:1812-1825 and 1849-1855). Each applied change overwrites the pickup (lines 882-885), and no accepted-pickup anchor is stored anywhere. The client preview does the same (route_change_controller.dart:158-165). CONTRACT.md:160 says 'Move pickup up to N m, further = cancel/rebook', and the mock's own comment calls it 'the accepted pickup moved'. Chaining small moves gets around that limit.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u14_test.dart against InProcessMockClient (since deleted). Booked a ride, set driver_to_pickup, then applied four route-quote + PATCH routeChange pickup moves of about 278 m each (zone limit 500 m). Every move returned 200: 'move 0 ok pickupLat=59.3318 … move 3 ok pickupLat=59.3393', about 1.1 km from the accepted pickup. Result: '00:00 +1: All tests passed!'

verdicts.corrected_title: The Q40 pickup-move limit is checked per move against the current pickup, so chained moves after accept take the pickup past the limit without a cancel/rebook
verdicts.reason: _routeChangeDenied (in_process_mock_client.dart:1849-1855) compares the body with ride['pickupLat'/'pickupLng'] through _pickupMoveMeters (1808-1826). The applied change overwrites those fields (in_process_mock_client.dart:882-886). The client does the same against ride.pickupLat (route_change_controller.dart:156-165). Nothing keeps the pickup as it was at accept, and there is no cumulative cap. CONTRACT.md:162 defines the rule as 'Move pickup up to N m, further = cancel/rebook', and openapi.yaml:6876 says 'How far the rider may move the pickup after accept; further = cancel and rebook'. Chaining moves defeats that rule. Impact: the driver is sent far from the accepted pickup, but receives a pickup_moved notice each time. Low.
verdicts.repro: Ran the throwaway test test/_audit_u13u14_test.dart (since deleted). It books a ride, sets it to driver_to_pickup, then makes 4 moves of about 445 m each (limit 500, ZoneDefaults.maxPickupMoveMeters) using route-quote and PATCH routeChange. Output: 'move 1 ok ... move 4 ok pickup=59.3453 status=driver_to_pickup' and 'total from accepted: 1779 m'. All 4 moves returned 200.

confirmed.title: Mock safety PIN is predictable: on the web demo it is always one of 10 values ending in 000, and the mock saves it in plain text
confirmed.description: `_newPin` sets `n = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch % 10000`. On dart2js, `DateTime.now()` has millisecond precision (the microsecond part is 0), so `microsecondsSinceEpoch` is always a multiple of 1000 and `n` is `(ms % 10) * 1000`. Every PIN issued or rotated on the public web demo, the transport the Pages build actually runs, ends in 000: there are only 10 possible PINs, and the digit is just the last digit of the current millisecond. The rider page then says 'Your driver must confirm your PIN before starting the trip' over a code anyone can guess. The mock also writes the digits in plaintext to localStorage (`movera_safety_demo_v1`, persist() line 87-94), although safety_data_sources.dart:146-149 says web keeps the PIN 'in memory only (P-06) — never in this plaintext prefs blob'. Verified by reading only (no web test runner).
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the GitHub Pages demo, Safety › PIN shows e.g. '7000'. Change PIN gives '3000', '0000' and so on, always ending in 000.
confirmed.evidence:
safety_mock_api.dart:155-161 `final now = DateTime.now().toUtc(); final n = now.microsecondsSinceEpoch % 10000; return { 'pinId': 'pin_${now.microsecondsSinceEpoch}', ... 'pin': n.toString().padLeft(4, '0'),`
:87-94 `await prefs.setString(storageKey, jsonEncode({'preferences': preferences, 'pin': pin, ...}))`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Generate the mock PIN with `Random.secure().nextInt(10000)`. Do not persist the digits in the plaintext demo blob.

verdicts.corrected_title: Mock safety PIN is predictable: on the web demo it is always one of 10 values ending in 000, and the mock saves it in plain text
verdicts.reason: lib/core/api/safety_mock_api.dart:155-158 builds the PIN as DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch % 10000. On web (dart2js), DateTime only has millisecond precision, so microsecondsSinceEpoch is ms*1000 and the PIN is (ms % 10)*1000. Every PIN made at :35, :113 and :202 is one of 0000, 1000 ... 9000. This is the mock backend (safetyMockForProcess, :491) that the web demo runs on, so nothing real can be bypassed. The visible fault is that the demo shows a fake-looking, guessable PIN. The plain-text save in persist() (:87-94) is the mock server's own state, not the client cache that the P-06 comment at safety_data_sources.dart:146-149 describes, so that part is only a minor mismatch.
verdicts.repro: Read _newPin and its three call sites. Relied on dart2js DateTime having millisecond precision (microsecond part always 0). No web test was run.

verdicts.reason: The arithmetic is right. On dart2js DateTime.now() has millisecond precision with microsecond == 0, so microsecondsSinceEpoch % 10000 == (ms % 10) * 1000, giving only 10 possible PINs. But this is the in-process mock backend's own state (lib/core/api/safety_mock_api.dart:155-161), standing in for a server that issues PINs ('serverAuthoritative': false). On the web demo no real driver ever checks the PIN, so a guessable code protects nothing. The localStorage blob movera_safety_demo_v1 (:11, :87-94) is the mock server's persistence, not the app's SafetyCache. The P-06 promise in safety_data_sources.dart:146-149 applies to the app-side cache, and that code still holds the PIN in memory on web. A real backend generates its own PIN. Under the rules, mock demo data with no false success shown is not a defect.
verdicts.repro: Worked the values by hand. dart2js DateTime is millisecond-based, e.g. ms=1729500000123 gives us=1729500000123000 and us % 10000 = 3000. Read safety_mock_api.dart:80-161 and safety_data_sources.dart:135-160 to confirm the plaintext write is the mock server's store, separate from the app cache's P-06 handling.

verdicts.corrected_title: Mock PIN generator collapses to 10 values on web (dart2js), so the public demo always shows a PIN ending in 000 and Change PIN keeps the same digits about 1 time in 10
verdicts.reason:
Both checkers agree on the arithmetic, and a dart2js run now confirms it. What is left is whether this counts as a defect. It does, but only as a low one, and not for the security reason the finder gave.

1. The fault is real. lib/core/api/safety_mock_api.dart:156-157 sets the PIN to `DateTime.now().toUtc().microsecondsSinceEpoch % 10000`. In the installed SDK (3.13.5), the web DateTime in dart-sdk/lib/_internal/js_shared/lib/date_time_patch.dart:78-87 sets `_microsecond = 0` for `_now()` and `_nowUtc()`, and line 165 defines `microsecondsSinceEpoch => 1000 * _value + _microsecond`. So every PIN is (ms % 10) * 1000. The Wasm path is the same: wasm/js_common/date_patch_patch.dart:15 uses `Date.now() * 1000`.

2. The public demo hits this path. .github/workflows/publish-web-live.yml:45-48 builds web with `lib/main_demo.dart` and `MOVERA_FLAVOR=demo`. lib/app/config/env.dart:81-84 turns on mock transport for the demo flavor, and lib/core/api/api_client.dart:28-31 then uses `InProcessMockClient(persistSafety: true)`, which gets its Safety mock from `safetyMockForProcess()` (safety_mock_api.dart:491). `_newPin` is called at :35 (reset), :113 (first PIN) and :202 (POST /pin/rotate). SafetyStore.load (lib/features/safety/data/safety_store.dart:57) and rotatePin (:118) show these digits as they are, in pin_verification_page.dart:119-124 and waiting_sheet_bits.dart:542-543.

3. The rider can see it. Every PIN on the live demo is one of 0000, 1000 ... 9000. Because the new PIN is drawn from the same 10 values, Change PIN returns the digits already on screen about 10% of the time, and no error appears (safety_controller.dart:202-210 only sets an error on an exception). The code means to produce a plausible 4-digit PIN that stays put; the FLOW-9 comments at :8-10 and :56 show effort spent on exactly that. On the VM the same code gives about 10,000 values. So this is a platform bug in the mock, not the excluded case of "this is a mock".

4. The parts of the finding I reject:
   - **Security.** Nothing real is exposed. The mock never verifies a PIN (ARCH-22 at :206-207; docs/API_V1_MOCK.md, Safety section), and release flavors cannot use mock transport (env.dart:81-84).
   - **Plain-text PIN in browser storage.** The plain-text `movera_safety_demo_v1` write (:87-94) is intentional FLOW-9 persistence of the stand-in server's state. The P-06 promise in safety_data_sources.dart:146-149 and secure_ride_pin_store.dart:10-14 covers the app-side SafetyCache, which correctly saves only the '0000' placeholder (safety_data_sources.dart:195-197). That part is not a defect.

Severity is low: the effect is cosmetic and behavioural on the demo only, and touches no data, money or security.
verdicts.repro:
I copied the arithmetic of `_newPin` (safety_mock_api.dart:156-157, 161) into a standalone script, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/fdaddc0c-1375-5df5-ab76-276042ee8e3e/scratchpad/u16/pin.dart. The script calls it in a loop for 300 ms and collects the distinct values. I ran it two ways:
- Compiled with `dart compile js -O1` (dart2js, SDK 3.13.5 from /opt/flutter) and run under /opt/node22/bin/node, it printed `calls=863857 distinct=10 values=[0000, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000, 8000, 9000]`.
- Run on the Dart VM, the same file printed `calls=245166 distinct=9865 values=[0000, 0001, 0002, ...]`.

I also read the SDK source: js_shared/lib/date_time_patch.dart:78-87 (`_microsecond = 0` in `_now`/`_nowUtc`) and :165 (`microsecondsSinceEpoch => 1000 * _value + _microsecond`). I traced the call path publish-web-live.yml:45-48 (demo flavor), then env.dart:81-84, api_client.dart:28-31, in_process_mock_client.dart:166, :1208-1219, and safety_mock_api.dart:35/113/202, and from there to safety_store.dart:57/118 and pin_verification_page.dart:119-124.

I put no file in the repository. The scratch script is in the scratchpad only.

confirmed.title: PickupSchedule.zoneNow builds the zone wall-clock as a device-local DateTime: for a Tunis pickup on an EU-DST phone, during 02:00-02:59 Tunis on the EU spring-forward day, the earliest legal pickup is pushed an hour late
confirmed.description: `wallTime` computes the correct zone wall-clock components and then constructs `DateTime(year, month, day, hour, ...)` with the local-time constructor. Dart resolves a non-existent local time (the device's spring-forward gap) by shifting it, so when the device time zone differs from the zone's (RiderZones has Europe/Stockholm, Europe/Paris, Africa/Tunis; Tunis has no DST) the picker shows the wrong hour. `toUtc` (lines 74-86) uses `DateTime.utc`, so the round trip is asymmetric. Also the doc comment on `toUtc` says the summer offset is used in the non-existent hour, but the two-step guess yields the winter offset: wall 02:30 Stockholm on 2026-03-29 -> asUtc 02:30Z -> offsetAt = +2 -> guess 00:30Z -> offsetAt(00:30Z) = +1 -> 01:30Z (= 03:30 wall), not 00:30Z.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider with a Swedish phone books a reservation in the Tunis zone for 2026-03-29 02:30 Tunis time (instant 01:30Z): `wallTime('Africa/Tunis', instant)` -> `DateTime(2026,3,29,2,30)` in Europe/Stockholm does not exist -> shows 03:30. The reverse mapping of the shown value then lands on a different instant than the one stored.
confirmed.evidence: lib/core/config/zone_clock.dart:57-69 `static DateTime wallTime(String timeZone, DateTime instant) { ... return DateTime(local.year, local.month, local.day, local.hour, local.minute, local.second, local.millisecond); }` ; :71-73 doc `In the hour that does not exist (spring forward) the summer offset is used` vs :84-85 `final guess = asUtc.subtract(offsetAt(timeZone, asUtc)); return asUtc.subtract(offsetAt(timeZone, guess));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return `DateTime.utc(local.year, ..., local.millisecond)` (a UTC-flagged carrier of wall components, which never shifts) and have the pickers treat it as offset-free; fix the toUtc doc comment or the algorithm to match.

verdicts.reason: zone_clock.dart:60-68 rebuilds the zone's wall-clock time with the local DateTime constructor, so the device's DST rules apply to it. PickupSchedule.zoneNow (stockholm_schedule.dart:29-30) feeds this value to minimumPickup and the pickers, and scheduled_rides_controller.dart:64 maps the chosen value back with toUtc. With the device in Europe/Stockholm, 01:30Z on 2026-03-29 in the Tunis zone gives 03:30 instead of 02:30. The round trip then lands on 02:30Z, not 01:30Z. This is real but very narrow: once a year, a one-hour night window, and only when the device time zone differs from the pickup zone's and has DST.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_rc2b2_tz_test.dart, run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm (deleted afterwards). Output: 'wallTime tunis @01:30Z => 2026-03-29 03:30:00.000 hour=3', 'toUtc of that => 2026-03-29 02:30:00.000Z', 'zoneNow tunis => 2026-03-29 03:30:00.000', 'All tests passed!'.

verdicts.corrected_title: PickupSchedule.zoneNow builds the zone wall-clock as a device-local DateTime: for a Tunis pickup on an EU-DST phone, during 02:00-02:59 Tunis on the EU spring-forward day, the earliest legal pickup is pushed an hour late
verdicts.reason: zone_clock.dart:57-69 rebuilds the zone wall-clock with the local DateTime constructor, so a wall time inside the device zone's spring-forward gap is moved forward an hour. The only caller is PickupSchedule.zoneNow (stockholm_schedule.dart:29-30), which feeds minimumPickup, isLegalPickup and timePickerMinFor. The finding's own scenario (wallTime applied to a chosen reservation instant) does not occur, because wallTime is only ever applied to 'now'. The real effect is limited to a mismatched device and pickup zone (Stockholm/Paris phone, Tunis pickup, since Tunis has no DST) during one hour a year. The toUtc doc comment at 71-73 is also wrong: Stockholm 02:30 on 2026-03-29 resolves to 01:30Z, which uses the winter offset, not the summer one it claims.
verdicts.repro: I ran a throwaway test under TZ=Europe/Stockholm. ZoneClock.wallTime('Africa/Tunis', 2026-03-29 01:30Z) returned 03:30 (correct is 02:30). toUtc of that value returned 02:30Z, not the original 01:30Z. ZoneClock.toUtc(DateTime(2026,3,29,2,30), 'Europe/Stockholm') returned 01:30Z. PickupSchedule('Africa/Tunis') at now=01:15Z (02:15 Tunis): 'zoneNow=03:15 min=03:45'. A 03:15 Tunis pickup is reported not legal, although the correct minimum is 02:45.

confirmed.title: Telemetry version comment says CI passes MOVERA_APP_VERSION, but no workflow does, so every release-like build reports appVersion 'dev'
confirmed.description: CrashReporter attaches appVersion to every crash/telemetry record (crash_reporter.dart:24). The constant's contract is that CI passes the pubspec version with --dart-define=MOVERA_APP_VERSION. None of the production/staging builds in .github/workflows (android-release-signing, phase72/73/74/78/80/85, backend-readiness-gate) pass it, so release telemetry can never be told apart by version.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Every crash from the signed production APK is posted to /api/v1/telemetry/crashes with appVersion 'dev', so operators cannot tell which release crashes. Verified by grep.
confirmed.evidence:
lib/core/constants/app_version.dart:1-7 /// ... CI passes the pubspec version with `--dart-define=MOVERA_APP_VERSION=<version>`; local builds report `dev` ... const appVersion = String.fromEnvironment('MOVERA_APP_VERSION', defaultValue: 'dev');
grep MOVERA_APP_VERSION .github -> no matches
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass --dart-define=MOVERA_APP_VERSION=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml ...) in every release build step, or derive it from package info.

verdicts.reason: lib/core/constants/app_version.dart:1-7 defaults `appVersion` to 'dev' unless MOVERA_APP_VERSION is passed as a build define, and crash_reporter.dart:24 attaches it to every crash record. None of the `flutter build` steps in .github/workflows passes it. That includes android-release-signing.yml:49-52 (production APK), publish-web-live.yml:45-49, backend-readiness-gate.yml:101-104 and phase72/73/74/78/80/85. So every CI release build reports appVersion 'dev', which contradicts the comment that CI passes the version. Separately, side_menu.dart:60 hard-codes '1.0.0'.
verdicts.repro: Searched the whole repository for MOVERA_APP_VERSION: the only hits are in app_version.dart. Searched .github/workflows for `flutter build` and `dart-define` and listed every define each release build passes. None sets MOVERA_APP_VERSION.

verdicts.reason: app_version.dart:1-7 says CI passes `--dart-define=MOVERA_APP_VERSION`, with `defaultValue: 'dev'`. No workflow does this. The signed production build at .github/workflows/android-release-signing.yml:49-52 passes only MOVERA_FLAVOR=production and MOVERA_API_BASE_URL. The web build at publish-web-live.yml:45-49 passes flavor, base URL and map id. CrashReporter.record (crash_reporter.dart:24) attaches `appVersion` to every crash it sends to Observability.crashes, and the app wires it in di.dart:97. So every release crash reports appVersion 'dev'. Separately, side_menu.dart:60 hard-codes '1.0.0', so the version the user sees and the telemetry version disagree.
verdicts.repro: `grep -rn MOVERA_APP_VERSION` over the repo finds only lib/core/constants/app_version.dart and the audit JSON, so no workflow or script passes it. Read the `flutter build` steps in android-release-signing.yml and publish-web-live.yml. Traced the constant from crash_reporter.dart:24 to di.dart:97.

confirmed.title: docs/QA_HOOKS.md still lists moveraOpenSafety as absent from release builds, but code and CI intentionally expose a navigation-only bridge
confirmed.description: docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-11 states public release builds do not expose `moveraOpenSafety` and that hooks install only under kDebugMode or MOVERA_QA. `installSafetyNavigationBridge` sets exactly that global without any gate, and bootstrap calls it unconditionally (lib/app/bootstrap.dart:76-78) outside the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` block (lines 82-85). The gated `installSafetyQaOpener` (line 52) writes the same property name, so in QA builds whichever runs last wins. The code comment says this is intentional, so either the record or the code is wrong; per the audit rules a place where code does not do what the decision document says is reportable.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the public GitHub Pages build any page script (or the Maps JS SDK) can call `window.moveraOpenSafety()` and navigate the rider to the Safety hub; QA_HOOKS.md promises this surface is absent.
confirmed.evidence: lib/core/debug/web_qa_hooks_web.dart:67-81 `void installSafetyNavigationBridge(bool Function() open) { // This bridge is intentionally available in public web builds. ... globalContext.setProperty('moveraOpenSafety'.toJS, ...` ; lib/app/bootstrap.dart:76-78 `installSafetyNavigationBridge(() => pushPageOnce(() => const SafetyHub(), AppRoutes.safety));` (before the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` at :82); docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-9 `Public GitHub Pages **release** builds do **not** expose: ... - moveraOpenSafety`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either gate the bridge with moveraQaHooksEnabled (and use the gated installSafetyQaOpener only), or correct docs/QA_HOOKS.md / ARCHITECTURE.md to state that moveraOpenSafety is a public navigation-only hook.

verdicts.corrected_title: docs/QA_HOOKS.md still lists moveraOpenSafety as absent from release builds, but code and CI intentionally expose a navigation-only bridge
verdicts.reason: The mismatch with the document is real. docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-11 says release builds do not expose moveraOpenSafety. But bootstrap.dart:74-78 calls installSafetyNavigationBridge without a gate, and web_qa_hooks_web.dart:67-81 sets window.moveraOpenSafety unconditionally. This is clearly intentional: the code comments at web_qa_hooks_web.dart:68-70 and bootstrap.dart:74-75 say so, and qa-live-rider-flow.yml:115-141 asserts the bridge exists on public release. So the document is stale, not the code. The security effect is nil: the bridge only pushes the SafetyHub, which the rider can already open from the drawer, via pushPageOnce. It does not mutate state. The claim that whichever install runs last wins is moot, because registerWebQaHooks runs after the bridge only in QA builds, and both open the same screen.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: bootstrap.dart:73-85 runs the bridge before the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` block. Grep for moveraOpenSafety across docs, lib and .github: the docs say absent, while the CI workflow requires it to be present.

verdicts.corrected_title: docs/QA_HOOKS.md:9 still lists moveraOpenSafety as absent from public release builds, but the code (on purpose) exposes it as a public navigation-only bridge
verdicts.reason: The finding is accurate. bootstrap.dart:76-78 calls installSafetyNavigationBridge with no gate, before the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` block, and web_qa_hooks_web.dart:67-81 sets window.moveraOpenSafety unconditionally. The gated installSafetyQaOpener (:52) has no callers, so the overwrite race the finding describes cannot happen. The exposure is deliberate. The code comment (:68-70), the bootstrap comment (:74-75) and the CI workflow qa-live-rider-flow.yml:114-120 all say so, and the workflow even fails if the bridge is missing on public Pages. The behaviour is harmless: it only pushes the same SafetyHub the drawer already opens, via pushPageOnce. QA_HOOKS.md was edited later (ee9f4c1, 2026-10-17) than the bridge was added (2026-10-14) and still says it is not exposed, and ARCHITECTURE.md says window.movera* hooks are gated. So this is a real documentation contract mismatch, but the impact is a stale doc, not a security hole.

confirmed.title: A web JS flight stopped by a tap leaves MapView.pose at the flight's starting pose, so the next stepped glide starts from the wrong place
confirmed.original_title: A web JS flight stopped by a tap leaves MapView.pose at the flight's starting pose, so the next stepped glide starts from the wrong place
confirmed.description: While a JS flight runs, view.easing is true, so CustomGoogleMap._onMove ignores every camera report and view.pose stays at the pose from before the flight. On the web, Dart only learns where the camera is when the flight lands (_jsGlide sets pose = goal). If the flight is cancelled, interrupt() calls RiderMapBridge.cancelFlight and clears easing. _jsGlide's finally block skips its work because the generation changed. view.pose is never refreshed. A tap without a drag (pointerdown on .gm-style sets touching=true and interrupts) produces no further camera report. It also does not set movedByHandAt, so follow updates are not held. The next follow glide or 450 ms fitBounds ease runs on the Dart loop from view.pose, which is the pre-flight origin.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the web Home map, the rider taps recenter and taps the map (for example a marker) halfway through the 1 s flight. The camera stops mid-way, but pose still holds the pre-recenter view. The next follow update (a GPS fix) starts a Dart glide whose first frame jumps the camera back toward the old view before gliding to the target.
confirmed.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:86-89 `if (_jsFlight) { _jsFlight = false; final id = mapId; if (id != null) RiderMapBridge.cancelFlight(id); }` with no pose refresh; :364-375 `if (view.generation == generation) { if (arrived && view._goal != null) { view.pose = view._goal; ...` (skipped after interrupt). custom_google_map.dart:202 ignores reports while `view.easing`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When a JS flight is cancelled, read the live camera into view.pose, for example by having cancelFlight return the current pose or by calling controller.getVisibleRegion/zoom, or mark pose unknown so the next report is accepted.

verdicts.reason: interrupt() (map_camera_motion.dart:80-94) cancels the JS flight and clears easing, but it does not touch pose. _jsGlide's finally (:364-375) is skipped because the generation changed, and arrived is false anyway, since JS endFlight(false) runs on cancel (web/rider_map_camera.js:137-145). During the flight, CustomGoogleMap._onMove dropped every echo because easing was true (lib/shared/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:202). The only things that write pose are _onMove, _send and _jsGlide (grep). A tap without a drag sets touching through the map_touch_web pointerdown (lib/core/web/map_touch_web.dart:40). It does not call release(): the gesture layer only releases on a move of 6 px or more, a dblclick or a native zoom control (rider_map_camera.js:218-235). So movedByHandAt stays null. The next follow update through animateCamera(follow:true) passes _mayMove, and easeCameraTo steps _glide from view.pose, which is the pre-flight origin. Its first _approach frame (about a 5% share) lands next to the old view. One thing could save it: a trailing bounds_changed from the flight's last rAF frame arriving after pointerdown. That frame normally renders and dispatches within its own frame, before the input event, so nothing reliably refreshes pose.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only (read-only run, no flutter/dart executed). Traced easeCameraTo -> RiderMapBridge.flight -> _jsGlide, interrupt -> cancelFlight -> JS endFlight(false), all pose writers (grep '\.pose = '), the touch watcher in map_touch_web.dart and the release() conditions in rider_map_camera.js. No document records this as intentional.

verdicts.reason: On the web, a pointerdown on .gm-style goes through map_touch_web.dart to _fingerDown, which sets touching=true (custom_google_map.dart:173). That calls interrupt() (map_camera_motion.dart:80-90): generation goes up, easing becomes false and the JS flight is cancelled (rider_map_camera.js:145, endFlight(false)). The pose is not refreshed. After that, _jsGlide's finally block is skipped because the generation no longer matches (:364), so view.pose is not set to the goal. While the flight ran, every report was dropped because easing was true (custom_google_map.dart:202). So view.pose still holds the pose from before the flight. A tap without a drag never calls release() in the JS layer: pointerdown only stores pointerOrigin (rider_map_camera.js:222), and single-finger touchstart does not call releaseTouch. So movedByHandAt stays null and heldByRider is false once the finger lifts. onCameraIdle carries no pose. The next follow easeCameraTo calls interrupt() and then starts from view.pose (map_camera_motion.dart:324-325). Its first _approach frame is computed from the stale origin and sent with moveCamera, so the camera jumps back toward the old view. The only thing that could rescue it is timing: a trailing bounds_changed after the cancel. The web plugin reads the live map pose for each CameraMoveEvent (google_maps_controller.dart:279-288), so such an event would fix pose. But nothing guarantees one arrives.
verdicts.repro: Read-only, no run. Traced pointerdown, then map_touch_web onDown, _fingerDown, the touching setter, interrupt() and cancelFlight. Then traced _jsGlide's finally block (generation mismatch, so it is skipped) and _onMove's easing filter. Checked google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2: onBoundsChanged gives CameraMoveEvent(_gmViewportToCameraPosition(map)) and onIdle gives no pose. Then followed the next animateCamera(follow:true) path: _mayMove, easeCameraTo, interrupt, from = view.pose, _glide frame 0 and _send.
verdicts.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:86-90 has no pose refresh; :364 `if (view.generation == generation)` skips the landing assignment; custom_google_map.dart:202 drops reports while easing; rider_map_camera.js:218-223 pointerdown never calls release() for a plain tap.

confirmed.title: A recenter that joins a running follow glide is stepped on the Dart timer on the web and keeps the old glide's 240-frame cap, which can cut the flight short
confirmed.original_title: A recenter that joins a running follow glide is stepped on the Dart timer on the web and keeps the old glide's 240-frame cap, which can cut the flight short
confirmed.description: When easeCameraTo gets a flight-length goal (>= 600 ms, for example animateCamera(follow:false) from a recenter) while a damped follow glide is running, it converts that glide in place: it sets _flight and resets _flownMicros to 0. It never hands the flight to RiderMapBridge.flight, although the comment at lines 336-338 says web flights run on the browser frame clock so they do not stutter on a Dart timer in Safari. The loop variable `frame` in _glide also keeps counting from the start of the old glide, and the flight branch ends with `last = after >= 1 || frame >= _maxEaseFrames`. If the follow glide had already run about 180 frames (it was retargeted repeatedly without settling), the new 1 s flight is cut off after the remaining frames and snaps to its goal.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On web Safari, the Home map is gliding after a stream of GPS follow fixes when the rider taps recenter. The 1 s locate flight runs on the Dart 16 ms timer (the stutter the JS path exists to avoid). If the follow glide was already near frame 240, the flight lands with a jump after a fraction of a second.

confirmed.title: Road-route cache is unbounded and gets a new entry every 10 s of a live ride (driver position is part of the key)
confirmed.description: roadLine stores every resolved road geometry in a per-RoutingService map that is never evicted (`cache[key] = points`). The key is built from the endpoints at 5 decimals. AppScope holds one RoutingService for the app's lifetime (di.dart:191-192). Waiting's paintIfDue calls _refreshRoadRoute at most every 10 s (waiting_for_driver.dart:2097-2102). Its endpoints are the driver's live position and the pickup or destination (lines 2328-2357), so each refresh while the driver moves is a new key and a new cached polyline. confirmed.title: MotionEngine lerp window is anchored at the previous fix's timestamp, so with fixes 420 ms or more apart t clamps to 1 and the home puck snaps between raw smoothed fixes (pose heading is unused)
confirmed.description: ingest() is called once per delivered fix (HomeController._deliverFix, lib/features/home/application/home_controller.dart:518) and passes `startedAt: _from!.timestamp` with a 420 ms window. `_from` is the previous accepted sample, whose timestamp is at least one fix interval (typically >= 1 s) old, so `now - startedAt` always exceeds 420 ms and the interpolator clamps to t=1, returning `_to` verbatim. There is no ticker that calls lerp between fixes, so the 'interpolation' is a no-op and the rider marker snaps to each raw smoothed point; heading likewise jumps. Not a crash, but the animation math does not do what the component is for.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the home map the blue rider dot and heading cone jump between 1 Hz fixes rather than easing across the 420 ms window.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Record `startedAt = clock` when a new sample arrives and expose a `poseAt(now)` used by a frame ticker; or drop the interpolator if snapping is intended.

verdicts.corrected_title: MotionEngine lerp window is anchored at the previous fix's timestamp, so with fixes 420 ms or more apart t clamps to 1 and the home puck snaps between raw smoothed fixes (pose heading is unused)
verdicts.reason: motion_engine.dart:39-48 sets `_from = _to`, then calls lerp with `startedAt: _from!.timestamp` (the previous sample's GPS time), `now: DateTime.now()` and a 420 ms window. interpolator.dart:26-28 clamps `elapsed/total` to [0,1]. At the usual ≥1 Hz geolocator cadence, elapsed is at least the fix interval, so t=1 and the result is exactly `_to`. The only caller is HomeController._deliverFix (home_controller.dart:518), once per fix, and no ticker re-samples between fixes. home.dart:259-262 and _updateLocationVisuals (home.dart:1569-1585) paint the marker straight at that point without animating it. The finding's heading claim is moot: _deliverFix takes heading from position.heading/compass (home_controller.dart:531-536), not from pose.heading. The effect is cosmetic, but the component does not do what it exists for.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: MotionEngine.ingest -> PositionInterpolator.lerp math -> HomeController._deliverFix -> home.dart onFix -> _updateLocationVisuals/paintUserPuck. There is no frame ticker or animation controller on the puck position.

verdicts.corrected_title: MotionEngine starts its 420 ms window at the previous fix's GPS timestamp and nothing ticks between fixes, so the puck position snaps to each fix and the interpolator never animates
verdicts.reason: lib/core/motion/motion_engine.dart:41-49 calls lerp with `startedAt: _from!.timestamp`, the previous accepted fix's timestamp, and `now: DateTime.now()`. lib/core/motion/interpolator.dart:24-26 clamps `elapsed/420` to at most 1, so with fixes 420 ms or more apart t=1 and `_to` comes back unchanged. The only caller is HomeController._deliverFix (home_controller.dart:518), once per fix, and no frame ticker re-samples. The output therefore equals the raw fix and the interpolation does nothing. If fixes arrive less than 420 ms apart, it returns a partial point that stays put until the next fix. The heading part is misdescribed: pose.heading is never used for the puck. _deliverFix takes `heading` from the compass or position.heading (lines 532-537) and uses only pose.position and pose.cone.accuracy, so heading behaviour does not depend on this math.

confirmed.title: Polling drops fresh driver fixes whose coordinates did not change, so a driver stopped on the way to pickup shows 'Updating location…'
confirmed.description: The 'nothing changed' short-circuit compares version, updatedAt, status and lat/lng, but not the fix time (`location.at` from `driverLocation.measuredAt` / `locationAt`). Location-only updates keep the version (and, in the documented stand-in, updatedAt) unchanged. So when the driver is stationary, for example waiting at the pickup or stopped at lights, every new fix with identical coordinates is swallowed and `locationAt` never advances. DriverTrackingController's 5 s stale check then marks the ETA stale after `DriverEta.staleAfter` (25 s) and shows 'Updating location…' / 'Waiting for fresh location' even though fresh fixes are arriving.
