confirmed.title: A driver drop followed by a re-offer within one poll is labelled an admin reassign, so the rider never sees the 'driver cancelled' notice
confirmed.description: When a matched trip comes back as searching or offered, `_poll` calls `_reassignedByAdmin(ride, explicitKind)` (line 198) to decide between a driver drop and an admin reassign. With no `cancellation.actor` in the projection (the mock never sets one for the non-terminal driver cancel → searching, see `_apply` line 1426, which only fills it for terminals), the check falls back to `explicitKind != null && explicitKind != RealtimeKind.driverCancelled`. `explicitKind` is the kind of the latest committed event (`envelope['kind'] ?? ride['eventKind']`), not the kind of the event that ended the match. Dispatch normally re-offers the trip right after a driver drops it (`send_offer`, kind `trip_projection`). If that happens inside the 2 s poll window, the poll sees status `offered` with kind `trip_projection` and labels the driver drop as an admin reassign. The event then carries `reassignedBy: admin` and kind `trip_projection` instead of `driver_cancelled`, so the rider is never told their driver cancelled. Reproduced with a throwaway test against InProcessMockClient: after driver_to_pickup, `POST /status {command: cancel, actor: driver}` then `{command: send_offer, actor: system}`, then resync. Output: `status=RideStatus.cancelledByDriver kind=trip_projection adminReassign=true server=offered cancellation=null`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver cancels before pickup and dispatch sends the trip to the next driver within about 2 s. The rider's poll sees `offered` with kind trip_projection. Waiting treats it as an admin reassign (Q13 path): no 'your driver cancelled' notice, only a silent return to searching.
confirmed.evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:143-145 `final explicitKind = RealtimeKindWire.parse(envelope['kind'] ?? ride['eventKind']);`
:198 `final byAdmin = reassigned && _reassignedByAdmin(ride, explicitKind);`
:299 `return explicitKind != null && explicitKind != RealtimeKind.driverCancelled;`
in_process_mock_client.dart:1029 `'kind': ride['eventKind'],` (last event only)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Decide driver drop or admin reassign from the event or command that left the matched state, or from `cancellation.actor`. Do not use the newest event's kind. When the polled projection cannot tell, default to the driver-cancelled notice, or read `GET /trips/{id}/events?after=` for the skipped events.

confirmed.title: After a reload, the mock carries on with a ride the in-memory stand-in server no longer has, ignoring every 404
confirmed.description: The class contract says every step it shows is first committed on the stand-in server 'so the server projection and what the rider sees agree'. But `_enqueue` swallows every error, and `_assignNow` goes on to emit driverAssigned whatever `_persistAssignment` returned. The other steps (`_commit`) are fire-and-forget before the event is added. The in-process server keeps rides only in memory (ApiClient creates a fresh `InProcessMockClient` per page load and nothing re-seeds `rides`). So after a public Pages reload during Finding, the restored search runs on a ride the server does not have: POST /status answers 404, the error is ignored, and the rider is moved to Waiting with a made-up driver. The trip then plays out locally, and at the end POST /feedback answers 404. The same applies when the server refuses a commit for any other reason, for example a rider cancel that already landed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the public demo, the rider reloads while 'Finding a driver'. 25 s later a driver is 'found' and the trip completes, but the server has no such ride: route changes and the rating/tip POST fail with 404, and the completion screen shows that feedback could not be saved.
confirmed.evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:17-22 class doc `Every lifecycle step it shows is first committed on the stand-in server ... so the server projection and what the rider sees agree`
275 `await _persistAssignment(rideId);` then 301-303 `lastStatus = RideStatus.driverAssigned; _assignmentInFlight = false; _emit(RideStatus.driverAssigned);` (no check of the result)
786-793 `_commits = _commits.then((_) async { try { _observe(await call()); } catch (_) { // Mock transport: a refused or lost commit leaves the server as is. } });`
api_client.dart:30 `InProcessMockClient(persistSafety: true)` (only safety persisted)
Throwaway test on an id the server does not know: log `api.POST .../status ... status: 404` and then `statuses: [findingDriver, driverAssigned]; server knows ride: false`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Have `_enqueue` return the outcome and only emit a step whose commit succeeded (or resync from the server on refusal); for the demo, persist the mock's rides with the snapshot or re-seed the stand-in from the restored snapshot.

verdicts.corrected_title: After a reload, the mock carries on with a ride the in-memory stand-in server no longer has, ignoring every 404
verdicts.reason: The stand-in server keeps rides only in memory: `final Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> rides = {}` (in_process_mock_client.dart:82), and only safety data is persisted (restoreOnce at line 1208). docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:12 says 'In-memory only', but DECISIONS.md R-web requires a live ride to survive a reload on public Pages. So after a reload the restored ride is unknown to the server. On restore, MockRideRealtime.reconnectAndResync (mock_ride_realtime.dart:823-856) swallows the failed GET and re-emits the local status. _assignNow awaits _persistAssignment (line 275) and emits driverAssigned without checking the result (lines 301-303), and _enqueue swallows every commit error (lines 786-793). The rider sees a driver found and a trip played out that the server refused with 404, which contradicts the class contract at lines 17-22. The finding's second scenario, a cancel that already landed, is mostly guarded: cancelRide sets cancelled, and _assignNow re-checks cancelled and lastStatus after the persist (lines 277-281). The reload case is the real one.

This agrees with the finder's throwaway log (POST .../status -> 404, then statuses [findingDriver, driverAssigned], server knows ride: false). I did not rerun it.

confirmed.title: Mock driver never learns a pickup moved by a route change; it drives to and 'arrives' at the old pickup
confirmed.description: The mock's GPS approach and `_etaSeconds` use `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng`, which are set only once by `_hydratePickup()` after assignment. When the rider moves the pickup after accept (Q40, allowed up to maxPickupMoveMeters while accepted/driverToPickup), Waiting `_applyRouteChange` updates the tracking controller's pickup and the mock's destination only. It cannot update the mock's private pickup, and nothing re-reads it. The mock keeps walking to the old point and emits driverWaiting plus the 'arrived' signal within 50 m of the *old* pickup.

confirmed.title: History record time is overwritten with the Done-tap time; receipt date uses savedAt which lifecycle refreshes move
confirmed.description: `markCompleted` archives the trip with `endedAt` defaulting to now (completion time) (377-382, on_demand_ride_history_store.dart 197 `final ended = endedAt ?? DateTime.now();`). When the rider taps Done, `closeCompletedRide` archives again with the same `reservationId` and no `endedAt` (453-457), so `archive` replaces the record (146-148) and its `scheduledPickupAt` becomes the time the rider left the summary, which can be much later. Separately, the receipt's 'Date and time' comes from `DriverRepository._completedAtLabel(ride.savedAt)` (driver_repository.dart 59), and `savedAt` is rewritten by `persistCompletedStatus` (395-400) on each payment/rating event and by `RideSnapshotStore.touchCurrent` on every background/pagehide (ride_snapshot_store.dart 452) because completed-surface statuses are not terminal; after a restore `LastCompletedRide.remember(snapshot)` (ride_restore_coordinator.dart 383) therefore shows the last backgrounding time, not the completion time.

DateTime.now();` ; driver_repository.dart:59 `completedAt: _completedAtLabel(ride.savedAt),`

History therefore shows the Done-tap time. The receipt's 'Date and time' comes from LastCompletedRide.value.savedAt (driver_repository.dart:40,59). savedAt is rewritten on every payment or rating event by persistCompletedStatus (active_ride_controller.dart:395-400). It is also rewritten on every lifecycle touch by RideSnapshotStore.touchCurrent (ride_snapshot_store.dart:452). touchCurrent skips only isTerminal statuses, and the completed-surface statuses (tripCompleted, paymentProcessing, paymentFinalized, ratingPending) are not terminal (ride_status.dart:59-89). confirmed.title: After a route-change PATCH whose response was lost, a later route change shows and reports a locally computed difference, not the server's differenceMinor
confirmed.description: `differenceKr` is `newPriceKr - oldPriceKr`, where `oldPriceKr` is the device's `_price`. The server charges `differenceMinor = newMinor - current fare`. The client parses that value into `quote.differenceMinor` but never shows it, and `showRouteUpdated` uses `updated.price - ride.price` as well. When the device price lags the server, the rider is shown a wrong charge. This happens when a PATCH reached the server but its response was lost: `_send` reports `network`, Waiting keeps the old route and price, and it never reads the route back from the projection.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A first destination change times out on the client after the server applied it and captured +49 kr. The rider sees 'Couldn't update route' and tries again. The second quote's sheet says '+49 kr charged now to Visa' and the snackbar repeats it, but the server's difference is 0 and nothing is charged.
confirmed.evidence:
route_change_controller.dart:66 double get differenceKr => newPriceKr - oldPriceKr;
:213 oldPriceKr: ride.price,
waiting_for_driver.dart:1091 differenceKr: updated.price - ride.price,
in_process_mock_client.dart:2091 'differenceMinor': newMinor - currentMinor,
confirmed.suggested_fix: Show `quote.differenceMinor` (the server's), and after a lost PATCH response re-read the trip projection before offering another change.

The server's `differenceMinor`, parsed at :219-224, is only sent back as `expectedDifferenceMinor`. After a lost PATCH response, `_send` maps it to network (:366-368). Waiting's `_price`/route stay old (`_currentRide`, waiting_for_driver.dart:1021-1036, `_price => _changedPrice ?? widget.price` :1018), and nothing re-reads the projection. confirmed.title: A route change committed on the server but whose PATCH response is lost (15 s timeout or network drop) is reported as failed, and Waiting keeps the old route and price unless the rider retries
confirmed.description: `apply` maps any non-ApiError (ClientException) and any retryable ApiError (TIMEOUT, NETWORK, 5xx) to `RouteChangeFailure.network`. Waiting's snapshot, map, destination and price stay as before. The PATCH may have been applied: the server changed the destination, notified the driver and charged the difference. Realtime projections are never read for the route, so Waiting keeps showing the old destination and price for the rest of the ride unless the rider retries.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In trip, the rider changes the destination and confirms +kr 60. The PATCH lands but the response is lost, and the rider sees 'Couldn't update the route. Try again.' and closes the picker. The driver drives to the new destination and the card is charged kr 60, while the rider's map and price still show the old trip. Traced by reading the code.
confirmed.evidence:
route_change_controller.dart:339-351 `throw RouteChangeException(switch (error.detail) { ... _ => RouteChangeFailure.network, }); } catch (_) { throw const RouteChangeException(RouteChangeFailure.network); }`
route_change_flow.dart:118-122 `} on RouteChangeException catch (error) { messenger ... showSnackBar(SnackBar(content: Text(error.message))); return null; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: For a retryable apply failure, re-send the same request (the key is stable) or re-read the projection and adopt the server's route and fare before telling the rider it failed.

verdicts.reason: _send (route_change_controller.dart:330-357) maps any retryable ApiError or transport exception to RouteChangeFailure.network. The flow shows the snackbar and returns null (route_change_flow.dart:118-122). Waiting's route, map and price change only through _applyRouteChange on a successful result (waiting_for_driver.dart:1089, :1226-1240). Nothing reads the route or fare back from a server projection or GET. The PATCH carries a stable idempotency key (:255-268), so the server may already have applied it. If the rider gives up after the error, Waiting keeps the old destination and price while the server and the driver have the new ones. A retry runs preview again first, which creates a new quote and so a new key, so the stable key does not reconcile this case. It is a lost-response edge case, hence low.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of apply/_send, route_change_flow onFinish error handling, and every write of _destinationAddress/_changedPrice in waiting_for_driver.dart (only _applyRouteChange). No reconciliation path found.

verdicts.corrected_title: A route change committed on the server but whose PATCH response is lost (15 s timeout or network drop) is reported as failed, and Waiting keeps the old route and price unless the rider retries
verdicts.reason: api_client.dart:42/59 sends PATCH with a 15 s timeout and no retry (only GET has _getWithRetry at :268). Any timeout or ClientException is mapped to RouteChangeFailure.network (route_change_controller.dart:339-351), and route_change_flow.dart:118-122 shows the snackbar and returns null. Waiting changes _destinationAddress and price only through the route-change result (waiting_for_driver.dart:219, 1018, 1229). It never adopts the destination or fare from realtime or the projection, so the rider's screen stays on the old route while the server, the driver and the charge use the new one. The stable idempotency key (:254-258) only helps if the exact same request is resent. A retry from the picker runs preview again, which gets a new routeQuoteId and therefore a new key. A retry may still fix the screen, but if the rider closes the picker the mismatch stays for the rest of the ride. Nothing in the decision documents says this outcome is accepted.
verdicts.repro: Traced the code: ApiClient._send PATCH (no retry, a TimeoutException after 15 s) -> RouteChangeController._send catch-all -> RouteChangeException(network) -> RouteChangeFlow snackbar, return null -> Waiting state unchanged. I checked waiting_for_driver.dart for any other place that writes _destinationAddress or price and found only line 1229 (the route-change result). Not run, because it needs a server that commits and then drops the response.

confirmed.title: In EUR/TND zones, route changes under 0.5 major units are shown as 'Same price' and skip the card confirmation step, though the difference is charged or refunded
confirmed.description: The sheet treats |newPrice − oldPrice| < 0.5 as no change: the copy says 'Same price', the struck-through old price is hidden and the payment step is skipped. In EUR or TND zones (Q7: the trip's currency), fares have cents or millimes, so a real change of, for example, 0.40 € is presented as the same price. apply() still sends expectedTotalMinor = the new total, and the server charges the difference. The same threshold hides the difference in showRouteUpdated (route_change_flow.dart:185).
confirmed.failure_scenario: In Paris (EUR) the rider moves the destination slightly. The quote goes from 18.20 € to 18.60 €. The sheet says 'Same price' next to 18.60 € and confirms with no payment step, and the card is charged 0.40 € more.
confirmed.evidence:
route_change_sheet.dart:93 `if (_cash || _diff.abs() < 0.5) { Navigator.pop(context, const RouteChangeDecision(confirmed: true));`
route_change_sheet.dart:125-126 `if (diff.abs() < 0.5) { priceNote = context.l10n.samePrice;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare minor units (newTotalMinor vs the booked total in minor units) and treat any non-zero difference as a change.

verdicts.reason: route_change_sheet.dart:93 skips the payment step when _diff.abs() < 0.5, and :125-126 then shows 'Same price'. _diff is quote.differenceKr = newPriceKr - oldPriceKr in major units (route_change_controller.dart:66, newPriceKr = price.major at :213). The mock prices on the zone's step: EUR stepMinor 5 (0.05 EUR) and TND 100 (0.1 DT) in mock_catalog_fares.dart:87-99,125-128, through rates.roundToStep in in_process_mock_client.dart:2082. EUR zones exist (rider_zones.dart:51). So a route quote that differs by 0.05-0.45 EUR is reachable. The rider sees 'Same price' and confirms with no card step, while apply sends the new total and the mock captures the difference (:927). route_change_flow.dart:185 likewise hides the charged amount in the follow-up notice.
verdicts.repro: Traced the RouteChangeSheet threshold, then RouteChangeQuote.differenceKr, the mock _routeChangePricing (in_process_mock_client.dart:2060-2095) and MockZoneCurrency steps. Checked rider_zones for an EUR zone. No guard compares in minor units.
verdicts.corrected_title: In EUR/TND zones, route changes under 0.5 major units are shown as 'Same price' and skip the card confirmation step, though the difference is charged or refunded

verdicts.reason: route_change_sheet.dart:93 (`_cash || _diff.abs() < 0.5`) skips the payment step, and :125-126 shows samePrice. `_diff` is `newPriceKr - oldPriceKr` in major units (route_change_controller.dart:66). EUR fares move in steps of 0.05 € (mock_catalog_fares.dart:89-94, stepMinor 5), and the mock's _routeChangePricing (in_process_mock_client.dart:2046+) rounds the new fare to that step. So a small destination move in the Paris zone gives a real difference of 0.05-0.45 €, and route_change_flow.dart:185 uses the same 0.5 threshold. Apply still sends the new total in minor units (route_change_controller.dart:247), so the rider is charged a difference the sheet called 'Same price', with no payment confirmation. In SEK (1 kr step) a non-zero difference is always at least 1.0, so only fractional currencies are affected.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand: old 18.20 €, new 18.60 € gives _diff = 0.4000000000000057; abs() < 0.5 is true, so Navigator.pop(confirmed: true) runs with no _paymentStep and the note is samePrice. Checked that EUR stepMinor = 5 makes such differences reachable. The rate is 0.095 €/kr, so a few hundred metres of extra route costs well under 0.5 €.

confirmed.title: A no-show or other pre-trip terminal status stays hidden behind the 'Your driver has arrived' sheet until the rider dismisses it
confirmed.description: The arrived sheet opens when the driver reaches the pickup (`_maybeAnnounceArrival`) and is closed in code only when the trip starts (lines 396-403). Terminal statuses go through `_queueStageNavigation` / `_drainStageNavigation`, which refuse to act while `!_routeIsCurrent` (line 525), and the arrived sheet is a modal route above Waiting. No-show is the terminal that by definition happens while the driver is waiting at the pickup, which is exactly when this sheet is up. The rider therefore keeps seeing 'Your driver has arrived', with the driver's name and plate, after the server has closed the trip. History archival and the snapshot clear are also held back until dismissal.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver arrives and the arrived sheet opens. The rider does not come out. After 5 minutes the driver marks no-show, and tracking reports noShow, which is queued because the route is not current. The rider looks at the phone and sees 'Your driver has arrived · MVR 204', with no hint that the ride has ended as a no-show and may carry a fee. Only after swiping the sheet away do the no-show sheet and Home appear.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:396-403: `if (_arrivedSheetShowing && DriverEta.isInTrip(status)) { ... closeRouteByReference(route); }` (trip start only)
417-419: `if (status.isTerminal && !status.isCompletedSurface) { _queueStageNavigation(status); return; }`
521-526: `if (... || !_routeIsCurrent) { return; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Also close `_arrivedSheetRoute` (by reference, as for trip start) when a terminal or cancelledByDriver status arrives, then drain the stage navigation.

verdicts.reason: The arrived sheet opens at driverWaiting (waiting_for_driver.dart:458-475). Code closes it only on trip start (396-403). driver_arrived_sheet.dart has no timer or auto-dismiss: its only pop is the rider's button at line 153. A no-show (or admin cancel or expiry) at that stage goes through _queueStageNavigation (417-419). _drainStageNavigation then returns early while !_routeIsCurrent (521-526), because the sheet is the current route. So the terminal stays queued until the rider dismisses the sheet, and _onNavigationChanged drains it then. No-show is by definition raised while the driver waits, which is exactly when this sheet is up.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _maybeAnnounceArrival -> showDriverArrivedSheet (checked for timers and pops), _onLiveTick's terminal branch, the _drainStageNavigation guard, and _onNavigationChanged.

verdicts.reason: The arrived sheet is a MoveraSheet modal (driver_arrived_sheet.dart:26). _onLiveTick closes it in code only when DriverEta.isInTrip(status) (waiting_for_driver.dart:396-403). A noShow or other terminal status goes to _queueStageNavigation (:417-419), and _drainStageNavigation returns early while !_routeIsCurrent (:521-526). _onLiveTick also returns before any setState, so even the screen under the sheet is not updated. No other no-show handler exists outside this screen (grep RideStatus.noShow in lib shows only the mapping, history and terminal-sheet spec). The rider keeps seeing 'Your driver has arrived' until they dismiss the sheet. _onNavigationChanged then drains the queue (:500-509), so the effect is delayed, not lost.
verdicts.repro: Traced the _onLiveTick, _queueStageNavigation and _drainStageNavigation guards, and grepped for any global terminal or no-show handler. Not run.

confirmed.title: In-trip 'Arrive by HH:MM' on the sheet freezes because the rebuild signature ignores ETA changes during the trip
confirmed.description: _onLiveTick rebuilds only when _sheetSignatureFor changes. That signature uses eta.headline() and eta.subtitle(), which return the constant 'Ride in progress' and 'to drop-off' copy during the trip (driver_eta.dart:99-101, 117-121). The sheet headline and RiderInTripPanel headline come from _tripHeadline, computed from eta.seconds at build time (1665-1669). So an ETA change during the trip never rebuilds the sheet, and its arrival time stays at the value from the last rebuild. The map's destination time pin does update (paintIfDue -> _syncTimePins), so the map and the sheet disagree.
confirmed.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a throwaway widget test: an in-trip Waiting, emit with etaSeconds 600 shows 'Arrive by 01:47'. A later fix with etaSeconds 3600 still showed 'Arrive by 01:47' (expected about 02:37). The rider stuck in traffic is told they will arrive 50 minutes earlier than the live ETA.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:430-432 `if (signature == _sheetSignature) return; _sheetSignature = signature; setState(() {});`
waiting_for_driver.dart:440-443 `final headline = eta?.headline(status: status) ?? ...; return '${status.name}|$headline|$subtitle|${driver?.id ?? ''}'`
waiting_for_driver.dart:1668 `return context.l10n.arriveBy(clockTime(DateTime.now().add(Duration(seconds: seconds))));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Include the in-trip arrival minute (or eta.seconds rounded to a minute) in _sheetSignatureFor.

verdicts.reason: _onLiveTick (waiting_for_driver.dart:425-432) calls setState only when _sheetSignatureFor changes. During the trip DriverEta.headline/subtitle return constant copy (driver_eta.dart:98-101, 117-121) and are not affected by stale. The 'Arrive by' text comes from eta.seconds at build time (_tripHeadline, ~1665-1669). Waiting has no periodic setState: the only periodic timer is the Ride check still timer at 1118, and it does not rebuild. So an in-trip ETA change does not rebuild the sheet until some unrelated rebuild happens (a sheet drag, a status or connection change).
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the signature contents, the DriverEta copy and the timers in Waiting. The reporter's throwaway widget test showed 'Arrive by 01:47' unchanged after etaSeconds went from 600 to 3600. That matches the code. I did not rerun it.

verdicts.reason: _onLiveTick calls setState only when _sheetSignatureFor changes (waiting_for_driver.dart:426-432). The signature is status|headline|subtitle|driverId|degraded (:440-445). During the trip, DriverEta.headline and subtitle return the constant etaRideInProgress and etaToDropoff copy (driver_eta.dart:98-101, 117-121), so eta.seconds is not in the signature. The sheet's 'Arrive by HH:MM' comes from _tripHeadline, which runs DateTime.now()+eta.seconds only at build time (:1671-1675, used at :1680 and :1883), and no AnimatedBuilder or ListenableBuilder rebuilds it from _tracking. An in-trip ETA change therefore leaves the arrival time frozen until some unrelated rebuild happens.
verdicts.repro: Traced the signature against the DriverEta in-trip strings and the build-time _tripHeadline. Not run myself. The reporter's widget test (600 s, then 3600 s, both showing 'Arrive by 01:47') matches the trace.

confirmed.title: 'Driver has arrived' modal pops up again after every reload during the waiting stage
confirmed.description: _maybeAnnounceArrival is documented as 'say it once and never again for this ride', but `_arrivalAnnounced` lives only in State memory. A restored Waiting starts tracking at driverWaiting (via _knownStatus). The first live tick passes `_tracking.status == RideStatus.driverWaiting`, so the arrived sheet opens again on top of the restored screen, even though the rider already dismissed it before the reload.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver arrives, and the rider dismisses the arrived sheet and walks out. The phone browser reloads. The 'Your driver has arrived' sheet opens again over Waiting, and again after each later reload.
confirmed.evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:447-463 `/// ... say it once and never again for this ride.` ... `if (!explicitArrival && _tracking.status != RideStatus.driverWaiting) return; _arrivalAnnounced = true;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Persist the announced flag per rideId (for example in the snapshot or session storage) and check it before showing the sheet.

verdicts.reason: _arrivalAnnounced exists only in State memory (waiting_for_driver.dart:204) and nothing persists it per rideId. After a reload, _knownStatus (waiting_for_driver.dart:~352) seeds tracking at driverWaiting (driver_tracking_controller.dart:101-104). The first event from a fresh subscription calls onChange (driver_tracking_controller.dart:184). A fresh ApiRideRealtime poll is not deduplicated against a poll object that has no state yet. The 5 s staleness timer (line 197-203) also calls onChange. _onLiveTick then calls _maybeAnnounceArrival (line 421), and the check at 459-461 passes because status == driverWaiting, so the sheet opens again. The effect is cosmetic: the sheet is dismissible and its content is still true.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: initState -> _tracking.start(initialStatus: _knownStatus) -> realtime listen -> onChange -> _onLiveTick -> _maybeAnnounceArrival. No stored flag, and no check on initialStatus, stops the sheet from reopening.

verdicts.reason: `_arrivalAnnounced` is a plain State field set to false (waiting_for_driver.dart:204) and is never persisted. On restore, `_knownStatus` seeds tracking at driverWaiting (355-360, 269). The first tick, or any navigation-epoch post-frame (`_onNavigationChanged`, 505-506), then passes the check at 459-463 and opens the arrived sheet again. No per-ride flag is stored anywhere. Impact is small: the information is correct, it is just repeated.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_u49u52_test.dart: saved a snapshot, restoreFromBackend(driverWaiting, id:'u49'), pushed WaitingForDriver, then MockRideRealtime.emit(driverWaiting). Output: 'u49 arrived sheets: 1'. The sheet opened on the restored screen. File deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: Route change and 'change destination instead' are offered on scheduled live rides but can never succeed
confirmed.description: _routeEditable depends only on tracking status, so the ⋯ buttons (_openDetails) and the cancel sheet's offerDestinationChange are enabled for ReservationLiveRide pages too. _currentRide() builds a RideSnapshot whose rideId is the local reservation id. RouteChangeController.preview then posts /api/v1/rides/<reservationId>/route-quote. Reservations are device-local (LocalReservationRepository), so the server has no such ride and answers 404, which _send maps to RouteChangeFailure.network ('route update failed'). The rider is offered an action that always fails, with a misleading network error, and the map is parked and rebuilt each time.
confirmed.failure_scenario: During a scheduled ride the rider taps 'Change destination instead' on the cancel sheet, picks a new address and taps See new price. The result is always 'couldn't update the route' and the ride continues unchanged.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:1004 `bool get _routeEditable => !_tracking.status.isTerminal && !_completedOpened;`
waiting_for_driver.dart:811 `offerDestinationChange: _routeEditable,`
route_change_controller.dart:199-203 `_api.post('/api/v1/rides/$id/route-quote', ...`
in_process_mock_client.dart:817-820 `final ride = rides[parts[4]]; if (ride == null) { status = 404;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Disable route editing when widget.realtime/onCancel indicate a reservation-backed page, or route it through the reservation controller.

verdicts.reason: ReservationLiveRide.pageFor passes rideId: ride.reservationId and persistRideSnapshot: false (reservation_live_ride.dart:75-77). _routeEditable checks only tracking status (waiting_for_driver.dart:1010), so the cancel sheet's offerDestinationChange and _openDetails are enabled on reservation pages. _currentRide falls back to a RideSnapshot carrying the reservation id (waiting_for_driver.dart:1038-1057). RouteChangeController.preview then POSTs /api/v1/rides/<reservationId>/route-quote (route_change_controller.dart:198-203). Reservations are device-local in every build that has them: di.dart:144-146 uses LocalReservationRepository, otherwise the Disabled one. Nothing creates a server ride for a reservation, so the mock answers 404 not_found (in_process_mock_client.dart:817-820). _send maps that code to RouteChangeFailure.network through the default branch (route_change_controller.dart:348). No document records this as intended.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: reservation_live_ride.dart pageFor -> WaitingForDriver._routeEditable/_currentRide -> RouteChangeController.preview -> in-process mock route-quote handler; checked di.dart repository selection and the error mapping. No test run.

verdicts.reason: _routeEditable (waiting_for_driver.dart:1010) checks only the tracking status. The reservation page (reservation_live_ride.dart:52-80) passes rideId: reservationId and has no flag that disables route editing. _currentRide (lines 1021-1050) builds a RideSnapshot with that id. RouteChangeController.preview then posts /api/v1/rides/<reservationId>/route-quote (route_change_controller.dart:199-203). Reservations are device-local only (di.dart:143-146 LocalReservationRepository; the mock dispatch never registers a server ride), so the in-process mock returns 404 because rides[id]==null (in_process_mock_client.dart:817-820). The action shown always fails.
verdicts.repro: Traced by reading the code: ReservationLiveRide.pageFor -> WaitingForDriver(rideId: reservationId) -> _changeRoute -> openRouteChange -> preview POST -> mock 404 branch. I grepped for any reservation handling in in_process_mock_client.dart and found only fee rules.

confirmed.title: A rebuilt Waiting map (after a route change) shows no car until the next tracking event, which never comes if the feed is already quiet and stale
confirmed.description: _changeRoute parks the map, which removes _WaitingRideMap, and then rebuilds it. The new _WaitingRideMapState builds its markers in initState and _prepareMapVisuals using _currentDriverPosition(), and that reads _driverAnimTo. _driverAnimTo is filled only by _updateDriverAnimation from paintIfDue, which runs only on the next _onLiveTick. The tracking controller already holds the driver's last fix (tracking.eta), but the new map does not use it. If the feed is quiet (driver standing at the pickup with no new fix), the car stays off the map.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver is waiting at the pickup and the rider changes the destination. When the route sheet closes, the map shows pickup and destination but no car until the driver's app sends another fix.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:2028-2033 `void initState() { super.initState(); _markers = _buildMarkers(); unawaited(_prepareMapVisuals()); }`
waiting_for_driver.dart:2270 `final driverPosition = _currentDriverPosition();` (null until paintIfDue)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Seed the animation from widget.tracking.eta in initState (call _updateDriverAnimation, or paintIfDue after the first frame).

verdicts.corrected_title: A rebuilt Waiting map (after a route change) shows no car until the next tracking event, which never comes if the feed is already quiet and stale
verdicts.reason: _changeRoute (waiting_for_driver.dart:1075-1091) parks the map and then unparks it, so a new _WaitingRideMapState is created. Its initState (2035-2039) and _prepareMapVisuals (2310-2324) call _buildMarkers, and _buildMarkers reads _currentDriverPosition() (2270). That value is null because _driverAnimTo is set only by _updateDriverAnimation (2106-2138). _updateDriverAnimation is called only from paintIfDue (2097), and paintIfDue is called only from _onLiveTick (424). Nothing seeds the new state from widget.tracking.eta. _onLiveTick runs only when DriverTrackingController.onChange fires. That happens on a realtime event; ApiRideRealtime drops unchanged projections at api_ride_realtime.dart:202-208. It also happens on a staleness flip, and the stale check only notifies when the stale state changes (driver_tracking_controller.dart:196-203, driver_eta withStalenessCheckedAt:86-87). When fixes keep coming (the mock every 3 s, or the driver app's 1 s stream), the gap lasts only a few seconds. When the driver's feed has already gone quiet and stale, nothing ever fires, so the car stays off the map.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the unpark, initState, _buildMarkers and paintIfDue callers, plus the onChange sources in the tracking controller and the poll dedupe in ApiRideRealtime. No test was run.

verdicts.reason: _changeRoute (waiting_for_driver.dart:1077) parks the map, and the build (around line 1470) puts in a ColoredBox in place of _WaitingRideMap. When the sheet closes, `_mapParked = false; setState` builds a fresh _WaitingRideMapState. Its initState (2036-2040) calls _buildMarkers, and _currentDriverPosition (2148) returns _driverAnimTo, which is null in a new state. The only code that fills it is _updateDriverAnimation, called from paintIfDue (2092). paintIfDue runs only from the parent's _onLiveTick (424). onMapCreated (2423-2428) calls only _refreshRoadRoute, which does not set markers. widget.tracking.eta still holds the last fix, but nothing reads it until the next tick. The next tick can come from any realtime event, because the else branch of the tracking controller keeps the eta coordinates, or from a stale flip (driver_tracking_controller.dart staleCheck: only when `stale` changes, staleAfter 25 s). So the gap is usually short: the driver app on Android publishes about every 1 s (driver_location_service.dart intervalDuration 1 s). But if the feed is quiet and the eta is already stale (for example a web driver standing still at the pickup), no flip happens and the car stays missing until the next event.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: _changeRoute -> _parkMapForStageChange -> new _WaitingRideMapState.initState -> _buildMarkers -> _currentDriverPosition() == null because _driverAnimFrom and _driverAnimTo are unset. The only writer of _driverAnimTo is _updateDriverAnimation, called only from paintIfDue, which only _onLiveTick calls. No widget test was run (it needs the map platform).

confirmed.title: Pre-trip 'Arrive by' destination pin ignores the stops the rider added
confirmed.description: Before boarding, `_syncTimePins` computes the arrival as now + minutes to pickup + `estimatedTripMinutes(pickup, destination)`, a straight pickup-to-destination estimate. `widget.stops` is not used, so adding a stop (or several) never moves the shown arrival time.
confirmed.failure_scenario: While the driver is on the way, the rider adds a stop 5 km off the direct line. The 'Arrive by 08:19' pin over the destination stays at 08:19.
confirmed.evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:2228-2243 now.add(Duration(minutes: toPickupMin + estimatedTripMinutes(GeoPoint(widget.pickupPosition...), GeoPoint(widget.destinationPosition...))))
confirmed.suggested_fix: Sum the estimate over pickup → stops → destination.

verdicts.reason: Before boarding, _syncTimePins (waiting_for_driver.dart:2224-2246) computes the arrival as now + minutes to pickup + estimatedTripMinutes(pickup, destination). estimatedTripMinutes (select_ride_geometry.dart:55-68) is straight-line distance x 1.35 at 40 km/h. widget.stops is never used there, so adding a stop that changes the route does not move the 'Arrive by' pin. It is a rough estimate shared app-wide (Select ride and Finding also leave stops out), so the impact is a modest wrong time on a secondary label. Once the rider is on board, the server's eta seconds are used instead.
verdicts.repro: Static read of _syncTimePins and estimatedTripMinutes, and checked the other callers (select_ride.dart:822, finding_drivers.dart:475). No test was run.

verdicts.reason: Before boarding, _syncTimePins (waiting_for_driver.dart:2232-2250) computes arrive = now + toPickupMin + estimatedTripMinutes(pickup, destination). estimatedTripMinutes (select_ride_geometry.dart:55-68) is a haversine from one point to another, times 1.35, at 40 km/h, with a minimum of 3 min. widget.stops is never used. didUpdateWidget rebuilds markers when the stops change, but the label key does not change, so the pin stays the same.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand. Sergels torg (59.3326,18.0649) to Odenplan (59.3429,18.0498) is about 1.4 km: 1.4*1.35/40*60 = 2.8, raised to the 3 min minimum. Through Liljeholmen (59.3105,18.0230) it is about 3.0 km + 4.0 km = 7 km, which is about 14 min. The 'Arrive by' pin is about 11 min early and does not move when the stop is added.

confirmed.title: Driver car (and Finding's nearby cars) never rotate on web: Marker.rotation is ignored by google_maps_flutter_web
confirmed.description: Waiting computes an interpolated heading for the car and passes it as `rotation: _currentDriverHeading()` with `flat: true`. Finding passes `rotation: vehicle.bearing` (finding_drivers.dart:433). google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2 never maps rotation or flat onto the JS marker (convert.dart:516: "Flat and Rotation are not supported directly on the web."). The top-down car bitmap (MoveraVehicleMarker, headlight dot at the top) therefore always points north on the web. Home already handles this plugin gap by pre-rotating its puck bitmaps on web (home.dart:1521-1541, 1575-1583). The driver markers do not, so the heading work in _bearingDegrees and lerpHeading has no visible effect on the main web platform.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the web demo, the driver heads east along a street towards the pickup, or the trip runs west. The car icon slides sideways, still pointing north, instead of facing where it is driving. Nearby cars on Finding likewise ignore their bearing. On Android and iOS the same code rotates correctly. Not run; read from the plugin source.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:2298-2304 `Marker(markerId: const MarkerId('driver'), position: driverPosition, rotation: _currentDriverHeading(), flat: true, ...)`
finding_drivers.dart:433 `rotation: vehicle.bearing,`
google_maps_flutter_web convert.dart:516 `// Flat and Rotation are not supported directly on the web.`
home.dart:1576-1577 `// The web bitmap is turned on screen, not on the ground: take the map's own bearing off`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reuse Home's approach for the car on web: a small cache of pre-rotated car bitmaps per heading bucket, with heading minus the map bearing. Give those icons explicit width/height or asset URLs so the blob leak above is not made worse.

verdicts.reason: The resolved google_maps_flutter_web is 0.5.14+2. Its _markerOptionsFromMarker (convert.dart:500-517) never sets rotation or flat and says 'Flat and Rotation are not supported directly on the web.' The driver marker relies on rotation: _currentDriverHeading() with flat: true (waiting_for_driver.dart:2298-2306). The icon is the directional top-down MoveraVehicleMarker (movera_map_markers.dart:70). CustomGoogleMap has no web rotation workaround. Home works around the same gap by pre-rotating bitmaps on web (home.dart:1521-1583), which shows this is a known limitation that was not applied to the driver car. So on web the car always points north.
verdicts.repro: Read /root/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/google_maps_flutter_web-0.5.14+2/lib/src/convert.dart:500-517 (no rotation mapping) and checked the version in pubspec.lock. Grepped lib for any web rotation handling: only home.dart has it. Not run in a browser.

verdicts.reason: The pinned plugin google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2 builds MarkerOptions without rotation or flat (convert.dart:497-517: "Flat and Rotation are not supported directly on the web."). The driver marker (waiting_for_driver.dart:2305-2313, rotation: _currentDriverHeading(), flat: true) and the Finding cars (finding_drivers.dart:433, rotation: vehicle.bearing) use the plain MoveraVehicleMarker bitmap with no pre-rotation for web. The only code in lib that pre-rotates for web is Home's puck (home.dart:1521-1583, _webRotatedPuck / _rasteriseRotatedPuck). So on web the top-down car always points north.
verdicts.repro: Read the plugin source in ~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/google_maps_flutter_web-0.5.14+2/lib/src/convert.dart. A grep for 'rotation' in the plugin's lib finds no mapping. pubspec.lock pins that version. A grep for 'rotation' in rider lib finds only the two driver-car markers and the native puck path in home_controller. Not run in a browser.

confirmed.title: Share-trip button on Waiting and in-trip panels is a 40x40 target, below the 44 px floor
confirmed.description: WaitingShareButton is `Padding(EdgeInsets.all(10), child: Icon(size: 20))` inside a circular InkWell, so the hit area is 40x40. A11y.minTapIOS documents 44 as 'the floor for every tap target', and MoveraIconButton uses 48. This button is in the pickup header (_fixedPickupHeader) and the in-trip panel header, a main safety action.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rider in a moving car tries to share the trip from the in-trip panel and misses the 40 px circle. The tap lands on the sheet or the headline instead.
confirmed.evidence:
waiting_sheet_bits.dart:81-91 `child: InkWell(
          customBorder: const CircleBorder(),
          onTap: () => _share(context),
          child: const Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.all(10),
            child: Icon(

confirmed.title: Successful OTP or provider sign-in waits for push registration (Firebase init, getToken, POST /push/devices) before the rider can continue
confirmed.description: verifyOtp and signIn both `await _registerPushBestEffort()` before returning, so PhoneVerification keeps the Verify button busy and SignIn keeps the provider button busy until FirebasePushService.register() finishes. That means Firebase initialize, requestPermission, getToken (no timeout) and _replaceToken's POST (15 s timeout). Push consent is kept across sessions (movera.push_consent.v1 is not wiped, see the separate finding), so this happens on every later sign-in on a device where consent was ever given. This is the sign-in counterpart of the known cold-start finding at bootstrap.dart:130.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a poor connection a rider who once allowed notifications enters the correct code. The spinner keeps going for up to 15 s or more while the push device POST times out, then Home opens. It looks as if sign-in is hanging.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Run registration with unawaited() after entering the app, as the bootstrap comment intends for the first frame.

verdicts.reason: auth_controller.dart:35 and :45 await _registerPushBestEffort() before verifyOtp or signIn returns, and phone_verify.dart:137 awaits verifyOtp before moving on. In a non-mock build (di.dart:121-123, 354-356) with stored consent 'accepted' (push_permission_gate.dart:75), this calls FirebasePushService.register() (firebase_push_service.dart:198-241): initialize, requestPermission, getToken with no timeout, then POST /push/devices. The try/catch in _registerPushBestEffort and _register only catches errors; it does not limit how long these take. On a slow network, sign-in therefore appears to hang. The mock and demo transport is close to instant, so only production is affected.
verdicts.repro: Traced verifyOtp/signIn -> registerIfConsented -> _register -> FirebasePushService.register. Checked the enabled flag in di.dart. No test was run.

verdicts.reason: lib/features/auth/application/auth_controller.dart:35 and :45 `await _registerPushBestEffort()` before returning. That calls PushPermissionGate.registerIfConsented (push_permission_gate.dart:69-77), which for an accepted consent runs FirebasePushService.register (firebase_push_service.dart:198-240): initialize, requestPermission, getToken (no timeout), then POST /api/v1/push/devices. lib/features/auth/presentation/phone_verify.dart:137 awaits verifyOtp with _submitting=true and only then calls enterMoveraApp/RiderNameScreen. So a slow push registration holds the Verify spinner after the OTP has already succeeded. The try/catch only swallows errors. It does not bound the time.
verdicts.repro: Traced the call chain verifyOtp -> _registerPushBestEffort -> registerIfConsented -> _push.register -> _replaceToken POST, and checked that phone_verify.dart:137-147 navigates only after the await. Effect only with production Firebase push (enabled=true) and stored consent 'accepted'. In mock mode register is a no-op.

confirmed.title: Sign-out abandons the pending-cancel flush after 5 s, and the still-running flush can write the previous rider's queued cancels back after the wipe
confirmed.description: UserDataWipe.flushPendingCancels wraps FindingDriverController.flushPendingCancels() in `.timeout(5 s)`. A timeout only stops the wait; the flush keeps running in the background while signOut goes on to clear tokens and run() removes `movera_pending_cancels`. The flush loop uses the list it read at the start. For each entry it re-reads the trip with a GET (up to 2 x 15 s). When the version moved on it calls `PendingCancelStore.add(cancel.forVersion(version))`, which writes the key again. It then POSTs: with the tokens gone that is a 401 with no access token, which is not a permanent failure, so `continue` keeps the entry. The previous rider's cancel now sits in the outbox, and the next session's reconnect or launch flush sends it with the new rider's token. The doc block says that must not happen ('sending them later with another rider's session would cancel nothing or the wrong thing'). `_flushInFlight` also stays set, so a new flush started meanwhile joins the stale run.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a slow network, rider A signs out with a queued end-early or cancel. The GET re-read takes about 7 s, past the 5 s budget, so sign-out clears the tokens and wipes storage. The GET then answers with a newer version, the entry is re-added, and the POST fails 401. Rider B signs in, and every reconnect retries A's cancel under B's session.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give the flush a cancellation token or a session generation that the wipe bumps. Make PendingCancelStore.add a no-op once the session it started under is over, and clear `_flushInFlight` in the wipe.

verdicts.reason: UserDataWipe.flushPendingCancels only times out the wait (user_data_wipe.dart:80). AuthController.signOut then continues to _auth.signOut and UserDataWipe.run (auth_controller.dart:90-108), and run removes movera_pending_cancels (user_data_wipe.dart:100-104). The orphaned _flushPendingCancels keeps its pre-wipe list (finding_driver_controller.dart:1458). Once its GET re-read returns a newer version, it calls PendingCancelStore.add (lines 1474-1477). add writes the key with no session check (pending_cancel_store.dart:274-282). The POST then goes out with no token, gets a 401, and isPermanentCancelFailure does not count 401 as permanent (pending_cancel_store.dart:158-162), so `continue` keeps the entry. _flushInFlight also stays set until the run ends (finding_driver_controller.dart:1419-1423). The race exists, but it is narrow: it needs a queued cancel at sign-out, a re-read slower than 5 s but within the request timeout, and a version bump in between. The leftover entry is A's ride, so under B it is refused or retried uselessly, not used to cancel B's ride. That makes it low severity.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of signOut, then UserDataWipe.flushPendingCancels and run, then _flushPendingCancels, _rereadForReplay, PendingCancelStore.add, and isPermanentCancelFailure. Not run as a test.

verdicts.reason: UserDataWipe.flushPendingCancels (user_data_wipe.dart:77-87) only stops waiting after 5 s. The flush (finding_driver_controller.dart:1454-1505) keeps running on the list it read at the start. When the re-read shows a newer version, it writes the entry back with PendingCancelStore.add (1476-1477). A POST that fails with a non-permanent error is kept (`continue`, 1487-1494; isPermanentCancelFailure accepts only 404/409/410/422, pending_cancel_store.dart:158-162). This reaches a real failure because AuthController.signOut (auth_controller.dart:88-108) clears the tokens and runs UserDataWipe.run, which deletes movera_pending_cancels. The re-add can land after that delete. run() also deletes movera_rider_fingerprint, so enterSessionAs (user_data_wipe.dart:165-176) sees previous == null for the next rider and does not wipe again, and the stale entry survives into rider B's session. Impact is limited. The race needs the GET re-read to answer after the 5 s budget and after sign-out completes, within the 15 s ApiClient timeout. Under B's token the server should refuse the ride (404 drops the entry; 403 keeps retrying it), so a wrong cancellation is unlikely. What remains is a previous-rider record leaking across the wipe and being retried. Low.
verdicts.repro: Ran the throwaway test test/_audit_u68_test.dart (since deleted). It enqueues a cancel for r1 with expectedVersion 1, uses a fake HTTP client whose GET answers after 300 ms with version 5 and whose POST answers 401, and calls FindingDriverController.flushPendingCancels(api) with a 100 ms timeout, standing in for the 5 s budget. It then removes movera_pending_cancels the way run() does. Output: 'timed out: TimeoutException', 'after wipe: 0', then 'POST .../cancel status: 401', 'ride.cancel.flush_failed', and 'after stale flush: 1 [r1 v5]'.

confirmed.title: The new-rider name step is decided once from isNewRider; a reload or kill on that step skips it forever
confirmed.description: verifyOtp saves the session tokens first. Only then does PhoneVerification show RiderNameScreen as the root, and only when that one response says isNewRider. Nothing stores 'name still missing', and nothing checks for an empty profile name later. If the app is killed or the web page reloads on the name screen, the next cold start finds a session and opens Home directly: RiderRestoreCoordinator._root has no name check. The server will not say isNewRider again, because the rider is now known. The rider ends up with no name, which the screen itself says 'the driver will look for'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A brand-new rider verifies their code on the web demo and reloads the tab on 'What should we call you?'. They land on Home with 'Welcome to Movera', are never asked for a name again, and drivers see no rider name.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Persist a 'name pending' flag with the session, or show RiderNameScreen whenever a signed-in profile has an empty name.

verdicts.reason: phone_verify.dart:137-147 shows RiderNameScreen only when this one verifyOtp response has isNewRider. By then the session tokens are already saved, and no 'name pending' flag is stored. On a cold start or reload, RideRestoreCoordinator.root() (ride_restore_coordinator.dart ~444-453) finds a session, skips the sign-in branch and returns pageFor(snapshot or adoptServerActiveTrip()). Nothing checks for an empty name. A real backend would then report the rider as known (the in-process mock forgets known phones on reload, but the restored session means the rider never verifies again anyway). The effect is mitigated: account_home.dart:81 shows 'Add your name' (D-024) when the name is empty, so the rider can still fix it by hand. They are just never prompted, and drivers see no name until they do.
verdicts.repro: Traced verifyOtp, then showMoveraRoot(RiderNameScreen), then RiderNameScreen._save (the only place the name is written, rider_name.dart:55-75), then the cold-start root(). Searched lib for isNewRider and empty-name checks: there is no other gate, apart from the 'Add your name' prompt on the account screen.

verdicts.reason: The name step's only entry is phone_verify.dart:140-147, and it depends on that one response's `isNewRider`. By then verifyOtp has stored the tokens. Tokens survive a reload or kill: SecureTokenStore uses sessionStorage on web (web_session_token_store_web.dart, secure_token_store.dart:9) and secure storage on native. On cold start, RideRestoreCoordinator._root (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:416-453) sees a session through _defaultHasSession (lines 171-175), so _shouldRequireSignIn returns false and it goes to pageFor(...) or Home with no profile-name check. RideRestoreGate only treats a RiderNameScreen it was explicitly shown as an auth root (ride_restore_gate.dart:41). Nothing in lib checks for an empty profile name. RiderNameScreen has no skip (only `_save`, rider_name.dart:117), so a name is meant to be required, and the reload leaves a nameless rider. A real server would not answer isNewRider again because the rider is no longer new. The rider can still type a name in the profile editor, which keeps this low.
verdicts.repro: Traced the path by hand: phone_verify.dart:137-147, then token persistence (SecureTokenStore and sessionStorage on web), then ride_restore_coordinator.dart:171-190 and 416-453 with no name check, then the Home greeting falling back to displayName (side_menu.dart:176). Searched lib for isNewRider, RiderNameScreen and empty-name checks: the only entry is phone_verify.dart:140. No test was run.

confirmed.title: The profile sent to the server says language 'en' while the app speaks the zone language, until the rider picks one by hand
confirmed.description: RiderProfileData.language defaults to 'en'. AppLanguageController (the language the app actually uses: the rider's choice, else the zone default, Swedish in Stockholm) never writes it into the profile. Only pickAppLanguage does. RiderNameScreen._save (and every other profile save) sends `language: 'en'` in the PATCH (FLOW-7: the server uses the language for the rider), even though the rider has been using the app in Swedish all along.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A new rider in Stockholm signs up with the Swedish UI and enters their name. The server stores language 'en', so server-sent messages and receipts arrive in English.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Send AppScope.instance.language.code (or keep the profile language in step with AppLanguageController) instead of the default.

verdicts.reason: RiderProfileData.defaults() sets language to defaultLanguage 'en' (profile.dart:175,196). The only writer of the profile language is pickAppLanguage (language_picker.dart:29). AppLanguageController.code = _choice ?? _zoneDefault (app_language_controller.dart:30), and the zone default is sv in SE and fr in FR/TN per CONTRACT.md:228, but it never writes into the profile. RiderNameScreen._save (rider_name.dart:65-69) updates only the name and sends the whole profile, and synced_profile_repository.dart:62 puts 'language': profile.language in the PATCH. A new Stockholm rider using the Swedish UI is therefore stored server-side as 'en'. The profile.dart:173-174 comment ('English until the rider picks') explains the format, not a decision to report a language the rider is not using. The impact is limited: the in-process mock only stores the value, and no server-sent texts exist yet.
verdicts.repro: Traced RiderNameScreen._save -> ProfileController.update -> SyncedProfileRepository body() (line 62). Grepped every writer of copyWith(language:) (only language_picker.dart:29) and read AppLanguageController load/useZone/choose.

verdicts.reason: RiderProfileData.defaults() sets language to 'en' (profile.dart:175,196). AppLanguageController.code falls back to the zone default, which is 'sv' in Sweden (app_language_controller.dart:30, 54-58), but it never writes into the profile. Only pickAppLanguage does (language_picker.dart:27-29), and its own doc says 'the profile keeps the same code for the server'. RiderNameScreen._save (rider_name.dart:65-69) PATCHes the profile via copyWith(name:), and synced_profile_repository.dart:62 sends 'language': 'en' while the UI is in Swedish. The mock stores what it receives (in_process_mock_client.dart:1144). profile.dart:174 says 'English until the rider picks a language', but that predates the zone-default behaviour and contradicts the picker's stated intent. Severity is low because the contract names no server feature that reads the profile language yet, so the receipt and message impact in the finding is not shown.
verdicts.repro: Traced from RiderNameScreen._save to ProfileController.update, then SyncedProfileRepository (line 62 body), then the mock PATCH handler. Confirmed that no code path copies AppLanguageController.code into RiderProfileData except pickAppLanguage, by grepping `language` in the profile presentation and application files.

confirmed.title: Sign-out shows no progress and does not block taps while flush, push unregister and server sign-out run
confirmed.description: After the confirm dialog closes, confirmAndSignOut awaits signOutAndShowSignIn and shows no progress or barrier. The sequence is: flushPendingCancels (up to 5 s), push.unregister (POST, 15 s timeout, plus deleteToken), POST /auth/sign-out (15 s timeout), and the wipe. On a slow network that can take 30 s or more. The menu, Account and Home remain usable throughout, so the rider can tap Sign out again (a second dialog and a concurrent second signOut and wipe) or start a booking with the still-valid token. That booking is then wiped locally (snapshot cleared, FindingDriverController disposed) while the server ride stays searching.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a weak connection the rider confirms Sign out, sees nothing happen, goes back to Home and books a ride. POST /rides succeeds with the old token and Finding opens. Seconds later the wipe disposes the search and Sign in appears, while the server ride keeps looking for a driver for a rider who has left.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Show a modal progress barrier (or disable navigation) from the confirm until showSignInRoot, and ignore repeated sign-out taps while one is running.

verdicts.corrected_title: Sign-out shows no progress and does not block taps while flush, push unregister and server sign-out run
verdicts.reason: sign_out_flow.dart:42-43 closes the confirm dialog and then awaits signOutAndShowSignIn with no barrier or progress indicator. AuthController.signOut (auth_controller.dart:89-111) awaits flushPendingCancels, push.unregister and _auth.signOut, each of which can take seconds on a slow network. Neither caller, side_menu.dart:702 nor account_home.dart:245, guards against re-entry, so Sign out can be tapped again and a second dialog and signOut run. The booking scenario is reachable but unlikely: the rider would have to finish a whole booking during that window, and UserDataWipe.resetInMemory (user_data_wipe.dart:113-119) then disposes FindingDriverController without cancelling the ride on the server, because the cancel flush already ran first. The repeated wipes are idempotent. The real defect is the missing feedback and missing re-entry guard.
verdicts.repro: Traced confirmAndSignOut -> signOutAndShowSignIn -> AuthController.signOut -> UserDataWipe.run/resetInMemory and both callers. The mock transport makes this near-instant, so only production builds are affected. No test was run.

verdicts.reason: lib/features/auth/presentation/sign_out_flow.dart:42-43: after the dialog pops true, signOutAndShowSignIn awaits AuthController.signOut (auth_controller.dart:89-111): flushPendingCancels (bounded by _flushBudget), push.unregister (network), _auth.signOut (network), then UserDataWipe.run. It shows no barrier or busy state, and the callers (side_menu.dart:702, account_home.dart:245) have no re-entry guard. On a slow production network the rider can tap Sign out again or start a booking with the still-valid token, and UserDataWipe.run (user_data_wipe.dart:92-97, resetInMemory, RideSnapshotStore.clear, clearSearchLive) then wipes it locally. The window exists only when network calls are slow, so this is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Read sign_out_flow.dart in full, the AuthController.signOut sequence and both call sites. There is no _busy flag, no ModalBarrier and no disabled state between the confirm and showSignInRoot. Not run, since a slow-network timing repro needs the production push and auth transports.

confirmed.title: The duplicate-ride stand-down cancel is sent once and never queued, so a failure leaves two live rides
confirmed.description: When a booking response arrives while another Finding owns a ride, `_standDownIfFindingOwned` POSTs `/cancel` for the duplicate directly. It does not go through the pending-cancel outbox. If that POST fails (offline or 5xx), the exception escapes `_submitFinding`. `_sendOrRecover` treats it as may-have-booked and replays, the replay hits the same stand-down, and the error finally reaches Select Ride as `bookingUncertain`. Nothing remembers that the duplicate must be cancelled, so it stays live on the server. Long network stalls on Book now (up to 15 s plus 15 s plus a 30 s GET) widen the window for this race.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Book now request is stuck on a flaky network. Meanwhile another Finding for a different ride becomes active (restore or push). The booking response arrives and the stand-down cancel fails on the same bad network. The rider sees 'couldn't confirm your booking' while two rides are live on the server. Traced by reading the code.
confirmed.evidence: booking_coordinator.dart:774-782 `// The race-losing backend ride must be explicitly stood down; never leave two live rides. final cancelIntent = createdRideId; await _client.post('/api/v1/rides/$createdRideId/cancel', ... idempotencyKey: _duplicateCancelMutation.keyFor(cancelIntent),);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Enqueue the stand-down through `PendingCancelStore.enqueue` before sending, so the outbox flush retries it, and do not treat the stand-down's failure as a booking failure.

verdicts.reason: booking_coordinator.dart:777-782 sends the stand-down cancel with a plain `_client.post` and calls `_duplicateCancelMutation.succeeded` only if that post succeeds. Nothing calls PendingCancelStore.enqueue on this path; the outbox is only filled from finding_driver_controller.dart:1175. If the post fails, the exception leaves `_submitFinding` (line 682 or 738) and `_sendOrRecover` (lines 442-457) treats a retryable ApiError as may-have-booked. It replays, the replay reaches the same stand-down and fails again, and then `_adoptActiveTrip` runs. That returns null when the active trip has a different destination, or it hits the stand-down a third time (line 488). The code clearly expects this race: comments at lines 735-737 and 774-775, and the reconcileCreatedFinding path at select_ride.dart:1582-1586. It still needs a Finding owner for a different ride to appear while a slow booking is in flight, plus a failed cancel, so it is a narrow edge case.

confirmed.title: On web only, matchRange can return offsets past the original string (e.g. 'İ' folds to two code units), so the suggestion highlight is misplaced or substring throws RangeError
confirmed.description: `foldForSearch` lowercases with `toLowerCase()`, which can change string length. On web (JS semantics), 'İ' (U+0130) becomes 'i̇', two code units. `matchRange` returns indices into the folded text, and `_highlighted` applies them to the original with `substring(start, end)`. Once the text contains such a character, the highlight shifts, and a match near the end gives `end > text.length`, a RangeError during build.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A suggestion titled 'İzmir Kebab' (5+6 chars), with the rider typing 'kebab': folded index 7, end 12, but the original length is 11, so substring throws RangeError and the results list shows an error widget (or a grey box in release).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Fold character by character while keeping a map from folded index to original index, or clamp and validate the range before calling substring.

verdicts.corrected_title: On web only, matchRange can return offsets past the original string (e.g. 'İ' folds to two code units), so the suggestion highlight is misplaced or substring throws RangeError

On the Dart VM (Android/iOS) toLowerCase keeps the length, so mobile is not affected. On web (a supported PWA target, DECISIONS R-web) dart2js uses JS toLowerCase, which maps U+0130 to 'i' plus U+0307 (two code units). The ranges then shift, and a match near the end gives end > length, a RangeError during build. Titles come from backend/geocoder JSON (PlaceSuggestion.fromJson), so a name such as 'İzmir Kebab' is a realistic input.

The web behaviour rests on the Unicode SpecialCasing mapping that JS String.prototype.toLowerCase applies unconditionally. A Chrome test run would settle the web part fully.

confirmed.title: Finding's elapsed counter adds one per timer tick instead of reading searchStartedAt, so after timers are paused the 'Still looking' copy and the raise-offer card come late (a server-ended search is still caught by the resync on resume)
confirmed.description: `start()` works out `elapsedSeconds` from `snapshot.searchStart` once (ARCH-3 / RIDE-5: 'elapsed counts from when this search started'). After that, `_startTick` only adds `elapsedSeconds += 1` each periodic tick. Timers are suspended while a mobile app is in the background, and browsers throttle them in hidden tabs (iOS Safari suspends the tab; Chrome drops to about one tick a minute after 5 minutes). Neither Finding nor its controller has a lifecycle hook (only Home and AppLifecycleObserver observe lifecycle), so after a pause the counter stays behind wall-clock time. Everything gated on it fires late: `isDelayed`/searchDelayed, `showPriceBump` (`elapsedSeconds >= priceBumpAfter.inSeconds`), `_reachSearchTimeout` and the periodic `checkServerSearchState`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider books, waits 30 s, then switches apps for 4 minutes while the search goes on. When they come back, Finding shows about 30 s elapsed and the early 'searching' copy. 'Still looking for a driver' (3-minute mark) and the server check behind it only appear 2.5 minutes later, although the search has really run 4.5 minutes, so a server-ended 'no driver found' is noticed late too.
confirmed.evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:337-340 `final sinceStart = DateTime.now().difference(snapshot.searchStart); elapsedSeconds = sinceStart.isNegative ? 0 : sinceStart.inSeconds;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:418-428 `_tick = Timer.periodic(const Duration(seconds: 1), (timer) { ... elapsedSeconds += 1; _evaluatePhase(); _afterElapsed(1); ...`
confirmed.suggested_fix: On each tick, recompute elapsed from `_snapshot.searchStart` (`DateTime.now().difference(searchStart).inSeconds`) and pass the real step to `_afterElapsed`, so a resumed tick catches up at once.

verdicts.corrected_title: Finding's elapsed counter adds one per timer tick instead of reading searchStartedAt, so after timers are paused the 'Still looking' copy and the raise-offer card come late (a server-ended search is still caught by the resync on resume)

The resume handler (app_lifecycle.dart:15-22 -> resumeIfNeeded, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:576-600) returns early because next == showing, so Finding is not restarted and the counter is never recomputed. So isDelayed, showPriceBump, _reachSearchTimeout and the periodic server check fire late by the time timers were suspended or throttled. The finding overstates one part: resumeIfNeeded calls reconnectAndResync(id) (580, 166-167), which pushes the server state through realtime, so a search the server already ended is not noticed late. What remains is the copy and cards appearing late on Finding.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of start(), _startTick, AppLifecycleObserver and resumeIfNeeded. Not run.

verdicts.reason: elapsedSeconds is computed from searchStart only in start() (finding_driver_controller.dart:337-340). After that, _startTick (418-428) adds 1 per Timer.periodic callback. A Dart periodic timer does not replay missed ticks after the isolate is suspended (iOS background, web hidden-tab throttling), so the counter falls behind wall-clock time. Nothing re-syncs it on resume: AppLifecycleObserver (lib/app/lifecycle/app_lifecycle.dart:15-22) calls RideRestoreCoordinator.resumeIfNeeded, which returns early when the surface is still Finding (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:599 `if (next == showing) return null`), and Finding has no lifecycle observer. As a result isDelayed, showPriceBump, the 3-minute _reachSearchTimeout and the 15 s server checks (_afterElapsed, 441-453) fire late by the time spent in the background. Low severity: realtime still delivers server status changes, so mainly the copy, the raise card and the backup poll are late.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: Dart Timer.periodic skips missed periods (it does not replay them), the counter only does `elapsedSeconds += 1`, and no resume hook calls start() or recomputes elapsed. Example: 30 s elapsed, then 240 s in the background. The resumed tick gives elapsedSeconds=31 while wall-clock time is about 270 s, so the 180 s mark is reached about 150 s late.

confirmed.title: checkServerSearchState ignores _cancelQueued: on a restore past searchTimeout, a server cancelled_by_rider is handled as a foreign terminal (no History record, generic sheet instead of the committed-cancel flow)
confirmed.description: The realtime listener treats `cancelledByRider` while `_cancelQueued` as the queued cancel landing (`_confirmQueuedCancel`: archive, why-sheet). `checkServerSearchState` checks neither `_cancelQueued` before nor after its await. On a restore whose search is past `searchTimeout`, `start()` schedules `_reachSearchTimeout` as a microtask, which starts the GET before the async `_adoptQueuedCancel` has set `_cancelQueued`. When the GET answers cancelled_by_rider, it calls `_completeTerminal(cancelledByRider)`. That status is not in the archive list, so History gets no record, `_queuedReasonId` is lost, and `_handleTerminal` (with `_match.cancelled` false) shows the generic terminal sheet instead of the committed-cancel flow.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider cancels offline 4 minutes into a search and reloads. The restore flush times out (no answer in 4 s), so Finding is restored as Cancelling…. The server-state GET comes back cancelled_by_rider. The ride ends with the generic sheet, is not in History, and the queued reason is never sent.
confirmed.evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:355-360 `if (elapsedSeconds >= searchTimeout.inSeconds) { scheduleMicrotask(_reachSearchTimeout); } ... unawaited(_adoptQueuedCancel(snapshot.rideId));`
finding_driver_controller.dart:503-509 post-await guard has no `_cancelQueued`
finding_driver_controller.dart:527-529 `if (status.isTerminal) { _realtime.unsubscribe(); await _completeTerminal(status);`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1027-1034 archive list omits cancelledByRider
confirmed.suggested_fix: In checkServerSearchState, after the await, route `status == cancelledByRider` with `_cancelQueued` (or a stored outbox entry) to `_confirmQueuedCancel()`. Or skip the check while a cancel is queued.

verdicts.reason: The gap in the code is real. checkServerSearchState (finding_driver_controller.dart:491-535) never checks _cancelQueued, and on a terminal status it calls _completeTerminal, whose archive list omits cancelledByRider (1027-1034). The microtask GET (355-357) can therefore end a ride that has a queued cancel without the committed-cancel flow. Reaching it needs a narrow ordering. The coordinator first runs the outbox flush (_dropIfCancelQueued, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:118-164); if it gets 'sent', the ride is archived and dropped before Finding mounts. Finding's _flushQueuedCancel joins the same in-flight flush (1419-1420). If that flush resolves first, _onOutboxOutcome -> _confirmQueuedCancel takes the correct path, and a realtime cancelledByRider event while _cancelQueued also does (374-378). The bad path needs a GET sent at least 4 s after the cancel POST to return cancelled_by_rider before the cancel's own response or the realtime event, for example when the cancel's response is lost after the server applied it. In the in-process mock the flush answers at once, so this does not happen there. To settle it: an ApiClient test that holds the cancel POST response, returns cancelled_by_rider for GET /rides/{id}, and checks whether History has no record and the generic sheet is shown.

verdicts.corrected_title: checkServerSearchState ignores _cancelQueued: on a restore past searchTimeout, a server cancelled_by_rider is handled as a foreign terminal (no History record, generic sheet instead of the committed-cancel flow)
verdicts.reason: start() resets _cancelQueued=false (finding_driver_controller.dart:313), schedules _reachSearchTimeout as a microtask when elapsed >= 180 s (355-357), and _reachSearchTimeout calls checkServerSearchState (476). The GET is therefore sent before _adoptQueuedCancel (1221-1247) sets _cancelQueued. Neither the pre-await guard (490-496) nor the post-await guard (503-509) checks _cancelQueued. A cancelled_by_rider answer goes to _completeTerminal (527-529), which sets _terminated, archives nothing for cancelledByRider (1027-1034) and clears the store. _onOutboxOutcome and _confirmQueuedCancel are then ignored because _terminated is set (1262-1266, 1304). _handleTerminal sees _match.cancelled false and shows the generic terminal sheet (finding_drivers.dart:316-330). Reachable when the restore flush in _dropIfCancelQueued (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:131-150) gets no answer while the server did apply the cancel, so Finding restores. The race is then between that GET and the controller's own re-flush. Two claims in the finding are wrong: the outbox entry is not left behind (the re-flush still runs and removes it on sent/gone), and the reason is not lost (it is carried in the queued cancel body, pending_cancel_store.dart:77-80).

verdicts.reason:
I confirmed this by running a test. checkServerSearchState (lib/features/finding_driver/application/finding_driver_controller.dart:488-535) never checks _cancelQueued, either before its await (490-496) or after it (503-509). When the GET answers cancelled_by_rider, it goes straight to _completeTerminal (527-529). That sets _terminated and clears the store, but its archive list (1027-1034) leaves out cancelledByRider, so nothing is written to History. Because _terminated is now set, the later outbox outcome is dropped in _onOutboxOutcome (1262-1266) and _confirmQueuedCancel (1304) also bails, so the committed-cancel flow never runs. finding_drivers.dart:318 then sees _match.cancelled == false and shows the generic terminal sheet (331) instead of the why-sheet.

How it is reached: a restore of a search that is already past the 3-minute searchTimeout. start() schedules _reachSearchTimeout as a microtask (355-357), so the GET goes out on mount. Meanwhile the restore flush is still in flight: the coordinator only times out its own 4 s wait (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:64-67), and _flushQueuedCancel joins that same flush (1419-1420). ARCHITECTURE.md:13-16 and :44 say a rider cancel of a live ride is archived to History, so the missing record is wrong behaviour, not a design choice. The race is narrow, but it is an edge path with wrong behaviour that lasts, so I rate it medium.

Two parts of the finding are wrong, and I measured both. First, the outbox entry is not left behind: when the held flush answers, it removes the entry (outbox=0). Second, the reason is not lost to the outbox: the queued body carries it. So the real harm is no History record plus the generic sheet in place of the why-sheet.

confirmed.description: `cancelSearch` sets `_cancelInFlight = true` and stops the tick, then awaits `PendingCancelStore.enqueue` outside any try. If SharedPreferences throws (web quota/blocked storage), the error escapes `cancelSearch`. In the sheet, `_confirm` closes with false and rethrows. In `_confirmCancel`, `await request` throws before `_cancelSheetOpen = false`, so `_drainDeferredNavigation` returns early from then on. In the controller, `_cancelInFlight` stays true: `cancelSearch` returns ignored, and `_completeAssigned` only sets `_assignmentPending` ("wait for the cancel"), which nothing ever resolves.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In a browser where localStorage writes throw, the rider taps Cancel request. The sheet closes, nothing is sent, the timer stops and the X does nothing. When a driver accepts, the rider is never moved to Waiting.
confirmed.evidence:

finding_driver_controller.dart:939-944 `if (_editInFlight || _cancelInFlight) { _assignmentPending = true; return; }`
