verdicts.reason: cancelSearch sets _cancelInFlight=true and cancels the tick (finding_driver_controller.dart:1101-1106), then awaits _requestServerCancel, whose first statement `await PendingCancelStore.enqueue(...)` (1175) is outside the per-attempt try (try starts at 1182). enqueue -> add -> prefs.setStringList (pending_cancel_store.dart:~268) has no catch, PreferencesStore.setStringList forwards straight to SharedPreferences (preferences_store.dart), and shared_preferences_web 2.4.3 calls window.localStorage.setItem without a catch (line 93/204), so a QuotaExceededError escapes. Nothing resets _cancelInFlight; later cancelSearch calls return ignored (1098) and _completeAssigned only sets _assignmentPending (939-944), which only cancelSearch/_onOutboxOutcome resolve. In the screen, `final result = request == null ? null : await request;` (finding_drivers.dart:586) throws before `_cancelSheetOpen = false` (595), and _drainDeferredNavigation returns early while _cancelSheetOpen is true (finding_drivers.dart:268-272), so matches and terminals never navigate. The trigger is narrow: a storage write has to throw while the earlier reads work, which in practice means a web quota error. That makes it low severity.

verdicts.reason: The wedge does happen if `PendingCancelStore.enqueue` throws: finding_driver_controller.dart:1101 sets `_cancelInFlight` and the `await` at 1175 has no try, and finding_drivers.dart:586/595 never clears `_cancelSheetOpen`. But the trigger cannot really happen. enqueue first reads, then writes one small string list through the same SharedPreferences instance (pending_cancel_store.dart:274-281, preferences_store.dart:9-19). By the time the rider can tap Cancel on Finding, the app has already written the live-ride snapshot to the same localStorage through RideSnapshotStore.save. That write is unguarded and awaited, and per DECISIONS.md R-web the search depends on it. So blocked storage would already have failed before this screen. Modern browsers do not throw on setItem for a list this small: they throw only on quota, and the app stores only small JSON there. The codebase does not treat a storage failure as a handled case anywhere on this path. The same speculative trigger was refuted for the unawaited snapshot save in this controller.

Checked the UI path finding_drivers.dart:567-614. I wrote no test because the precondition (setStringList throws while every earlier prefs write succeeded) has no real trigger on the targets.

verdicts.reason:
The failure chain is in the code and a run reproduced it. cancelSearch sets `_cancelInFlight = true` and cancels the tick (finding_driver_controller.dart:1101-1106). It then awaits `PendingCancelStore.enqueue` at 1175, which is outside the per-attempt try that starts at 1182. Nothing resets `_cancelInFlight` when enqueue throws. Every later cancelSearch returns `ignored` (1097-1099), and `_completeAssigned` only sets `_assignmentPending` (939-944), so a driver accepting is silently swallowed. The run showed all of this, and it showed the wedge stays after storage recovers.

In the UI, the sheet's `_confirm` closes in a finally (cancel_ride_sheet.dart:152-157). The error then rethrows from `await request` (finding_drivers.dart:586) before `_cancelSheetOpen = false` (595). From then on `_drainDeferredNavigation` returns early at 272, so no match or terminal state can navigate.

The reproducer's objection is about the trigger, and it does not hold. The wedge does not need storage to be broken all the time. One failed write to the outbox is enough, and it is permanent. localStorage quota is shared by the whole origin and changes over time. The web build is served from the account's shared origin baccarisverige-ux.github.io (.github/workflows/qa-device-pwa-responsive.yml:57), so an earlier successful snapshot save does not mean this later write will succeed. shared_preferences_web 2.4.3 calls `localStorage.setItem` with no catch, so a QuotaExceededError reaches the caller. The codebase also does treat storage failures as a real case elsewhere. The same controller guards the outbox read (`PendingCancelStore.find` in try/catch at 1225-1229), and location_repository.dart:71-82, push_permission_gate.dart:55-60 and local_reservation_repository.dart:35-41 guard their writes.

On native, setStringList returns false and does not throw. So the trigger is limited to web and needs a quota error, which makes this low severity. It is minor but real.

confirmed.title: A non-version 409 on the foreground search cancel always shows 'driver already accepted', but under the contract that 409 only happens when the trip has already ended (expired / no driver / admin or driver cancel)
confirmed.description: Apart from version_mismatch and already-cancelled-by-rider, `_requestServerCancel` maps any 409 to `driverAccepted` without looking at the error projection's status. The outbox path (`_refusalResult`) re-reads the trip to tell "driver accepted" from "already over", but the foreground path does not. The contract says 409 means "the ride moved on first", which includes the search expiring (expired / no_driver_found) or an admin/system cancel at the same moment.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The search expires on the server just as the rider taps Cancel request, and the server answers 409 with projection status expired. The rider sees "A driver already accepted your ride", then the no-driver-found sheet when realtime delivers the terminal.

verdicts.corrected_title: A non-version 409 on the foreground search cancel always shows 'driver already accepted', but under the contract that 409 only happens when the trip has already ended (expired / no driver / admin or driver cancel)
verdicts.reason: _requestServerCancel maps every 409 that is not version_mismatch and not already-cancelled-by-rider to SearchCancelResult.driverAccepted (finding_driver_controller.dart:1205-1210). Per contracts/CONTRACT.md:32,83, a driver accepting first produces 409 version_mismatch, which is handled here as stale. A rider `cancel` is a legal transition from accepted/driver_to_pickup/arrived (trip_transitions.dart:101), so it is never an invalid_transition. A plain 409 invalid_transition therefore only comes back for a trip that is already terminal (expired, no_driver_found, cancelled by the driver or admin). For exactly that case the screen shows l10n.driverAlreadyAccepted (finding_drivers.dart:603-606), and then the terminal sheet once realtime catches up. The outbox path (_refusalResult) re-reads the trip and tells these cases apart, but the foreground path does not. It only happens on a race at the end of the search, so it is low severity.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: finding_driver_controller.dart:1194-1211; contract rules CONTRACT.md:32 (stale -> version_mismatch) and :83 (anything not in the table -> invalid_transition); rider cancel transition set in trip_transitions.dart:101; UI mapping in finding_drivers.dart:603-606. No test run.

verdicts.reason: The scenario cannot reach the `driverAccepted` mapping. Every cancel sends `expectedVersion: ride.projectionVersionOf(id)` (finding_driver_controller.dart:1178). Both realtime transports keep that value current (di.dart:196-206 passes `onProjectionVersion: ride.observeProjectionVersion`; api_ride_realtime.dart:213), and so does the create response (booking_coordinator.dart:234/681). The reference server checks the version before the transition (in_process_mock_client.dart:704-706 `_versionMismatch` comes before `_apply` at 718-720, and CONTRACT.md:34 says the same). A server-side expiry or system/admin cancel the rider has not yet seen bumps the version, so the answer is 409 `version_mismatch`. That maps to `stale` ('ride just changed', line 1207), not to driverAccepted. If the transport has already seen the terminal version, the controller gets the terminal event itself. A plain 409 invalid_transition with a terminal projection needs a cancel with no known version, or a version equal to the terminal one that the controller has not processed. That is only a sub-second window around the first poll after a web reload. Separately, the 'driver already accepted' label is mostly moot, because a rider cancel is allowed from requested through arrived (CONTRACT.md:107), so an acceptance race also comes back as version_mismatch.
verdicts.repro: Traced the mock cancel handler (in_process_mock_client.dart:672-720, _versionMismatch at 1448-1465, _invalidTransition at 1675-1687), the version plumbing (ride_session.dart:40-66, di.dart:196-206, api_ride_realtime.dart:205-213) and the controller mapping (finding_driver_controller.dart:1197-1210). Worked through the race by hand: expiry → version v+1; the rider sends v → 409 version_mismatch → isVersionMismatch true (api_error.dart:36) → SearchCancelResult.stale.

verdicts.corrected_title: A second Cancel tap on a search the server already ended is reported as "a driver already accepted"
verdicts.reason:
The mapping ignores the trip's status, and the app reaches it on the same end-of-search race through its own code, though not on the single tap the finding describes.

On the single tap, the reproducer is right. The cancel sends the version the rider last saw, and the mock checks the version before the transition (in_process_mock_client.dart:705, before _apply at :718). A search that ends on the server bumps the version (_touch, :1358). The answer is therefore version_mismatch, which the app shows as stale ("ride just changed"). I ran it with expired, cancelled_by_system and cancelled_by_admin, and all three came back stale.

What the reproducer missed is the stale branch itself. It records the new version from the refusal's projection (finding_driver_controller.dart:1200 `ride.observeProjection((error as ApiError).projection)`) but never acts on that projection's terminal status. It turns the screen back to searching and only asks realtime to resync (:1148-1162). If the rider taps Cancel again before that resync lands, the second request carries the terminal version. The version check passes, and the server answers 409 invalid_transition because the trip is expired. Lines 1205-1210 then return driverAccepted, and finding_drivers.dart:603-606 shows l10n.driverAlreadyAccepted for a search that expired.

The same thing happens after a refused pickup or price edit, because _staleEdit (:893) records the terminal version the same way. It also happens when no version is known (cold restore before the first poll), but only against the mock, which skips the version check when expectedVersion is missing.

The label is never right on this branch. Under the contract a rider cancel is allowed from requested through arrived (CONTRACT.md transition table), so a driver accepting first can only produce version_mismatch. A plain invalid_transition means the trip is already over. ARCHITECTURE.md:18's "409 (driver already accepted)" describes the old meaning and is not a decision to label ended trips that way.

The window is short (one resync poll, at most about 2s with ApiRideRealtime's 2s poll interval) and needs two taps, so the severity is low.
verdicts.repro:
Throwaway test /home/user/movera-rider-app/test/_audit_u99_decider_test.dart (now deleted). It used InProcessMockClient to book a ride and record its version (v1), a fake RideRealtime that sends no events, and the real FindingDriverController. Steps: POST /rides/{id}/status {status: expired} makes the version 2, then cancelSearch(), then cancelSearch() again. Output:
"ApiError(version_mismatch, The trip is at version 2, not 1.) ... first tap -> SearchCancelResult.stale, known version now 2, terminated=false"
"ApiError(invalid_transition, cancel is not allowed while the trip is expired.) ... second tap -> SearchCancelResult.driverAccepted (server status expired)".
A matrix over expired / cancelled_by_system / cancelled_by_admin gave stale whenever the version from before the trip ended was known (the finding's single-tap case). It gave driverAccepted when no version was known, or when the terminal version had already been recorded. All 10 cases passed.

confirmed.title: Search elapsed clock freezes while a cancel is in flight or queued, and resumes from the frozen value after a refusal or stale result (e.g. an offer sent or lapsed during the replay)
confirmed.description: ARCH-3/RIDE-5 say elapsed counts from when the search started (`start()` derives it from `snapshot.searchStart`). `cancelSearch` and `_adoptQueuedCancel` cancel the 1-second tick. After a refusal (409/422/stale, or an outbox refused/stale outcome) `_startTick()` just restarts it, so `elapsedSeconds` misses the whole in-flight or offline period. The still-looking mark (searchTimeout), the periodic server check cadence, the price-bump time, the copy rotation and the progress bar all run late by that amount, while a reload would jump to the true value.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider's cancel sits queued for 2 minutes offline, then is refused because a driver was about to accept, but the match falls through. The search shows 1:00 elapsed instead of 3:00, and the "Still looking for a driver" card and server check come 2 minutes late.
confirmed.evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:1105-1106 `_tick?.cancel(); _tick = null;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1242-1243 (queued adopt) `_tick?.cancel(); _tick = null;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1151-1152 `} else if (!_assigned) { _startTick(); }`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1284-1285 `} else if (!_assigned) { _startTick();`
finding_driver_controller.dart:339-340 `final sinceStart = DateTime.now().difference(snapshot.searchStart); elapsedSeconds = ...`
confirmed.suggested_fix: In `_startTick` (or on refusal), recompute `elapsedSeconds` from `_snapshot.searchStart`, and run `_afterElapsed` for the skipped span.

verdicts.reason: elapsedSeconds is derived from snapshot.searchStart only in start() (finding_driver_controller.dart:339-340). After that it is only incremented by the 1-second Timer in _startTick (416-428), which does not resync to searchStart. cancelSearch (1105-1106) and _adoptQueuedCancel (1242-1243) cancel the tick. The queued branch (1123-1137) does not restart it, so the clock stays frozen for the whole time the cancel is queued. After a refusal, cancelSearch (1151-1152) and _onOutboxOutcome (1284-1285) just call _startTick(), so the time spent in flight or queued is lost. The search-timeout mark, the server-check cadence (_afterElapsed 440-453), isDelayed/price-bump (183,198) and the copy (225) all run late by that amount, while a reload would recompute the true value. This is real but limited to the cancel-refused edge path.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _startTick/_afterElapsed and every place that cancels or restarts the tick (1105, 1123-1137, 1151, 1242, 1285). No test run.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism is real. The tick stops at finding_driver_controller.dart:1105-1106 and 1242-1243, and on a refusal `_startTick` (417-429) resumes `elapsedSeconds += 1` from the frozen value without going back to `snapshot.searchStart` (339-340). But the scenario that would make it matter cannot really happen, and the effect that can happen is harmless. (1) Foreground: the freeze lasts as long as the cancel POST, which is milliseconds normally and at most 2×15 s on timeouts (api_client.dart:42). It ends in a refusal only on 409 version_mismatch, so the clock is a few seconds late at most. (2) Queued for minutes, then refused while the search goes on: a rider cancel is legal from requested through arrived (CONTRACT.md:107). The outbox re-reads and re-targets the current version before replaying (finding_driver_controller.dart:1472-1477), so `refused`/`stale` means the trip moved on, which in practice is a match. A match stops the tick anyway (_completeAssigned). The finding's 'refused, then the match falls through' needs a chain that is purely speculative. The comment at 1141-1144 ('Pick up where the search was') shows the resume is deliberate.
verdicts.repro: Hand trace: cancelSearch → tick cancelled at elapsed E. The POST times out after 15 s, the retry returns 409 version_mismatch → stale → _startTick at 1151 → the clock resumes at E while the true value is E+15+rtt. Queued path: _flushPendingCancels updates the version before the POST (1472-1477), and _refusalResult (1586-1630) returns refused/stale only for a trip that is still live and refused, which a live searching trip does not produce under the transition table.

verdicts.reason: Both checkers agree on the mechanism. `cancelSearch` (finding_driver_controller.dart:1105-1106) and `_adoptQueuedCancel` (1242-1243) stop the tick. `_startTick` (417-429) then only adds 1 per second. The refusal paths (1151-1152, 1284-1285) restart the tick from the frozen value and never recompute it from `snapshot.searchStart`, even though the comment at 337-340 says elapsed counts from when the search started so that a reload does not change it. The reproducer said a refusal while the trip is still searching cannot really happen. That is wrong. The contract has `searching ⇄ offered`: the server sends an offer and the offer lapses, and each step raises the trip version while the rider still sees "Still searching" (contracts/CONTRACT.md:86 and 93-95). The outbox re-reads the trip and replays the cancel at that version (1472-1477). If an offer goes out or lapses between the re-read and the POST, the server answers 409 version_mismatch. `_refusalResult` (1625-1627) then returns `stale` for a trip that is still live, and `_onOutboxOutcome` resumes the tick from the frozen value (1284-1285). That is ordinary dispatch churn, not a far-fetched chain of events. The foreground path loses up to about 15 s or more (one timed-out attempt, api_client.dart:42), and the queued path loses the whole offline period. Severity stays low. The window is narrow, and the effects are UI marks: the still-looking card, the price bump, the copy and how often the server is checked. The server ends the search on its own (105-108), and realtime keeps listening throughout.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_u100_test.dart, and deleted it after the run. It starts the controller with searchTimeout set to 4 s and an offline ApiClient. `cancelSearch()` returns queued, then the test waits 5 s. Next it calls `FindingDriverController.flushPendingCancels` with a server whose GET returns status searching at v4 and whose POST cancel returns 409 version_mismatch with an offered projection at v5. It waits 1.5 s, then starts a new controller from the same snapshot to act as a reload. Output: "results={u100: PendingCancelResult.stale} refused=1", "elapsed at queue=0, after 5s queued=0, after refusal+1.5s=1, wall-clock=6", "stillLooking=false showStillLooking=false (searchTimeout 4s)", and for the reload "elapsed=6 stillLooking=true". The test passed ("00:06 +1: All tests passed!"), so the live search is 5 s behind and the still-looking mark was missed, while a reload jumps to the true value.

confirmed.title: Cancel reason attached to an outbox entry is silently dropped when the replay re-read finds the trip already cancelled
confirmed.description: For a queued cancel that the server already applied (the response was lost), Finding commits through the realtime listener (lines 375-378 → `_confirmQueuedCancel`) without removing the outbox entry. The why-sheet then calls `sendCancelReason`, and `PendingCancelStore.attachReason` finds the stale entry, stores the reason on it and returns true, so no POST is made (line 1376). When the outbox is later flushed, `_rereadForReplay` sees `cancelled_by_rider` and returns `sent` without sending anything, then the entry is removed. The reason never reaches the server, although the doc says it "rides along with a cancel still queued in the outbox". The mock contract stores a later reason on a cancelled ride, so the code plainly expects the server to have it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a flaky network the cancel POST lands but both responses time out, so it is queued. The next poll shows cancelled_by_rider, Finding commits and the why-sheet opens. The rider picks "Driver too far" and Send. The reason is written into the outbox entry, and the next flush drops it unsent. Support/admin never see the rider's cancel reason.

finding_driver_controller.dart:375-378 `if (_cancelQueued && event.status == RideStatus.cancelledByRider) { unawaited(_confirmQueuedCancel()); return; }` (no PendingCancelStore.remove)

finding_driver_controller.dart:1549-1551 `if (status == TripStatus.cancelledByRider) { return (result: PendingCancelResult.sent, version: version); }`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1498 `await PendingCancelStore.remove(cancel.rideId);`

verdicts.reason: Sequence: a queued cancel is confirmed by realtime. The listener calls _confirmQueuedCancel (finding_driver_controller.dart:375-378) -> _commitCancelled (1295-1335), and neither removes the PendingCancelStore entry. _onTerminal -> _handleTerminal -> _finishCommittedCancel opens the why-sheet (finding_drivers.dart:316-321, 621-633) -> sendCancelReason. attachReason finds the lingering entry, writes the reason into it and returns true, so sendCancelReason returns without the POST (1376). On the next flush (reconnect watcher or bootstrap), _rereadForReplay sees cancelled_by_rider and returns sent with no request (1549-1551), and the entry is removed (1498). The reason never reaches the server, although the sendCancelReason doc (1337-1341) and the mock server's R-O3 handling (in_process_mock_client.dart:690-701) expect a reason to be stored on a ride that is already cancelled. A cancel whose POSTs time out twice after the server already applied it returns `queued` and keeps the outbox entry (finding_driver_controller.dart:1182-1216). The next realtime poll reports cancelled_by_rider, and the listener calls `_confirmQueuedCancel` (375-378). That commits (1303-1314, 1316-1343) but never calls `PendingCancelStore.remove`. That realtime path does not start a flush either (the flush at 381 is only for `isSearching`). The UI then opens the why-sheet (finding_drivers.dart:318-321 → _finishCommittedCancel → 633 sendCancelReason). `sendCancelReason` stores the reason locally and then returns early at 1376, because `attachReason` (pending_cancel_store.dart:322-327) finds the stale entry, writes the reason into it and returns true, so no POST is made. The next flush (reconnect or next launch) runs `_rereadForReplay`, which sees cancelled_by_rider and returns `sent` without POSTing (1549-1551). The entry is then removed (1498). verdicts.repro: Traced the path by hand through finding_driver_controller.dart:1182-1216 (queued), 375-378 (realtime confirm, no outbox removal), 1303-1314, finding_drivers.dart:316-321/620-634, sendCancelReason 1351-1376, pending_cancel_store.dart:322-327, and the flush at 1465-1500 with _rereadForReplay 1549-1551. confirmed.title: Re-tapping cancel while an unreachable attempt is still queued resends the first tap's expectedVersion and reason: a 409 'ride just changed' if the trip moved on, or a server reason that differs from the one History archives
confirmed.description: `enqueue` returns the existing entry whenever one with the same command exists, keeping its `expectedVersion` from the first tap and its `reasonId`. `PendingCancel.body(fallback)` prefers the stored reason (`reasonId ?? fallbackReason`). On Waiting a second cancel after `pendingRetry` therefore sends the old version and the old reason. If the trip moved on meanwhile (e.g. assigned → arriving bumps the version), the mock answers 409 version_mismatch, which becomes `stale`, and the rider sees 'ride just changed' and must tap a third time. If it succeeds, the server keeps reason 1 while `_commitCancelled(reasonId: reason2)` archives reason 2 in History.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider cancels with reason 'plans_changed' and gets 'We couldn't reach Movera'. The driver's status advances and the connection returns. The rider taps Cancel again with 'driver_not_suitable'. The POST carries expectedVersion=old and reason 'plans_changed'. The result is 409 version_mismatch and 'Your ride just changed'. On the next try the server stores 'plans_changed' while History says 'driver_not_suitable'.
confirmed.evidence:
pending_cancel_store.dart:295-300 `final existing = await find(rideId); if (existing != null && existing.command == command && existing.idempotencyKey != null) { return existing; }`
pending_cancel_store.dart:78 `...CancelReasonCodes.riderCancelBody(reasonId ?? fallbackReason),`
active_ride_controller.dart:215-220 `final entry = await PendingCancelStore.enqueue(rideId: id, reasonId: reasonId, command: command, expectedVersion: session.projectionVersionOf(id));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: On a new rider tap, refresh the entry with the current version and reason (new key, since the body changed), as the flush does with `forVersion`.

verdicts.reason: PendingCancelStore.enqueue (pending_cancel_store.dart:295-300) returns the existing entry whenever the command matches and a key exists, so the second tap keeps the first expectedVersion and reasonId. body(reasonId) at active_ride_controller.dart:227 prefers the stored reason (pending_cancel_store.dart:78 `reasonId ?? fallbackReason`). After pendingRetry the Waiting screen resets _leaving/_cancelling and lets the rider cancel again with a new reason (waiting_for_driver.dart:853-859). A 5xx is not a permanent failure (pending_cancel_store.dart:158-162), so realtime can stay connected and no reconnect flush runs. In that case the version keeps moving and the second tap goes out with the old expectedVersion. The mock then answers 409 version_mismatch (in_process_mock_client.dart:1453-1458), which maps to `stale` and shows 'ride just changed'. If the second tap succeeds instead, the server stores reason 1 while _commitCancelled archives reason 2 (active_ride_controller.dart:151, 312). The flush path refreshes the version with forVersion (finding_driver_controller.dart:1476); the rider-tap path does not. Reusing the key is deliberate (idempotency), but keeping the stale version and the first reason on a new tap is not covered by any decision. Effect: one extra tap and a History reason that differs from the server's.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _requestServerCancel → PendingCancelStore.enqueue → entry.body, the Waiting _confirmCancel/_showCancelProblem flow, isPermanentCancelFailure, the reconnect-only flush watcher (finding_driver_controller.dart:1428-1445) and the mock's _versionMismatch. No test run.

verdicts.reason: PendingCancelStore.enqueue (pending_cancel_store.dart:295-300) returns the existing entry whenever one exists for the same command, so the new reasonId and the current projectionVersionOf(id) passed at active_ride_controller.dart:215-220 are dropped. body() then sends reasonId ?? fallback (line 78), so the stored first reason wins. confirmed.title: 'Try again' after no driver found books a fresh quote without asking the rider to confirm a changed price (Select Ride asks in that case)
confirmed.description: `_requestAgain` calls `submitFinding(price: ended.price, ...)` without any quote fields. In `BookingCoordinator._resolveQuoteBinding`, `suppliedCount == 0`, so it fetches a new quote and calls `..validate()` without `requestedPrice`. The `ended.price` the rider last saw is never compared. `_prepareFinding` then books `effectivePrice = binding.total.major`, which can be higher or lower. Select Ride stops for `_acceptNewPrice` whenever the price to book differs from the one shown (RIDE-1/2). This path books silently, and the new search starts at whatever the server quotes now. A raised offer the rider made in the previous search is also lost. The new price only appears afterwards, on the payment line.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider raised the offer from 120 kr to 140 kr, the server then answered noDriverFound, and the rider taps 'Try again'. A new ride is created at the fresh quote, say 165 kr in surge, or the plain 120 kr without the raise, with no confirmation step. The rider believes they re-requested the same 140 kr ride.

finding_drivers.dart:352-368 `rideId = await (widget.booking ?? BookingController()).submitFinding( ... price: ended.price, quoteCurrency: ended.currency, ...` (no quoteId/quoteSignedPayload/quoteExpiresAt/quoteTotalMinor)
booking_coordinator.dart:567-574 `final binding = _BookingQuoteBinding(... totalMinor: quote.totalMinor, ...)..validate();` (no requestedPrice)

confirmed.title: `_refreshRoadRoute` has no request generation, so an older road-route answer can overwrite the route drawn for a changed destination
confirmed.description: `_adoptRoute` (line 395-406) and `_applyRouteChange` (line 700-711) update `_pickupPosition`/`_destinationPosition`, clear `_roadRoutePoints`, redraw, and then call `unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute())`. `_refreshRoadRoute` awaits `roadRoutePolyline(from: _pickupPosition, to: _destinationPosition)` (a network call via `RoutingService.roadLine`) and on return only checks `mounted` and `route.points.length < 2` before assigning `_roadRoutePoints = route.points` and redrawing. There is no check that the answer is for the route currently adopted. When a route change happens while the previous road request is still in flight (or a slow first request is beaten by the second), the older polyline lands last and is drawn between the new pickup/destination markers.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider changes the destination from the Finding screen (or the server's route-change event arrives) right after the screen opened. The new destination marker appears, then the road line for the OLD destination is drawn on the map and stays until another route change or ride stage.
confirmed.evidence: finding_drivers.dart:506-519 `Future<void> _refreshRoadRoute() async { if (_stops.isNotEmpty) return; final route = await roadRoutePolyline( id: 'route', from: _pickupPosition, to: _destinationPosition, color: RiderRouteStyle.color, ); if (!mounted || route.points.length < 2) return; _roadRoutePoints = route.points; _loadMapBits(); setState(() {}); }` | :403-405 `_roadRoutePoints = null; _loadMapBits(); if (_mapReady) unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute());` | :709-711 same in `_applyRouteChange`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Capture `from`/`to` (or a `++_routeGeneration`) before the await and discard the result when `_pickupPosition`/`_destinationPosition` changed (or the generation moved on) in the meantime.

verdicts.reason: finding_drivers.dart:506-519 `_refreshRoadRoute` only checks `mounted` and `points.length < 2` after awaiting `roadRoutePolyline`. Nothing ties the answer to the pickup and destination in effect when the request was sent. `_applyRouteChange` (701-711) and `_adoptRoute` (397-406) change the endpoints and start a new request, but a request started earlier by onMapCreated (852) is never cancelled. `RoutingService.roadLine` (core/maps/routing_service.dart:37-83) is a network POST with a 15s timeout (api_client.dart:42). On failure it falls back to a 2-point straight line, which also passes the `< 2` check, so even a timed-out old request overwrites the new route. It is worse when the new route has stops: `_refreshRoadRoute` returns early, and a late old answer sets `_roadRoutePoints`, which `_loadMapBits` (441-449) draws in preference to the stops line. The sibling screen guards this: waiting_for_driver.dart:2368-2378 checks `_routeKey != requestKey`. Finding has no such guard. The window is narrow: the first request has to still be pending when the rider finishes the route-change flow, which is plausible on a slow network.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Followed the writers of `_pickupPosition`, `_destinationPosition` and `_roadRoutePoints` (lines 163-165, 399-405, 705-711, 516) and the callers of `_refreshRoadRoute` (405, 711, 852), through `roadRoutePolyline` (route_polyline.dart:43) into `roadLine` (timeout, straight-line fallback, cache keyed by endpoints). Compared with the requestKey guard in waiting_for_driver.dart:2378. `_applyRouteChange` is reached only from the rider's own route-change flow (line 683), not from a server event, so that part of the scenario is wrong but the race holds.

verdicts.reason: finding_drivers.dart:506-518 `_refreshRoadRoute` awaits `roadRoutePolyline` and then only checks `mounted` and `route.points.length < 2` before assigning `_roadRoutePoints`. Nothing ties the answer to the `_pickupPosition`/`_destinationPosition` it was requested for. Two requests can be in flight at once: the first starts in `onMapCreated` (:852), and `_applyRouteChange` (:701-711) starts another after a rider edit (:683). `RoutingService.roadLine` (routing_service.dart:37-80) goes to the network. With a 15 s ApiClient timeout (api_client.dart:42), it falls back to a straight line for the OLD points on timeout or error, so the old request can land after the new one. `_loadMapBits` (:441-449) prefers `_roadRoutePoints` over everything, so the stale line replaces the new route. It also replaces the stops path: when the new route has stops, the new call returns at once (:508) and the late old answer still overwrites. The old line then stays until the next route change. One correction: the finding mentions a 'server route-change event', but `_applyRouteChange` is only called from the rider's own edit at :683.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand. A starts in onMapCreated with (P, D1). The rider edits the destination: _applyRouteChange sets D2, clears _roadRoutePoints and starts B with (P, D2). B returns first (cache hit, fast reply, or the stops early return). A then returns after up to 15 s (timeout gives line(P, D1)) and sets _roadRoutePoints to the P to D1 polyline, which _loadMapBits draws between the P and D2 markers. Needs the first request to still be pending when the edit finishes, so it only happens on slow or stalled networks. No widget test was run because FindingDrivers needs the full AppScope.

confirmed.title: Location permission is requested again immediately after the rider denies it, and again on every app resume
confirmed.description: _awaitCurrentFix loops two attempts; if the first detectCurrent returns quickly with permissionDenied (target == null), the second attempt starts a fresh detectCurrent, which calls location.requestPermission() again (home_controller.dart:369-371) — a second system prompt right after the first 'Deny'. didChangeAppLifecycleState(resumed) also calls _detectCurrentAddress() whenever _currentLatLng == null (home.dart:266-267), so an Android rider who denied once gets the prompt on each return to the app until Android auto-blocks it. iOS/web report deniedForever after one refusal, so only Android (and 'denied' on older Android indefinitely) is affected.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Android rider taps Where to with location not yet granted, denies the prompt; within the same tap the prompt appears a second time (attempt 2). Later, every time they switch apps and come back, the prompt is shown again.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:343-350 `for (var attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) { ... await _detectCurrentAddress().timeout(left, onTimeout: () {}); if (!mounted) return null; final fix = _tripPickupLatLng ?? _currentLatLng; if (fix != null) return fix; }`
home_controller.dart:368-371 `var permission = await location.checkPermission(); if (permission == LocationPermission.denied) { permission = await location.requestPermission(); }`
home.dart:266-267 `} else if (_currentLatLng == null) { _detectCurrentAddress(); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Stop retrying when the first attempt ended in a permission failure (track the last DetectedLocation.failure), and on resume only re-detect when the last state was not permissionRequired.

verdicts.reason: home_controller.dart:368-371 calls location.requestPermission() whenever checkPermission() returns `denied`. Nothing stops it from running again after a fresh refusal. location_repository.dart:24-25 calls Geolocator directly and nothing caches the answer. In _awaitCurrentFix (home.dart:343-350) attempt 1 runs whenever attempt 0 got no fix. It never checks the failure reason, even though the comment says the retry is only meant to start 'once permission is granted'. The resume handler (home.dart:266-267) also re-detects whenever _currentLatLng == null and never checks HomeLocationState.permissionRequired. When Home's startup detect has already ended in 'denied', both attempts in the onFinish path (home.dart:807) start a new detectCurrent, so an Android rider is asked again within the same tap. On Android 11+ the OS turns a second refusal into deniedForever, so the extra prompts stop. On Android 10 and older they keep coming until 'Don't ask again' is ticked. iOS and web return deniedForever after one refusal, so they are not affected.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home.dart:332-357 (_awaitCurrentFix retry loop), home.dart:324-328 (the in-flight join is cleared on completion, so the retry starts a new detect), home_controller.dart:357-399 (detectCurrent permission branch), home.dart:250-268 (resume handler), core/location/location_repository.dart:24 (direct Geolocator call). Nothing returns early on a permission failure. No runtime test: the OS permission dialog cannot be driven from flutter test.

verdicts.reason: detectCurrent() calls requestPermission() whenever checkPermission() is `denied` (home_controller.dart:368-371). On Android, geolocator_android's checkPermission never reports deniedForever: a not-granted permission always comes back as `denied` (PermissionManager.java:64). Nothing remembers that the rider already said no. The resume handler re-detects whenever `_currentLatLng == null` (home.dart:266-267), and `_awaitCurrentFix` makes a second fresh attempt when the first returns quickly with permissionDenied (home.dart:343-350). On Android the permission dialog itself pauses the activity (inactive) and resumes it when closed. So right after the rider taps Deny, the resume handler asks again at once. On Android 10 and older the prompt keeps coming back until the rider ticks "Don't ask again". On Android 11+ the OS stops it after the second refusal. iOS and web report deniedForever and are not affected.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_rider43_46_test.dart (now deleted). It pumped the real Home with GeolocatorPlatform.instance set to a fake whose checkPermission and requestPermission both return denied, then sent inactive followed by resumed three times. Output: `after mount requests=1`, `after resume #1 requests=2`, `after resume #2 requests=3`, `after resume #3 requests=4`. Every resume calls requestPermission again. The two-attempt loop in _awaitCurrentFix I traced by hand (home.dart:343-350) and did not run.

confirmed.title: Home can start GPS tracking, pulse and compass on its disposed location controller if it is replaced while the puck icons are being built
confirmed.description: _runDetectCurrentAddress awaits _prepareLocationPuckIcons() (picture rasterisation, which spans frames) and then calls _locationCtl.bindLiveLocation without re-checking mounted. If Home is disposed in that window, for example when the restore coordinator replaces the root on cold start, startTracking subscribes to the position stream on an already disposed controller. That subscription is never cancelled and keeps GPS on. startPulse and startHeading create periodic timers (850 ms and 100/250 ms) that are never cancelled, and _startCompass runs again after dispose() stopped it. A later stream error calls _setState -> notifyListeners on a disposed ChangeNotifier. The new ui.Images are also kept on the dead State.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a cold start that restores a ride, Home is built, its first fix lands, and the root is replaced while the puck bitmaps are still being drawn. The rider is on the ride screen, but a dead Home location subscription and two periodic timers keep running for the rest of the session.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Check `if (!mounted) return;` after `await _prepareLocationPuckIcons()`. Make bindLiveLocation/startTracking/startPulse no-ops after the controller is disposed.

verdicts.corrected_title: Home can start GPS tracking, pulse and compass on its disposed location controller if it is replaced while the puck icons are being built
verdicts.reason: home.dart:363 checks `mounted` only after detectCurrent. Line 379 awaits _prepareLocationPuckIcons (two async createVisual calls), and line 380 then calls _locationCtl.bindLiveLocation without re-checking. dispose (home.dart:273+) has already disposed _locationCtl (home_controller.dart:717-738 cancels the subscription and timers). The late bindLiveLocation (home_controller.dart:649-657) then opens a new getPositionStream subscription and an 850 ms Timer.periodic, and restarts the compass and heading poller. Nothing cancels them afterwards: the isMounted closures only make the callbacks return early. Home is disposed whenever the gate's root is replaced (ride_restore_gate.dart show/_setChild via replaceRootSurface), for example by resumeIfNeeded after enterMoveraApp or by sign-out. The finding's cold-start example is wrong, though: on a cold start, RideRestoreGate awaits root() before showing any child, so Home is never built and then replaced. The race window is only the few frames of puck rasterisation, so this is rare.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _runDetectCurrentAddress await points, HomeLocationController.dispose and bindLiveLocation/startTracking/startPulse/startHeading, and RideRestoreGate root replacement. Not run; the timing is too narrow for a deterministic widget test.

verdicts.reason: The mounted check really is missing after `await _prepareLocationPuckIcons()` (home.dart:379-380). The window, though, is only the first-ever rasterisation of two 65x75 canvas pictures (movera_map_markers.dart:15-45, toImage plus PNG encode, a few milliseconds), because `??=` skips both awaits on any later detect. To hit the leak, Home would have to be disposed inside that window, right after the first accurate fix landed (detectCurrent itself takes seconds, guarded at home.dart:363). The restore coordinator's root swap waits on its own session, read and resync timing that has nothing to do with the fix. No realistic caller lines the two up, so the scenario depends on speculative timing.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand. _prepareLocationPuckIcons awaits createVisual twice only while the icons are null. Every other await in _runDetectCurrentAddress is preceded or followed by a mounted check, or is a no-op after dispose. I did not try to force disposal inside the window, because there is no real caller that produces that timing.

verdicts.reason:
The defect is real, and a run shows that it leaks. In _runDetectCurrentAddress, the only mounted check is at home.dart:363, right after detectCurrent. Line 379 then awaits _prepareLocationPuckIcons (home.dart:1516-1519), and line 380 calls _locationCtl.bindLiveLocation without checking mounted again. On a Home State's first detect, the icons are still null, so the `??=` really does await MoveraRiderPuckMarker.createVisual twice (movera_map_markers.dart:43-47, Picture.toImage plus PNG toByteData). Both are engine round trips, so a frame and a dispose can happen in between. HomeLocationController.dispose (home_controller.dart:717-738) has already cancelled _positionSub and the timers. Nothing in bindLiveLocation (649-657), startTracking (448), startPulse (636-647) or startHeading checks whether the controller was disposed. The new getPositionStream subscription (bestForNavigation, 8 m filter) and the 850 ms Timer.periodic are therefore created afterwards and never cancelled. The isMounted closures only make their callbacks return early.

The run proved this (output in the repro field). There is no recorded decision covering it in DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md or QA_HOOKS.md.

The finding's trigger is wrong, though. On a cold start, RideRestoreGate awaits root() before showing any child (ride_restore_gate.dart:58-62), so Home is never built and then swapped out. The real triggers are a root swap that runs at the same time as Home's first fix:
- enterMoveraApp (auth_navigation.dart:19-27) shows Home and immediately runs resumeIfNeeded. With a kept ride, that call replaces Home after the session check, snapshot read and network resync (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:560-604), while Home is fetching its fix and reverse-geocoding.
- Opening a notification (notification_navigation.dart:123).
- Signing out.

These flows have independent timing, and the window is only the first rasterisation of the puck (milliseconds to a few frames). The race is possible but rare, and it only happens on an edge path. That is why the reproducer called it speculative. Its argument that no caller lines the two up does not hold, because these callers run concurrently and nothing orders them. When the race is lost, GPS stays subscribed and a periodic timer runs for the rest of the process, so this is a real leak at low severity.
verdicts.repro:
I wrote a throwaway test, /home/user/movera-rider-app/test/_audit_u120_test.dart (now deleted). It installs a GeolocatorPlatform fake that grants permission, returns a fix from getCurrentPosition, and returns a broadcast StreamController from getPositionStream, counting onListen and onCancel. The test pumps Home inside ScreenUtilInit/MaterialApp, as test/home/audit_fix_location_recovery_test.dart does, and pumps 20 x 50 ms so the fix lands. It then calls pumpWidget(SizedBox.shrink()) to dispose Home, and finally uses tester.runAsync to let toImage and toByteData finish. I ran it with `PATH=/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH flutter test test/_audit_u120_test.dart`. Output:
"U120 before dispose: currentCalls=1 listens=0 cancels=0 hasListener=false"
"U120 right after dispose: listens=0 cancels=0 hasListener=false"
"U120 after rasterisation: listens=1 cancels=0 hasListener=true"
The run then failed with "A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed. Timer (duration: 0:00:00.850000, periodic: true) created: HomeLocationController.startPulse (home_controller.dart:642) <- bindLiveLocation (home_controller.dart:656) <- _HomeState._runDetectCurrentAddress (home.dart:380)".
So the position stream was subscribed and the pulse timer created after Home and its controller were disposed, and neither is ever cancelled. Fix: add `if (!mounted) return;` after `await _prepareLocationPuckIcons()` at home.dart:379, and make the controller's start* methods do nothing once it has been disposed.
verdicts.corrected_title: Home starts GPS tracking and the pulse timer after dispose if it is torn down during the first puck rasterisation (no mounted check at home.dart:379-380); triggered by a root swap that races the first fix (resumeIfNeeded after sign-in or a notification, sign-out), not by a cold start

confirmed.title: Backing out of Plan your ride while it is preparing a Book for later route still opens the date picker over Home
confirmed.description: RoutePickerPage has no PopScope while _finishing. On Android, system back pops it while onFinish (_confirmRouteSelection) is still running, which can take up to 8 s in _awaitCurrentFix or the destination geocode. _confirmRouteSelection checks only Home's mounted and then pushes ScheduleDateTimeSelector.choose(context, ...) from Home's context. The picker is gone and _showRouteAddressPicker already returned with a null draft, so any time chosen there is thrown away.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider taps Book for later, picks a destination, and while the spinner shows (waiting for a first GPS fix) presses Back to leave. A few seconds later the date and time picker pops up over Home, and choosing a time does nothing.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass a cancellation or 'still open' check from the route picker to onFinish (or block pop while _finishing), and stop _confirmRouteSelection when the picker is gone.

verdicts.reason: RoutePickerPage has no PopScope (none in lib/features/destination_search/presentation/route_picker_page.dart; the _finishing overlay at :1097-1105 only blocks taps). System or browser back pops it while widget.onFinish is still awaiting. _confirmRouteSelection (home.dart:826-883) checks only Home's `mounted`, which stays true. It awaits _prefillPickup/_awaitCurrentFix (up to 8 s, home.dart:332-357), resolvePlace and timeZoneAt, then calls ScheduleDateTimeSelector.choose(context, ...) with Home's context (home.dart:865). The picker's _finish then returns at route_picker_page.dart:415 (`!mounted`). _showRouteAddressPicker already got a null draft from push (home.dart:902/944), so the chosen time is thrown away.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: route_picker_page _finish (390-417), home.dart _showRouteAddressPicker push/onFinish (900-944), and _confirmRouteSelection (826-883). grep found no PopScope in the route picker and no 'still open' check passed to onFinish.

verdicts.reason: RoutePickerPage has no PopScope and BottomToTopTransition does not block popping either (grep found no PopScope/canPop in route_picker_page.dart or the transition). The _finishing overlay at route_picker_page.dart:1097 only blocks taps. While onFinish is awaiting, a system or browser back pops the page. Three awaits can run that long: _prefillPickup -> _awaitCurrentFix (8 s deadline, home.dart:338), _locationCtl.resolvePlace (home.dart:838) and riderConfig.timeZoneAt (home.dart:858). The pop completes the push in _showRouteAddressPicker with null, and home.dart:946 `if (draft == null || !mounted) return;` ends the flow. _confirmRouteSelection only checks Home's `mounted` (home.dart:856/862), which is still true, so it then calls ScheduleDateTimeSelector.choose(context, ...) with Home's context (home.dart:863). The rider's chosen time goes back to RoutePickerPage._finish, which is no longer mounted and returns at route_picker_page.dart:415. The choice is discarded.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: route_picker_page.dart:390-416 (_finish, no pop guard), home.dart:826-891 (_confirmRouteSelection, guarded only by Home.mounted), home.dart:900-946 (_showRouteAddressPicker returns on a null draft). No PopScope anywhere on that route.

confirmed.title: Recenter button is hidden after a recenter that was interrupted or blocked, leaving the map off the rider with no way back
confirmed.description: _recenterOnUser unconditionally ends with `setState(() => _showRecenterButton = false)`. The flight future completes early when a finger touches the map (MapView.touching -> interrupt() completes _done, map_camera_motion.dart:76-94), and the refinement glide `_flyToUser(fresh, follow: true)` is a no-op when heldByRider (google_map_provider.dart:81, 102). In both cases the camera is not on the rider, any 'show' decision made by _handleMapCameraMove during the rider's pan is overwritten with false, and the button only returns after the next camera move event.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider taps recenter; while latestFix() runs (up to 9 s) they pan the map elsewhere (button correctly shows). latestFix returns a point >15 m away, the follow glide is refused because the map is held, then _showRecenterButton = false: the map stays where they panned and the recenter button is gone until they move the map again.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:1664-1668 `await _flyToUser(fresh, follow: known != null); } else { await flight; } if (mounted) setState(() => _showRecenterButton = false);`
map_camera_motion.dart:306 `if (view.touching) return Future<void>.value();`
google_map_provider.dart:102 `if (map == null || !_mayMove(map, follow)) return;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Only clear _showRecenterButton when the glide actually landed (e.g. re-evaluate with AppScope.instance.camera.showRecenter against the last camera pose), or leave it to _handleMapCameraMove.

verdicts.reason: _recenterOnUser always ends with setState(() => _showRecenterButton = false) (home.dart:1668), whether or not the camera reached the rider. The first glide uses follow:false (home.dart:1639). A finger on the map calls interrupt(), which completes the flight early (map_camera_motion.dart:71-94). A fresh fix that would move the camera is sent with follow:true (home.dart:1663), and _mayMove refuses it while heldByRider (google_map_provider.dart:79-81; followHold is 12 s, map_camera_motion.dart:55). latestFix is a bestForNavigation getCurrentPosition that can take up to 9 s (home_controller.dart:613-622). If the rider pans and lets go before it returns, the 'show' value that _handleMapCameraMove set during the pan (home.dart:1615-1628) is overwritten with false. The map is left away from the rider and the recenter button (home.dart:1943) is hidden. It comes back on the next camera move, so the effect is minor.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home.dart:1631-1684, 1615-1629 and 1943; map_camera_motion.dart:44-94; google_map_provider.dart:79-108; home_controller.dart:613-622. The final hide does not depend on whether the camera reached the rider.

verdicts.reason: `_recenterOnUser` always ends with `setState(() => _showRecenterButton = false)` (home.dart:1668), whether or not the camera reached the rider. Only _handleMapCameraMove turns the button back on (home.dart:1615-1629), so it needs another camera-move event. Suppose the rider touches the map during the 1 s flight: touching=true calls interrupt(), which completes the flight's future (map_camera_motion.dart:71-94). They pan away and lift their finger while latestFix (bestForNavigation, up to 9 s, home_controller.dart:613-622) is still running. When latestFix returns, either `await flight` resolves at once (fix within 15 m), or the follow:true refinement is refused because heldByRider is true (google_map_provider.dart:81, 102). Either way the button is set to false while the map sits where the rider panned it. It stays hidden until they move the map again. The effect is minor and the rider can recover with one more pan.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand (needs a real map controller): tap → _flyToUser(known, follow:false) → finger down → interrupt() completes _done → pan, onCameraMove sets the button to shown → finger up, no more camera events → latestFix resolves → `await flight` (already complete) or a refused follow glide → `_showRecenterButton = false`. Nothing between those steps checks the camera pose.

confirmed.description: FeatureFlags.release sets enableScheduledRide/enableBookingLater false, and AppScope composes DisabledReservationRepository. ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/backend-readiness-gate.md say Book for later is 'switched off in staging/production'. No UI reads flags.scheduledRides or flags.bookingLater (the only flag consumers are RideSelectionController and wallet.dart's businessProfile). The release build still shows AdvanceBookingCard, the Schedule bottom-nav item, the WhereTo card's schedule action, the side menu 'Later' chip and History's schedule button. Each runs route picker, date/time, Select Ride and Set pickup. Only on Book does createReservation reject with ReservationsUnavailableException ('Booking for later isn't available yet, so nothing was booked.'). The comment in reservation_controller wiring also leaves rulesSource null, so the flow runs on default rules.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A production rider taps 'Schedule' on Home. They choose a destination, a date and time, a category and a pickup, then tap Book. They get 'Booking for later isn't available yet, so nothing was booked.' The feature the docs say is switched off is fully offered, and the rider wastes the whole flow. Verified by reading the code.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Gate every Book-for-later entry point (Home card, nav item, WhereTo, side menu, History, plan-return) on AppScope.instance.flags.scheduledRides || bookingLater.
