confirmed.title: Your month card has no load generation, so an older history read can overwrite a newer one
confirmed.description: `_load` runs on every history-store change and every ReservationController notification, plus once at start. Each call awaits `defaultRides()` (in release a server trip list, see ARCHITECTURE), then setState with whatever it got. Nothing orders the results, so a slow read that started before a ride was archived can finish after a newer read and put the stale month back. The card stays wrong until the next change event.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A reservation update starts load A. The ride completes and is archived, which starts load B. B returns first and shows 4 rides; A returns later with the pre-archive list and shows 3. Home shows 3 rides this month until something else changes.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Increment a generation counter per _load and ignore results from superseded calls.

verdicts.reason: home_journey_section.dart:184-193 has no generation or sequence guard. Every history change and every ReservationController notification starts a _load (:166-172), and each one does setState with whatever it gets back. In release, defaultRides() calls ApiRideHistoryRepository.loadOnDemand (ride_history_repositories.dart:30-53), which makes up to 5 sequential GET pages. That makes it realistic for a load that started earlier to finish later and overwrite a newer result. The only guard is `mounted`. The scheduled part is read after the await, so only the on-demand list goes stale. The card stays wrong until the next change event. It is informational only, so severity is low.
verdicts.repro: Traced the listeners (:166-172), _load (:184-193), OnDemandHistoryController.load to rideHistory.loadOnDemand, and the multi-page API repository. Nothing orders or drops superseded results.

verdicts.reason: _load (home_journey_section.dart:184-193) awaits the loader and then calls setState with whatever it got. It has no generation or sequence check, so whichever call finishes last wins. In release, defaultRides -> OnDemandHistoryController.load -> ApiRideHistoryRepository.loadOnDemand (ride_history_repositories.dart:30-50) fetches up to 5 pages over the network, so replies can arrive out of order. Two separate triggers can overlap: the OnDemandRideHistoryStore.changes stream and the ReservationController listener (lines 166-174). The stale month stays until the next change event. The effect is informational only.
verdicts.repro: Wrote and ran a throwaway test (test/_audit_u126_test.dart, since deleted) using the ridesLoader and changes hooks. After the first load it fired two changes, completed the second load with 1 ride and then the first with 0. Output: 'after B: 1' then 'after A: zero=1 one=0', and the test passed. The older result replaced the newer one.

confirmed.title: Chat message times use the Material 12/24-hour locale default instead of the app's 24-hour rule
confirmed.description: _messageTime formats with `TimeOfDay.fromDateTime(sentAt.toLocal()).format(context)`, which follows MaterialLocalizations.timeOfDayFormat: for the 'en' locale that is 'h:mm a' (12-hour, '3:05 PM') unless MediaQuery.alwaysUse24HourFormat is set. Every other time in the app is forced to 24-hour ('08:05') by L10n.formatTime (l10n.dart:111-114, 'as Movera shows it in every language') and ReservationFormat.time, so a rider using English in Sweden sees '3:05 PM' on chat bubbles but '15:05' on the Waiting sheet and notifications for the same moment.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider with app language EN opens the driver chat: bubbles show '3:05 PM' while the ride sheet shows 'Pickup 15:05'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use L10n.formatTime(sentAt.toLocal()) in chat.dart.

verdicts.reason: chat.dart:196 formats with TimeOfDay.format(context), which follows MaterialLocalizations. MaterialApp uses locale language.locale (app/app.dart:37), which is Locale('en') for English, and nothing overrides MediaQuery.alwaysUse24HourFormat. L10n.formatTime (l10n.dart:111-114) is documented as the 24-hour clock 'as Movera shows it in every language' and is not used here. On web, or on a device without the 24-hour setting, English riders get 12-hour times in chat bubbles.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r48_test.dart: MaterialApp(locale: Locale('en'), the app's localizationsDelegates), TimeOfDay.fromDateTime(15:05).format(c). It printed 'EN FORMAT: 3:05 PM' and passed ('All tests passed!'). The file was deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: lib/features/messages/presentation/chat.dart:194-196 formats with TimeOfDay.fromDateTime(sentAt.toLocal()).format(context). That follows the MaterialLocalizations of the MaterialApp locale (app.dart:37 locale: language.locale), and no alwaysUse24HourFormat override exists anywhere in lib. With 'en' this gives a 12-hour time. L10n.formatTime (l10n.dart:111-114) is documented as the 24-hour time 'as Movera shows it in every language'. Only English riders are affected; fr and sv already show 24-hour times.
verdicts.repro: Wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_r48chat_test.dart, that pumps RiderMessageBubble with sentAt 15:05 under MaterialApp(locale: en/fr/sv, AppLocalizations delegates). Output: 'en bubble texts=[hi, 3:05 PM] formatTime=15:05', 'fr bubble texts=[hi, 15:05]', 'sv bubble texts=[hi, 15:05]'. Result: All tests passed. File deleted.

confirmed.title: Hard-coded English UI strings in localized screens (notification toast, account security errors)
confirmed.description: The app ships en/fr/sv (`L10n.languages`) and every other user-facing string on these screens goes through `context.l10n`. These do not: `MoveraToast.show(context, 'This ride has ended.')` shown when a notification row's ride can no longer be opened (154); `errorMessage = 'Account security is unavailable right now.'` and `'Could not update active sessions.'` (account_security_controller.dart:240, 265) which `SecurityPage` renders directly (security.dart:924, 1090). A Swedish or French rider sees English here.
confirmed.failure_scenario: App language Svenska; rider taps an old ride notification: toast reads "This ride has ended." in English. Security page fails to load: "Account security is unavailable right now." in English.
confirmed.evidence:
notification_navigation.dart:154 `MoveraToast.show(context, 'This ride has ended.');`
account_security_controller.dart:240 `errorMessage = 'Account security is unavailable right now.';`
account_security_controller.dart:265 `errorMessage = 'Could not update active sessions.';`
security.dart:924 `body: _security.errorMessage ?? context.l10n.securityUnavailableBody,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add ARB keys and use `L10n.current`/`context.l10n` for these three strings.

verdicts.reason: notification_navigation.dart:154 `MoveraToast.show(context, 'This ride has ended.')` is a literal string, and it is reached from notifications.dart:103 when the ride can no longer be opened. account_security_controller.dart:42 and :67 (not 240/265 as the finding says) set the English literals 'Account security is unavailable right now.' and 'Could not update active sessions.' security.dart:72 (`_security.errorMessage ?? ...securityUnavailableBody`) and :233-238 show them in preference to the localized ARB text. None of the three strings is in app_sv.arb or app_fr.arb, and no decision document exempts them.
verdicts.repro: Static. Grepped the ARB files for the literals (no match; only `securityUnavailableBody` exists, which these literals replace). Traced the callers: openNotificationRide is called from notifications.dart:103, and errorMessage is read at security.dart:72 and :233.

verdicts.reason: notification_navigation.dart:154 `MoveraToast.show(context, 'This ride has ended.')`, account_security_controller.dart:42 `'Account security is unavailable right now.'` and :67 `'Could not update active sessions.'` are literals. security.dart:72 and :233-238 render `errorMessage` directly. The app ships en/fr/sv (lib/l10n/app_*.arb, L10n.languages), and no decision document exempts these strings. The line numbers in the finding (240/265, 924/1090) are stale; the real lines are 42/67 and 72/238.
verdicts.repro: Grepped lib for the three literals: each appears only at the lines named, with no l10n lookup. Checked that security.dart:72 (`body: _security.errorMessage ?? ...`) and :238 (`_security.errorMessage!`) show them as they are. In Swedish, a failed load or a tap on an ended-ride notification shows English text.

confirmed.title: A push with a title but no body shows its raw wire type (e.g. 'ride.driver_assigned') as the notification text
confirmed.description: The subtitle falls back to `payload.type` when the body is empty. The type is the internal event code that PushPayload requires (`ride.`/`trip.` prefixes), not text meant for the rider, so it is shown untranslated in every language.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The server sends a notification titled 'Your driver is here' with no body. The Notifications list shows 'Your driver is here' over the line 'ride.driver_arrived'.
confirmed.evidence:
notifications_repository.dart:51-52
        title: title?.isNotEmpty == true ? title! : 'Movera',
        subtitle: body?.isNotEmpty == true ? body! : payload.type,
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use an empty subtitle, or a localized label per known type, when there is no body.

verdicts.reason: notifications_repository.dart:52 sets subtitle to payload.type when the body is empty. Only pushes with both title and body empty are skipped (line 28), so a push with a title and no body is stored with its raw wire type (e.g. 'ride.driver_arrived', as required by push_payload.dart:29-41) as the subtitle. notifications.dart:178 renders notification.subtitle to the rider as-is, untranslated. Neither the contract nor the documents define title-only pushes as invalid.
verdicts.repro: Traced firebase_push_service.dart:151 -> PushPayload -> PushCoordinator._handleForeground/_handleOpened (push_coordinator.dart:63/74) -> NotificationsRepository.ingest:46-60 -> NotificationsScreen card text at notifications.dart:178. The contracts/ folder has no push format that requires a body.

verdicts.reason: notifications_repository.dart:52 uses `subtitle: body?.isNotEmpty == true ? body! : payload.type`. The guard at lines 28-30 drops a push only when both title and body are empty, so a push with a title and no body gets the raw type code as its visible subtitle. PushPayload.fromMap requires a non-empty type (push_payload.dart:29-31), so the fallback always has a value to show. No document marks this as intended.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway unit test: NotificationsRepository().ingest(PushPayload(type: 'ride.driver_arrived', title: 'Your driver is here'), read: false). It printed 'u128 subtitle=ride.driver_arrived'.

confirmed.title: Notification feed is ordered by ingest time, not sentAt: a tray notification tapped later is inserted above newer foreground ones
confirmed.description: ingest() always does `_items.insert(0, ...)`, even though each item carries `at` (the sentAt). Pushes received while the app is in the background are not ingested until the rider taps them from the system tray (PushCoordinator._handleOpened -> ingest(read: true)). By then newer foreground pushes may already be in the feed. The cold-start initial message is also ingested only after start() has subscribed to foreground messages. In both cases an older notification lands at the top.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Push A ('Your receipt', sent 12:00) arrives while the app is backgrounded and stays in the tray. The rider opens the app from its icon, and foreground push B (12:30) is ingested. Later they tap A in the tray. The Notifications list now shows A 12:00 above B 12:30.
confirmed.evidence:
notifications_repository.dart:85-99 `final at = (payload.sentAt ?? _now()).toLocal(); _items.insert(0, AppNotification(... at: at, ...));`
push_coordinator.dart:73-74 `Future<void> _handleOpened(PushPayload payload) async { _notifications.ingest(payload, read: true);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Insert at the position given by `at` (newest first), not always at index 0.

verdicts.reason: ingest always calls _items.insert(0, ...) (notifications_repository.dart:47), even though each item carries `at` from payload.sentAt (FCM sentTime, firebase_push_service.dart:151). The screen shows the list in stored order with no sort (notifications.dart:75-90). A background push enters the feed only when the rider taps it in the tray (push_coordinator.dart:73-74, ingest read:true), so if a newer foreground push was ingested first, the older one ends up above it. The cold-start initial message has the same problem, because takeInitialMessage is handled after the foreground subscription is set up (push_coordinator.dart:35-59). Nothing documents arrival order as intended.
verdicts.repro: Traced PushCoordinator.start/_handleForeground/_handleOpened -> NotificationsController.ingest -> NotificationsRepository.ingest; checked the feed rendering in notifications.dart:73-110 for any sort on `at` (none). The line numbers in the finding are slightly off: the insert is at :46-60, not :85-99.
verdicts.corrected_title: Notification feed is ordered by ingest time, not sentAt: a tray notification tapped later is inserted above newer foreground ones

verdicts.reason: ingest always does `_items.insert(0, ...)` (notifications_repository.dart:47), and all() (line 18) returns the list unsorted. Nothing in lib/features/notifications sorts by `at`. A tray push the rider taps after newer foreground pushes arrived goes through PushCoordinator._handleOpened -> ingest(read: true) (push_coordinator.dart:73-74) and lands at the top with its older sentAt time.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway unit test: I ingested B (sentAt 12:30, foreground), then A (sentAt 12:00, opened from the tray, read: true). It printed 'u129 order=[A@1 Jan 12:00, B@1 Jan 12:30]', so the older item shows first.

confirmed.title: A push sent the day before is labelled with no day (as today) when it is ingested on the day after spring-forward, because Duration.inDays between local midnights is 0 (23h)
confirmed.description: _formatTime computes `today.difference(day).inDays` where both are local midnights built with DateTime(y,m,d). On the day after a spring-forward transition the two midnights are 23 hours apart (verified by throwaway test under TZ=Europe/Stockholm: DateTime(2026,3,30).difference(DateTime(2026,3,29)) == 23:00:00), so inDays == 0 and the function returns only the clock, dropping the 'Yesterday' prefix the FLOW-18 comment promises. More generally, any day count across a DST change is one short (a notification from 3 days ago reads as 2 days -> still fine, but 2 days ago reads as 1 -> 'Yesterday').
confirmed.failure_scenario: Sunday 29 Mar 2026 (Europe/Stockholm) at 23:10 a 'Driver arrived' push arrives. On Monday 30 Mar the Notifications list shows it as '23:10' (today) instead of 'Yesterday 23:10'; a push from Saturday 28 Mar shows as 'Yesterday'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare calendar days with UTC-constructed midnights: `DateTime.utc(now.year, now.month, now.day).difference(DateTime.utc(time.year, time.month, time.day)).inDays`.

verdicts.corrected_title: A push sent the day before is labelled with no day (as today) when it is ingested on the day after spring-forward, because Duration.inDays between local midnights is 0 (23h)
verdicts.reason: notifications_repository.dart:92-97: today.difference(day).inDays is computed from local midnights, and on 30 Mar 2026 in Stockholm the gap is 23h, so inDays is 0 and only the clock is returned. The finding's scenario is misdescribed, though. The label is worked out once, at ingest (line 53, time: _formatTime(at)), and the UI shows the stored string (notifications.dart:190), so a push that arrived Sunday already reads '23:10' because it was 'today' then. The bug only shows when a push whose sentAt (firebase_push_service.dart:151, message.sentTime) is the previous day is ingested on that Monday. That happens, for example, when the rider taps yesterday's tray notification (push_coordinator.dart:56-58, 73-74) or a push is delivered late.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway probe under TZ=Europe/Stockholm printed 'days 0' for DateTime(2026,3,30).difference(DateTime(2026,3,29)).inDays. Traced ingest callers in push_coordinator.dart and the display at notifications.dart:190.

verdicts.corrected_title: Notification day label uses Duration.inDays between local midnights; a notification ingested the day after spring-forward with a sentAt on the previous day is labelled as today
verdicts.reason: notifications_repository.dart:92-96 computes DateTime(today).difference(DateTime(day)).inDays. Across the spring-forward night the two local midnights are 23 hours apart, so inDays is 0 and line 96 returns only the clock. Note the label is computed once, at ingest (line 53, time: _formatTime(at)), using _now() at ingest. The bug therefore needs a push whose sentAt falls on the previous day but which is ingested on the day after the transition (for example a late delivery, or one opened from the tray the next morning). The finding's scenario (arrives Sunday, is shown Monday) is really the separate issue that labels are frozen at ingest, not the DST problem.
verdicts.repro: I ran a throwaway test under TZ=Europe/Stockholm with NotificationsRepository(now: 2026-03-30 09:00). Output: 'diff=23:00:00.000000'. A push with sentAt 2026-03-29 23:10 got 'label=23:10' instead of 'Yesterday 23:10'. A push with sentAt 2026-03-28 14:00 got 'label=Yesterday 14:00' instead of '28 Mar 14:00'. The control case, now 2026-10-14 with sentAt 2026-10-13 23:10, got 'control=Yesterday 23:10'.

confirmed.title: Notification time label is frozen at ingest, so items never become "Yesterday …"
confirmed.description: FLOW-18 says only today's items show just the time and older ones name the day. `_formatTime(at)` is evaluated once when the item is ingested (206-213) and stored in `AppNotification.time`; `_formatTime` compares against `_now()` at that moment (248-261). The screen renders `notification.time` (notifications.dart:630) and never recomputes from `at`. The feed is in-memory for the process, so any app/tab left open across midnight shows yesterday's pushes with a bare clock.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Push at 23:50 shows "23:50"; the next morning the same row still says "23:50" instead of "Yesterday 23:50".
confirmed.evidence:
notifications_repository.dart:206-213 `final at = (payload.sentAt ?? _now()).toLocal(); _items.insert(0, AppNotification(... time: _formatTime(at), at: at, ...`
notifications.dart:630 `text: notification.time,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Format from `notification.at` at build time (or recompute labels on emit).

verdicts.reason: lib/features/notifications/data/notifications_repository.dart:46-53 computes `time: _formatTime(at)` once inside ingest(), and _formatTime (lines 88-101) compares against `_now()` at that moment. AppNotification.time is a final String (domain/notifications.dart:19), copyWith keeps it (line 31), and the row renders `notification.time` (presentation/notifications.dart:190); nothing reformats from `at`. The feed is an in-memory singleton (NotificationsRepository.shared), so a session left open across midnight keeps a bare clock on yesterday's items, which breaks the FLOW-18 rule written in the comment at lines 86-87. The line numbers in the finding are stale, but the code it describes is accurate.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Followed ingest -> _formatTime -> AppNotification.time -> the notifications.dart:190 render. The only other write is markRead/copyWith, which copies `time` unchanged. No timer, rebuild or locale hook recomputes the label.

verdicts.reason: The audit's line numbers are out of date, but the code does what it says. lib/features/notifications/data/notifications_repository.dart:46-53 computes `time: _formatTime(at)` once, when the item is ingested. `_formatTime` (lines 88-101) compares against `_now()` at that moment, and the result is stored as a String in AppNotification.time (domain/notifications.dart:16). The screen renders `text: notification.time` (presentation/notifications.dart:190) and never reformats from `at`. The feed is an in-memory singleton (`NotificationsRepository.shared`) with no recompute anywhere, so a process that stays alive past midnight keeps showing a bare clock. That contradicts the FLOW-18 comment at lines 86-87.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c2b3v_test.dart, since deleted. It injected now=2026-10-20 23:50, ingested a push, then moved the clock to 2026-10-21 08:00 and read all().first.time. Output: `AUDIT51 before=23:50 after=23:50 at=2026-10-20 23:50:00.000`. After midnight FLOW-18 expects "Yesterday 23:50".

confirmed.title: Unread notifications are marked only by an 8 px dot with no semantics
confirmed.description: _buildNotificationCard shows unread state solely as an 8 px primary-colour circle Container. The card's GestureDetector/Text semantics carry no unread flag or label, so screen-reader users cannot tell new notifications from read ones.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A TalkBack user opens Notifications after a driver update and hears every card the same way, with nothing to tell which notifications are new.
confirmed.evidence:
notifications.dart:195-205 `if (!notification.read) ...[
                4.width,
                Container(
                  width: ResSize.w * 8,
                  height: ResSize.w * 8,
                  decoration: BoxDecoration(
                    color: AppColor.primary,
                    shape: BoxShape.circle,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add a localized 'Unread' semantics label (or Semantics(label:) on the card) when !notification.read.

verdicts.reason: _buildNotificationCard (notifications.dart:195-205) shows the unread state only as an 8 px Container with no Semantics, and the file has no Semantics or unread label anywhere. Unread notifications really occur: PushCoordinator ingests foreground pushes with read:false (push_coordinator.dart:63). So screen-reader users get no read/unread distinction. The finding mentions a GestureDetector, but the card itself is a plain Container wrapped by a tap handler at line ~95; the conclusion still holds.
verdicts.repro: Read notifications.dart in full (grep for Semantics/unread found none) and traced where the read flag is set (notifications_repository.dart, push_coordinator.dart:63/74). No test run.

verdicts.reason: notifications.dart:195-205 marks an unread notification only with an undecorated 8px Container circle. The card (lines 130-208) and its wrapping GestureDetector (lines 98-113) have no Semantics, so the screen reader gets the same nodes (title, subtitle, time) for read and unread cards. Nothing in the ARB files gives an unread label.
verdicts.repro: Read the card builder and its only caller (NotificationScreen ListView.builder, notifications.dart:93-115). No Semantics/semanticsLabel/ExcludeSemantics wraps the dot or the card, and no 'unread' key exists in lib/l10n/*.arb.

confirmed.title: Card brand error 'We accept Visa and Mastercard' is shown untranslated under the card number
confirmed.description: CardInput.brandError is an English const. add_card_page.dart `_numberError` returns it directly: `if (CardInput.brandRejected(digits)) return CardInput.brandError;` (:125), and the same text is thrown as ArgumentError(CardInput.brandError) (:153) which add_card_page.dart:170 displays via `e.message`. All sibling errors on that page use context.l10n (cardCheckNumber, cardUseMmYy, cardExpired, cardCvc3), so this one field error stays English in fr/sv.
confirmed.failure_scenario: French rider types a card number starting with 3 (Amex) on Ajouter une carte: the inline error reads 'We accept Visa and Mastercard'.
confirmed.evidence: saved_cards_controller.dart:67 `static const String brandError = 'We accept Visa and Mastercard';`; add_card_page.dart:125 `if (CardInput.brandRejected(digits)) return CardInput.brandError;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add an ARB key (cardBrandsAccepted) and return context.l10n.cardBrandsAccepted from _numberError; keep the controller's ArgumentError for programmer errors only.

verdicts.reason: saved_cards_controller.dart:67 defines brandError as an English const. add_card_page.dart:125 _numberError returns it directly whenever CardInput.brandRejected(digits) is true, and add_card_page.dart:403 renders it as the inline field error. Typing a number that starts with 3 or 6 is enough to trigger it. The sibling errors (cardCheckNumber, cardUseMmYy, cardExpired, cardCvc3) all come from context.l10n. The ArgumentError route at add_card_page.dart:170 is effectively unreachable because _save is guarded by _valid (:156), so only the inline error is a real path. It is a visible l10n gap on an edge input, not main-path wrong behaviour, so low rather than medium.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _numberError -> CardInput.brandRejected -> brandError -> AppTextField error at add_card_page.dart:403. Grep found no ARB key for this text. No test run.

verdicts.reason: add_card_page.dart:125 returns CardInput.brandError, a const English string defined at saved_cards_controller.dart:67, as the inline error under the number field. No ARB key exists for it: grep for 'Visa' in the .arb files finds only unrelated Swedish 'visa' (show) strings. The other field errors on the same page use context.l10n. The ArgumentError path (saved_cards_controller.dart:153, shown through add_card_page.dart:170 e.message) is effectively unreachable, because _save is gated on _numberOk, so the live defect is the inline error only. Severity is low: a validation hint stays English, and the behaviour is otherwise correct.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test (since deleted): MaterialApp with locale fr, AppLocalizations delegates, L10n.use('fr'), AddCardPage, enterText '3782' into add-card-number. Output: 'r52 english error shown: 1', while the save button on the same page read 'Enregistrer la carte'. Test passed.

confirmed.title: Saved cards that expire after being saved stay listed and selectable, including as the default, in demo/dev builds
confirmed.description: Expiry is checked only when a card is added (CardInput.expiryInFuture in add()). list() returns every stored card. RideSelectionController.savedCardItems offers every listed card as a booking method, and the Payments tab offers it as the default (wallet.dart:987). Neither checks expMonth/expYear against today. A card that expired after it was saved can therefore be preselected and used to book.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo build. In August 2026 the rider saves a card expiring 09/26. In October 2026 Select Ride still lists 'Visa •••• 4242 · Expires 09/26' and preselects it if it is the default. The ride is booked against an expired card with no warning.
confirmed.evidence:
saved_cards_controller.dart:142 `List<SavedCard> list() => List.unmodifiable(_cards);`
saved_cards_controller.dart:179 expiry is checked only in add(): `if (!CardInput.expiryInFuture(expMonth, expYear, now: now))`
ride_selection_controller.dart:217-223 `for (final card in _savedCards.list()) RidePaymentItem(brand: card.methodBrand, ...)`
wallet.dart:987 `for (final card in _offers('card') ? _cards.list() : const <SavedCard>[])`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Filter out expired cards, or show them as disabled, when building the payment lists (CardInput.expiryInFuture(card.expMonth, card.expYear)). Fall back to the default method when the saved default card has expired.

verdicts.reason: Expiry is checked only in add() (lib/features/payments/application/saved_cards_controller.dart:156-158). list() at :120 returns every stored card, and the cited consumers (ride_selection_controller savedCardItems, wallet.dart default-method list) never compare expMonth/expYear to today. A card that expired after it was saved stays selectable and can be the default. Scope is narrow: saved cards are a device-only feature that release builds switch off (ARCHITECTURE.md:67-70, ARCH-7). So this happens only in demo/dev, and only when a card expires between saving and use.
verdicts.repro: Static. Read the SavedCardsController add/list paths and grepped lib for any other expiry check on saved cards (none). Checked ARCHITECTURE.md for the release composition.

verdicts.reason: Saved cards are a demo, device-only feature. ARCHITECTURE.md:68-70 says release builds reject device-only repositories, and saved cards are switched off in staging and production until their server side exists. saved_cards_controller.dart:96 marks the list as 'demo: stored on this device'. In the demo, no card is ever charged, expired or not, so booking on an expired demo card does not show a success that a valid card would have achieved. The missing re-check at list() (line 121) only affects the intentional mock. Reaching it also needs a card saved before its expiry month and the same install kept until after it.
verdicts.repro: Traced saved_cards_controller.dart list() and add() (expiry is checked only in add, via CardInput.expiryInFuture), ride_selection_controller.dart:218 and the release switch-off in ARCHITECTURE.md:68-70. Did not run a test, because the behaviour is reachable only in demo builds.

verdicts.reason:
Confirmed, low severity. The app has its own rule for card expiry: "A card is usable through the last day of its expiry month" (lib/features/payments/application/saved_cards_controller.dart:83-89). That rule is only checked when a card is added, in add() at :158 and in add_card_page.dart:115/138. Nothing checks it again later. list() at :121 returns every stored card. byMethodBrand at :133 resolves any card. RideSelectionController.savedCardItems (lib/features/ride_selection/application/ride_selection_controller.dart:217-224) and payments() at :240 offer every card. restoreDefaultPayment brings back an expired default card. The Payments tab (lib/features/wallet/presentation/wallet.dart:987) also lists every card. A search of lib found no other expMonth/expYear check.

The reproducer's argument is that this is an intentional mock. It does not hold. ARCHITECTURE.md:68-70 and FeatureFlags.release (lib/core/feature_flags/feature_flags.dart:48-53) only say that saved cards are switched off in staging and production. Nothing in DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md or QA_HOOKS.md says the demo should skip expiry. The demo does model expiry, since it refuses expired cards with "This card has expired". Within that demo, the same card is refused when added today but still offered, preselected and booked with once it expires after being saved. That is real wrong behaviour.

It is low severity rather than higher for three reasons:
- It is reachable only in demo/dev builds (lib/app/di.dart:147-149).
- No money moves.
- It only happens when a card expires between being saved and being used on the same install.
verdicts.repro:
Throwaway test test/_audit_u131_decider_test.dart (now deleted). It used SavedCardsController with a MemorySavedCardsStore and called add(number 4242424242424242, expMonth 9, expYear 2026, now: DateTime(2026,8,15), id 'c1'). It then built a RideSelectionController with a MemoryDefaultPaymentStore, selected card:c1, and restored the default in a second controller. The system date was 2026-10-21. Output:
today=2026-10-21 07:11:26.807968
expiryInFuture(9,2026) today: false
add today: This card has expired
payments: [google|Google Pay|..., card:c1|Visa •••• 4242|Expires 09/26, cash|Cash|...]
default stored: card:c1
restored selected: card:c1 Expires 09/26
+1: All tests passed!
So the card add() refuses today is still listed, chosen and brought back as the booking default.

confirmed.title: A failed PATCH of the default payment method is swallowed, and the next read() puts the server's old default back, so the rider's choice silently reverts
confirmed.description: save() sets `_defaultId = brand` first and then only logs a PATCH failure. Nothing retries the PATCH. read() then overwrites `_defaultId` with the server's `defaultMethodId` whenever the GET succeeds. RideSelectionController calls read() on every Select Ride open (restoreDefaultPayment), so after one failed PATCH the next open preselects the old method with no message.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Release build with a flaky network. At Select Ride the rider switches from Cash to Google Pay. The PATCH /payment-methods/default fails and is logged as payments.default_save_failed. They back out and open Select Ride again. The GET succeeds with defaultMethodId 'cash', and Cash is preselected again, so the rider may book with a method they had changed away from.
confirmed.evidence:
api_payment_method_repository.dart:55-68 `_defaultId = brand; try { await _api.patch('$path/default', ...); } catch (error) { AppLog.warning('payments.default_save_failed', ...); }`
api_payment_method_repository.dart:40-43 `final json = await _api.get(path); _defaultId = _string(json['defaultMethodId']) ?? _defaultId;`
ride_selection_controller.dart:609 `unawaited(store.save(selected.brand));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep a pending-save flag: retry the PATCH on the next read(), and don't let the server value overwrite the local choice until the PATCH succeeds. Or surface the failure so the UI can tell the rider.

verdicts.reason: api_payment_method_repository.dart:55-68: save() sets _defaultId and then only logs a PATCH failure. Nothing sets a pending flag and nothing retries. read() at :40-52 overwrites _defaultId with the server's defaultMethodId whenever the GET succeeds. restoreDefaultPayment (ride_selection_controller.dart:572-582) calls store.read() when Select Ride opens, so after a failed PATCH the old method is preselected and no message is shown. This differs from SyncedProfileRepository, which marks syncPending and retries. The preselected method is visible on the Select Ride row before booking, so the impact is limited: low.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _persistSelectedBrand calls unawaited(store.save), the swallowed PATCH failure, then read() reverting to the GET value, then restoreDefaultPayment selecting it. No retry path found (grep for default_save and pending).

verdicts.reason: save() (api_payment_method_repository.dart:55-68) sets _defaultId = brand, then only logs a PATCH failure; nothing marks the save as pending or retries it. read() (lines 40-52) sets _defaultId to the server's defaultMethodId whenever the GET succeeds, so the server's old default replaces the rider's local choice. RideSelectionController.restoreDefaultPayment (ride_selection_controller.dart:572-582) calls store.read() and preselects that value, and the save comes from unawaited(store.save(...)) at line 609, so the rider gets no message. The preselected method is visible on screen, so this is low severity.
verdicts.repro: Wrote and ran a throwaway test (test/_audit_u132_test.dart, since deleted). It built ApiPaymentMethodRepository on an ApiClient backed by a MockClient that returns 503 for PATCH and {defaultMethodId:'cash'} for GET. save('googlePay') logged 'payments.default_save_failed', and the read() that followed printed 'after save read -> cash'.

confirmed.title: After a late GPS fix, the 'Location off, set pickup' placeholder is passed through as the booking pickup label and overwrites the address Home just detected
confirmed.description: isUnusablePickupLabel only rejects empty text, 'current location' and raw coordinates. bookingPickupAddress therefore returns locationOffPickupLabel unchanged instead of reverse-geocoding the real position. Home reaches it with a real fix in two ways. (1) The first detect failed or was denied, and the fix arrives later through _awaitCurrentFix: _prefillPickup keeps address: clean, the old placeholder, at home.dart:811. (2) The recover path above. SelectRide then opens with pickupAddress 'Location off, set pickup' (translated by L10n.place) and pickupIsFallback false. Set pickup later re-resolves it because its own _isPlaceholder covers 'location off', but Select ride, and the pickup Home remembers in _pickupAddress, say location is off while it works.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider denies location, then allows it in the browser and taps Where to -> a destination. _awaitCurrentFix gets a fix, but Select ride shows the pickup as 'Location off, set pickup' next to a map centred on their real position.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Treat locationOffPickupLabel (isPlaceholderPickupLabel) as unusable in isUnusablePickupLabel/bookingPickupAddress so a real point is reverse-geocoded.

confirmed.title: `_idle` turns a superseded (null) reverse-geocode into the 'Pickup location' fallback and can overwrite the newer resolved address
confirmed.description: Every `onCameraIdle` (line 345-349) calls `_idle()`, which awaits `_pickup.reverse(_center)`. `PickupMapController.reverse` (pickup_controller.dart:53-74) deliberately returns `null` for a call that was superseded by a newer one (`if (!_stale.isCurrent(generation)) return null;`). `_idle` does not distinguish 'superseded' from 'no address': `isUnusablePickupLabel(null)` is true, so it does `setState(() { _address = pickupLocationFallbackLabel; _search.text = label; })`. The two lookups are independent HTTP requests (AppGeocoding dedupes only identical keys), so when the newer request B completes before the older request A, B's continuation writes the real street and A's continuation then overwrites it with 'Pickup location'. `_confirmPosition` (line 296-305) books `confirmedPickupAddress(_address, position)`, which keeps that fallback string. Contrast set_pickup_page.dart:550-570 `_resolveAddressNow`, which guards with its own `_resolveGeneration` and `_isAwayFrom(at, _center)` before applying.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider drags the pin, lets go (request A starts), nudges it once more and lets go (request B starts). B answers first and shows 'Klockarvägen 37'; A then answers (as null, superseded) and the card flips to 'Pickup location'. The rider confirms and the booking/driver gets the neutral label 'Pickup location' although the street had been resolved.
confirmed.evidence: confirm_pickup_spot.dart:222-233 `Future<void> _idle() async { if (_moving) return; final address = await _pickup.reverse(_center); if (!mounted) return; final label = isUnusablePickupLabel(address) ? pickupLocationFallbackLabel : address!.trim(); setState(() { _address = label; _search.text = label; }); }` | pickup_controller.dart:61 `if (!_stale.isCurrent(generation)) return null;` | pickup_address.dart:18-23 `bool isUnusablePickupLabel(String? label) { final clean = label?.trim() ?? ''; return clean.isEmpty || ...` | confirm_pickup_spot.dart:300 `final address = confirmedPickupAddress(_address, position);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give `_idle` its own generation counter (or read `_pickup`'s) and return without touching state when the lookup was superseded or when `_isAwayFrom(at)`; only apply the fallback label when the current lookup genuinely returned no address.

verdicts.reason: PickupMapController.reverse (pickup_controller.dart:53-74) returns null for any call superseded by a newer one, because the StaleGuard generation is no longer current. _idle (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:222-233) checks only `mounted` after the await, then maps null to pickupLocationFallbackLabel and calls setState. Nothing compares against a generation, against _center or against _moving. So whenever an older lookup A completes after a newer lookup B, A overwrites B's resolved street with 'Pickup location'. This ordering is realistic. AppGeocoding.reverse (app_geocoding.dart:68-86) serves B from its cache keyed at 5 decimal places, or from a quicker HTTP or Nominatim reply, while A is still on the network. _confirmPosition (:296-305) then books confirmedPickupAddress(_address), so the booking and the driver get 'Pickup location' even though a street had been resolved. Compare _refreshCurrentFix (:174), which does guard with _isAwayFrom.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the onCameraIdle -> _idle -> PickupMapController.reverse -> StaleGuard.isCurrent path, plus the AppGeocoding cache and in-flight dedupe, which only merges identical keys, so a cache hit for B returns immediately while A is pending. No widget test was run.

verdicts.reason: `PickupMapController.reverse` returns null when a newer call has superseded it (pickup_controller.dart:61). `_idle` (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:222-233) cannot tell that apart from 'no address': `isUnusablePickupLabel(null)` is true, so it sets `_address`/`_search.text` to 'Pickup location' with no generation check and no `_isAwayFrom` check. Compare `_refreshCurrentFix` at :175, which has that check. AppGeocoding.reverse (app_geocoding.dart:66-85) answers a cached or in-flight key at once, so out-of-order completion is realistic: the rider drags back to a spot already resolved (B comes from cache) while an earlier lookup A is still on the network. `_confirmPosition` then books `confirmedPickupAddress('Pickup location')`, which keeps the label (pickup_address.dart). Home's `bookingPickupAddress` does not count 'Pickup location' as unusable, so it is never re-resolved. Even when answers arrive in order, the card shows 'Pickup location' for a moment. Impact is limited: the coordinates still travel with the booking, so only the label is wrong.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_vq7c1b3_test.dart: real PickupMapController with a geocoder that answers lat 1 after 100 ms and lat 2 after 10 ms. Ran `_idle`'s exact label logic for A(lat 1), then B(lat 2) 5 ms later. Output: `AUDIT57 idle(2.0) -> Klockarvagen 37`, then `AUDIT57 idle(1.0) -> Pickup location`, then `AUDIT57 final display=Pickup location confirmed=Pickup location`. Test file deleted.

confirmed.title: Set pickup can stay on 'Finding the address…' forever when the pin returns near its last rest point during a lookup
confirmed.description: _resolveAddressNow returns early when the pin moved during the lookup (_isAwayFrom(at, _center)) without clearing _resolving, and relies on a later resolve to reset it. A later resolve is only started by _onCameraIdle when _center is more than about 15 m from _routeStart, and _routeStart is that same 'at' point. If the rider drags away while the lookup is running and lets go within about 15 m of where it started, no new resolve runs. _resolving stays true and the card subtitle reads 'Finding the address…' with no lookup running. _addressIsStale also stays true, so Confirm books a dropped-pin label although the street was known.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider moves the pin, and while its street loads they nudge the map again and let it settle back on almost the same spot. The pickup card keeps saying 'Finding the address…' indefinitely, and the confirmed pickup is 'Dropped pin · …' instead of the street.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reset _resolving (and re-run the lookup for the current point) instead of returning silently when the pin moved.

verdicts.reason: set_pickup_page.dart:553-556 sets `_resolving = true` and returns early, without resetting it, when `_isAwayFrom(at, _center)` is true at the moment the lookup answers. Two paths clear `_resolving`: a later `_resolveAddressNow`, or `_glideTo` with an address (608-609). `_onCameraIdle` (493) only starts a new resolve when `_center` is more than 0.00015 degrees from `_routeStart`, and `_routeStart` equals `at` (496). The stuck state needs one continuous drag: the lookup answers while the pin is away, and the drag ends back within about 0.00015 degrees of the start. Then no new resolve runs, `_resolving` stays true, and the card shows findingTheAddress (1109). `_addressIsStale` stays true, so `_confirm` waits on the already-completed `_resolveTask` (736) and books `droppedPinPickupAddress` (754-756). The window is narrow but the path is real. Moving the pin again, or tapping a chip or search, recovers it.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the `_onCameraIdle`, `_resolveAddressNow` and `_confirm` state writes. `_center` is written only at 595 and 876. No test was run.

verdicts.reason: set_pickup_page.dart:556 returns when `_isAwayFrom(at, _center)` without resetting `_resolving`, which line 553 set to true. A new resolve only starts from `_onCameraIdle` when `_isAwayFrom(_center, _routeStart)` (:493), and `_routeStart` was set to that same `at` (:496). If the lookup finishes mid-drag and the map comes to rest within 0.00015 degrees of `at` (:460-462), no new resolve runs. The card keeps showing findingTheAddress (:1109). `_confirm` (:736) then waits on the finished `_resolveTask` and books `droppedPinPickupAddress` because `_addressIsStale` is still true (:753-755).

It needs a drag-and-return during the lookup, so this is an edge path. Not run as a test.

confirmed.title: Set pickup address search has no try/catch (a failed geocode shows no feedback) and no staleness guard against a pin moved while it was pending
confirmed.description: _searchAddress closes the sheet, then `final found = await _pickup.search(text)` (PickupMapController.search -> geocoding.geocodeAddress, up to the 8 s API timeout, no generation/stale check and no try/catch) and unconditionally calls `_glideTo(found.position, address: ...)`, which rewrites _center/_routeStart/_address and animates the camera. While the search is pending the page is fully interactive (no busy state), so a drag, a spot chip or My location can already have moved the pin; the old search then overrides it. ConfirmPickupSpot._lookup (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:286-293) has the same shape. The page's own reverse lookups and requotes are generation-guarded (RIDE-12), only the forward search is not. A thrown search (offline) is also uncaught here, so the snackbar 'addressNotFoundMoveMap' never appears.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider types 'Storgatan 1' and submits, then immediately drags the pin to the exact entrance; 3-8 s later the geocode answers and the pin jumps back to Storgatan 1 with that label, the quote re-runs, and the rider confirms a pickup they did not choose.
confirmed.evidence:
set_pickup_page.dart:700-710 `final text = query?.trim() ?? ''; if (text.isEmpty || !mounted) return; final found = await _pickup.search(text); if (!mounted) return; if (found == null) { ...snackbar...; return; } await _glideTo(found.position, address: found.address ?? text);`
pickup_controller.dart:113-120 `Future<PickupMapFix?> search(String query) async { final result = await geocoding.geocodeAddress(query); ...` (no stale guard, no catch)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Bump a generation (or compare _center/_routeStart before and after) around the search and ignore a result once the pin has moved or a newer search started; wrap in try/catch and show the not-found snackbar on failure.

verdicts.corrected_title: Set pickup address search has no try/catch (a failed geocode shows no feedback) and no staleness guard against a pin moved while it was pending
verdicts.reason: set_pickup_page.dart:702 awaits _pickup.search(text) with no try/catch. pickup_controller.dart:113-120 and AppGeocoding.forward/_forwardFromApi (app_geocoding.dart:46-65, 94-106) do not catch either, and they apply an 8 s .timeout. So when the rider is offline or the request times out, the future started from InkWell onTap (:1121) ends as an uncaught async error and the 'addressNotFoundMoveMap' snackbar never shows. Nothing marks the page busy during the search, and _glideTo (:576-623) unconditionally rewrites _center/_routeStart/_address. Unlike the reverse lookups, it has no generation check on entry. A pin drag or chip tap made while the search is pending is therefore overwritten when the search returns. Impact is limited: the pin then goes to the address the rider explicitly searched for, the jump is visible before Confirm, and the mock geocoder answers almost at once. Hence low, not medium. confirmed.title: CurvedAnimations created in build leak a status listener on _lift/_sheet on every rebuild
confirmed.description: _PickupPin.build creates a new CurvedAnimation(parent: lift, ...) on every build, and _reveal creates one on _sheet for each of four sections on every build of SetPickupPage. In Flutter 3.47 the CurvedAnimation constructor calls parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection), which is removed only by dispose() (animations.dart:392/441). Its docs say 'Do not recreate it on every build as it would leak'. SetPickupPage rebuilds on every spot load, address resolve, requote, glide and bags tap, so the listeners and the CurvedAnimations they retain pile up for the page's lifetime.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rider who adjusts the pin many times on Set pickup triggers dozens of rebuilds. Each one adds five status listeners to the two controllers, so every pin lift and sheet status change has to iterate an ever-growing listener list, and leak tracking reports undisposed CurvedAnimations.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Create the CurvedAnimations once (in initState, or in a StatefulWidget for _PickupPin) and dispose them.

verdicts.reason: _PickupPin.build (set_pickup_page.dart:1491-1495) and _reveal (:1036-1039, called four times per _sheetView build) construct CurvedAnimation on each build and never dispose them. In the installed Flutter, animations.dart:390-392 adds a status listener to the parent in the constructor, and only dispose() (:439-442) removes it. The docs there say this leaks. The listeners pile up on _lift and _sheet for the page's lifetime. The leak is bounded because both controllers are disposed in dispose (:429-430), so it is low.
verdicts.repro: Read /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/animation/animations.dart:387-442. Confirmed that the CurvedAnimations are created in build paths and that no CurvedAnimation dispose exists in set_pickup_page.dart.

verdicts.reason: _PickupPin.build (set_pickup_page.dart:1491-1495) and _reveal (:1036-1039) build a new CurvedAnimation on every build. In Flutter 3.47 the constructor calls parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection) (animations.dart:392), and only dispose() removes it (:441-445). These instances are never disposed, so each rebuild of SetPickupPage (setState on resolve, requote, bags, glide) adds about 5 status listeners to _lift and _sheet until the page's controllers are disposed. The leak is bounded to the page's lifetime and the per-listener cost is tiny.
verdicts.repro: Read the Flutter SDK source at /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/animation/animations.dart:389-393 and :441-445. Checked that _PickupPin is not const (it takes the _lift field) and that _reveal is called from _sheetView on every build.

confirmed.title: 'Sign out other devices' reports failure when the sign-out succeeded but the follow-up GET failed
confirmed.description: signOutOtherDevices() POSTs the sign-out and ignores its response, although the mock returns the new `security` in that response. It then does a separate GET. If the POST succeeds but the GET fails (network drop, timeout), the controller's catch sets 'Could not update active sessions.' and leaves the old state, still listing the other devices and still holding a fresh reauthenticatedAt. The server has already revoked those sessions and cleared reauthenticatedAt. A retry therefore gets 403 reauth_required and shows the same error.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider confirms Sign out other devices. The POST returns 200 and the GET times out. The Security page shows 'Could not update active sessions.' and still lists the iPhone session, although it was revoked. Retrying fails with 403.
confirmed.evidence:
account_security_repository.dart:14-17 `await _api.post('/api/v1/account/security/sessions/sign-out-others'); return load();`
account_security_controller.dart:63-67 `state = await _repository.signOutOtherDevices(); ... } catch (_) { errorMessage = 'Could not update active sessions.'; }`
in_process_mock_client.dart:572-577 the POST answer already carries 'security'
confirmed.suggested_fix: Decode the `security` from the POST response. If only the refresh fails, report success and reload in the background.

verdicts.reason: AccountSecurityRepository.signOutOtherDevices (account_security_repository.dart:14-17) ignores the POST response. docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:53 documents that response as {security}, and the mock returns it (in_process_mock_client.dart:564-576). The method then does a separate GET. If the POST succeeds and the GET fails, the controller's catch (account_security_controller.dart:63-67) shows 'Could not update active sessions.' and keeps the old state. That old state still lists the revoked sessions and still has a fresh reauthenticatedAt, so the guard at lines 52-57 allows a retry. The retry hits 403 reauth_required, because the server cleared reauthenticatedAt (mock line 571), and shows the same error. This needs a network failure between the two calls, so it is an edge case.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the repository, the controller, the mock POST handler, and the API_V1_MOCK.md wire format.

verdicts.reason: account_security_repository.dart:14-17 ignores the POST response, which already carries 'security' (in_process_mock_client.dart:572-576), and then sends a separate GET. ApiClient has a real http.Client path (api_client.dart:28-31). The GET is retried only on TimeoutException (api_client.dart:268-281, 2 x 15 s), so a socket error or two timeouts after a successful POST throws. account_security_controller.dart:63-67 catches it, shows 'Could not update active sessions.' and keeps the old state, which still lists the revoked sessions and a fresh reauthenticatedAt. A retry passes the client guard (hasFreshReauthentication on the stale state) and gets 403 reauth_required, because the server cleared reauthenticatedAt. This needs a network failure in the short window between the two requests, which makes it an edge case.
verdicts.repro: Traced repository -> controller -> mock handler by reading the code. Not run: the in-process mock has no way to make only the follow-up GET fail.

confirmed.title: Pending profile sync (name/consents) is lost on app restart; class doc promises resend on launch
confirmed.description: `_syncPending` is a plain in-memory field (301). `save()` keeps the local copy and swallows the PATCH failure, setting `_syncPending = true` (341-352); `hydrate()` only resends `if (_syncPending)` (313-316). After the app is killed the flag is false again, so a name/consent change that never reached the server is not resent on the next launch, contrary to the class comment ("sent again with the next save or launch"). The driver app shows the rider's name from this profile.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider renames themselves while offline, closes the app; next launch the server still has the old name until the rider edits the profile again.
confirmed.evidence:
synced_profile_repository.dart:301 `bool _syncPending = false;`
synced_profile_repository.dart:313-316 `Future<void> hydrate() async { await _cache.hydrate(); if (_syncPending) await _sync(_cache.current); }`
synced_profile_repository.dart:349-351 `} catch (error) { _syncPending = true; ...`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Persist the pending flag (e.g. a `movera_profile_sync_pending` pref) and read it in `hydrate`, or compare a stored "last synced" hash with the cache.

verdicts.reason: synced_profile_repository.dart:30 `bool _syncPending = false;` exists only in memory. _sync's catch sets it to true, and hydrate() (:41-44) resends only if it is true. hydrate is called once at bootstrap (app/bootstrap.dart:112) on a fresh instance (di.dart:181), so after a restart the flag is always false and the unsent PATCH is never retried. That contradicts the class doc (:17-19, 'sent again with the next save or launch'). Nothing else PATCHes the profile on launch. The local copy is kept, so there is no local data loss, but the server (and the driver app's rider name) stays stale until the next edit.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: every write of _syncPending in the file, the hydrate callers (bootstrap.dart:111-112) and the SyncedProfileRepository construction in di.dart:181. No persisted pending flag exists.

confirmed.title: 'Days left' on a promotion uses local-midnight Duration.inDays, so it is one day short across spring-forward and says 'Ends today' for a promotion that ends tomorrow
confirmed.description: validityText builds two local midnights and uses `last.difference(today).inDays`. When the range includes the spring-forward night, the two midnights are 23 h apart per transition, so inDays rounds down. Every count across the DST change is one day short. When the promotion ends the day after the change, days is 0 and the sheet shows 'Ends today'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a throwaway test run under TZ=Europe/Stockholm. A promotion with endsAt '2026-03-30T18:00:00' viewed at 2026-03-29 12:00 showed 'Ends today' (expected '1 day left'). A promotion ending on 15 Apr viewed on 1 Mar showed 'Valid until 15 Apr 2026 · 44 days left' (expected 45).
confirmed.evidence:
promotion_details_sheet.dart:110-113
`final today = DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day);`
`final last = DateTime(ends.year, ends.month, ends.day);`
`final days = last.difference(today).inDays;`
`if (days <= 0) return L10n.current.endsToday;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Count calendar days with UTC dates: `DateTime.utc(ends.year, ends.month, ends.day).difference(DateTime.utc(now.year, now.month, now.day)).inDays`.

verdicts.reason: promotion_details_sheet.dart:110-113 takes the difference between two local DateTime midnights and calls .inDays. Across Stockholm's spring-forward night (2026-03-29) those midnights are only 23 h apart, so the count drops by one day. When the promotion ends the next day the result is 0, and line 113 returns endsToday. No guard and no UTC normalisation anywhere in validityText.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u158_test.dart run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm: DateTime(2026,3,30).difference(DateTime(2026,3,29)).inDays printed 'DAYS 0 CET CEST'; 'All tests passed!'. File deleted.

verdicts.reason: promotion_details_sheet.dart:110-112 subtracts two local-midnight DateTimes and takes .inDays. Across the spring-forward night the gap is 23 h, so inDays truncates to one day fewer. With ends one day after the change, days is 0 and line 113 returns endsToday. Nothing corrects for DST. The market is SEK/Stockholm (DECISIONS.md), so this hits the real users once a year.
verdicts.repro: Ran a throwaway test test/_audit_b12x_test.dart under TZ=Europe/Stockholm (since deleted). validityText(endsAt 2026-03-30 18:00 local, now 2026-03-29 12:00) printed 'A: Ends today' instead of 1 day left. endsAt 15 Apr, viewed 1 Mar, printed 'B: Valid until 15 Apr 2026 · 44 days left'; the correct count is 45.

confirmed.title: ReservationPriceChange treats any change under 0.5 major units as unchanged, so EUR/TND edits under half a unit show a zero difference and a 'price unchanged' summary
confirmed.original_title: ReservationPriceChange treats any change under 0.5 major units as 'unchanged', so euro and dinar edits show a 0 difference between two different prices
confirmed.description: ReviewChangesPage builds ReservationPriceChange(previous: original.price, next: draft.price, currency: original.currency). It shows the previous and new prices, then a difference of kr(0) whenever `unchanged`. The 0.5 threshold suits whole-kronor SEK display only. EUR is formatted with cents and TND with millimes (formatMoney), so a real change of up to 0.49 EUR or 0.499 DT is shown as a zero difference. The class also holds a single currency, so when the edited pickup is priced in another currency (draft.currency = selection.currency) the two amounts are subtracted across currencies.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Paris (EUR) reservation was booked at 12.35 €, and the edit re-quotes it at 12.70 €. Review changes shows Previous '12,35 €', New '12,70 €', Difference '0,00 €'. The rider confirms an edit that costs 0.35 € more while being told the difference is zero.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare in minor units with Money.fromLegacyMajor(next, currency) != Money.fromLegacyMajor(previous, currency), or set the threshold at half a displayed unit per currency. Refuse, or show separately, a change across currencies.

verdicts.reason: reservation.dart:178 sets `unchanged => delta.abs() < 0.5`. review_changes.dart:23-27 builds the change from original.price and draft.price, and review_changes.dart:110-112 shows kr(0) when unchanged. ReservationFormat.kr (reservation_format.dart:95) calls formatMajor(whole: true). In shared/formatters/money.dart:24-37 `whole` rounds only SEK; EUR and TND keep their minor digits. The EUR and TND markets exist in rider_app_config.dart:490 and :529. So a 0.35 EUR change shows as '0,00 €', and change.summary (reservation.dart:181) says resPriceUnchanged. The cross-currency half is weaker: the class uses original.currency for both amounts, but an edit that moves the pickup into another market is an edge case. The rider still sees both real prices on the cards above.
verdicts.repro: Read-only static trace (no flutter/dart run). Worked by hand: previous 12.35, next 12.70, delta 0.35 < 0.5 so unchanged; kr(0,'EUR') -> formatMoney(Money(0,'EUR'), whole:true) -> '0,00 €'.

verdicts.reason: reservation.dart:178 `unchanged => delta.abs() < 0.5` is a whole-krona threshold, and review_changes.dart:110-111 then shows kr(0, currency) as the difference. EUR and TND fares are not whole units: mock_catalog_fares.dart sets EUR stepMinor 5 (0.05 €) and TND stepMinor 100 (0.1 DT), and money.dart:34-37 always prints EUR and TND to the minor unit. So 12.35 -> 12.70 € gives delta 0.35 < 0.5: the row shows '0,00 €' and the summary says resPriceUnchanged, while the Previous and New rows show different prices. The cross-currency part is speculative: it needs an edit whose pickup moves into another zone, and I did not trace that path.
verdicts.repro: Read only, no run. Worked by hand: 12.70 - 12.35 = 0.35 (double, about 0.35000000000000142), abs < 0.5, so unchanged is true. That leads to formatMajor(0,'EUR'), which prints '0,00 €'. The 0.05 € fare step comes from MockZoneCurrency.eur in lib/core/api/mock_catalog_fares.dart.

verdicts.reason: _nextRide (home_reservation_chrono.dart:199-204) returns the earliest isUpcoming ride. A no-driver ride is still scheduled or driverAssignmentPending, both of which count as upcoming (reservation_status.dart:15-21). Nothing cancels it automatically: startLiveIfDue (reservation_controller.dart:328-395) never cancels, and isNoDriverFound is only a predicate. If the rider dismisses the sheet, choice is null and the code returns without resolving (line 119). _openLiveIfNeeded (lines 132-136) checks only _nextRide().revealsDriver, so a later ride B that goes en route is never auto-opened. The only other caller of ReservationLiveRide.open is upcoming_reservation.dart:102, which is reached manually. Tapping the chrono calls _openRide(A) and opens the no-driver sheet again (lines 156-160).
verdicts.repro: Read-only static trace of _nextRide, _openLiveIfNeeded, _promptNoDriverIfNeeded and isUpcoming, plus a grep for other ReservationLiveRide.open callers.

verdicts.reason: _nextRide (home_reservation_chrono.dart:199-204) always returns the earliest upcoming ride. A no-driver ride keeps the scheduled or driverAssignmentPending status (isNoDriverFound, reservation_controller.dart:306-316, is derived and nothing changes the status), so it stays in upcoming() (:141-142) until resolveNoDriverFound runs. Dismissing the sheet (choice == null at :119) only sets _promptedNoDriverId. _openLiveIfNeeded (:132-136) checks only _nextRide().revealsDriver, so a later ride that reveals its driver is never auto-opened, and tapping the chrono reopens the no-driver sheet (:158-163). Reachable in demo or mock dispatch when ride A gets no driver but ride B does.
verdicts.repro: Read only, no run. Traced it by hand with A at 09:00 (no driver, dismissed) and B at 11:00 (driver en route at 10:58): _nextRide() returns A, A.revealsDriver is false, so the function returns early and B is never opened.

verdicts.corrected_title: Home reservation chrono's countdown overflows its 54 px disc at large text sizes (no textScaler clamp); in French 'Maintenant' breaks mid-word

confirmed.title: Reservation cancel reason codes 'no_driver_found' and 'rider_cancelled_live' show as raw English text
confirmed.description: The controller records no-driver cancels with the code 'no_driver_found' (ReservationController.noDriverFoundReason), and the live screen records 'rider_cancelled_live'. reasonLabel only maps CancellationReason ids and the _reasonLabels table, which has 'system_no_driver' but not these two codes. Both fall through to the snake_case prettifier, so they show as untranslated English in the reservation status body (resBodyCancelledReason) and in the History detail 'Reason:' line. Verified with a throwaway test in fr: reasonLabel('no_driver_found') returned 'No driver found' and reasonLabel('rider_cancelled_live') returned 'Rider cancelled live'.

confirmed.suggested_fix: Map 'no_driver_found' to termNoDriverFound and 'rider_cancelled_live' to a translated label in _reasonLabels, or record 'system_no_driver' instead.

Those are shown inside the localized resBodyCancelledReason (statusBody, :178-182) and in the History reason line (history/presentation/ride_history.dart:561). The canonical contract code is system_no_driver (contracts/contract.json:585, lib/core/contracts/cancel_reasons.dart:28). No document makes this intentional.
verdicts.repro: Traced the writers and reasonLabel. I grepped lib/ for both strings: no mapping exists anywhere. The finding's own throwaway fr test also reported reasonLabel('no_driver_found') == 'No driver found'.

confirmed.title: cardDate 'Tomorrow' label breaks on the spring-forward day because today.add(Duration(days:1)) is not the next local midnight
confirmed.description: cardDate compares `day == today.add(const Duration(days: 1))` where today is a local midnight. Dart's add() works in absolute time, so on the DST switch day the result is 01:00 of the next day, not midnight (verified by throwaway test: DateTime(2026,3,29).add(Duration(days:1)) == 2026-03-30 01:00:00 under Europe/Stockholm). The equality then fails and the reservation card falls through to weekdayDate instead of 'Tomorrow, 30 Mar'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Sunday 29 Mar 2026 a Stockholm rider with a reservation on Monday 30 Mar sees 'Mon, 30 Mar' on the upcoming card instead of 'Tomorrow 30 Mar'. Same for Tunisia or any zone with DST on its switch day.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Build tomorrow as `DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + 1)` (calendar arithmetic) instead of adding a Duration.

verdicts.reason: reservation_format.dart:143 compares day == today.add(const Duration(days: 1)). On a DST change day that sum is not the next local midnight, so the equality fails and cardDate (used at :205 for the reservation card line) falls through to weekdayDate instead of 'Tomorrow'. This happens on both the spring and the autumn switch. The Tunisia example in the finding is wrong because Tunisia has no DST, but Sweden and France are affected.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_r64dst_test.dart and ran `TZ=Europe/Stockholm flutter test test/_audit_r64dst_test.dart`. Output: 'add=2026-03-30 01:00:00.000 eq=false' and 'fall add=2026-10-25 23:00:00.000 eq=false', then 'All tests passed!'. The file was deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: reservation_format.dart:139-145 compares the calendar day `day` with today.add(const Duration(days:1)). DateTime.add adds absolute time, so on a DST switch day the result is not the next local midnight, the equality fails, and cardDate falls through to weekdayDate. It is reached through historyWhen (:204-205), which is used by the upcoming/reservation cards (reservation_widgets.dart:382) and the History detail (ride_history.dart:546). This affects both switch days, not only spring. The Tunisia example is wrong because Tunisia has no DST; Stockholm, the primary market in DECISIONS.md:42, does.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm. Output: 'today=2026-03-29 00:00 add1d=2026-03-30 01:00 calendarTomorrow=2026-03-30 00:00 equal=false' and 'today=2026-10-25 00:00 add1d=2026-10-25 23:00 calendarTomorrow=2026-10-26 00:00 equal=false'. Control: 'today=2026-06-01 ... equal=true'. So on 29 Mar and 25 Oct 2026, a ride the next day gets the weekday label instead of 'Tomorrow'.

verdicts.corrected_title: Live scheduled ride rebuilds ride notes by substring search: 'Bags 3+' shows as plain Bags, and rider free text can turn on Pet/Baby/Child chips
verdicts.reason: reservation_live_ride.dart:34-41 never sets manyBags, and it uses note.contains(). select_ride.dart:1141 sets manyBags through withBagLevel(spot.bagLevel) on the schedule path, and _driverNote (1206-1213) joins the rider's free text with RideNotes.selected ('Bags 3+'). The scheduled note therefore holds 'Bags 3+' and the rider's words. WaitingNotesAndPin (waiting_sheet_bits.dart:481) then shows 'Bags', not 'Bags 3+', and a text like 'Petra meets you' adds a Pet chip. The impact covers only the rider's own live screen: the driver gets the reservation's raw note string, so the claim that the 'driver-facing summary is wrong' is overstated.
verdicts.repro: Traced the note from SelectRide._driverNote -> ScheduledRideCheckout -> Reservation.note -> ReservationLiveRide.notesOf -> WaitingForDriver.notes -> WaitingNotesAndPin, and checked RideNotes.selected labels.

verdicts.reason: notesOf (reservation_live_ride.dart:34-42) rebuilds the notes by substring search and never sets manyBags. SelectRide._driverNote (select_ride.dart:1206-1213) stores the rider's own text joined with RideNotes.selected labels, including 'Bags 3+' (ride_notes.dart:35-41). So 3+ bags is lost, and free text that contains 'Pet', 'Baby', 'Child' or 'Bags' turns on flags. The result goes to WaitingForDriver.notes, which renders the chips in WaitingNotesAndPin (waiting_for_driver.dart:1928) and carries them into the snapshot (:1053).

confirmed.title: Scheduled live ride offers route/destination changes that cannot work: the route quote is sent to /rides/{reservationId}, which the API does not know (404)
confirmed.description: pageFor reuses WaitingForDriver and does not turn off route editing. _routeEditable is true until the ride ends, so the three-dots route screen and the cancel sheet's 'change destination' offer are shown. RouteChangeController then posts to /api/v1/rides/{rideId}/route-quote with the reservation id (rsv_...). The API has no such ride: the in-process mock answers 404 not_found when rides[id] is null. The rider is offered an edit that cannot work, and a successful local change would never reach the reservation record anyway.
confirmed.failure_scenario: During a scheduled ride with the driver en route, the rider opens ride details and changes the destination. Pricing the change fails (404), or in the cancel sheet they choose 'change destination' instead of cancelling and get an error.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add a WaitingForDriver flag to turn off route changes for reservation live rides, or route reservation edits through ReservationController.

verdicts.reason: ReservationLiveRide.pageFor (reservation_live_ride.dart:64-77) passes rideId: ride.reservationId and has no flag to turn off route editing. _routeEditable (waiting_for_driver.dart:1010) depends only on terminal status and _completedOpened, so _openDetails/_changeRoute (1015, 1067) and the cancel sheet's offerDestinationChange (817) stay available. _currentRide (1021-1058) builds a snapshot carrying the reservation id, and RouteChangeController posts /api/v1/rides/{rsv id}/route-quote (route_change_controller.dart:200-201). Reservations never enter the mock's rides map, which only POST /api/v1/rides fills (in_process_mock_client.dart:597-610), so the mock answers 404 not_found at 817-820. The contract (CONTRACT.md:129,244) defines route-quote on trip ids only. The rider is offered an edit that always fails, but an error is shown and the app does not claim success.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the WaitingForDriver route-change path with the reservation id, and of the mock route-quote handler plus its rides map population. Grepped reservations code for any /rides route-change path (none).

verdicts.corrected_title: Scheduled live ride offers route/destination changes that cannot work: the route quote is sent to /rides/{reservationId}, which the API does not know (404)
verdicts.reason: pageFor (reservation_live_ride.dart:64-120) gives WaitingForDriver no way to turn off route editing. _routeEditable (waiting_for_driver.dart:1010) depends only on terminal status and on the completion screen having opened. So the three-dots menu (onMore: _openDetails at :1895/1910/1926) and the cancel sheet's offerDestinationChange (:817-822) are both available. _currentRide (:1021-1059) builds a snapshot whose rideId is the reservation id, because persistRideSnapshot=false means no stored snapshot matches it. RouteChangeController then posts to /api/v1/rides/$id/route-quote (route_change_controller.dart:199-203). Reservations live in LocalReservationRepository and are never in the mock's rides map, so the mock answers 404 not_found (in_process_mock_client.dart:817-820). The rider gets an error, not a false success, so this is low severity.
verdicts.repro: Traced the full path: ReservationLiveRide.pageFor, then WaitingForDriver._openDetails, then _changeRoute, then openRouteChange, then RouteChangeController.quote, then InProcessMockClient route-quote, where rides[rsv id] is null and it returns 404. Nothing on that path checks for a reservation realtime or for persistRideSnapshot. I did not run a widget test.

UpcomingReservationPage only rebuilds when the ReservationController notifies, and nothing rebuilds it on a timer. While the rider stays on the page past freeUntil, it still says cancelling is free until HH:mm. The cancel sheet works out fresh terms, so the fee does appear before confirming.

verdicts.reason: upcoming_reservation.dart:438-442 builds the summary from cancelTermsFor(ride) with now=_clock() (reservation_controller.dart:117-124), but only at build time. The page rebuilds only through _refresh (upcoming_reservation.dart:50,61-64) when ReservationController notifies. The controller's clock sweep notifies only when a status changes (reservation_controller.dart:373-396: assignment inside 2 min of pickup, or en-route), and nothing fires when freeUntil passes. ReservationFormat.cancellationSummary (reservation_format.dart:256-267) therefore keeps showing freeUntilThen. The effect is small: the cancel action works out fresh terms (upcoming_reservation.dart:131), so the fee is shown and agreed before anything is charged.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: the page's listeners (initState :48-52), every notifyListeners in reservation_controller.dart (none is time-based apart from the status sweep at :396), and cancellationSummary. Not run.

verdicts.reason: The KnowCard text comes from cancelTermsFor(ride), which uses _clock() and is only worked out during build (upcoming_reservation.dart:438-442). The page rebuilds only from _reservations.addListener(_refresh) (:50, :61-63) or from its own busy-flag setStates (:114-180). The controller's clock pass notifies only when `changed`, and that happens only inside the 2-minute pre-pickup window (reservation_controller.dart:373, :396). Rules and config refreshes notify only when the value changes (:80-105). No Timer exists on this page; the only periodic Timer in reservations is home_reservation_chrono.dart:64, which belongs to another widget. So between freeUntil and pickup minus 2 min, a page left open keeps the freeUntilThen text ('Free until 09:00 ... After that, cancelling costs 50 kr'). That wording names a time that has already passed. It should switch to freeEndedCostsNow (reservation_format.dart:260-264). This is harmless for money: the cancel action works out fresh terms before confirming (upcoming_reservation.dart:131). No decision doc covers it.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: the page listener, then every notifyListeners site in reservation_controller.dart, then the clock pass's `changed` condition (untilPickup <= 2 min). With pickup at 10:00 and a 60-minute window, freeUntil is 09:00. From 09:00 to 09:58 nothing notifies, so the build-time text stays on 'freeUntilThen'. I did not run a widget test.

confirmed.title: RideSession.reset() keeps the previous rider's booked category, payment method id and offer ceiling, and they carry into the next rider's adopted ride
confirmed.description: reset() is documented as 'Back to "no ride" at the end of a rider's session'. It clears rideId, status, versions and quote, but not bookedCategoryId, bookedPaymentMethodId or bookedMaxOfferMinor. backendReconcile clears these fields only when both the current and the incoming ride id are non-null and differ. After reset, rideId is null, so the next ride never clears them. RideRestoreCoordinator._adoptBookingIds and BookingCoordinator's active-trip adoption then fall back to the stale session values whenever the server projection omits a field (`snapshot.maxOfferMinor ?? session.bookedMaxOfferMinor`). FindingDriverController.start writes them into the new snapshot, and WaitingForDriver prefers `ride.bookedCategoryId` over the stored category for the waiting-fee terms.

Rider B signs in and opens a ride B booked on another device, adopted from GET /rider/trips/active, whose projection has no maxOfferMinor. B's search is stored and priced with A's 600 kr offer ceiling and A's payment method id, and Waiting loads waiting terms for A's category.

After that rideId is null, so backendReconcile's isNewRide (ride_session.dart:106-112) needs a non-null currentRideId and is false, and the booked* fields survive. The restore paths (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:323-329 and 499-505 -> _adoptBookingIds at 396-400) and booking_coordinator.dart:498-501 then fall back to the stale values with '??'. contracts/openapi.yaml defines no maxOfferMinor on the trip projection, so against a real backend snapshot.maxOfferMinor is always null and the previous rider's ceiling is used. That ceiling drives FindingDriverController.maxOfferPrice (finding_driver_controller.dart:213-216) and the raise check (:792-795). The previous rider's category also feeds waiting_for_driver.dart:296/780. The server still enforces its own ceiling, so the damage is limited to wrong client-side limits and terms.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of reset() callers, backendReconcile, _adoptBookingIds, booking_coordinator adoption, finding_driver_controller.start (275-277) and an openapi.yaml grep (no maxOffer field). Not executed.

The adoption paths then fall back to the stale values whenever the projection leaves a field out: booking_coordinator.dart:498-501, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:396-400, and finding_driver_controller.dart:275-277 writes them into the snapshot. ride_projection.dart:66 shows maxOfferMinor is optional (_int may return null). The leak needs a rider switch on one device plus an adopted ride whose projection omits a field, so the impact is low.
