confirmed.title: A catalog answer that changes the category ids while Set pickup is open starts a list re-quote at the unconfirmed original pickup that can overwrite the pin's quote
confirmed.description: _onCatalogChanged runs _loadQuotes() whenever the ids differ (for example, the server list replacing the 14 built-in ids on first use). _loadQuotes prices every category at _pickupPosition, which is still the original point while Set pickup is open. RIDE-11 protects the pin quote only from list loads begun before it (quoteFromPin bumps _quoteGeneration). A list load begun after the pin quote is adopted overwrites the selected category's authoritative quote with the original point's price. Book now then shows a 'price updated' dialog asking the rider to accept the original pickup's price for the moved pickup.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a slow first launch, the ride-types answer lands while the rider is on Set pickup with the pin already moved and re-priced. The selected ride's quote reverts to the original point's price, and the booking dialog proposes that wrong price for the moved pickup.
confirmed.evidence:
select_ride.dart:435 `if (!sameIds) unawaited(_loadQuotes());`
select_ride.dart:475-480 `distanceMeters: straightLineMeters(_pickupPosition, ...), pickupPoint: _geoPoint(_pickupPosition),`
ride_selection_controller.dart:401-402 `if (generation != _quoteGeneration) return; adoptQuote(rideId, quote);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Defer catalog-triggered re-quotes while the booking flow (_bookingInFlight / Set pickup) is open, or skip overwriting a quote adopted from a pin after the list load began.

verdicts.reason: _onCatalogChanged (select_ride.dart:424-436) starts _loadQuotes whenever the ids differ. It quotes at _pickupPosition, which is still the original point while Set pickup is open; it only changes on confirm (select_ride.dart:1490). quoteFromPin bumps _quoteGeneration only at the moment it is called (controller:431-432). A list load that begins after it gets a newer generation and adoptQuote overwrites authoritativeQuotes for the selected id (controller:401-402). On confirm, _quoteAfterPickup returns that list quote (select_ride.dart:559-560), which differs from spot.fareTotalKr, so _acceptNewPrice offers the original pickup's price for the moved pickup (select_ride.dart:1517-1521). No guard defers catalog-triggered re-quotes during Set pickup. The window is narrow: the ride-types answer must land late, with different ids that still include the selected one, after the pin was re-priced. Example: the bootstrap load failed and fell back to the built-in list, and SelectRide's refresh answers late.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: refreshCatalog is called in initState (select_ride.dart:346), RideCatalogController._set notifies on change (ride_catalog_controller.dart:93-98), _loadQuotes uses _pickupPosition (select_ride.dart:463-483), and the generation handling is in quoteFromPin/_loadQuote (ride_selection_controller.dart:394-446). Not reproduced at runtime.

verdicts.reason: There is no guard on this path. _onCatalogChanged calls _loadQuotes whenever the catalog ids change (select_ride.dart:435). _loadQuotes takes a new generation (beginQuotes) and prices every category at _pickupPosition, which is reassigned only after Set pickup returns (select_ride.dart:1490). For the selected ride, adoptQuote (controller:401-402) overwrites the authoritative pin quote. quoteFromPin's RIDE-11 protection (controller:432-434) only invalidates list loads that began before it. On Confirm, _quoteAfterPickup (select_ride.dart:547-583) returns that still-fresh quote for the original point. The shown != quote.totalMinor check (select_ride.dart:1510-1513) then opens 'Price updated' with the original point's price, and accepting it books that quote for the moved pickup. The window is narrow. With the in-process mock, the bootstrap catalog load (bootstrap.dart:127) answers at once. A real server needs the ride-types answer to land after the rider has moved the pin and the pin quote has come back, and with different ids than before: for example, a 15 s api timeout (api_client.dart:42) that falls back to a cache list, or a later server list replacing a cache list. Real but low.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: select_ride.dart:424-436, 464-483, 498-514, 547-583, 1478-1513; ride_selection_controller.dart:337-414 (loadQuotes/_loadQuote generation checks) and 420-450 (quoteFromPin); ride_catalog_controller.dart:46-98 (load, cache fallback, notifyListeners on changed ids). confirmed.title: Scheduled booking does not re-quote a quote that expired during the date picker and Set pickup; booking fails with a no-price toast and needs two more taps
confirmed.description: `_book` checks `quoteIsAvailable` once, then `_bookScheduled` opens the date-time picker and Set pickup (and possibly the picker again for return rides) before `ScheduledRideCheckout.run` → `draftFrom` → `ScheduledRideBooking.quotedPrice`, which throws `ScheduledQuoteRequiredException` as soon as `authoritativePriceFor` is null. Quotes expire after 2 minutes (in_process_mock_client.dart:2173 and catalog_quote_repository.dart:35), so a rider who spends more than two minutes choosing a time and pickup spot gets the `resErrNoPriceBook` toast and nothing is booked; Book now handles the same situation by re-quoting in place (`_quoteAfterPickup`, RIDE-2) but the scheduled path has no equivalent. Tapping Book again then shows 'price unavailable, refreshing' and the rider must repeat the picker and pickup steps.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider taps Schedule, spends 3 minutes picking Saturday 07:00 and adjusting the pickup pin, taps 'Confirm and schedule' → toast that no price is available; reservation not created; second attempt repeats every step.
confirmed.evidence: select_ride.dart:1110-1116 `if (_selection.scheduledFor == null) { await _chooseLater(); } ...`; select_ride.dart:1155-1176 `created = await ScheduledRideCheckout.run(...)` with no re-quote before it; scheduled_ride_booking.dart:26-28 `final price = selection.authoritativePriceFor(categoryId, now: now); if (price == null) throw ScheduledQuoteRequiredException(categoryId);`; in_process_mock_client.dart:2173 `'expiresAt': WireTime.format(DateTime.now().add(const Duration(minutes: 2))),`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Before `ScheduledRideCheckout.run`, reuse `_quoteAfterPickup(ride)` (awaiting `_pinQuote`, re-quoting from the confirmed pickup when stale) and pass its price, mirroring `_bookNow`.

confirmed.description: _bookNow captures `selected` and `payment`, parks the map, and _openSetPickup then awaits _homePosition() (saved-places hydrate up to 600 ms plus a Home geocode up to 900 ms) before pushing Set pickup. During that window only the Book CTA is disabled (_bookingInFlight). Ride tiles (_selectRide, line 2187), the payment row (_showPaymentPicker) and the calendar button (_showBookingPicker) still respond. A tap on another category highlights it, but Set pickup and the booking use the captured one. A tap on Pay with or the calendar pushes that page or sheet, and Set pickup then opens on top of it.

The only lock is on the Book CTA (`onTap: _bookingInFlight ? null : _book`, line 2490). None of these check _bookingInFlight: _selectRide (lines 650-665), _rideTile's InkWell (line 2187), _showPaymentPicker (line 1024) and _showBookingPicker (line 956). confirmed.title: The 'Price updated' dialog has no time limit, so a quote that expires while it is open fails the booking with a generic error after the rider accepted
confirmed.description: _bookableQuote guarantees only 10 s of quote life (_quoteMargin) before _acceptNewPrice opens. The dialog waits for the rider indefinitely, and the quote is not re-checked or refreshed after they accept. Mock quotes live 2 minutes. If the rider takes longer, BookingCoordinator refuses the expired quote locally (booking_coordinator.dart:630) and the rider sees 'bookingFailed' right after tapping 'Book for X'.

select_ride.dart:1515-1520 `if (shown != null && ... != quote.totalMinor && !await _acceptNewPrice(shown, authoritativePrice)) {...}` followed directly by submitFinding with `quote.expiresAt` (1543)
booking_coordinator.dart:630 `(!isReplay && !quoteExpiresAt.isAfter(DateTime.now())) ||`

BookingCoordinator then throws StateError('A fresh authoritative quote is required for booking') when !quoteExpiresAt.isAfter(now) (booking_coordinator.dart:630-637). mayHaveBooked is false for a local StateError, so the rider sees the generic bookingFailed snackbar (select_ride.dart:1560-1570) after explicitly accepting the new price. confirmed.title: A card the rider closed comes back after a quick reload when its close was queued behind a slow alert send
confirmed.description: `_close` clears `_session` immediately, but the local save that marks the event resolved happens inside the queued 'close' job. Jobs run one after another (`_enqueue`). If an earlier alert job is still waiting on the API (up to the 15 s ApiClient timeout when offline), the close job and its local `keep(status: resolved)` have not run yet. If the page reloads or the app is killed in that window, the event is still pending/acknowledged on disk, so `unanswered()` returns it and the non-dismissible card reopens. The rider's final answer (for example 'I'm OK' or the note) was never saved.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Offline: the rider taps a red row (the alert POST hangs), then taps Done within a few seconds and the card folds away. The browser reloads before the 15 s timeout. The card is back on the trip screen, blocking it, and the Done/note answer is lost.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:681-693: `void _close(RideCheckSession closing) { _session = null; ... _changed(); ... _enqueue('close', () async { await _service.submitAnswers(...` 
ride_check_controller.dart:731-732: `final previous = _queue; _queue = previous == null ? run() : previous.then((_) => run());`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Save the closing answers and resolved status to the local cache synchronously in `_close`, before enqueueing the network part.

verdicts.reason: _close (ride_check_controller.dart:681-711) sets _session = null and folds the card away straight away. The local write that marks the event resolved is inside submitRideCheckAnswers (safety_store.dart:452-454, keep + _local.save with isFinal -> resolved), and that only runs when the queued 'close' job starts. _enqueue (ride_check_controller.dart:719-732) chains jobs with previous.then, so the close job waits until the earlier 'alert' job's postRideCheckAnswers returns. With the real http.Client that can take up to the 15 s ApiClient timeout (api_client.dart:42). The alert job has already saved the event as acknowledged (safety_store.dart:452-454, non-final with answers). If the app reloads or is killed in that window, RideCheckService.unanswered (ride_check_service.dart:97-107) returns that acknowledged event, and resume() (ride_check_controller.dart:421-458) rebuilds the card from it. The final answer (Done, I'm OK or the note) was never saved or sent. Nothing guards this. The in-process mock answers immediately, so this only happens against a real or slow backend, which keeps it low.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _sendAlert -> _enqueue('alert') -> RideCheckService.submitAnswers -> SafetyStore.submitRideCheckAnswers (local save as acknowledged, then awaits the remote call). Then _close -> _enqueue('close') is chained behind it. After a reload, RideCheckController.resume -> RideCheckService.unanswered reads cachedRideCheckEvents, skips only resolved/stale events, and returns the acknowledged one. Not run.

verdicts.reason: ride_check_controller.dart:681-692 `_close` sets `_session = null` straight away. The only write that marks the event resolved is in safety_store.dart:452-453 (`keep(withAnswers(..))` with `isFinal` giving `resolved`, then `_local.save`), and it runs inside the queued 'close' job. `_enqueue` (ride_check_controller.dart:731-732) chains that job after the earlier 'alert' job. The alert job awaits `_remote.postRideCheckAnswers`, and the ApiClient timeout is 15 s (api_client.dart:41). Until then the cached event stays `acknowledged`: the alert job saved it with answers and isFinal=false (safety_store.dart:428-432). `unanswered()` skips only resolved/stale events (ride_check_service.dart:97-107), so `resume()` (ride_check_controller.dart:420-456) rebuilds the card, and the Done/I'm OK/note answer is lost. This can only happen on a real HTTP transport with a stalled connection. The in-process mock answers within microseconds, and a fully offline fetch usually fails at once, so the window is narrow. That is why the severity is low.
verdicts.repro: Hand trace, not run. I read the order of operations in _sendAlert, _close and _enqueue (ride_check_controller.dart:645-733), submitRideCheckAnswers (safety_store.dart:411-462), unanswered (ride_check_service.dart:97) and resume (ride_check_controller.dart:420). Nothing marks the event resolved before the queued job runs, and no persisted 'closing' flag exists.

confirmed.title: A failed stop (NO_AUDIO / SAVE_FAILED) leaves an orphan recording entry with endedAt == null (and any 0-byte or captured file) that nothing ever cleans up
confirmed.description: `start()` registers the recording in the cache (`initDeviceAudio` / `initAudio`) before capture. In `stop()`, when the recorder returns null (missing or 0-byte file) the service throws NO_AUDIO without deleting that cache entry. The native recorder also leaves the 0-byte file on disk, because it only checks the file and returns null (safety_recorder_native.dart:39-41). When completeDeviceAudio/completeAudio throws, SAVE_FAILED leaves the captured m4a on disk with no localPath recorded anywhere. A recording interrupted by an app kill likewise stays as an entry with endedAt == null (isRecording == true) forever. These entries and files accumulate in `movera_safety_cache_v1` and Documents.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The rider taps Record and then Stop within a fraction of a second, so the encoder writes 0 bytes. The card says 'No audio file was captured.' The cache keeps a recording with no file and an endedAt timestamp, and the empty .m4a stays in safety_recordings. Repeating this grows both.
confirmed.evidence:
safety_audio_service.dart:87-91: `final path = await _recorder.stop(); _active = null; if (path == null) { throw SafetyAudioException('NO_AUDIO', L10n.current.audioNoFile); }`
safety_audio_service.dart:102-104: `} catch (_) { throw SafetyAudioException('SAVE_FAILED', L10n.current.audioSaveFailed); }`
safety_recorder_native.dart:39-41: `if (path == null || !await File(path).exists() || await File(path).length() == 0) { return null; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: On NO_AUDIO, delete the store entry and the empty file. On SAVE_FAILED, keep the localPath in memory and retry, or delete the file.

verdicts.reason: start() adds the recording to the cache (safety_store.dart:466-478 initDeviceAudio / 494-508 initAudio), and createdAt is set while endedAt is null. In stop(), the NO_AUDIO branch (safety_audio_service.dart:89-91) throws without calling _store.deleteAudio or _recorder.delete. The native recorder returns null for a 0-byte file and leaves it on disk (safety_recorder_native.dart:39-41). The SAVE_FAILED catch (safety_audio_service.dart:102-104) drops `path`, so nothing refers to the m4a any more. stopIfRecording (118-141) only cancels the recorder; it removes nothing either. No code reads or prunes _cache.recordings apart from these methods, so the entries and files pile up. The effect is small: no UI lists the entries, and the cache JSON is tiny.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of safety_audio_service.dart start/stop/stopIfRecording, SafetyStore init/complete/deleteAudio (safety_store.dart:466-550) and NativeSafetyRecorder.stop. Grepped lib for every reader of `.recordings` and found only the store itself. Found no cleanup path for these entries or files.

confirmed.title: Ride check recording keeps the microphone on after session expiry replaces the trip screen with Sign in
confirmed.description: The only things that stop a Ride check recording are answering the card (`_close`) and the ride-end paths in ActiveRideController. On session expiry, `onSessionExpired` re-roots to Sign in and keeps the ride (di.dart:104-116). Waiting and the card's layer are disposed, but RideCheckController keeps `_session` and the audio service keeps `_active`, so the recorder keeps capturing on the Sign in screen with no Stop control. If a different rider then signs in, `enterSessionAs` wipes and `SafetyController.resetShared()` discards the service, so the recorder can no longer be stopped by any code path.
confirmed.failure_scenario: During an unanswered card the rider records. The alert POST gets a 401 and the token refresh fails, so the app shows Sign in. The microphone indicator stays on and the recording grows until the process dies, or until the same rider signs back in and returns to the card.
confirmed.evidence:
di.dart:104-115: `onSessionExpired: () async { ... AppScope.showSignInOnSessionExpired?.call(); }` (no audio stop)
safety_controller.dart:71-77: `static void resetShared() { RideCheckController.resetShared(); _shared?.dispose(); _shared = null; ...` (audio not stopped)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call `audio.stopIfRecording` on session expiry and in SafetyController.resetShared before discarding the service.

verdicts.reason: Only three places stop a recording: RideCheckController._close (ride_check_controller.dart:692), Safety Kit sheet close (ride_safety_kit.dart:146), and the ride end in ActiveRideController (active_ride_controller.dart:468 -> SafetyController.stopRecordingForRideEnd). onSessionExpired (di.dart:104-116) only clears the last fix and re-roots to SignIn (app.dart:15-17), so nothing stops the mic there. RideCheckController.dispose (ride_check_controller.dart:819-826) and the card widgets' dispose do not stop audio either. If a different rider then signs in, UserDataWipe (user_data_wipe.dart:135) calls SafetyController.resetShared (safety_controller.dart:71-77). That drops _shared without stopping audio, and SafetyController has no dispose override that would. After that, stopRecordingForRideEnd sees `_shared == null`, and no reference to the running AudioRecorder is left. This needs a real 401 with a failed refresh while a recording runs, so it is an edge path. But a hot microphone with no Stop control is a real privacy leak, so I rate it medium rather than low.
verdicts.repro: Traced every stopIfRecording/stop caller with grep, plus di.dart onSessionExpired, app.dart registerSessionExpiredNavigation, UserDataWipe.enterSessionAs -> SafetyController.resetShared -> RideCheckController.resetShared/dispose. None of them touches the audio service.

verdicts.reason: On session expiry, di.dart:104-116 only clears the last fix and calls showSignInOnSessionExpired, which does showMoveraRoot(SignIn) (app.dart:15-17). Waiting's dispose (waiting_for_driver.dart:1265-1280) only calls RideCheckController.detachTrip, which just nulls _monitor (ride_check_controller.dart:255-258). It does not touch _session or the audio. The ActiveRideController that would call stopRecordingForRideEnd belongs to the disposed Waiting state (waiting_for_driver.dart:189), so a ride end can no longer stop the recording either. The only stop paths are ride_check_controller.dart:692 (_close), ride_safety_kit.dart:146 and active_ride_controller.dart:468. If a different rider signs in, UserDataWipe.resetInMemory calls SafetyController.resetShared (user_data_wipe.dart:135). That disposes RideCheckController and drops the SafetyController (safety_controller.dart:71-77) without stopIfRecording, so the native AudioRecorder is orphaned while still recording. verdicts.repro: Traced the code only. I grepped every stopIfRecording / stopRecordingForRideEnd / resetShared caller in lib and read the dispose paths of Waiting, RideCheckController and SafetyController. None of them stops the active recording on session expiry or on resetShared. I did not run a test, because it needs the native recorder plus a 401 with a failed refresh during an open card.

confirmed.title: Safety Kit audio cannot start without a successful server init (fails offline); each successful init also leaves an orphaned optimistic recording in the persisted cache
confirmed.description: The Kit records with `deviceOnly: false`, so `start()` awaits `_store.initAudio`, a `_write` that must reach POST /safety-audio/init. Offline, the remote fails, `_write` reverts and rethrows, and the Kit shows 'recording failed': a rider in a dead zone cannot record from the Safety Kit at all, although the file is saved locally. When init succeeds, the server returns its own id (`aud_$requestId` in the mock), not the optimistic id. `apply(confirmed)` only removes entries with the confirmed id, so the optimistic entry with the local id stays in the cache forever with endedAt == null.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Offline in a tunnel, the rider opens the Safety Kit and taps Record audio. The note says recording failed and the microphone never starts. Online, every Kit recording adds two cache entries, one of which is never completed.
confirmed.evidence:
safety_store.dart:494-507: `final rec = AudioRecording(id: 'aud_${newRequestId()}', ...); return _write(() => _remote.initAudio(rideId: rideId), rec, (value) { _cache.recordings = [..._cache.recordings.where((r) => r.id != value.id), value]; },);`
safety_mock_api.dart:363: `'id': 'aud_$requestId',`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Start capture locally first and register with the server best effort (queue the init when offline). In apply, replace the optimistic entry by its local id.

verdicts.corrected_title: Safety Kit audio cannot start without a successful server init (fails offline); each successful init also leaves an orphaned optimistic recording in the persisted cache
verdicts.reason: `SafetyAudioService.start` (safety_audio_service.dart:57-59) awaits `_store.initAudio` before the microphone starts. `_write` (safety_store.dart:81-101) reverts and rethrows when the remote fails, so ride_safety_kit.dart:196-212 shows recordingFailed and nothing is recorded offline. The duplicate entry is also real: the optimistic `aud_<local>` entry is added, then `apply(confirmed)` removes only entries matching the server id (`aud_$requestId`, safety_mock_api.dart:363), so the local one stays with endedAt == null. However, nothing outside SafetyStore reads `_cache.recordings` (grep finds only internal writes at :487 and :530), so the orphan is invisible junk in local storage, not a visible stuck 'recording' row.
verdicts.repro: Traced start() to initAudio, then _write, the mock init response, and every reader of recordings by grep. Not run.

verdicts.reason: Neither half causes harm a rider can see. (1) The duplicate is real: the optimistic id `aud_${newRequestId()}` (safety_store.dart:496) differs from the mock's `aud_$requestId` (safety_mock_api.dart:363), and apply only removes entries with the confirmed id (:505). But nothing reads `_cache.recordings` for display. grep shows its only users are the store's own write paths (safety_store.dart:475-543) and serialization (safety_data_sources.dart:24-106), and the QA snapshot (safety_controller.dart:128-137) leaves recordings out. The effect is one orphan JSON entry per recording in the local cache. (2) Offline start fails because this path registers with the server first (`_write` reverts and rethrows, safety_store.dart:92-101). SafetyAudioService.start then throws before the mic opens (safety_audio_service.dart:57-60), so the rider gets an honest failure message, not a false success, and no audio is lost. The server-registered init/complete contract is the documented design (features/safety/README.md:45-47). Recording on the device first while offline would be a feature request, not a defect.
verdicts.repro: Traced by code reading. Followed initAudio through `_write` and the mock /safety-audio/init route, then grepped every reader of `recordings` in lib/. Confirmed the duplicate id mismatch and that no reader is visible to the rider. Not run.

verdicts.reason:
I'm confirming only the duplicate-entry half, at low severity. The offline half is a design choice, not a defect.

Duplicate entry (real, and I reproduced it). initAudio (safety_store.dart:494-507) adds an optimistic entry with the id `aud_${newRequestId()}`. The server sends back its own id, `aud_$requestId` (core/api/safety_mock_api.dart:363). The apply step at :505 only removes entries that match the server's id, so the local-id entry is never replaced. That entry keeps endedAt == null, which makes isRecording true (audio_recording.dart:32). Nothing ever completes it, and deleteAudio (:543) only removes the server-id entry. So the orphan stays in the saved cache even after the rider deletes the recording, along with its rideId and createdAt.

This is a known defect pattern, not a design choice. createContact in the same file already fixes the identical case with the FLOW-20 comment, 'the confirmed row replaces the optimistic one even when the server assigns its own id' (safety_store.dart:168-176). initAudio never got that fix.

Why only low: both checkers are right that nothing displays `_cache.recordings`. It is used only by the store's own write paths and by serialization in safety_data_sources.dart. The QA snapshot (safety_controller.dart:128-137) leaves it out. So the 'stuck as recording' state exists only in local storage. Three things make it real anyway:
- a stale 'still recording' row is saved for every Safety Kit recording,
- local storage grows without limit,
- a record that a recording happened on that ride survives after the rider deletes the recording.

Offline half (not a defect). Start does fail offline before the mic opens: `_write` reverts and rethrows (:92-101), so `start` throws at safety_audio_service.dart:57-59. But the server-registered init/complete contract is documented in lib/features/safety/README.md:45-47, and the only device-only path is Ride check (RC5). The failure is honest, not a false success, and no audio is lost. One small flaw: a network error falls through to the catch-all in ride_safety_kit.dart:206-209. That shows recordingFailed, 'Check microphone access and try again', which points the rider at the wrong cause.
verdicts.repro:
I wrote and ran a throwaway test, test/_audit_u207_test.dart, then deleted it; git status is clean afterwards. It used a SafetyStore with a spy SafetyLocalDataSource and ApiSafetyRemoteDataSource(ApiClient(client: InProcessMockClient())), with SafetyAudioService running a fake recorder that grants permission.

Online run (start, stop, delete) printed:
- `active id=aud_5bc52e487ffa586e7c61b5b0`
- `after start: [aud_748e878e0c1e524801bf84d6 ended=null, aud_5bc52e487ffa586e7c61b5b0 ended=null]`
- `after stop: [aud_748e878e0c1e524801bf84d6 ended=null isRecording=true, aud_5bc52e487ffa586e7c61b5b0 ended=2026-10-21 07:03:56Z isRecording=false]`
- `after delete: [aud_748e878e0c1e524801bf84d6 ride=ride_a ended=null isRecording=true]`

Offline run, with a remote whose initAudio throws: `offline error=Exception: SocketException: network unreachable micStarts=0 isRecording=false cached=0`. That is an honest failure before the mic starts.

Result: `00:00 +2: All tests passed!`

confirmed.title: SwedishPhone.toE164 accepts a trunk zero after +46 and stores an invalid contact number
confirmed.description: After normalising, the function only checks that the part after `+46` is 7–10 digits (116-119). Input like `+46 070 123 45 67` (a very common way to write a Swedish mobile) becomes `+46070…`, which passes (10 digits) and is stored as the emergency contact's `phoneE164` and sent to the share/alert backend, but is not a dialable E.164 number.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider adds a trusted contact as "+46 070 123 45 67"; it is saved as +46070 123 45 67 and shown as such; the number cannot be reached by the safety team.
confirmed.evidence: phone_e164.dart:115-119 `if (!value.startsWith('+46')) return null; final rest = value.substring(3); if (rest.length < 7 || rest.length > 10) return null; if (!_digits.hasMatch(rest)) return null; return '+46$rest';`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Strip a leading `0` from `rest` (or reject it), and require the national number to start with a non-zero digit.

verdicts.reason: lib/features/safety/domain/phone_e164.dart:4-18 (the file is 29 lines, so the cited line 116 is wrong). After '+46' is detected, `rest` is only checked for length 7-10 and all digits, so a trunk '0' is kept. The emergency contact form is a free-text TextField (emergency_contacts_page.dart:327-330, keyboardType phone, no formatter), and SafetyStore.addContact (safety_store.dart:136-155) saves whatever toE164 returns as phoneE164. Its duplicate check also misses '+4670...' against '+46070...'. The auth path (auth_navigation.dart:68-71) is safe because it only adds +46 when the input has no leading 0.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r94_test.dart (since deleted) printed `r83: +460701234567` for SwedishPhone.toE164('+46 070 123 45 67'). All tests passed.

verdicts.reason: lib/features/safety/domain/phone_e164.dart:14-18 (the finding's line 116 is wrong; the file has 29 lines). When the input already starts with '+46', none of the rewrite branches at :7-13 run. The only checks are rest.length in 7..10 and all digits, so a trunk 0 after +46 gets through. The add/edit contact form passes the raw field text (emergency_contacts_page.dart:270). SafetyStore.createContact (safety_store.dart:136) accepts it and stores and POSTs '+460701234567'. The display helper cannot fix it: rest starts with '0', so phone_e164.dart:27 shows '+46 0701234567'. The sign-in path has its own guard (auth_navigation.dart:65-72) that only covers the national-number field; it does not apply to contacts. No guard rejects a 0 after +46.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c2b5_test.dart (since deleted). SwedishPhone.toE164('+46 070 123 45 67') printed 'rider-83 toE164 => +460701234567 display => +46 0701234567'. SafetyStore(memoryOnly).createContact(name:'Mum', phone:'+46 070 123 45 67') went through the mock POST /api/v1/safety/contacts (status 200) and printed 'rider-83 stored => +460701234567'.

confirmed.title: The monitor marks a trigger as fired even when the card could not open (another card up), so that trigger is lost for the rest of the trip
confirmed.description: RideCheckMonitor._fire adds the trigger to `_fired` before the controller tries to open it. RideCheckController.open returns `busy` when any session is up (line 379), and the result is ignored (`unawaited(open(...))` at lines 274/290, and the tripEnded result). Because `_canFire` checks `_fired`, the trigger can never fire again on this trip. The droppedFar check at finish is lost if an unanswered mid-trip card is still up, and an off-route hit is lost while a long-stop card is open.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A long-stop card is open and the rider has not answered. The driver then finishes 5 km from the drop-off. tripEnded fires droppedFar, open() returns busy, and droppedFar is now marked fired. After the rider answers the long-stop card, no 'finished far from drop-off' check ever appears for this trip.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mark the trigger fired only when open() returns shown, or queue the detection and open it after the current card closes.

verdicts.reason: ride_check_monitor.dart:251-253 _fire adds the trigger to _fired before the controller has opened anything, and _canFire (:248) blocks that trigger afterwards. ride_check_controller.dart:379 returns busy when _session != null. addSample/checkStill (:273-275, :289-291) drop the result with unawaited(open(...)), and waiting_for_driver.dart:1222 drops the tripEnded result too. Nothing re-queues a detection that got busy. An off-route hit during an open long-stop card is therefore lost for the trip, although the condition would otherwise re-fire on the next sample. The same goes for droppedFar at the finish while a mid-trip card is unanswered. The open() doc says it does not open 'when another card is up', but that covers not showing the card, not discarding it permanently in the monitor.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: RideCheckMonitor._offRoute/_stoppedFor/tripEnded, then _fire, then controller.addSample/tripEnded, then open() busy branch; no retry or queue anywhere, and session clearing at :682 does not re-run detections.

verdicts.reason: RideCheckMonitor._fire (ride_check_monitor.dart:251-254) adds the trigger to _fired before the controller tries to open it, and _canFire (:248-249) blocks it from then on. RideCheckController.open returns busy while a session is up (ride_check_controller.dart:379). addSample and checkStill ignore that result (:273-275, :289-291). The only production caller of tripEnded also ignores it and calls it once (waiting_for_driver.dart:1220-1222, guarded by _rideCheckEnded). So droppedFar, or an off-route hit, that arrives while another card is open is never shown for that trip.
verdicts.repro: Wrote the throwaway test test/_audit_u208_test.dart, using the same setup as the 'RideCheckController gates' group in test/safety/ride_check_triggers_test.dart, then deleted it. The car stood still for 130 s, which opened longStop. tripEnded was then called 5 km from the drop-off, imOk() answered the card, and tripEnded was called again. Output: 'session1 RideCheckTrigger.longStop', 'tripEnded -> RideCheckOpenResult.busy', 'after imOk session null', 'tripEnded again -> RideCheckOpenResult.noTrigger'. All tests passed.

confirmed.title: Ride check distances use '.' as decimal separator in Swedish/French ('1.2 km')
confirmed.description: `formatRideCheckDistance` builds the bold part of the card's reason line with `toStringAsFixed`, which always uses '.'. RideCheckPage and the demo page format admin's km the same way (ride_check_page.dart:44-50, ride_check_demo_page.dart:158-159). Swedish and French need ','. This code is separate from lib/shared/formatters/money.dart (the known finding), so fixing that file does not fix these strings.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Swedish UI: the dropped-far card reads 'Resan slutade 3.6 km från …' and the RideCheck page shows 'mer än 2.5 km' instead of '3,6 km' / '2,5 km'.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_check_trigger.dart:243-244: `final km = meters / 1000; return '${km.toStringAsFixed(km >= 10 ? 0 : 1)} km';`
ride_check_page.dart:44-46: `t.offRouteKm.toStringAsFixed(0) : t.offRouteKm.toStringAsFixed(1);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Format with NumberFormat for the current locale (the same helper the money formatter fix will use).

verdicts.reason: formatRideCheckDistance (ride_check_trigger.dart:238-245) uses `toStringAsFixed`, which always prints '.' as the decimal separator. Its output goes straight into the card's reason line (ride_check_card.dart:55, 84), for any distance from 1 to 10 km (one decimal). ride_check_page.dart:44-50 formats the admin's offRouteKm and finishFarFromDropoffKm the same way, and the result is put into Swedish and French strings (app_sv.arb:991, 993, 1002, e.g. 'mer än {km} km'). Swedish and French use ',' as the decimal separator. No locale-aware formatter is applied, and the docs record no decision that allows '.'. Cosmetic only.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: formatRideCheckDistance callers in ride_check_card.dart, ride_check_page.dart km strings, sv/fr arb placeholders. Searched lib for NumberFormat and found no locale formatting on these paths.

verdicts.reason: formatRideCheckDistance (ride_check_trigger.dart:238-245) uses `toStringAsFixed`, which always writes '.'. It feeds the card's reason line (ride_check_card.dart:55,84). RideCheckPage (ride_check_page.dart:44-50) formats admin's km the same way. No locale-aware number formatting (NumberFormat) exists anywhere in lib/, and nothing in DECISIONS.md marks this as intended. The text is wrong in Swedish and French but harmless otherwise.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand. formatRideCheckDistance(3600): km = 3.6, so toStringAsFixed(1) gives '3.6 km' in every locale (Dart's toStringAsFixed ignores locale). Swedish/French should show '3,6 km'. grep -rn NumberFormat lib finds only an unrelated card-number TextInputFormatter.

confirmed.title: `_ContactEditorState._save` calls setState in its catch block without a mounted check; the editor is a dismissible sheet
confirmed.description: `_ContactEditor` is shown through `MoveraSheet.show` (line 42-46) with the defaults `swipeDismissible = true, barrierDismissible = true` (movera_sheet.dart:22-23), so the rider can swipe it away while `await widget.controller.addContact/editContact` is in flight. The success branch guards with `if (mounted) Navigator.pop(context);` but the catch branch does `setState(() { _error = ...; _saving = false; })` unconditionally. If the save fails after the sheet was dismissed, `setState` runs on a disposed State: an assertion error in debug ('setState() called after dispose()'), a null-check error on `_element` in release, surfacing as an unhandled async error from the button's unawaited `_save()` future.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider taps Save on the emergency-contact sheet, swipes the sheet down during the request, and the request then fails (offline, server error). The app logs/reports an unhandled 'setState() called after dispose()' error from `_ContactEditorState._save`.
confirmed.evidence: emergency_contacts_page.dart:284-291 `if (mounted) Navigator.pop(context); } catch (_) { setState(() { _error = widget.controller.error ?? context.l10n.contactSaveFailed; _saving = false; }); }` | :42-46 `await MoveraSheet.show<void>( context: context, builder: (context) => _ContactEditor(controller: _ctl, existing: existing), );` | movera_sheet.dart:22-23 `bool swipeDismissible = true, bool barrierDismissible = true,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add `if (!mounted) return;` at the top of the catch block (mirroring the success branch).

verdicts.reason: emergency_contacts_page.dart:284-291: the success branch checks `if (mounted)`, but the catch branch calls setState(...) and reads `context.l10n` without a check. The editor opens through MoveraSheet.show with the defaults swipeDismissible/barrierDismissible = true (movera_sheet.dart:22-23), and there is no PopScope in the editor. The save awaits a remote call: SafetyStore.createContact -> _write(() => _remote.createContact(...)) (safety_store.dart:165), so the rider has time to dismiss the sheet. SafetyController.addContact rethrows failures (safety_controller.dart:228-233). onPressed is `_saving ? null : _save` (:396), which does not await the Future. So a remote failure after dismissal throws 'setState() called after dispose()' (or a null-check error on _element in release), and it escapes as an unhandled async error. The rider sees nothing; the only effect is a spurious crash report.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _edit -> MoveraSheet.show (dismissible) -> _ContactEditor._save -> controller.addContact/editContact -> SafetyStore remote write (async network) -> failure rethrown -> catch block setState with no mounted guard.

verdicts.reason: emergency_contacts_page.dart:286-290: the catch block calls setState with no mounted check, while the success branch at :284 does check. The sheet opens through MoveraSheet.show (emergency_contacts_page.dart:42-46), whose defaults are swipeDismissible/barrierDismissible = true (movera_sheet.dart:22-23), so it can close while controller.addContact is waiting on the network. SafetyController.addContact rethrows (safety_controller.dart:228-233), and so does SafetyStore._write (safety_store.dart:97-100). The effect is limited to an error report: setState after dispose (an assert in debug, a null-element error in release) escapes as an unhandled async error from the unawaited onPressed future. The rider sees nothing wrong.
verdicts.repro: Wrote the throwaway test test/_audit_r84_contactsave_test.dart. It uses a SafetyStore whose remote createContact waits on a Completer and then throws. The test opens 'Add contact', enters Kim / 0701234567, taps Save, pops the sheet route, then completes the gate. flutter test output: 'setState() called after dispose(): _ContactEditorState#717ab(lifecycle state: defunct, not mounted)' with stack '#2 _ContactEditorState._save (package:movera_rider/features/safety/presentation/emergency_contacts_page.dart:287:7)'. File deleted.

confirmed.title: Return-ride picker silently moves a stale or off-grid prefill: choose() clamps before initState, so the 'pickup time updated' notice never shows
confirmed.description: choose() calls session.captureSchedule(initial), which already runs clampPickup. initState then compares clampPickup(existing) with existing, and both are the already clamped value, so _pickupCorrectionMessage is never set. SelectRide relies on this picker for return-ride prefills ('opens on the prefill clamped to the next legal slot'). The rider's return time can be moved (for example 21:07 to 21:10, or a past time to now+30) with no notice.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A return ride is prefilled at origin+3h = 21:07, which is off the 5-minute grid. The picker opens at 21:10 with no 'pickup time updated' line, so the rider does not know the time was changed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass the raw initial time to the selector (for example a separate field), or compare against the unclamped value.

verdicts.corrected_title: Return-ride picker silently moves a stale or off-grid prefill: choose() clamps before initState, so the 'pickup time updated' notice never shows
verdicts.reason: choose() calls session.captureSchedule(initial) (select_date_time.dart:55), which stores PickupSchedule.clampPickup(at) (scheduled_rides_controller.dart:36-38). initState then computes clampPickup(existing, now) on that already-clamped value (select_date_time.dart:93-102). clampPickup is idempotent: roundToFive drops seconds and keeps a grid minute (stockholm_schedule.dart:39-45, 87-99), and both calls use the real clock, so corrected == existing and _pickupCorrectionMessage stays null. The one exception is a minute boundary crossed between the two calls. The affected path is real. select_ride.dart:1112-1115 and 1143-1150 open the picker with initial: _selection.scheduledFor exactly when _returnTimeNeedsPicker says the return prefill is stale or illegal. That is the case where the notice was meant to explain the moved time, and the picker opens at the corrected time with no explanation.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of ScheduleDateTimeSelector.choose -> ScheduledRideSession.captureSchedule -> PickupSchedule.clampPickup, then _ScheduleDateTimeSelectorState.initState. Callers with initial: select_ride.dart:1115 (_chooseLater(initial:)) and 1145. home.dart:864 passes no initial and is unaffected.

confirmed.title: After a rebuild that happens without a pick (e.g. backing out of the category step), a pickup time that has gone stale greys out Continue with no correction message
confirmed.description: _goNext has a branch that moves an illegal pickup to the next legal slot and shows 'pickup time updated'. A real path still exists. goToNextStep in schedule_ride.dart:126-151 awaits the category selector and then calls setState in its finally block. The same ScheduleDateTimeSelector State is kept (the rider-88 comment at select_date_time.dart:181), so a rider who spends more than one slot boundary on the category step and comes back gets a rebuild. _continueButton (select_date_time.dart:807-811) then computes legal=false and disables the button, while _pickupCorrectionMessage stays null and the old time is still shown. The auto-correction in _goNext (:157-165) cannot run because onPressed is null. The rider can recover by tapping the time row and picking again, so the impact is low.

confirmed.title: HorizontalSwipe keeps the drag origin in build-local variables, so a rebuild mid-drag resets start to 0: a leftward drag is swallowed or read as a right swipe
confirmed.description: `start` and `last` are plain locals declared inside `build()` and captured by the three drag closures. GestureDetector re-syncs recognizer callbacks on every rebuild (RawGestureDetectorState.didUpdateWidget -> _syncAll re-initialises onStart/onUpdate/onEnd), so if the widget rebuilds while a finger is down, onUpdate/onEnd run with a fresh `start = 0`. `distance = last - start` then equals the absolute x position of the finger (always > 56 on a phone), so `right` is true regardless of direction. Callers: lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:2177 wraps the Home sheet inside an AnimatedBuilder (rebuilds on every sheet tick and on every Home setState, e.g. each GPS fix delivered by HomeLocationController._deliverFix) with only onSwipeLeft -> a slow left swipe is swallowed and a fast one is cancelled because both `left` and `right` are true; lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_tab_page.dart:42 sets both callbacks, so a rebuild during a leftward drag pops the page with `HomeTabs.previousOf(tab)` (the wrong neighbour). Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (deleted): a 100 px leftward drag with one setState mid-drag printed `left=0 right=1`; the identical drag without the rebuild gave `left=1 right=0`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider on Home drags the sheet left to open Payment while a location fix arrives (Home rebuilds ~1 Hz): nothing opens, or on a bottom-bar page the app pops to the previous tab instead of the next one.
confirmed.evidence: lib/shared/widgets/horizontal_swipe.dart:22-23 `double start = 0; double last = 0;` (inside build) ... :26 `onHorizontalDragStart: (d) => start = last = d.globalPosition.dx,` :30 `final distance = last - start;` :32 `final right = velocity > _minVelocity || distance > _minDistance;` ; lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:2177 `child: HorizontalSwipe(` under `AnimatedBuilder` (~home.dart:2105); lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_tab_page.dart:42-45. Test run: `left=0 right=1 ... Expected: <1> Actual: <0>`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make HorizontalSwipe a StatefulWidget (or keep start/last in a ValueNotifier/record owned outside build) so the drag origin survives rebuilds; alternatively use DragStartDetails/DragEndDetails only (d.velocity + accumulated delta from onHorizontalDragUpdate stored in State).

verdicts.corrected_title: HorizontalSwipe keeps the drag origin in build-local variables, so a rebuild mid-drag resets start to 0: a leftward drag is swallowed or read as a right swipe
verdicts.reason: horizontal_swipe.dart:22-23 declares start and last inside build(). After a rebuild, the recognizer gets the new closures (start=0), so distance at :30 becomes the finger's absolute x and `right` is true. On Home the swipe sits inside the sheet's AnimatedBuilder (home.dart:2105-2131, 2177), which rebuilds on every sheet-controller tick and on any Home setState. The finding's main trigger is wrong, though: GPS fixes do not setState Home. The onFix handlers (home.dart:382-387) only repaint the puck through _locationCtl, and _refreshPickupLabelIfMoved rebuilds only after 75 m. So the realistic triggers are a sheet still settling, a promotion or saved-places change, or the recenter button toggling mid-drag. HomeTabPage (home_tab_page.dart:40-46) rebuilds only when its route rebuilds the cached page, which is rare. The mechanism is real, but on an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_r93_test.dart: a StatefulBuilder wrapping HorizontalSwipe, a 100 px leftward drag in 10 steps with one setState+pump halfway. It printed `rebuild: left=0 right=1` (test passed and the file was deleted). Also checked the Home rebuild sources at home.dart:259-264, 382-387, 705-724, 1569-1586 and 1782-1806.

verdicts.corrected_title: HorizontalSwipe keeps drag origin in build-local variables; a rebuild of the Home sheet mid-drag resets start to 0, so a leftward swipe is swallowed (Home only has onSwipeLeft)
verdicts.reason: horizontal_swipe.dart:22-33 declares start/last inside build(). A rebuild re-syncs the recognizer callbacks to new closures with start=0, so distance = last - 0 is the absolute x position and `right` becomes true. The mechanism is real. The finding overstates how reachable it is. (1) GPS fixes do not setState Home. onFix only repaints the puck through the controller (home.dart:259-263 and _updateLocationVisuals at :1569-1586), so the claimed '~1 Hz rebuild' is wrong. (2) HomeTabPage never rebuilds mid-drag: RightToLeftTransition's pageBuilder returns the same `page` instance (navigation_transition.dart:131, page built once at home.dart:1846), and HomeTabPage.build depends on no inherited widget. The 'pops to the wrong neighbour' path therefore cannot happen. What remains is Home's sheet HorizontalSwipe (home.dart:2177) inside the AnimatedBuilder/Builder. It rebuilds on discrete events that can land during a swipe: _trackSettledSnap's setState 140 ms after the sheet settles (home.dart:1762, 1794), _destinationSheetOpen (:1802), promotion refresh completion (:1725), and saved-places stream updates (:174-177). The result is an occasional swallowed swipe-left to Payment, a minor but real defect.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_r93_test.dart: a host StatefulWidget wraps HorizontalSwipe, and a slow 100 px leftward drag runs with and without one setState mid-drag. Output: 'rebuild=false left=1 right=0' and 'rebuild=true left=0 right=1'. File deleted. Also traced which Home setState sources can fire during a drag, and that the route builder reuses the page instance.

confirmed.title: Transition builders allocate an undisposed CurvedAnimation on every transition frame, leaking status listeners on the route controller for the route's lifetime and losing curve-direction continuity on mid-animation reversal
confirmed.original_title: Transition builders create a new CurvedAnimation on every frame and never dispose it, so status listeners pile up on long-lived routes
confirmed.description: Each transitionsBuilder (TopToBottomTransition:28, RideStageTransition:61, SwitchTransition:99, _sheetCover:169, _sideCover:193) constructs a CurvedAnimation. In this Flutter SDK the CurvedAnimation constructor always calls parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection), and only dispose() removes it. _ModalScopeState rebuilds buildTransitions through a ListenableBuilder on Listenable.merge(animation, secondaryAnimation) (flutter routes.dart:1101-1102, 1204-1208), so the builder runs on every tick of the route's own animation and of every route pushed or popped above it. Each tick leaves one more status listener on the route's AnimationController for the route's lifetime. Flutter's own CurvedAnimation docs (animations.dart:410-411) say not to recreate it on every build because it leaks. A fresh CurvedAnimation per frame also drops the curve-direction memory, so a pop that starts mid-push jumps to the reverse curve.
confirmed.failure_scenario: SelectRide or FindingDrivers (RideStageTransition) stays in the stack while many pages and sheets are pushed and popped above it. Each transition frame (about 20 per 360 ms push) adds another dead status listener to that route's controller. Memory grows with every navigation over the route, and every later status change iterates the whole list.
confirmed.evidence: navigation_transition.dart:28 `final curved = CurvedAnimation(parent: animation, curve: MoveraCurves.open, reverseCurve: MoveraCurves.close);` (and :61, :99, :169, :193). /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/animation/animations.dart:389-392 `CurvedAnimation(...) { ... parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use `CurveTween(curve: ...)` chained on the animation, for example `animation.drive(CurveTween(curve: MoveraCurves.open))`, or move the curves into a StatefulWidget that owns and disposes its CurvedAnimation.

verdicts.reason: navigation_transition.dart:28,61,99,169,193 each build a new CurvedAnimation inside transitionsBuilder, and nothing disposes it. The Flutter SDK constructor at animations.dart:389-392 calls parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection), and only dispose() removes that listener. The parent is route.animation, which is _controller!.view (routes.dart:247-250), meaning the AnimationController itself. _ModalScopeState wraps _buildFlexibleTransitions in a ListenableBuilder on Listenable.merge(animation, secondaryAnimation) (routes.dart:1101-1102, 1204-1208). So every tick of the route's own animation, and every tick of a route pushed or popped above it, adds one more status listener to that controller. The value listeners used by FadeTransition and SlideTransition are removed correctly in didUpdateWidget, so only the status listeners pile up. The direction-memory part is also real: a fresh CurvedAnimation starts with _curveDirection null and takes parent.status (animations.dart:430), so a route that reverses mid-push switches to reverseCurve at once (SwitchTransition, _sideCover, _sheetCover and TopToBottom all set reverseCurve), which makes a visible jump. No guard prevents either effect. Impact is small: the listeners are tiny, they are freed when the route's controller is disposed, and they only grow during animation frames, never while idle.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only, no flutter/dart run (read-only). Read the app file, then /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/animation/animations.dart:389-435 and /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/routes.dart:247-250, 328, 1101-1102, 1204-1235. Nothing in DECISIONS.md or ARCHITECTURE.md mentions this pattern.

verdicts.reason: navigation_transition.dart:28, 61, 99, 169 and 193 each build a new CurvedAnimation inside transitionsBuilder, and nothing disposes it. In this SDK the constructor calls parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection) (animations.dart:389-392), and only dispose() removes that listener. _ModalScopeState wraps _buildFlexibleTransitions in a ListenableBuilder on Listenable.merge(animation, secondaryAnimation) (routes.dart:1101-1102, 1204-1208), so the builder runs again on every tick of the route's own animation and of its secondaryAnimation. No guard exists. The extra listeners live until the route's controller is disposed with the route, so the leak is bounded by how long the route stays in the stack. The cost per tick is small, which is why it rates low. The direction claim also holds: each new instance reads parent.status, so once a pop reverses a push mid-flight, every new CurvedAnimation picks reverseCurve (the reversal case animations.dart:404-407 avoids) and the curve jumps. RideStageTransition has no reverseCurve and a zero reverse duration, so this part does not apply to it. The leak still does.
verdicts.repro: Read-only run: no flutter or dart commands. I traced routes.dart:1098-1250, where the ListenableBuilder over the merged animations calls buildTransitions -> transitionsBuilder on every animation tick, and the CurvedAnimation constructor and its doc warning at animations.dart:389-416. Worked by hand for a 360 ms push at 60 fps: about 21 builder calls, so about 21 status listeners added and never removed, plus about the same again for each push or pop above the route through secondaryAnimation.
verdicts.evidence: navigation_transition.dart:28 `final curved = CurvedAnimation(parent: animation, curve: MoveraCurves.open, reverseCurve: MoveraCurves.close);` with no dispose; animations.dart:391 `parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection);`

confirmed.title: Connection banner and MoveraEmptyState are read twice by screen readers: an explicit Semantics label plus the unexcluded child Texts (empty state is at lib/shared/design_system/movera_empty_state.dart)
confirmed.original_title: Screen readers announce the connection banner twice: an explicit Semantics label is set and the child Texts are still read
confirmed.description: The banner wraps its content in Semantics(liveRegion: true, label: '<title>. <body>'), but the title and body Text widgets below it are not excluded. Neither is a semantics boundary, so their labels merge into the same node and the live-region announcement reads the title and body twice. MoveraEmptyState (movera_empty_state.dart:29-31, Semantics(container: true, label: '$title. $message') above the same two Texts) has the same duplication on every empty and loading screen.
confirmed.failure_scenario: TalkBack or VoiceOver user on the trip screen: the connection drops and the live region announces 'Reconnecting. <body>' and then 'Reconnecting <body>' again. History's loading and empty states are read twice in the same way.
confirmed.evidence: realtime_connection_banner.dart:34-38 `Semantics(key: ..., liveRegion: true, label: spec.semantics, child: DecoratedBox(... Text(spec.title ...), Text(spec.subtitle ...)` where spec.semantics = '${L10n.current.rtReconnecting}. ${L10n.current.rtReconnectingBody}'. movera_empty_state.dart:29-31 `Semantics(container: true, label: '$title. $message', child: ... Text(title) ... Text(message)`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the visual content in ExcludeSemantics, or drop the explicit label and keep only the Texts.

verdicts.reason: realtime_connection_banner.dart:34-38 sets Semantics(liveRegion: true, label: spec.semantics) with no container and no excludeSemantics. Its descendants (DecoratedBox, Padding, Row, Column, two Text widgets) contain no semantics boundary and no ExcludeSemantics. The Texts' labels therefore merge into the same semantics node as the explicit label 'title. body', and the node reads that label followed by title and body again. The banner is used on ride-critical screens: waiting_for_driver.dart:1518, finding_drivers.dart:903 and ride_completed.dart:331. MoveraEmptyState is at lib/shared/design_system/movera_empty_state.dart:29-31, not under widgets/ as the finding says. Its Semantics(container: true, label: '$title. $message') sits above Text(title) and Text(message) with no exclusion. Its SingleChildScrollView may put the Texts in a child scroll node instead of merging them, but the screen reader still reads the title and message twice. The decision documents do not record any accessibility choice that would make this intentional.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only, no flutter/dart run (read-only). Read the banner build tree, its three callers, movera_empty_state.dart:29-70, and grepped DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and QA_HOOKS.md for semantics decisions (none found). Fix: add excludeSemantics: true to both Semantics widgets.

verdicts.reason: realtime_connection_banner.dart:34-38 is a Semantics with liveRegion: true and an explicit label, but container is false and there is no excludeSemantics or ExcludeSemantics. The Text widgets at :64 and :73 sit under it with no semantics boundary between them (DecoratedBox, Padding, Row, Column and Expanded create none). Their labels therefore merge into the same node as the explicit label, giving "Reconnecting. <body>\nReconnecting\n<body>", so the live region announces the text twice. Nothing under lib/shared excludes this subtree; the only ExcludeSemantics there is in movera_icon_button.dart:63. MoveraEmptyState is actually at lib/shared/design_system/movera_empty_state.dart:29-31, not the path the finding gives. It also duplicates, but differently: SingleChildScrollView adds its own scroll semantics node, so the Texts become a child node under the container's label rather than being joined into one label. The screen reader still reads the title and message twice when moving through the screen.
verdicts.repro: Read-only run: no flutter or dart commands. I read realtime_connection_banner.dart:20-100 and movera_empty_state.dart:1-80 and applied the semantics merge rules by hand: a non-container Semantics config merges with any child config that is not a boundary, and their labels are joined with newlines. I did not run a widget test. A semantics-tree dump from tester.getSemantics(find.byKey(ValueKey('realtime-reconnecting'))) would confirm the label text.
verdicts.evidence: Semantics(key: ValueKey('realtime-${state.name}'), liveRegion: true, label: spec.semantics, child: DecoratedBox(... Text(spec.title) ... Text(spec.subtitle)))

confirmed.title: screenHorizPadding is computed once (lazy top-level), so after a web/desktop window resize side gutters stay at the first scale (e.g. 16 px vs 20 px) while ResSize-scaled layout rescales
confirmed.description: `double screenHorizPadding = ScreenUtil().setWidth(16);` is evaluated on first read and never again. lib/app/screen_scale.dart:45-47 deliberately rebuilds ScreenUtilInit with new bounds on a window resize so widths rescale, but every consumer of this global (lib/features/messages/presentation/chat.dart:107-314, lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:1990-2002, lib/features/ride_complete/presentation/trip_detail.dart:28, driver_info.dart:40) keeps the padding computed for the first window size while the rest of the layout (ResSize.w, which is a getter) rescales. If the first read happens before ScreenUtilInit has run (any host that builds one of those widgets directly) the value is derived from ScreenUtil's uninitialised defaults for the rest of the process.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Desktop/web rider resizes the browser window from phone width to 1280 px: everything scaled through ResSize.w grows to the 1.25 bound, but the side gutters in Chat, Home's location card and Trip detail stay at the old 16 x (old scale) value, leaving misaligned edges.
confirmed.evidence: lib/shared/widgets/responsive_size.dart:3 `double screenHorizPadding = ScreenUtil().setWidth(16);` ; lib/app/screen_scale.dart:45-47 `// The root View provides this MediaQuery, so a window resize rebuilds // ScreenUtil with new bounds.` ; home.dart:1990 `left: screenHorizPadding,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make it a getter: `double get screenHorizPadding => ScreenUtil().setWidth(16);`.

verdicts.reason: responsive_size.dart:3 is a top-level variable with an initializer, so Dart evaluates it lazily once and caches it. MoveraScreenUtilInit (screen_scale.dart:44-53) re-inits ScreenUtil with new bounds on resize, so ResSize.setWidth changes while screenHorizPadding stays fixed. Consumers mix the two: home.dart:1990-2002 uses screenHorizPadding next to ResSize.h, and chat.dart, trip_detail.dart, driver_info.dart and others (18 uses) use it too. On mobile the orientation is locked (bootstrap.dart:69), so this is limited to resizing on web or desktop. The finding's second claim is wrong. Reading the variable before ScreenUtilInit throws a LateError, it does not compute and keep default values, and Dart re-runs a lazy initializer that threw on the next read. So the value does not stay at 'uninitialised defaults'.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_r96b_test.dart (deleted after): pumped MoveraScreenUtilInit at 375x812, then resized to 1280x812 and re-pumped. Output: 'w=375.0 global=16.0 res=16.0' / 'w=1280.0 global=16.0 res=20.0'. The global stays at 16 while ResSize gives 20. Calling ScreenUtil().setWidth(16) before init printed 'LateError'.
verdicts.corrected_title: screenHorizPadding is computed once (lazy top-level), so after a web/desktop window resize side gutters stay at the first scale (e.g. 16 px vs 20 px) while ResSize-scaled layout rescales

verdicts.reason: responsive_size.dart:3 is a top-level variable with an initializer. Dart initialises it lazily, once, on first read. ResSize.w (line 7) is a getter. MoveraScreenUtilInit (screen_scale.dart:44-53) rebuilds ScreenUtil with new bounds on a window resize, so screenHorizPadding keeps the first window's scale. Mobile is locked to portrait (bootstrap.dart:69), so this only happens when a web or desktop window is resized. That path is real, since there is a web build. The claim about reading it before ScreenUtilInit is speculative and not supported: an initializer that throws is re-run on the next read, so I dropped that part. The effect is a gutter that is off by a few pixels against layout that does rescale (16.64 vs 20 px).
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_r96c4b5_test.dart (deleted afterwards). It pumped MoveraScreenUtilInit at 390x844, read screenHorizPadding, resized to 1280x800 and pumped again. Output: `390: global=16.64 live=16.64 | 1280: global=16.64 live=20.0 scaleW=1.25`. Test passed: the global value stays at the first window's scale.
verdicts.corrected_title: screenHorizPadding is computed once from the first window size, so on web or desktop its gutters do not rescale after a window resize while ResSize-based layout does

confirmed.title: core -> features/di import guard only matches single-quoted package: imports, so a relative import from lib/core bypasses it (no current breach)
confirmed.description: The architecture guard extracts directives with `^\s*(?:import|export)\s+'([^']+)'` and then only flags URIs that start with `package:movera_rider/features/` or equal `package:movera_rider/app/di.dart`. A file under lib/core that writes `import '../../features/x/y.dart';`, `import "package:movera_rider/features/x/y.dart";`, or a `part`/deferred/conditional form reaches features without tripping the guard. Relative imports are already in use elsewhere in lib (e.g. lib/features/home/presentation/home_map_style.dart:1, lib/shared/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:12,14), so the style is not forbidden by lint. No current violation exists, so this is a gap in the gate, not a live breach.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A developer adds `import '../../features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart';` to a file in lib/core; `flutter test test/architecture/guard_test.dart` still passes and the documented 'core is feature-agnostic' rule in ARCHITECTURE.md is silently broken.
confirmed.evidence:
test/architecture/guard_test.dart:188-206:
```dart
    final directive = RegExp(
      r"^\s*(?:import|export)\s+'([^']+)'",
      multiLine: true,
    );
    ...
    for (final file in dartUnder('lib/core')) {
      for (final uri in importsOf(file.readAsStringSync())) {
        expect(
          uri.startsWith('package:movera_rider/features/') ||
              uri == 'package:movera_rider/app/di.dart',
          isFalse,
```
confirmed.suggested_fix: Match both quote styles (`['"]([^'"]+)['"]`), resolve relative URIs against the file's directory before checking, and also reject any resolved path under lib/features or lib/app/di.dart; optionally add `always_use_package_imports` to analysis_options to make relative imports impossible.

confirmed.title: lock_test idempotency-key tests are vacuous: failNext fails the quote POST, so only one ride POST is ever made and no keys are compared (coverage exists elsewhere)
confirmed.description: Both 'failed finding retry reuses the same logical booking key' (lines 105-126) and 'changed finding intent receives a new booking key' (lines 128-161) set `RecordingMockClient()..failNext = true` and expect the first `submitFinding` to throw. But `BookingCoordinator.submitFinding` first calls `_resolveQuoteBinding` (POST /api/v1/quotes) before posting /api/v1/rides, and `InProcessMockClient.failNext` returns 500 to the next request of any path. So the 500 hits the quote request; the rides endpoint is never reached on the failed attempt, and `RecordingMockClient.send` (which only records POST /api/v1/rides, lines 19-26) records nothing. The second submit records exactly one key. Both tests then assert `hasLength(1)` and `isNotNull`, which is satisfied regardless of whether the coordinator reuses, rotates, or never sends an idempotency key. Neither test compares a key across attempts, so the 'reuse' and 'new key' semantics are untested. Reproduced with a throwaway test (test/_audit_lock_vacuous_test.dart, since deleted) recording request paths: after the failed submit, `rideKeys` was empty and exactly one `POST /api/v1/quotes` had been made; the second submit produced one ride key; `flutter test` output: `00:00 +1: All tests passed!`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A regression that generates a fresh Idempotency-Key on every retry (so a network blip double-books a ride), or that drops the header entirely on retry, passes both tests unchanged, while the test names claim the opposite is guaranteed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the failure hit the rides endpoint (e.g. a mock that fails only `POST /api/v1/rides` once, or pre-fetch the quote and pass the quote binding), then assert `idempotencyKeys` has length 2 and `keys[0] == keys[1]` for the retry case and `keys[0] != keys[1]` for the changed-intent case.

confirmed.description: batch5-phase69-test-integrity.yml requires this file as one of the six 'real Rider journeys'. So for homeRideCount, ridesLeft, validUntilDays(days), driverTripCount, tripSharingStarted, safetyContactsCount, retrySeconds and resSeatsPayment(count), the test never checks that `{count}`/`{days}` survives in fr/sv. confirmed.title: 'duplicate payment key returns same intent family' asserts only the amount, so it cannot detect a second intent (or the wrong intent) being returned
confirmed.description: The test creates two intents with key 'dup' and asserts `second.amountMinor == 5000`. Any newly created intent for 5000 öre satisfies that, so idempotency is not tested. It also hides a defect in the mock: on a reused key MockPaymentGateway returns `_intents.values.last`, the most recently created intent of any key, not the one created for that key. ops_test 'top-up idempotency key reused' uses a single key too, so the mismatch is never seen.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Remove the idempotency check, so every call creates `pi_<new>`, and the test still passes. Or create key A (100 kr), then key B (200 kr), then retry A. The mock returns B's 200 kr intent, and no test notices.
confirmed.evidence:
test/wallet/gateway_test.dart:28-41  await gw.create(amountMinor: 5000, ..., idempotencyKey: 'dup'); final second = await gw.create(..., idempotencyKey: 'dup'); expect(second.amountMinor, 5000);
lib/core/payments/mock_payment_gateway.dart:21-23  if (_usedKeys.contains(idempotencyKey) && _intents.isNotEmpty) { return _intents.values.last; }
confirmed.suggested_fix: Assert `second.id == first.id`. Add a two-key case and key the mock's map by idempotency key.

verdicts.reason: The test at test/wallet/gateway_test.dart:28-41 checks only `second.amountMinor == 5000`, so it would still pass if idempotency were removed. The mock bug is real too. At lib/core/payments/mock_payment_gateway.dart:21-23, a reused key returns `_intents.values.last`, which is the most recent intent for any key. `_intents` is keyed by intent id, not by idempotency key (line 30). The app impact is very small. WalletController.topUp (lib/features/wallet/application/wallet_controller.dart:132-160) only reuses a key after a failed attempt. With the mock, `create` throws only through `failNext`, and that happens before the key is recorded (line 17-20). `confirm` always succeeds. So a retry of key A after key B is not reachable in the running app. This is a test-integrity gap plus a latent mock defect, not a user-facing bug.
verdicts.repro: Wrote and ran test/_audit_u242_test.dart (since deleted). It called create with key A at 10000, then B at 20000, then A at 10000 again. Output: `a=pi_cabec76a... b=pi_72febc1f... a2=pi_72febc1f... amt=20000`, so the retry of A returned B's 20000 intent. The test runner reported 'All tests passed!' because the test only printed the values. I also traced the only runtime caller, wallet_controller.dart:153.

verdicts.reason: The only check in test/wallet/gateway_test.dart:40 is `expect(second.amountMinor, 5000)`. It never compares `second.id` with the first intent's id, so a gateway with no idempotency at all, minting a fresh pi_ for 5000 on every call, would still pass. The mock defect behind it is real too. lib/core/payments/mock_payment_gateway.dart:21-22 returns `_intents.values.last` for any reused key. `_intents` is keyed by intent id (line 30), not by idempotency key, so retrying key A after key B was created returns B's intent. Mocks are intentional (ARCHITECTURE.md:12), but this is wrong mock behaviour, and the test is too weak to catch it. The mock is wired into the app in mock-transport builds (lib/app/di.dart:118-119) and used by WalletController.topUp (wallet_controller.dart:134-157). The top-up path removes a key on failure and retries with the same key, so this is reachable in dev/mock builds, though not in release.
verdicts.repro: I wrote and ran a throwaway test, test/_audit_u242_test.dart (since deleted). It called create with key A (10000), then key B (20000), then key A again. Output: `a=pi_9d138ca15cb50a9bc4ee5911 b=pi_2970f9dacb61791255cac116 a2=pi_2970f9dacb61791255cac116 a2amt=20000`, followed by `All tests passed!`. The retry with key A got B's intent and amount back. Reading the existing test shows that only amountMinor is checked, so removing the idempotency branch would not make it fail.
