verdicts.repro: Read the matrix test (lines 1-260) and the workflow steps (lines 30-45). Confirmed that the evidence files run in the same job's full-suite step.

refuted.title: After Retry on the 'can't track ride' screen, Ride check is never attached, the waiting terms are never loaded and the known stage is not seeded
refuted.description: initState attaches Ride check (attachTrip), starts the long-stop timer and loads the waiting terms only when a rideId exists at mount (265-277). When rideId is missing, _missingRideId is set. _retryTracking later starts tracking once a rideId is available, but it does not call attachTrip, _startRideCheckStillTimer or _loadWaitingTerms, and it omits initialStatus: _knownStatus(rideId). The ride then runs without the Ride check safety monitor and without the waiting fee counter. Until the first accepted event it shows the driverAssigned default even if the session knows the ride is in trip.
refuted.failure_scenario: Waiting mounts before the session's rideId is set, so 'We can't track this ride' is shown. The rider taps Retry and the live ride appears. Ride check never monitors the trip (no long-stop or off-route alerts), and no waiting fee counter appears when the driver arrives.
refuted.evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:362-371 `void _retryTracking() { ... setState(() => _missingRideId = false); _tracking.start( rideId: rideId, initial: widget.driver, onChange: _onLiveTick, ); }`
waiting_for_driver.dart:272-277 `RideCheckController.shared.attachTrip(...); _startRideCheckStillTimer(rideId.trim()); unawaited(_loadWaitingTerms());` (only in initState)
refuted.suggested_fix: Share one 'begin tracking' helper between initState and _retryTracking that does attachTrip, the still timer, _loadWaitingTerms and initialStatus.

verdicts.reason: _retryTracking only does anything if _rideId becomes non-null after Waiting mounted without one (waiting_for_driver.dart:362-364 returns early otherwise). No reachable path does that. Of the three constructors, the reservation one always passes rideId (reservation_live_ride.dart:76). Finding opens Waiting only after a match, when submitFinding has already set the session rideId (finding_drivers.dart:352, 538). The restore path seeds the session rideId from the snapshot before building Waiting (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:322-327). If snapshot.rideId is null, nothing sets it later. The only other writers of session rideId are backendReconcile (from a subscription, which never starts without an id) and reset (sets it to null). So the state where Retry starts tracking without the Ride check / waiting-terms setup cannot be reached. In practice Retry is a no-op.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of every WaitingForDriver construction (grep 'WaitingForDriver(') and every writer of RideSession.rideId (ride_session.dart:145, 207).

refuted.title: BookingCoordinator's unfinished attempt (key plus replay closure) survives sign-out and is replayed for the next rider
refuted.description: `AppScope.instance.booking` is a process singleton. `UserDataWipe.resetInMemory` resets the ride session, Finding, pickup, profile, wallet and others, but never the BookingCoordinator. After a booking that timed out or got a 5xx (`maybeCreated`), `_attempt` is deliberately kept with its idempotency key and a `replay` closure capturing the first request body: the quote id and signed payload, address strings, wallet amount and notes. `_autoQuoteBinding` is kept too. If a different rider signs in on the same device within `BookingAttempt.reuseWindow` (5 min) and books the same intent (same ~11 m pickup/destination cells, category, payment id such as 'cash', notes, wallet flag), `_attemptFor` returns the old attempt. `_prepareFinding` then calls `attempt.replay`, sending the previous rider's body under the previous rider's key with the new rider's token. The in-process mock scopes idempotency only by method+path+key (in_process_mock_client.dart:286-308). If the first request had been stored, it returns the previous rider's ride, and the new rider's session and snapshot adopt it.
refuted.failure_scenario: Rider A's Book-now request times out and the mock stored the created ride. A signs out within 5 minutes. Rider B signs in on the same tablet and books the same route with Cash. B's tap replays A's stored request, so B's Finding screen shows A's ride id with A's pickup label and quoted fare, and B's snapshot now holds A's ride. Not run; traced from the code.
refuted.evidence:
lib/features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart:34-37 `Future<String>? _inflight; BookingAttempt? _attempt; String? _autoQuoteIntent; _BookingQuoteBinding? _autoQuoteBinding;`
lib/features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart:69-76 failure keeps `_attempt` unless refused
lib/features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart:355-361 `final attempt = _attemptFor(intentKey); ... if (replay != null) { id = await _sendOrRecover(attempt, replay, ...`
lib/features/auth/application/user_data_wipe.dart:113-143 resetInMemory has no booking reset
refuted.suggested_fix: Add a `reset()` to BookingCoordinator that clears _attempt, _inflight and the auto-quote binding, and call it from UserDataWipe.resetInMemory.

verdicts.reason: It is true that UserDataWipe.resetInMemory (user_data_wipe.dart:113-143) never resets AppScope.instance.booking. The harmful replay, however, needs a timed-out or 5xx Book now whose in-call recovery (_sendOrRecover replay plus _adoptActiveTrip, booking_coordinator.dart:434-454) also failed. Then sign-out, sign-in by a different rider on the same device, and a booking of the identical intent (same ~11 m pickup and destination cells, category, payment id, notes, wallet flag) must all happen inside 5 minutes of the first tap (booking_attempt.dart:31-33). Even then the replayed body is essentially the second rider's own intent. The in-process mock is single-rider (rides map, userId 'rider-local'), so there is no second rider's data to leak in this build. A real server judges the replay with the new rider's token. The scenario is speculative, and a missing reset() is only hygiene.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of BookingCoordinator._attemptFor/_releaseWhenDone/_prepareFinding/_sendOrRecover, BookingAttempt.matches, UserDataWipe.resetInMemory, and in_process_mock_client.dart:267-308 (idempotency) and :597-610. No test run.

refuted.title: OfferWire.parse drops Offer.kind, expiresAt, driverEarnings and reasonCode: system Exclusive offers become Radar trips, the countdown ignores the server's expiry, and `wallet` shows as Card
refuted.description: The contract `Offer` carries `kind` (radar | exclusive | assigned | reservation | next_trip), `expiresAt`, `driverEarnings` and, for Exclusive offers, `reasonCode`. `OfferWire.parse` reads `kind` only to tell `reservation` (line 89) and `next_trip` (line 309) apart. RideOffer has no field for an Exclusive offer, and `isAdminDirectAssign` is just `source == admin && groupId == null`. So a dispatch Exclusive offer (`kind: exclusive, source: system`) becomes an ordinary Radar trip: no one-driver Accept/Decline flow, and no auto-offline count (Q16) for it. `expiresAt` is never read, so the card countdown uses the local `DriverOfferRules.radarTime` / `exclusiveAcceptTime` from when the card appears. An offer loaded late (from `GET /driver/offers` after a reconnect, or delivered late on the feed) shows a full timer while the server has already expired it. `driverEarnings` (required, includes driverBonus) is ignored; the net fare is later recomputed locally from a label. `_payments` has no `wallet` entry, so a wallet-paid offer shows 'Card'.
refuted.failure_scenario: Once ApiDispatchRepository is installed, dispatch sends this driver an Exclusive offer. It appears among Radar trips with a fresh 15 s timer, not as the Exclusive card. If the server's expiresAt was 5 s away, the driver taps Match after it lapsed and gets 'expired'. Missed Exclusive offers never count towards auto-offline.
refuted.evidence:
api_dispatch_repository.dart:14-19 `_payments = {'cash': 'Cash', 'card': 'Card', 'apple_pay': 'Apple Pay', 'google_pay': 'Google Pay'}`
:59-95 `return RideOffer(id: text('offerId'), tripId: text('tripId'), version: whole('version'), ... payment: _payments[json['paymentMethod']] ?? 'Card', reservationTime: json['kind'] == 'reservation' && at != null ? ... : null, ...)` (no kind/expiresAt/driverEarnings/reasonCode)
dispatch_repository.dart:185-186 `bool get isAdminDirectAssign => source == OfferSource.admin && groupId == null;`
refuted.suggested_fix: Carry `kind`, `expiresAt`, `driverEarnings` and `reasonCode` into RideOffer. Drive the Exclusive/Radar choice and the countdown from them. Map `wallet` to its own label.

verdicts.reason: The cited file is in the driver app (/home/user/Movera-driver-app/lib/core/dispatch/api_dispatch_repository.dart). The task names that app as cross-reference only, so this is not a defect in the rider app. It is also unreachable at runtime: `ApiDispatchRepository(` is constructed only at its own declaration (api_dispatch_repository.dart:137) and in test/round3/driver_admin_offers_dispatch_test.dart:55, never in the driver app's lib. The finding's own scenario starts with 'Once ApiDispatchRepository is installed'. No real caller reaches OfferWire.parse today, so no Exclusive offer, expiresAt or wallet value is ever parsed wrongly.
verdicts.repro: Searched the driver app's lib and test folders for `ApiDispatchRepository(`. The only hits are the class declaration and one test, with no use in the app's lib. Read OfferWire.parse at :13-95 and found it does drop kind, expiresAt and driverEarnings, but only on a path nothing installs.

refuted.title: 'compile-time release env parser' test exercises AppEnv.parseFlavor, which the app never uses; the real compile-time parser treats unknown or mis-cased flavors as demo
refuted.description: AppEnv.current derives the flavor with an exact-match ternary chain on the MOVERA_FLAVOR define. Anything else (e.g. 'Production', 'prod', ' production') silently becomes AppFlavor.demo: in-process mock API, mock payments, NoopPush, and a seeded demo wallet balance in bootstrap. parseFlavor (trim + lowercase) is referenced only by this test, so the test passes while the code path it claims to cover is untested and behaves differently. main.dart (the default `flutter build` target) has no flavor assertion, so a release built with `-t lib/main.dart --dart-define=MOVERA_FLAVOR=Production` ships as demo with every release guard skipped (allowsMockTransport is true for demo).
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator builds `flutter build apk --release --dart-define=MOVERA_FLAVOR=Production -t lib/main.dart`. The app starts as demo, with mock rides, a fake driver and a seeded wallet, and no composition guard fires. CI's 'compile-time release env parser' test stays green because it never touches AppEnv.current's parser. Worked by hand; nothing was run.
refuted.evidence:
lib/app/config/env.dart:32-41 flavor: _flavorName == 'production' ? AppFlavor.production : _flavorName == 'staging' ? ... : AppFlavor.demo,
lib/app/config/env.dart:59-64 static AppFlavor parseFlavor(String value) { ... flavor.name == value.trim().toLowerCase() ...
test/architecture/phase72_actual_release_composition_test.dart:17-25 test('compile-time release env parser distinguishes demo and production', () { expect(AppEnv.parseFlavor('demo'), ...
lib/main.dart:3-5 void main() { bootstrap(); }
refuted.suggested_fix: Build AppEnv.current's flavor from parseFlavor (or reject unknown values), make main.dart refuse a non-demo-looking but unknown define, and test the actual const path.

verdicts.reason: The test does call AppEnv.parseFlavor, which only that test uses (env.dart:59). But for the names CI actually passes ('demo', 'staging', 'production'), parseFlavor and AppEnv.current's exact-match chain (env.dart:32-42) give the same result. Both send unknown values to demo; parseFlavor's orElse also returns AppFlavor.demo. So the test hides no wrong behaviour on a real path. The failure scenario needs an operator to build a release with the plain dev entrypoint lib/main.dart and a mis-cased 'Production' define. Every release workflow uses -t lib/main_production.dart or lib/main_staging.dart with the exact lowercase name (.github/workflows/batch6-phase78-push.yml:99, batch6-phase80-payments.yml:109, batch7-phase85-final-certification.yml:92-100). main_production.dart:5-10 throws a StateError when AppEnv.current.flavor is not production, so a mis-cased define on the release entrypoint fails at startup instead of silently shipping as demo. At most the test name overstates what it covers. That is not a reachable defect.
verdicts.repro: Read env.dart, main.dart, main_production.dart and the phase72 test. Searched for parseFlavor (only the test uses it) and for MOVERA_FLAVOR in the workflows (all exact lowercase names, all on the flavor-guarded entrypoints). Static only.

refuted.title: Outbox flush replays a cancel queued during search against a trip a driver has since accepted, and rebases expectedVersion so the server cannot refuse it
refuted.description: RC-03 and the controller's own comments say a cancel queued during the search must never cancel a ride a driver accepted meanwhile. Line 381 says "never for a ride a driver already accepted", lines 948-950 say "the stale request leaves the outbox so it cannot cancel the matched ride later", and ARCHITECTURE says a driver-accepted race moves the rider on to Waiting. The flush (`_flushPendingCancels`) runs from the reconnect watcher, the bootstrap flush, the restore `_dropIfCancelQueued` flush and the Finding listener. It re-reads the trip first. `_rereadForReplay` accepts the cancel whenever `TripStateMachine.apply(status, 'cancel', rider)` is non-null, and the rider `cancel` transition is legal from accepted, driver_to_pickup and arrived (trip_transitions.dart:101). Then, when the version moved (a driver accepting bumps it), `cancel.forVersion(version)` mints a new key and sends the trip's current version. So the R-O2 version check, which would have answered 409 version_mismatch / stale, is defeated, and the server cancels the matched trip. The entry has no field saying it was queued while searching, so nothing else stops this.
refuted.failure_scenario: The rider taps Cancel request while offline, so the cancel is queued and the screen shows Cancelling…. A driver accepts on the server. Connectivity returns: the reconnect watcher's flush GETs the trip (accepted), rebases the version and POSTs the cancel, and the server cancels the accepted trip (possibly with a late-cancel fee and a driver penalty). Meanwhile Finding may already have received the match, shown "A driver already accepted your ride" and opened Waiting, which then dies as cancelled. After a reload (cold restore) the rider lands on Home with the ride archived as cancelled, although the documented outcome is that the match wins.
refuted.suggested_fix: Record on the entry the stage it was queued at (or keep the original expectedVersion). For a Finding cancel, treat any re-read outside requested/searching/offered as stale (report it so `_completeAssigned` / onCancelRefused runs), and do not rebase the version across a status change.

verdicts.reason: Replaying a queued cancel against a trip a driver has since accepted, with the version rebased, is an explicit owner decision (R-O2), not an oversight. test/ride/f1_end_early_version_test.dart:41-49 records the owner decisions ('an outbox replay reads the trip first and is neither refused spuriously nor sent when it no longer applies'). Its test 're-read first; still cancellable at a newer version: sent with it' (740-756) enqueues a cancel, then has `simulate(id, {'status': 'accepted'})` with the comment 'Meanwhile a driver accepted (the version moved on)', and expects results[id]==sent and server status cancelled_by_rider. The test at 758-781 checks the rebased expectedVersion and the new key. The code comment at finding_driver_controller.dart:1473-1475 states the same intent. The rider's command is legal from accepted (trip_transitions.dart:101), and the rider tapped Cancel and saw 'Cancelling…', so the server ending up cancelled is what they asked for. RC-03's 'match wins' (947-953, tested in rc_cancel_outbox_test.dart:291-306) covers the other order, when the app sees the match before any replay, and removes the entry. One residual inconsistency is left (not what this finding claims): if the realtime match lands after a flush has already read the entry but before its POST, Finding can show 'driver already accepted' and open Waiting just before the cancel lands. That is a narrow race whose result is still what the rider asked for.
verdicts.repro: Read the owner-decision header and the R-O2 'outbox replay after offline' group in test/ride/f1_end_early_version_test.dart:41-49,739-781, plus the RC-03 tests in test/ride/rc_cancel_outbox_test.dart:291-306. Traced _flushPendingCancels/_rereadForReplay (finding_driver_controller.dart:1454-1580). No new test needed, because the existing test asserts the reported behaviour as intended.

refuted.title: If the recorder's stop throws a platform error, the recording stays marked 'active' and the Ride check card raises an unhandled error
refuted.description: SafetyAudioService.stop() clears `_active` only after `_recorder.stop()` returns. NativeSafetyRecorder.stop can throw a PlatformException from the record plugin, or a FileSystemException from exists() or length(). In that case `_active` stays set, so isRecording stays true, the card keeps showing the running clock, and every later Start fails with ALREADY_RECORDING. RideCheckController.toggleRecording catches only SafetyAudioException on the stop branch, so the error escapes the InkWell callback as an unhandled async error and no note is shown. The Safety Kit has a generic catch; the card does not.
refuted.failure_scenario: On Android the recorder's stop throws, for example because the microphone was taken by another app. Tapping 'tap to stop' on the card throws an uncaught error, the card still shows 'Recording 1:23', and the rider cannot stop or restart recording from the card.
refuted.suggested_fix: Wrap `_recorder.stop()` in try/finally so `_active` is cleared (and cancel() is attempted), map other errors to SafetyAudioException, and add a generic catch on the stop branch of toggleRecording.

verdicts.reason: The failure needs the native recorder's stop to throw, and nothing in the code shows that happening on a normal path. NativeSafetyRecorder.stop (lib/features/safety/application/safety_recorder_native.dart:37-43) only calls record's AudioRecorder.stop and File.exists/length on a path it just wrote. The 'microphone taken by another app' trigger is a guess with no evidence that the plugin throws there. Web builds use the stub recorder (safety_recorder.dart conditional export), so the public demo cannot reach this. Even if stop did throw, the error is not unhandled: bootstrap.dart:102-105 sets PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError to log it and return true, and runApp runs inside runZonedGuarded (bootstrap.dart:134). So nothing crashes. The only real gap is that _active is not cleared in a finally block (safety_audio_service.dart:87-88), which is hardening rather than a reachable bug.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: ride_check_card.dart:1022 onTap -> RideCheckController.toggleRecording (ride_check_controller.dart:582-595) -> SafetyAudioService.stop (safety_audio_service.dart:76-88) -> NativeSafetyRecorder.stop. Checked the conditional platform export in safety_recorder.dart and the global error handlers in lib/app/bootstrap.dart:102 and :134. Not run, because the plugin failure cannot be triggered in a unit test.

refuted.title: Confirm pickup spot's address search and 'Use current location' land without checking whether the rider moved the pin meanwhile
refuted.description: _lookup awaits _pickup.search(query) (a network forward geocode) and then unconditionally sets _center, _address and animates the camera to the result. A pin the rider dragged in the meantime is yanked back. This is the same defect already reported for SetPickupPage._searchAddress, but in a different screen. _useCurrentLocation, after the camera move, awaits reverse(position) and writes the GPS street into _address without the _isAwayFrom(position) check that _refreshCurrentFix uses (line 175), so a pin dragged during the lookup gets the GPS street as its label.
refuted.failure_scenario: First case: the rider searches 'Odenplan', the lookup is slow, and they drag the map to a corner they can see instead. The result arrives, the map jumps back to Odenplan, and the rider's own spot is lost. Second case: the rider taps 'Use current location' and immediately nudges the pin across the road. The late reverse result labels the nudged pin with the GPS street.
refuted.suggested_fix: Record a generation or the pin position before each await, and drop the result when the pin has moved (_isAwayFrom), as _refreshCurrentFix already does.

verdicts.reason: The 'Use current location' case is guarded. PickupMapController.reverse uses a StaleGuard (pickup_controller.dart:53-62): when the rider nudges the pin, onCameraIdle -> _idle starts a newer reverse(), and the older lookup from _useCurrentLocation returns null. The null is then rejected by isUnusablePickupLabel at confirm_pickup_spot.dart:276, so the GPS street cannot label the nudged pin. In the search case, _lookup (283-293) moves the pin to the result the rider explicitly asked for. It sets _center and _address together, and the following animateCamera triggers onCameraMove and onCameraIdle, which re-reverse-geocodes, so position and label stay consistent. Landing on the searched place after the rider submitted that search is expected behaviour, not a race that corrupts state.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of confirm_pickup_spot.dart:223-293 and 338-349 (onCameraMove/onCameraIdle) and pickup_controller.dart:50-73 (StaleGuard in reverse).

refuted.title: Confirm pickup spot redraws a Flutter overlay above the map on every camera-move frame during a pinch, the pattern Set pickup removed after it crashed iPhone Safari
refuted.description: onCameraMove writes `_zoom.value = position.zoom` on every camera frame. During a pinch or wheel zoom (fractional zoom is on through rider_map_camera.js), the value changes every frame. The ValueListenableBuilder (line 354) then rebuilds and repaints the semi-transparent accuracy ring, sized from the zoom, that sits over the platform map. Set pickup documents that this exact pattern, a Flutter animation over a moving web map, "re-renders every canvas on each frame, and iPhone Safari ran out of graphics memory doing that and reloaded" (set_pickup_page.dart:466-471). That page was changed so nothing animates while the map slides. Confirm pickup spot, reached from Home's pickup prefill and from route change's 'pick on map', still does it.
refuted.failure_scenario: On iPhone Safari a rider opens Confirm pickup spot (or Confirm destination from Change route) and pinch-zooms the map. Every frame of the pinch repaints the overlay ring above the moving map, so Flutter's overlay canvas is re-rendered over the WebGL map each frame. This is the GPU-memory pressure the codebase blames for a Safari reload on Set pickup, so a reload or heavy jank is possible on lower-memory iPhones. Not run; based on the code and the in-repo incident note.
refuted.evidence:
confirm_pickup_spot.dart:339-344 `onCameraMove: (position) { _moving = true; _center = position.target; // D-011: the radius overlay follows zoom live ... _zoom.value = position.zoom; },`
confirm_pickup_spot.dart:354-363 `child: ValueListenableBuilder<double>(valueListenable: _zoom, builder: (context, zoom, _) { final radius = ConfirmPickupSpot.metersToPixels(...); return Container(key: const ValueKey('pickup-accuracy-overlay'), ...`
set_pickup_page.dart:468-471 `// ... the lift never runs while the map itself is sliding: animating over a moving map re-renders every canvas on each frame, and iPhone Safari ran out of graphics memory doing that and reloaded.`
refuted.suggested_fix: On web, update the ring only on onCameraIdle, or hide it while the camera moves. Another option is to draw it as a google_maps Circle, which the map renders itself.

verdicts.reason: The live zoom-following ring is intentional (D-011 comment at confirm_pickup_spot.dart:341-342). _zoom is a ValueNotifier, so the ring rebuilds only while the zoom value itself changes, never during a plain pan. The Set pickup incident note (set_pickup_page.dart:466-471) is about a lift animation running across a whole map slide, and that page still animates the pin over the web map on finger-down (_onMapFingerDown -> _lift.forward()). So 'the same pattern that crashed Safari' is an analogy, not a reproduced or traced failure. The finding says it was not run, and nothing in the repo ties a short pinch-zoom ring repaint to a reload.
verdicts.repro: Read onCameraMove/ValueListenableBuilder in confirm_pickup_spot.dart:338-375 and the set_pickup_page.dart lift code at 455-480. Not reproducible without an iPhone Safari device; speculative.

refuted.title: Picker's initial hydrate has no error handling: failures become unhandled async errors and saved Home/Work show 'Not saved yet'
refuted.description: `_places.hydrate().then(...)` has no catchError, so a storage read failure is an unhandled Future error. The Saved Places screen catches the same failure explicitly (FLOW-15). The chips then show the 'Not saved yet' fallback even when Home or Work exist. Because this picker is only opened from AddPlace with `allowCreateShortcut: false`, tapping those chips does nothing, with no error shown.
refuted.failure_scenario: Storage is blocked (Safari private mode or cleared site data), so PreferencesStore.load throws. Open Add place › location: an uncaught async error is logged, and Home/Work read 'Not saved yet' and do nothing when tapped.
refuted.suggested_fix: Catch the error, log it, and show the load-failed state (or hide the chips).

verdicts.reason: The failure cannot be reached. The picker opens only from AddPlace (add_place.dart:65). AddPlace opens only from SavedPlaces._openEditor, whose add and edit rows appear only when SavedPlaces' own hydrate succeeded: when _loadError is set, saved_places.dart:150-158 shows just the error and a retry button. A successful hydrate means SharedPreferences.getInstance() (preferences_store.dart:10) has already resolved, and it caches that instance, so the picker's later _store.load() cannot fail on storage. Even if it did, hydrate throws at saved_places_controller.dart:40, before the clear() at line 41, so the shared controller keeps the Home/Work values it already had. The chips would not fall back to 'Not saved yet'.
verdicts.repro: Traced picker caller add_place.dart:62-70 -> AddPlace callers saved_places.dart:61 (_openEditor, reachable only from rows in the non-error branch at :159-181) and pickup_location.dart:345 (inside the picker itself); traced hydrate (saved_places_controller.dart:39-44) -> HomeAddressRepository.load (home_repository.dart:26-27) -> PreferencesStore.load (preferences_store.dart:9-10).

refuted.title: save() reports failure after the place was already written, so a retry adds a duplicate custom place
refuted.description: `save` awaits `_store.save(...)` and then `hydrate()`. If the re-read throws after a successful write, the exception reaches AddPlace, which shows spSaveFailed and re-enables Save. A new custom place has no id (`widget.initial?.id` is null), so the retry generates another `place_<id>` and stores a second copy. The rider was told the first save failed.
refuted.failure_scenario: Storage write succeeds, the following read fails (for example quota or eviction on web). The rider sees 'Could not save', taps Save again, and Saved Places now lists the place twice.
refuted.suggested_fix: Return the saved place even if the refresh fails (catch and log hydrate errors separately), or keep the generated id in AddPlace state so a retry updates the same entry.

verdicts.reason: For this to happen, hydrate() (saved_places_controller.dart:39-44) would have to throw right after _store.save succeeded (:105-113). HomeAddressRepository.load (home_repository.dart:26-54) calls PreferencesStore.load(), which returns the cached SharedPreferences.getInstance() (preferences_store.dart:9-11). The reads are synchronous getters on an in-memory map that save() has just written, and the JSON decode is inside try/catch (home_repository.dart:31-46). A read that fails right after a successful write on the same cached instance is not a realistic path. Any type mismatch on getStringList would already have thrown in the load() at saved_places_controller.dart:63, before the write.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of save -> _store.save -> hydrate -> HomeAddressRepository.load -> PreferencesStore/SharedPreferences cached instance.

refuted.title: signOutOtherDevices ignores the session counter that load() uses, so a result for a signed-out rider can be written after clearLocal
refuted.description: clearLocal says 'A load still in flight for that rider is ignored when it lands' and bumps `_session`. load() checks it, but signOutOtherDevices does not: it assigns `state = await _repository.signOutOtherDevices()` and clears `loading` unconditionally. If sign-out (UserDataWipe → accountSecurity.clearLocal) happens while this request is in flight, the previous rider's security state (phone, email, sessions) can be stored again. Account and Personal info then show it to the next rider, because they only reload when state == null.
refuted.failure_scenario: A rider taps 'Sign out other devices' on a slow network, then signs out from the menu before the request finishes. The response lands after the wipe, and the next rider to sign in opens Account and sees the previous rider's phone number and email.
refuted.suggested_fix: Capture `_session` before the await and drop the result if it has changed, as load() does.

verdicts.reason: The missing session check is real code (account_security_controller.dart:63-70 writes `state` without comparing `_session`), but no current build can reach it. signOutOtherDevices returns early unless capabilities.signOutOtherDevices, capabilities.reauthentication and hasFreshReauthentication are all true (:51-58). The only backend is the mock, which serves both capabilities as false and `reauthenticatedAt: null` (in_process_mock_client.dart:143-152). The app has no reauthentication flow that could set reauthenticatedAt: the only grep hits for reauth in lib are capability checks and the 'reauthBeforeRevoke' label in security.dart:208-216. The Security screen's button is disabled under the same conditions (security.dart:214-216). This only becomes live once a real server turns on these capabilities with a reauth flow, so it is a latent hardening item, not a reachable bug.
verdicts.repro: Static. Traced the guard in the controller, the UI onTap condition, the mock's account security document and sign-out-others handler, and grepped lib for reauth writers.

refuted.title: Driver-drop tests replace the parked Finding route with a Text widget and then assert 'nothing archived, nothing wiped', so the parked Finding listener is never exercised
refuted.description: In the app, WaitingForDriver sits on top of a parked FindingDrivers route whose FindingDriverController listener is still subscribed. The listener has no `_assigned` guard, and `cancelledByDriver.isTerminal` is true, so it goes to `_completeTerminal`, which archives and clears. The driver-drop tests use `home: Text('audit-root')` or `Text('finding-parent')` as the parent. The code comment admits it: 'in the production stack that parent is the already parked Finding route'. They then assert `OnDemandRideHistoryStore.read()` is empty and that the ride is still findingDriver. The journey driver_cancel_research_test.dart, one of the six required Phase 69 journeys, does the same. The one test that does park a real Finding (finding_driver/audit_fix_research_route_test.dart) asserts only route and price, never History, the snapshot or the server status. The 'nothing archived, nothing wiped' guarantee is therefore never tested in the real stack.
refuted.failure_scenario: The known finding at finding_driver_controller.dart:394 (a parked Finding archives the drop as cancelled and clears the snapshot) is exactly what these tests would need to catch. With the real parent, the driver drop leaves a 'cancelled' History row and no snapshot, so a reload lands on Home. These tests stay green because the listener that does this is not in the tree.
refuted.suggested_fix: Push FindingDrivers first, let it match into WaitingForDriver (as audit_fix_research_route_test does), emit cancelledByDriver, and assert that History is empty, `RideSnapshotStore.read()?.status` is searching, and the session status is findingDriver.

verdicts.reason: The finding assumes a parked Finding route still has a live FindingDriverController listener underneath WaitingForDriver. It does not. FindingDrivers._openWaiting calls `_match.dispose()` before it pushes WaitingForDriver (lib/features/finding_driver/presentation/finding_drivers.dart:528, with the comment 'Freeze and detach'). dispose() sets `_disposed = true` and cancels `_sub` (finding_driver_controller.dart:1674-1682). Two further guards would stop any event that still arrived: the realtime listener returns first on `_disposed` (line 362), and `_completeTerminal` returns on `_disposed` (line 1010). So while Waiting is on screen, no parked Finding listener can archive a cancelledByDriver or clear the snapshot. A plain Text widget as the parent is therefore a faithful stand-in for what the parked route does during the driver drop. After Waiting pops `true`, Finding resumes through `_resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel` (finding_drivers.dart:556), and the real-stack test audit_fix_research_route_test.dart covers that path. The premise, 'the listener that does this is not in the tree', describes production too, so the claimed hidden failure (a 'cancelled' History row and a wiped snapshot) cannot happen this way. At most a reader could ask for a History assertion in the real-stack test as extra coverage. That is not a test-integrity defect.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only, no test run. Traced _openWaiting (finding_drivers.dart:521-556) to _match.dispose(), then FindingDriverController.dispose (finding_driver_controller.dart:1674-1686), the listener guard at line 362 and the _completeTerminal guard at line 1010. Read test/ride/waiting_external_terminal_test.dart:113-180 and test/finding_driver/audit_fix_research_route_test.dart in full.

refuted.title: The browser responsive job's RenderFlex/assertion console patterns are dead in a --release build, but the same gate's widget overflow matrix covers overflow
refuted.description: The responsive-browser job builds `flutter build web --release -t lib/main_demo.dart`. It then fails a viewport only if a console error matches `/RenderFlex overflowed|A RenderFlex|...|Another exception|Assertion failed/`, or if `document.documentElement.scrollWidth > innerWidth`. Flutter reports layout overflow (RenderFlex._debugReportOverflow and the overflow indicator) and assertion failures only inside `assert(...)`, and asserts are compiled out of release builds. The Flutter view is also sized to the viewport, so a widget overflowing inside the canvas never makes the document wider. Neither check can see a clipped layout. qa-device-pwa-responsive.yml:59 uses the same pattern against the live release Pages build.
refuted.failure_scenario: A French label or the Select Ride sheet overflows by 40 px at 320x568. In release the text is clipped with no console output, docWidth stays at 320, and 'Local Chromium + WebKit responsive matrix' passes. The final-candidate gate then reports the build as certified.
refuted.suggested_fix: Run the overflow matrix on a debug or profile build (for example `flutter build web --profile`, or `flutter run -d web-server` in debug), or rely on the widget-test overflow matrix. Keep the release check only for crashes.

verdicts.corrected_title: The browser responsive job's RenderFlex/assertion console patterns are dead in a --release build, but the same gate's widget overflow matrix covers overflow
verdicts.reason: The job builds with `flutter build web --release` (batch7-phase85-final-certification.yml:127-129). Layout-overflow reports and assertion messages come from debug-only asserts, so the fatalPattern alternatives at :192-193 ('RenderFlex overflowed', 'A RenderFlex', 'Assertion failed') can never match. The docWidth check (:255-259) cannot see clipping inside the Flutter view, which is sized to the viewport. qa-device-pwa-responsive.yml uses the same pattern against the release Pages build. The stated consequence (an overflowing build gets certified) is largely mitigated: the same certification workflow runs the full `flutter test` suite (:43-44), which includes test/responsive/frontend_responsive_matrix_test.dart and test/responsive/audit_fix_viewport_text_matrix_test.dart at Size(320, 568), with SelectRide among the screens. What is left is a misleading CI check that adds no overflow coverage in real browsers and fonts.
verdicts.repro: Read the workflow build step, fatalPattern and docWidth check, then grepped the same workflow for test steps and the responsive widget matrices for 320x568 and SelectRide coverage.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism is correct: the browser job builds --release (batch7-phase85-final-certification.yml:127-129). RenderFlex overflow reports and assertions are debug-only, so the RenderFlex and Assertion parts of fatalPattern (:192-193) never fire, and docWidth cannot grow from canvas-internal overflow. The stated consequence is refuted, though. The same certification workflow runs the full widget suite (`flutter test`, :43-44), and the final gate requires every job (:358-367). That suite runs in debug, where overflow fails the test, and it includes test/l10n/l10n_screens_test.dart:151-167, which pumps screens in fr and sv at 320x568 with 1.3x text, plus test/responsive/frontend_responsive_matrix_test.dart:67,115 at 320x568. So 'a French label overflowing at 320x568 still gets certified' is stopped by that guard. What remains is a dead regex branch in a job whose real purpose (crashes, pageerror, Maps runtime) still works: cosmetic at most.

The fr 320x568 overflow scenario falls in the debug widget suite that the same final gate runs. No run was needed.

verdicts.reason:
The mechanism is real, but the harm the finding claims does not happen. The responsive-browser job builds `flutter build web --release` (.github/workflows/batch7-phase85-final-certification.yml:127-129). In Flutter 3.47.6, RenderFlex reports overflow and paints the overflow indicator only inside `assert(() {...}())` (/opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/flex.dart, paint, ~1400-1456), so the 'RenderFlex overflowed', 'A RenderFlex' and 'Assertion failed' parts of fatalPattern (:192-193) can never match in that build. docWidth (:256-261) also cannot see clipping inside the canvas.

The failure scenario is that a French label or the SelectRide sheet overflows at 320x568 and the build still gets certified. That is blocked:
- The final-candidate gate requires every job, including analyzer-and-unit (:360-376, `test "$UNIT" = success`).
- That job runs the full debug `flutter test` suite (:43-44). There is no dart_test.yaml, and the overflow tests have no tags or skips.
- test/l10n/l10n_screens_test.dart:151-195 pumps SelectRide (defined at :76-83) and the other booking screens in fr and sv at Size(320, 568) with 1.3x text. It fails on any FlutterError collected by collectFlutterErrors (test/responsive/responsive_harness.dart:50-58).
- test/responsive/audit_fix_viewport_text_matrix_test.dart:65,118-170 covers SelectRide at 320x568 with 1.0, 1.3 and 2.0 text.

A throwaway run confirmed the harness catches exactly the scenario described. What is left is dead regex branches in a job whose real checks (pageerror, crash text, Maps runtime, Flutter surface) still work. That changes no behaviour, so it is cosmetic. No decision document covers it either way.
verdicts.repro: I wrote /home/user/movera-rider-app/test/_audit_rider_u1_decider_test.dart. It uses pumpMoveraScreen and collectFlutterErrors from test/responsive/responsive_harness.dart to pump a Scaffold whose Row holds a 360px-wide SizedBox with the text 'Choisissez votre course', at viewport 320x568, textScale 1.3, locale fr. It asserts that errors is not empty. Run with `PATH=/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH flutter test test/_audit_rider_u1_decider_test.dart`. Output: "AUDIT thrown=null errors=[A RenderFlex overflowed by 40 pixels on the right. at Row ...]" then "00:00 +1: All tests passed!". The file was deleted afterwards. So the debug widget suite, which the same final gate requires, catches a 40px overflow at 320x568. refuted.title: Push consent ('movera.push_consent.v1') survives sign-out and account switch, so the next rider is registered for push without seeing the in-app explanation
refuted.description: UserDataWipe removes only keys starting with 'movera_' (except deviceKeys). PushPermissionGate stores consent under 'movera.push_consent.v1' (a dot, not an underscore), so it is never removed, and it is not listed among the documented kept keys either. After rider A accepted the primer and signs out, rider B's sign-in calls registerIfConsented, finds 'accepted' and registers B's device token straight away. The OS permission is already granted, so B sees no prompt. B never saw or accepted the explanation, although UI-17 says registration is only for 'a rider who accepted the in-app explanation'.
refuted.failure_scenario: On a shared phone, rider A turns on ride updates and signs out. Rider B signs in and starts getting ride push notifications without ever being asked.
refuted.suggested_fix: Either clear the consent key in UserDataWipe or list it explicitly in deviceKeys with the decision documented.

verdicts.reason: The consent gate exists to keep the OS notification prompt behind an in-app explanation. Its class doc says so: push_permission_gate.dart:23-29, 'Keeps the OS notification prompt behind an in-app explanation ... never shows the OS prompt to a rider who has not accepted the explanation'. OS notification permission is device-level and has already been granted in this scenario, so rider B would never see a cold OS prompt either way. registerIfConsented (push_permission_gate.dart:69-77) then registers B's own session, so B gets B's own ride updates (auth_controller.dart:74-84). No data about another rider is exposed. Keeping the key behaves like the documented device-level keys. The key is missing from the deviceKeys doc comment, but that is a documentation gap, not wrong behaviour.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of PushPermissionGate.consent/registerIfConsented/accept and AuthController._registerPushBestEffort/signOut. signOut also unregisters and deletes A's FCM token (auth_controller.dart:95; firebase_push_service.dart unregister -> _gateway.deleteToken), so B registers a fresh token under B's session.

refuted.title: Web notification tap opens the app root and drops the ride id; firebase_messaging_web never emits opened/initial messages
refuted.description: The push handler stores payload.data (rideId, type, deepLink) on the notification. notificationclick ignores event.notification.data and opens or focuses './'. On web, firebase_messaging_web.getInitialMessage() always returns null and onMessageOpenedApp is never fed. So PushCoordinator's openRide/openNotifications routing (PushDestination.ride) can never run on web. On web, tapping a ride notification just lands on whatever the cold start restores, never on the notification's ride or on the Notifications screen.
refuted.failure_scenario: Web rider with the tab hidden gets a 'trip.completed' or 'ride.driver_assigned' notification for a ride and taps it. The SW focuses the tab, and the data is discarded. The app does not navigate to the ride or to Notifications, unlike Android/iOS, where onMessageOpenedApp routes it. Verified by reading the code.
refuted.suggested_fix: In notificationclick, encode the ride id or deep link into the opened URL, or postMessage it to the focused client, and handle it in Dart on web.

verdicts.reason: The worker's documented design (web/firebase-messaging-sw.js:8-11) is that it 'only shows background notifications and opens the app when one is tapped. Ride state stays authoritative from the backend and is reconciled when the app opens.' Focusing or opening the app root is that intended behaviour. The missing opened/initial routing is a firebase_messaging_web plugin limitation (getInitialMessage returns null at firebase_messaging_web.dart:93, and the plugin never feeds onMessageOpenedApp), not an app defect. A tapped ride notification still lands in an app that restores the live ride. At most this is a web-parity enhancement.
verdicts.repro: Read web/firebase-messaging-sw.js header and notificationclick (:89-100), and grepped firebase_messaging_web-4.2.5/lib: there is no onMessageOpenedApp feed, and getInitialMessage returns null.

refuted.title: Price-bump card rounds a SEK fare with öre to whole kronor, so its preview total and ceiling disagree with what the controller and server apply
refuted.description: For SEK the card computes from `major.round() * 100` for both the current fare and maxPrice. The controller adds the increase to the exact fare (`snapshot.fare.amountMinor + increase`) and checks it against the exact `maxOfferMinor`. SEK fares with öre happen when the demo promotion's percentage discount is applied in the quote (`(fullMinor * percentOff / 100).round()`). So the button preview ("Raise to 240 kr") is not the fare charged, and a typed total the card accepts as within the ceiling is refused locally by `confirmPriceIncreaseBy` with "couldn't update your offer".
refuted.failure_scenario: With a promo the fare is 133.45 kr and maxOfferMinor is 24000 (240 kr). The rider types 240. The card enables "Raise to 240 kr" and sends +107 kr. The controller computes 240.45 kr > 240 and returns false, and the rider is told the raise failed.
refuted.evidence:
price_bump_card.dart:88-90 `int _minorOf(double major) => _kronor ? major.round() * _unitMinor : Money.fromLegacyMajor(major, widget.currency).amountMinor;`
price_bump_card.dart:117-118 `final extra = total * _unitMinor - _currentMinor; if (extra <= 0 || total * _unitMinor > _minorOf(widget.maxPrice)) {`
finding_driver_controller.dart:790-796 `final next = Money(snapshot.fare.amountMinor + increase.amountMinor, currency).major; if (next > maxOfferPrice || ...) return false;`
refuted.suggested_fix: Compute the card's increase from the exact fare minor units (or send the target total and let the server price it), and compare against the exact maxOfferMinor.

verdicts.reason: The failure needs a SEK fare with öre, and no reachable path produces one. SEK uses stepMinor 100 (mock_catalog_fares.dart:84-88), so every quote is whole kronor (quote() at :157-161, with a 60% list-price floor). The demo promotion applies only to comfort, priority and premium (in_process_mock_client.dart:115), whose list prices are 339, 289 and 369 kr (mock_catalog_fares.dart:6-14). Their lowest fares (203, 173 and 221 kr) are all above 166.67 kr, so 30% off is always more than the 5000 öre cap. The clamp at in_process_mock_client.dart:2152-2157 then caps the discount at a whole 50 kr, which makes the booked fare (booking_coordinator.dart:190-192, quote.totalMinor) whole kronor. maxOfferMinor is also whole units (_maxOfferMinorFor at :1874-1877). In that case the card's major.round()*100 equals the exact fare, and the card agrees with the controller (finding_driver_controller.dart:790-795). Counting from whole kronor is also documented as intended at price_bump_card.dart:86-87. A 133.45 kr fare cannot occur in the app as built, and the real server's pricing is a PROPOSED contract.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: quote() rounding, the promo clamp and cap, the eligible ride types and their list-price floors, the booking fare source, and the ceiling formula. Discount = min(0.3*full, 50 kr), and 0.3*full is above 50 kr for every eligible fare, so the result is always whole kronor.

refuted.title: After a sign-out wipe the profile language resets to 'en' while the device language choice is kept, so the next profile PATCH reports English
refuted.description: language_picker says 'the profile keeps the same code for the server'. UserDataWipe keeps `movera_app_language` (a device key), so AppLanguageController still speaks the rider's chosen language. It resets the profile to defaults(), whose language is 'en'. The next profile save (for example the new-rider name step) sends language 'en' although the rider explicitly chose Swedish on this device and is using the app in Swedish.
refuted.failure_scenario: The rider picked Svenska in Account and signs out. A new rider signs in on the same device, the UI is still Swedish, and they enter their name. PATCH {language: 'en'}, so the backend and driver treat the rider as English-speaking.
refuted.evidence:
app_language_controller.dart:65-73 choose() saves to the device store only; language_picker.dart:29 the profile is updated only inside the picker
user_data_wipe.dart:67-71 'movera_app_language' is kept; :127 `scope.profile.clearLocal();`
profile.dart:196 `language: defaultLanguage,` ('en')
refuted.suggested_fix: When the profile is hydrated or reset, seed profile.language from AppLanguageController.choice when there is one.

verdicts.reason: The profile language is documented to be English until the rider picks a language in the profile language picker. profile.dart:173-175 says: "English until the rider picks a language", defaultLanguage = 'en'. Only pickAppLanguage writes it (language_picker.dart:26-30). movera_app_language is deliberately a device key (user_data_wipe.dart:67-71, owner Q48), so after a wipe the device language belongs to the device and to the previous rider, not to the new rider. The new rider in the scenario never chose Swedish, so sending 'en' is the documented default. The wipe also causes nothing: a fresh install in Stockholm shows Swedish by zone default and sends 'en' in the same way.
verdicts.repro: Traced AppLanguageController.choose (device store only), language_picker (the only writer of profile.language), UserDataWipe deviceKeys, profile.dart defaultLanguage and its comment, and the SyncedProfileRepository body.

refuted.title: POST /quotes and POST /payments/{id}/confirm go out without the Idempotency-Key that contracts/openapi.yaml requires. The mock never enforces the key.
refuted.description: openapi `components/parameters/IdempotencyKey` is `required: true` ('Required on every mutation') on `POST /quotes`, `POST /trips/{id}/route-quote` and `POST /payments/{id}/confirm`. The rider sends these without a key. ApiQuoteRepository posts `/api/v1/quotes` with no `idempotencyKey` (api_quote_repository.dart:29). RouteChangeController posts `/api/v1/rides/$id/route-quote` with none (route_change_controller.dart:200). ApiPaymentGateway.confirm posts `/api/v1/payments/$id/confirm` with none (api_payment_gateway.dart:85). The stand-in server never notices, because a request without a key just skips the replay table (`replayKey = key == null || key.isEmpty ? null : ...`). The rider app was never checked against the requirement. A contract server rejects these requests. Even a lenient one cannot de-duplicate a confirm that is retried after a lost response.
refuted.failure_scenario: On a backend that enforces the contract header, Select Ride gets no prices (quote request refused) and the in-trip destination change cannot be priced. A card confirm that is retried after a timeout has no key the server can use to recognise the repeat.
refuted.evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:286 `final replayKey = key == null || key.isEmpty ? null : '$method $path $key';`
api_quote_repository.dart:29 `final json = await api.post('/api/v1/quotes', body: {...});` (no idempotencyKey)
route_change_controller.dart:199-202 `() => _api.post('/api/v1/rides/$id/route-quote', body: {...draft.toRequest(), 'expectedVersion': ?version}),`

verdicts.reason:
The readers match the contract this app documents for these routes, and the failure in the finding cannot be reached.

1. The readers follow the documented shape. docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:101-104 defines both trip read models as PROPOSED (C-5): `GET /api/v1/rider/trips/active → {trip}` or `{trip: null}`, and `GET /api/v1/rider/trips?cursor= → {trips: [...], nextCursor}`. ARCHITECTURE.md:70-72 says release History and the active trip "use the proposed server routes in docs/API_V1_MOCK.md". docs/DECISIONS.md P4 says "Until a backend exists, each app keeps its current mock". active_trip_repositories.dart:17/29 and ride_history_repositories.dart:17/39 cite C-5 and read exactly that shape. The mock answers the same way (in_process_mock_client.dart:1156-1177).

2. No caller ever gets the openapi shape. Release-like flavors cannot use mock transport (env.dart:72-85), so `ApiActiveTripRepository` and `ApiRideHistoryRepository` (di.dart:150-155) only run against a real backend. contracts/openapi.yaml:1 says "PROPOSED; no backend exists".

3. The scenario fails before this code. It assumes a ride booked on a contract server. But the app books with `POST /api/v1/rides` and polls `GET /api/v1/rides/:id`, and openapi has no `/rides` path at all: its paths are `/trips`, `/trips/{tripId}` and so on (openapi.yaml:61-509). On such a server booking returns 404 first.

4. Changing the envelope alone would not fix anything. Even routed through `tripProjectionOf`, `RideProjection.toSnapshot` reads `destination` (ride_projection.dart:23), never the contract's `dropoff`, so a contract projection still returns null.

The gap is the documented, still-to-be-agreed migration (API_V1_MOCK.md:16-19; DECISIONS.md P1 "Rider rename is R4 (later)"), not a defect in the readers. Each shape is internally consistent: the stale "X-Api-Version v1" line in the doc is wrong, but the code sends 0.4 (api_client.dart:15). An earlier, related finding was refuted the same way (docs/audit-2026-10-21/raw/rider_audit_results.json:4016).

refuted.title: Not a bug: after a rider change, the same FCM token is registered again under the new rider's session, and the token-keyed push-device record moves to that rider
refuted.description: On explicit sign-out, AuthController.signOut calls push.unregister(), which unregisters the token on the server and calls FirebaseMessaging.deleteToken, so 'a signed-out Rider cannot keep receiving notifications for that session'. On session expiry, ApiClient._expireSession only clears tokens and opens Sign in. When a different rider then signs in, _enterSession -> enterSessionAs wipes local data but does nothing about push. FirebasePushService keeps `_registeredToken` and its inbound streams. _registerPushBestEffort -> register() gets the same FCM token, and `_replaceToken` skips unregistering because previous == token. The device token is never rotated, so the backend binding for the previous rider stays valid, and that rider's ride is usually still live (the DI comment says the ride goes on server-side).
refuted.failure_scenario: Rider A's session expires mid-ride on a shared phone. Rider B signs in on the same phone. The FCM token is still registered for A, so A's 'Driver arriving' and receipt pushes (driver name, plate, places) keep landing on B's phone, and B can tap them.
refuted.evidence:
auth_controller.dart:92-105 signOut: await AppScope.instance.push.unregister(); (only on explicit sign-out)
api_client.dart:220-225 _expireSession: await _tokens?.clear(); await _onSessionExpired?.call(); (no push unregister)
user_data_wipe.dart:165-176 enterSessionAs: if (wipe) await run(); (no push.unregister/deleteToken)
firebase_push_service.dart _replaceToken: if (previous != null && previous != token) await _unregisterToken(previous);
refuted.suggested_fix: When enterSessionAs detects a rider change, call push.deleteToken() (or a local-only unregister) before registering push for the new rider, so a fresh device token is minted.

verdicts.reason: The client-side part is accurate. On session expiry nothing calls push.unregister or deleteToken (only AuthController.signOut does, auth_controller.dart:95). enterSessionAs -> run (user_data_wipe.dart:165-176) does nothing about push. When B signs in, register() gets the same FCM token, and _replaceToken skips the unregister because previous == token, then POSTs /api/v1/push/devices {token} with B's auth. Whether A's pushes then reach B depends entirely on the backend. If registering an existing token rebinds it to the caller (the usual upsert-by-token design), A's binding is replaced and nothing leaks. If one token can stay bound to several riders, A's notifications reach B. docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:59-60 only defines {token, provider, platform} -> {status: registered}, and contracts/ has no push endpoint spec, so the code cannot decide it.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of firebase_push_service.dart register/_replaceToken/unregister, auth_controller.dart signOut and _registerPushBestEffort, and user_data_wipe.dart enterSessionAs. Searched contracts/ (CONTRACT.md, openapi.yaml, contract.json) for push: no definition. What would settle it: the backend's semantics for POST /api/v1/push/devices when the token is already registered to another rider (rebind vs add).

verdicts.reason: The client-side facts are correct. ApiClient._expireSession (api_client.dart:220-225) only clears tokens. enterSessionAs (user_data_wipe.dart:165-176) does not touch push. FirebasePushService._replaceToken (firebase_push_service.dart:276-296) re-posts the same FCM token without unregistering it when previous == token. Whether rider A's notifications then reach rider B depends entirely on the backend, which this repo does not define. Rider B's POST /api/v1/push/devices {token} is sent with B's access token, and the usual server design upserts a unique device token to the authenticated user, which would move the binding from A to B and send A's pushes nowhere. docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:59-60 does not say whether registration rebinds an existing token or adds a second owner. Also, push is NoopPushService under mock transport (di.dart:121-123), so this only matters against a real backend.
verdicts.repro: Read FirebasePushService.register, _replaceToken, _unregisterToken and unregister, ApiClient._expireSession, AuthController._enterSession and _registerPushBestEffort, and the push-devices contract in docs/API_V1_MOCK.md. One fact would settle it: does the backend's POST /api/v1/push/devices, when it gets a token already bound to another rider, rebind it (refuted) or keep both bindings (confirmed)?

verdicts.reason:
The client-side trace is correct, but the leak needs a server that keeps rider A's binding after rider B registers the same device token. Nothing in the repo supports that, and the client itself assumes the opposite.

1. The push-device API treats the token alone as the record's identity. Unregister is `POST /api/v1/push/devices/unregister {token}`, with no owner in the body (docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:59-60, firebase_push_service.dart:299-303). Both server models in the repo store exactly one record per token, so registering again overwrites it: `pushDevices[normalized] = {...}` (in_process_mock_client.dart:97, 512) and `pushDevices.set(token, ...)` (backend/src/index.js:101). A token-keyed API like this replaces the owner on register (upsert by token). It does not add a second owner.

2. If A ever registered push, B always registers again on sign-in. The consent key is `movera.push_consent.v1` (push_permission_gate.dart:39). It does not start with `movera_`, so `UserDataWipe.run` keeps it (user_data_wipe.dart:101). After `enterSessionAs`, `verifyOtp` and `signIn` call `_registerPushBestEffort` (auth_controller.dart:34-35, 44-45). That calls `registerIfConsented`, which sees `accepted` (push_permission_gate.dart:75) and then `register()`. `_replaceToken` then posts the same token with B's bearer token (firebase_push_service.dart:283-290).

3. So the token's single server record moves to B. A's pushes then have no device to go to, the same result as minting a fresh token. Before B signs in, the phone still gets A's pushes. That is intended: on expiry the ride and session data are kept on purpose, because the same rider usually signs back in (comment at di.dart:105-110).

What is left is a failure path the finding does not describe. If B's best-effort registration fails (network or APNs error), A's record stays. That is not the main-path leak the finding claims.
verdicts.repro:
Throwaway test /home/user/movera-rider-app/test/_audit_rider_u72_test.dart, now deleted; the tree is clean per git status. It used FirebasePushService with a fake gateway that always returns 'fcm-device-token', an ApiClient over an InProcessMockClient that records each request, and a MemoryTokenStore. Steps: save tokens for A, call register(), clear the tokens (what _expireSession does), save tokens for B, call register() again. Command: `PATH=/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH flutter test test/_audit_rider_u72_test.dart`. Output:
calls: [/api/v1/push/devices auth=Bearer access-A, /api/v1/push/devices auth=Bearer access-B]
pushDevices: {fcm-device-token: {token: fcm-device-token, provider: fcm, platform: android}}
deleteToken calls: 0
+1: All tests passed!
B's registration sends the same token with B's credentials. The server model keeps a single record per token, so B's registration replaces A's and no second binding for A remains.
verdicts.corrected_title: Not a bug: after a rider change, the same FCM token is registered again under the new rider's session, and the token-keyed push-device record moves to that rider

refuted.title: Not-found counter is not reset by non-404 failures, so non-consecutive 404s pause polling
refuted.description: `notFoundLimit` is documented as 'Consecutive 404s', but `poll.notFound` is reset only on a successful response. Timeouts, network errors and 5xx between two 404s leave it as it is, so an alternating pattern of 404 and timeout (for example a flaky gateway answering 404 during a deploy) reaches the limit. `_endNotFound` then cancels the timer, and the ride freezes until a resync. Per the known finding at line 383, a resync does not restart periodic polling.
refuted.failure_scenario: A sequence of 404, timeout, 404, 503, 404 pauses polling for a live ride, and the rider's screen stops updating.
refuted.evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:46-50 `/// Consecutive \`404\`s after which polling pauses`
102 `poll.notFound = 0;` (success path only)
264-271 `if (error is ApiError && error.statusCode == 404) { poll.notFound += 1; if (poll.notFound >= notFoundLimit) { _endNotFound(poll); return; } }` (no reset for other errors)
refuted.suggested_fix: Reset `poll.notFound = 0` in the catch block for any error that is not a 404.

verdicts.reason: It is true that poll.notFound is reset only on success (api_ride_realtime.dart:102) and not in the non-404 catch branch (264-271). But the scenario needs a server or gateway to answer 404 three times for a ride that exists. That condition already pauses polling by design when the 404s come back to back, which is the common way such a fault shows up. Counting 404s that have timeouts or 5xx between them changes almost nothing in practice, and the not-found pause is an intentional contract-v0.3.0 behaviour that reconnectAndResync undoes (379-390). The scenario is speculative and its effect is no worse than the documented consecutive-404 case.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _poll's catch block and reconnectAndResync. Not reproduced, because it needs a backend that sends false 404s.

Waiting regenerates its pins when the label key changes; Finding never does.
